entries.t: Ash Ketchum — depicted as a Chinpokomon trainer in the season 3 installment "Chinpokomon". Notable episodes: S03E11.
The "Lava and You" Boys — two teenagers who appeared in the Lava and You segment from the installment of the season 1, "Volcano". Notable episodes: S01E03.
200 Pregnant Mexican Women was spotted in the season 19 installment "Stunning and Brave". Notable episodes: S19E01.

The 24-Hour Clerks — convenience store workers, debuting in the season 11 installment "With Apologies to Jesse Jackson". They first work at Day Time 24 Night Time, and later in Kum & Go since "A Nightmare on Face Time". Notable episodes: S11E01, S16E12.
The 5th Graders — three bullies attending South Park Elementary. They debut in the season 4 installment "Fourth Grade". Notable episodes: S04E11.
The 60 Minutes Hosts — two television presenters who series up in the season 27 installment "Sermon on the 'Mount". Notable episodes: S27E01.

The Sixth Grader Leader — a sixth-grade boy at South Park Elementary. He was first seen in "The Unaired Pilot" and is among the trio of recurring 6th graders from the early seasons. He's among a few characters who cameoed as his future self in South Park: Post Covid. Notable episodes: S02E12, S03E10, SPECIAL.

entries.n: 6th Grader with Black Hair and Blue Shirt
entries.t: The 6th Grader with Black Hair and Blue Shirt — attends South Park Elementary, debuting in "Fourth Grade". He's among a few characters who cameoed as his future self in South Park: Post Covid. Notable episodes: S04E11, S08E05, SPECIAL.
k: 6th grader with black hair and blue shirt

entries.t: The 6th Grader with a Brown Hat — attends South Park Elementary, debuting in "The Unaired Pilot" and one of the trio of recurring 6th graders from the early seasons. He's among a few characters who cameoed as his future self in South Park: Post Covid. Notable episodes: S02E12, SPECIAL.
The 6th Grader with brown shirt — a background face in crowd scenes. He's a Sixth-grader at South Park Elementary, first seen in "Breast Cancer Show Ever". Notable episodes: S12E09.

The 6th Grader with Cyan Hat — attends South Park Elementary, debuting in "The Unaired Pilot" and one of the trio of recurring 6th graders from the early seasons. He's among a few characters who cameoed as his future self in South Park: Post Covid. Notable episodes: S06E13, SPECIAL.
The 6th Grader with Dark Blue Shirt — a background face in crowd scenes. He's a Sixth-grader at South Park Elementary, debuting in "Pre-School". Notable episodes: S08E10.
The 6th Grader with Green Jacket — a background face in crowd scenes. He's a Sixth-grader at South Park Elementary, first seen in "Stupid Spoiled Whore Video Playset". Notable episodes: S08E12.
The 6th Grader with Green Shirt — attends South Park Elementary, debuting in "Clubhouses". Notable episodes: S02E12, S04E11.
The 6th Grader with Orange Coat — a background face in crowd scenes. He's a Sixth-grader at South Park Elementary, debuting in "Pre-School". Notable episodes: S08E10.
The 6th Grader with Orange Hood — a background face in crowd scenes. He's a Sixth-grader at South Park Elementary, debuting in "Pre-School". Notable episodes: S08E10.

entries.n: 6th Grader with Yellow Shirt and Brown Pants
entries.t: The 6th Grader with Yellow Shirt and Brown Pants — a background face in crowd scenes. He's a Sixth-grader at South Park Elementary, debuting in "Pre-School". Notable episodes: S08E10.
k: 6th grader with yellow shirt and brown pants

entries.t: The 6th Graders Bruisers — a crew of 6th Graders, debuting in the game South Park: The Fractured But Whole as recurring enemies. They appear as background characters in some episodes of the series.

The 911 Truth Webmaster — seen in season 10's "Mystery of the Urinal Deuce" and season 12's "Britney's New Look". He runs 911truth.org — but secretly works for the government, selling the gullible on the idea that 9/11 was an inside job. Notable episodes: S10E09, S12E02.

The 9th Grader with Purple Shirt — an unnamed character who shows up in the season 5's installment "Scott Tenorman Must Die", where he and another unnamed 9th Grader are spotted as pals of Scott Tenorman. Notable episodes: S04E03, S05E04.

The 9th Grader with Red Hood — an unnamed character who was spotted in the season 5 installment "Scott Tenorman Must Die", where he and another unnamed 9th Grader are spotted as pals of Scott Tenorman. Notable episodes: S05E04.
A.W.E.S.O.M.-O 4000 — Eric Cartman's alter-ego in the season 8 installment "AWESOM-O". Notable episodes: S08E05.
Aaron Brown — once an American broadcast journalist and news reporter for CNN who shows up in the season 8 installment "Goobacks". Notable episodes: S08E07.
Aaron Hagen — a boy who shows up in the season 17 installment "Informative Murder Porn". Notable episodes: S17E02.
Abraham Lincoln — once the 16th President of the United States, debuting in the season 9 installment "Follow That Egg!". Notable episodes: S09E10.

Adam Borque — a South Park Elementary student. He shows up in the season 21 installment "Franchise Prequel", joining Professor Chaos' new army of minions. The Chaos Kids who are introduced in the installment are later heavily featured in the South Park video game, South Park: The Fractured But Whole. Notable episodes: S13E14, S21E04, S06E06.

Adam Richard Sandler — American actor-comedian renowned for his starring roles in films like Billy Madison, Happy Gilmore, and Big Daddy, as well as for his tenure on the television series Saturday Night Live. He was first referenced in the season 8 installment "AWESOM-O", and made his first appearance on South Park in the season 15 installment "Funnybot". Notable episodes: S15E02, S08E05.

Adolf Hitler — once head of the Nazi Party (Nationalist Socialist German Worker's Party) and German chancellor from 1933 to 1945, and also took on Germany's presidential powers in 1934. In South Park he's renowned for ranking among Eric Cartman's idols, emulating his powerful oratory as well as his campaign to exterminate the Jewish people. He first pops up briefly in the season 1 installment "Big Gay Al's Big Gay Boat Ride". Notable episodes: S01E04, S01E07.
The Adorable Bunnies — a large group of baby bunnies who series up in the season 4 installment "Pip". Notable episodes: S04E14.
Agent Connelly — an CIA agent who shows up in the season 3 installment "Starvin' Marvin in Space". Notable episodes: S03E13.
Agent Fields — an FBI agent who shows up in "Starvin' Marvin in Space" and "Lil' Crime Stoppers". Notable episodes: S03E13, S07E06.

Agent Tucker — once a member of the FBI Kids and the lads' rival while they played detectives in the season 7 installment "Lil' Crime Stoppers". He and a few pals wore matching outfits, with pricey toys seemingly purchased by their rich parents. Tucker would hold off until South Park Crime Unit got involved in a case before pulling "jurisdiction" on them and taking over their case, claiming FBI jurisdiction. Notable episodes: S07E06.
Aguilar — an immigrant kid from the season 23 installment "Mexican Joker". Notable episodes: S23E01.
The Air Israel Handler shows up in the season 24 installment "South ParQ Vaccination Special". Notable episodes: S24E02.
The Airsoft Armory Salesman — a worker for the South Park Airsoft Armory who shows up in the season 25 installment "Help, My Teenager Hates Me!". Notable episodes: S25E05.
The Airsoft Teenagers — a crew of teenagers that regular play Airsoft. They series up in the season 25 installment "Help, My Teenager Hates Me!". Notable episodes: S25E05.
Al Aziz Network — a news network that series up in the season 17 installment "Ginger Cow". Notable episodes: S17E06.

Al Gore — once the 45th U.S. vice president under the Clinton administration from 1993 to 2001, and ran against George Bush in 2000. He's known in the series mainly for attempting to warn people about ManBearPig, although he's also seen once while he's vice president, later returning to sue the community. Notable episodes: S03E14, S10E06, S24E02.
Al Gore's Secret Service Agents — security personnel appearing in South Park: The Stick of Truth.
Alfredo James Pacino, aka Al Pacino — an American actor most renowned for his roles in The Godfather and Scarface. He shows up in the season 18 installment "#HappyHolograms".
Albert Lincoln Roker Jr. — a television personality for the NBC News. He shows up in the season 14 installment "The Tale of Scrotie McBoogerballs". Notable episodes: S14E02.

Al-Qaeda — a terrorist organization known as militant religious extremists. The crew showed up in "Osama bin Laden Has Farty Pants" and "It's a Jersey Thing". They rescue South Park from New Jersey. Notable episodes: S05E09, S14E09.
Alan — a character residing in San Francisco. He appears in the season 10 installment "Smug Alert!". Notable episodes: S10E02.
Alan Jackson — an American country singer and songwriter who shows up in the season 6 installment "A Ladder to Heaven". Notable episodes: S06E12.
Alan — a security guard, frequently partnered with Mark seen in "Korn's Groovy Pirate Ghost Mystery" and "Trapper Keeper". Notable episodes: S03E10, S04E12.

Alana "Honey Boo Boo" Thompson — a reality TV personality and regular beauty-pageant contestant who shows up in the season 16 installment "Raising the Bar". She stars on the reality TV series, Here Comes Honey Boo Boo. She gets referenced in "A Nightmare on Face Time" where a man confuses Cartman's Hulk costume with a green Honey Boo Boo. Notable episodes: S16E09, S16E12.

Alanis Nadine Morissette — a Canadian singer, songwriter, producer, and occasional actress, most renowned for songs like "Hand in My Pocket", "Ironic", and "You Oughtta Know". Notable episodes: S02E14.
Alcoholics Anonymous — a support group for people struggling with substance and alcohol addiction. This group featured prominently in the season 9 installment "Bloody Mary". Notable episodes: S09E14.
Alec Baldwin — an American actor, renowned for his extensive film work and comedic roles on 30 Rock and Saturday Night Live. Notable episodes: MOVIE.
Alec Vaughn — an expert on county resources and preparedness, who shows up in the season 22 installment "Nobody Got Cereal?". Notable episodes: S22E07.
Alejandro White — a Mexican adopted child who shows up in the season 23 installment "Season Finale". Notable episodes: S23E06.
Alex — the receptionist for Super 12 Motel Plus who shows up in South Park: Post Covid. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
. Notable episodes: S07E07.
Alex Hart — a music record producer and manager of the Kincade Talent Agency. He shows up in the season 11 installment "Guitar Queer-O". Notable episodes: S11E13.
Alex Spanos — once the majority owner of the Los Angeles chargers who shows up in the season 18 installment "Go Fund Yourself". Notable episodes: S18E01.

Alexa — an AI-driven digital personal assistant first launched in November 2014. It was developed by Amazon and popularized by the Amazon Echo clever speaker released alongside it. Alexa, as a product, debuted in the season 21 premiere installment "White People Renovating Houses". Notable episodes: S21E01.

Alexandra Cartman, aka Cousin Alexandra — a Cartman relative debuting in "Merry Christmas Charlie Manson!": Elvin's sister, daughter of Uncle Stinky and Lisa, cousin to Eric and Fred, Liane's niece. Notable episodes: S02E16, S05E06.

Alexis Testaburger — South Park's city planner on the City Council, Wendy's mother, married to Mr. Testaburger. Her first name stayed unknown until South Park: The End of Obesity revealed it. Notable episodes: S06E10, SPECIAL.

Sayyid Ali Hosseini Khamenei, frequently known as just Ali Khamenei — once the second Supreme Leader of Iran from 1989 to 2026 who shows up in the season 17 installment "Ginger Cow". Notable episodes: S17E06.
Alice — a one-off character that was spotted in the season 4 installment "Fat Camp". Notable episodes: S04E15.
Alice's Parents — minor characters seen in "Fat Camp". Notable episodes: S04E15.
The Alien Chief of Security — a Visitor enemy fought in South Park: The Stick of Truth.
The Alien Pilots — Visitors fought in South Park: The Stick of Truth.
Alinicia — once a feat-performing turkey who was spotted in the season 4 installment "Helen Keller! The Musical". Notable episodes: S04E13.
Allah — the Arabic word for God, worshipped chiefly in Islam and the central deity of Muhammad's faith. Never shown physically, but mentioned throughout South Park.
Irwin Allen Ginsberg — once an American poet and writer who was spotted in the season 4 installment "Do the Handicapped Go to Hell?" as a Hell resident. Notable episodes: S04E09.
Allen Varcas — a 4th grade little league batter for the Conifer, CO baseball squad. He shows up in the season 9 installment "The Losing Edge". Notable episodes: S09E05.
Allie Nelson — a female fourth-grade student at South Park Elementary. She debuts in the season 11 installment "The List". Notable episodes: S11E14.
The Allied Atheist Alliance, frequently shortened to simply AAA — an organization founded in the mid-21st century in an alternate timeline. Notable episodes: S10E12.
Allison shows up in the season 11 installment "D-Yikes!" and briefly cameos in the season 12 installment "Britney's New Look". Notable episodes: S11E06, S12E02.
Allison Mertz — a female kindergartner, debuting in the season 12 installment "The Ungroundable". She's in the South Park Vampire Society. Notable episodes: S12E14.
Alois and Klara Hitler — once the parents of Adolf Hitler. They was spotted in the season 3 installment "Mr. Hankey's Christmas Classics". Notable episodes: S03E15.
Alonzo Fineski — a Romanian sex trafficker who shows up in the season 26 installment "Spring Break". He's based off former professional kickboxer Andrew Tate. Notable episodes: S26E06.
Alton Crawford Brown Jr. — an American celebrity chef who shows up in the season 14 installment "Crème Fraiche". Notable episodes: S14E14.
Amanda — the girl who appears during Chef's flashback in "The Tooth Fairy Tats 2000". Notable episodes: S04E01.

Amanda Harrison — the youngest daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Harrison and the sibling of Mark, Gary, Jenny, and Dave Harrison. She shows up in the season 7 installment "All About Mormons". Notable episodes: S07E12.
Amber Hankey — one of Mr. Hankey's children. She shows up in the season 4 installment "A Very Crappy Christmas" and South Park: The Stick of Truth. Notable episodes: S04E17.

The America's Most Wanted actors series up in the season 2 installment "Cartman's Mom — Still a Dirty Slut", where they were re-enacting the attempted assassination of Dr. Alphonse Mephesto. Notable episodes: S02E02.

The American Association of Retired Persons — a non-profit organization that lobbies the United States government on behalf of elderly and retired citizens. It shows up in the season 7 installment "Grey Dawn". Notable episodes: S07E10.
Amir shows up in the season 12 installment "Over Logging", where he — once seen as Shelley Marsh's internet boyfriend from Montana. Notable episodes: S12E06.
The Anchorman shows up in the season 3 installment "Mr. Hankey's Christmas Classics". Notable episodes: S03E15.
Anderson Cooper — an American journalist on CNN. He's first seen in the season 17 installment "Ginger Cow". Notable episodes: S17E06.
Andrew Mark Cuomo — an American politician, formerly the Governor of New York. He shows up in South Park: Post Covid: The Return of Covid. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.

Andrew Sutherland (also known as Johnny in South Park: The Fractured But Whole) — a male student at South Park Elementary. He's a recurring background character typically seen around the school. Notable episodes: S24E01, S12E09.
Andy Richter — a former co-host of Late Night with Conan O'Brien. He showed up in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. Notable episodes: MOVIE.

Andy Warhol — once an American visual artist, writer, and film director most renowned for being the leading figure of the pop art movement, who shows up in the season 2 installment "Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls" as a background character. Notable episodes: S02E09.

Angela Merkel — German politician, formerly Chancellor of Germany. Seen in "Pinewood Derby" and "Funnybot"; she joins world leaders negotiating with the alien Baby Fark McGee-Zax over "space cash", and returns with a cabinet colleague to destroy the threat to worldwide comedy: Tyler Perry. Notable episodes: S13E06, S15E02.
Angelina Jolie — an American actress, renowned for roles in numerous films like Lara Croft in Lara Croft: Tomb Raider and Jane Smith in Mr. & Mrs. Smith. Notable episodes: S11E03.
Angus Turner Jones — American ex-actor, famed as Jake Harper on Two and a Half Men — then TV's highest-paid child actor. Seen in season 14's "Poor and Stupid". Notable episodes: S14E08.

The Animal Liberation Front shows up in the season 9 installment "Free Willzyx". They're a crew of eco-terrorists who use violence to obtain what they feel is best for the animals they're "saving". Notable episodes: S09E13.
Ann Curry — a television personality for the NBC News. She shows up in the season 14 installment "The Tale of Scrotie McBoogerballs". Notable episodes: S14E02.
Anna Paulina Luna — an American politician who serves as a Member of the U.S. House of Representatives from Florida. She shows up in the season 27 installment "Sickofancy". Notable episodes: S27E03.

Annie Bennet Warbucks (1982 & 1999)/Bennet Stacks (2014) — the protagonist of the comics and films (1982, 1999 and 2014) of the same name, and also the primary character of the Broadway musical. She shows up in the season 9 installment "Ginger Kids". Notable episodes: S09E11.
Annie Bartlett — a female 5th grader who debuts in the season 12 installment "The Ungroundable". She's in the South Park Vampire Society. Notable episodes: S12E14.

Annie Knitts — a fourth-grade girl at South Park Elementary and one of the grade's popular girls, friends with Wendy, Heidi, Bebe, Red, Nichole, Nelly, Jenny, Lola, and most of the other fourth-grade girls. First seen in season 1's "Cartman Gets an Anal Probe"; early appearances cycled through several names for her (Jordan, Annie Faulk, Ashley, Annie Nelson). Notable episodes: S02E05, S08E12, S13E09, S17E10, S01E01, S03E05.
Anonymous821, whose real name — unknown, was an internet troll, debuting in the season 20 installment "Wieners Out". Notable episodes: S20E04.

Anthony Stephen Fauci — American physician, famed as a lead member of Herbert Garrison's White House Coronavirus Task Force during the U.S. COVID-19 pandemic. Seen in season 24's "The Pandemic Special". Notable episodes: S24E01.
Anthony Webster, who referred to himself online as MLKKK — once an internet troll, debuting in the season 20 installment "Wieners Out". Notable episodes: S20E06, S20E04.
The anthropologist shows up in the season 1 installment "Mecha-Streisand". Notable episodes: S01E12.

The Anti-Christ — the Woodland Critters' savior, much like how Jesus Christ is the savior for Christians. It was spotted in the season 8 installment "Woodland Critter Christmas". Notable episodes: S08E14.
António Manuel de Oliveira Guterres — a Portuguese politician, formerly the secretary-general of the United Nations. He shows up in the season 26 installment "Cupid Ye". Notable episodes: S26E01.
Anurag Saha Roy — an Indian quantum engineer, best known as the United Nations Summer of Solutions competition winner. He shows up in the season 26 installment "Cupid Ye". Notable episodes: S26E01.
The Apple Geniuses — a council of Apple Inc. employees. They're featured in "HUMANCENTiPAD". Notable episodes: S15E01.
The Apple Replacement Friend — a boy who briefly shows up in the season 15 installment "HUMANCENTiPAD". Notable episodes: S15E01.
Dr. Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, Ph.D. Jr. Notable episodes: S22E03.
Archangel Michael — a powerful angelic general from Heaven who shows up in the season 9 installment "Best Friends Forever". Notable episodes: S09E04.
Arnold Schwarzenegger — an Austrian-American actor and the former governor of California. He debuts in the season 14 installment "It's a Jersey Thing". Notable episodes: S14E09.
Arturo Gatti — once an Italian Canadian professional boxer and a world champion in two weight classes who showed up in "Dead Celebrities". Notable episodes: S13E08.

Ashley — a female 4th grader at South Park Elementary who debuted in the season 13 installment "Butters' Bottom Bitch". She's a schoolyard's version of a prostitute, as she exchanges kisses for cash. Notable episodes: S13E09.

The Asian Girls — a clique of new South Park Elementary pupils, usually found drawing art (especially yaoi) on the steps inside the school's main entrance. Formally introduced in season 19's "Tweek x Craig", with a few also in "Safe Space"; since then background faces. Other Asian-American girls at the school, like Liza Nelson, aren't part of the clique. Notable episodes: S19E06, S19E05.

Aslan the Lion — hailing from The Chronicles of Narnia. In South Park, he leads the Council of Nine in the "Imaginationland" trilogy, as well as leading the lions at the zoo in "Here Comes the Neighborhood". In "Imaginationland", he frightens Butters Stotch into tapping his "Key" powers to revive Santa Claus, and later other good characters, so the good creatures could defeat the evil ones. Notable episodes: S05E12.

Aunt Jemima — once a breakfast icon for the Quaker Oats Company who was spotted in the season 18 installment "Gluten Free Ebola", where she informs Eric Cartman, in his delirious dream, that the USDA's food pyramid is upside down. Notable episodes: S18E02.

Autumn — the dissatisfied ex-wife of Mr. Hankey and the mother of Cornwallis, Amber, and Simon. She shows up in the season 4 installment "A Very Crappy Christmas", and South Park: The Stick of Truth. She has a drinking problem and is frequently seen drunk. She broke up with Mr. Hankey as it was informed in "The Problem with a Poo" by Mr. Hankey. Notable episodes: S04E17, S22E03.

Ayman al-Zawahiri — once the leader of al-Qaeda, succeeding Osama bin Laden following his death in 2011, appearing in live-action footage of himself in "Cartoon Wars Part I". Notable episodes: S10E03.
Baahir Hassan Abdul Hakeem — a male fourth grader at South Park Elementary, who shows up in the season 11 installment "The Snuke". Notable episodes: S11E04.

Grogu, more popularly known as Baby Yoda — an alien creature from Disney+ Star Wars shows The Mandalorian and The Book of Boba Fett. He shows up in the season 23 installment "Basic Cable". Notable episodes: S23E09.

Babylonians — the ancient people of Babylonia (modern-day Iraq and Syria), known from the Bible for conquering the Kingdom of Judah and exiling the Jews in two waves (597 and 586 BC). On the show they get a joke mention as supposed builders of Egypt's pyramids in "Cartman's Mom is Still a Dirty Slut". Notable episodes: S02E02.
The Bakery Napoleon Bakers — once a group of workers for Bakery Napoleon. They was spotted in the season 10 installment "Hell on Earth 2006". Notable episodes: S10E11.
Banjo — hamster that shows up in the season 19 installment "Safe Space". Notable episodes: S19E05.

Barack Hussein Obama II — American politician, 44th U.S. president (2009–2017) and the first African-American in the office; succeeded by President Herbert Garrison after the 2016 election. Notable episodes: S12E02.
Barbara Garthunk — the receptionist for Dairy Gold Milk Company that shows up in the season 5 installment "How to Eat with Your Butt". Notable episodes: S05E10.

Barbra Streisand — a little-known singer and actress with a nose big enough to land stealth bombers on. The primary villain of "Mecha-Streisand", returning in "200", "201", and "South ParQ Vaccination Special". Notable episodes: S01E12, S24E02, S14E05, S14E06.
Barkley — a teenager who shows up in the season 16 installment "Faith Hilling". Notable episodes: S16E03.

Barky and Purry — Terrance and Phillip's pets as seen in the season 2 installment "Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus". They're also seen in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut, when Terrance and Phillip are singing the song "Uncle Fucka". Notable episodes: S02E01, MOVIE.
Barney — Officer Barbrady's K9 service dog. She debuted in the season 19 installment "Naughty Ninjas". Notable episodes: S19E07.

Barry Bonds — ex-American baseball player (Pirates, Giants). He presents the Special Olympics award in "Up the Down Steroid" alongside Jason Giambi and Mark McGwire — all three linked or allegedly linked to steroids — and reappears in "200" and "201". Notable episodes: S08E02, S14E05, S14E06.

Bartholomew "Bart" JoJo Simpson — hailing from The Simpsons, which has been both an inspiration and competitor to South Park. His first appearance was in "Cartoon Wars Part II" as he aided Cartman cancel Family Guy. Notable episodes: S10E04, S22E03.
Bartles, formerly Dave — attends South Park Elementary, debuting in "Clubhouses". Notable episodes: S12E02, S02E12.
The Bats — wild animals featured in South Park: The Stick of Truth.

Beatrice Arthur — once an American actress. She was most renowned for her role as Maude Findlay on Maude and Dorothy Zbornak on The Golden Girls. She was spotted in the season 13 installment "Dead Celebrities". Notable episodes: S13E08.
Beaky Buzzard — a fictional cartoon character who made a cameo as a handicapped camper at Lake Tardicaca in "Crippled Summer". Notable episodes: S14E07.

Bears — wild animals that debut in the season 1 installment "Volcano", but go on to become prominent as one of the primary antagonists of the season 3 installment "Jewbilee". They're also referenced a few times throughout the series and have showed up in South Park: The Stick of Truth. Notable episodes: S01E03, S04E02, S03E09.
The Beast — a Disney character who headlines the Disney fantasy film, Beauty and the Beast. He shows up in the season 23 installment "Band in China". Notable episodes: S23E02.

Beatrice McGullicutty, more commonly referred to as simply Ms. McGullicutty — an elderly resident at the Shady Acres retirement home who was featured as the primary antagonist in the season 21 installment "Hummels & Heroin". Notable episodes: S21E05.

Bebe Stevens — a female fourth-grade student at South Park Elementary who first shows up in "Cartman Gets an Anal Probe". She briefly became part of the lads' group in "Bebe's Boobs Destroy Society", but only because of her early developed breasts. Notable episodes: S01E05, S01E07, S01E01, S01E02, S06E10.

The Belarusian Farmers — once a group of protesters and farmers fighting the Belarusian government to keep their land from being developed. They was spotted in the season 16 installment "A Scause For Applause". Notable episodes: S16E13.

Ben — the head of the board of directors in one of the offices of Blizzard Entertainment, the company behind World of Warcraft, who shows up in the season 10 installment "Make Love, Not Warcraft". He's named by his girlfriend in "A Nightmare on Face Time". Notable episodes: S10E08, S16E12.

Benjamin Géza Affleck-Boldt, better known as Ben Affleck — an actor most renowned for his roles in Good Will Hunting, Armageddon, and Pearl Harbor. He debuts in the season 5 installment "How to Eat with Your Butt". Notable episodes: S05E10.

Ben Roethlisberger — pro football player, seen in season 14's "Sexual Healing". The Steelers' starting quarterback, and the youngest starting QB in NFL history to win a Super Bowl. Notable episodes: S14E01.

Benjamin Franklin — American founding father: polymath, author, printer, satirist, political theorist, politician, postmaster, scientist, inventor, civic activist, statesman, diplomat. Seen in "I'm a Little Bit Country" as a Continental Congress member in Cartman's 1776 flashback. Notable episodes: S07E04.
Benjamin Netanyahu — the present-day Prime Minister of Israel. He shows up in the season 27 installment "Conflict of Interest". Notable episodes: S27E05.
Benny — the bank teller at the Bank of South Park, who first shows up in "Margaritaville". Notable episodes: S13E03.
Benny Hill — once a British comedian who was spotted in the season 5 installment "Kenny Dies", on a television screen in the Planned Parenthood Clinic. Notable episodes: S05E13.

Beth — attends South Park Elementary. She debuted in "Stupid Spoiled Whore Video Playset" where she was participating in the "Stupid Spoiled Whore" fad. She's now commonly seen as a background character. Notable episodes: S07E05, S08E12.

Beth worked as Cartman's "bitch" in the season 10 installment "Miss Teacher Bangs a Boy". She's a part of Cartman's bounty hunter hall monitor group, which parodies Dog the Bounty Hunter, but does not speak. She's inspired by Beth Chapman, the wife of Dog. Chapman passed away from cancer in 2019. Notable episodes: S10E10.
Betsy — a female 4th grader who debuts in the season 24 installment "South ParQ Vaccination Special". Notable episodes: S24E02.
Betsy — a lesbian woman who debuts in the season 11 installment "D-Yikes!". Notable episodes: S11E06.

Betsy Donovan — once Clyde Donovan's mother and Roger Donovan's wife. She was of Dutch ancestry and per Clyde, she seemingly had a really good recipe for lemon bars. She passed away in "Reverse Cowgirl" after Clyde left the toilet seat up. Still, she was later seen alive in the episodes "Jewpacabra" and "You're Not Yelping", which is likely a continuity error. Notable episodes: S06E08, S16E01, S09E11, S16E04, S19E04.
Betsy MacIntosh — an eight-and-a-half month pregnant woman who shows up in the season 15 installment "Crack Baby Athletic Association". Notable episodes: S15E05.
Bev — a receptionist at South Park Elementary. She shows up in the season 27 installment "Wok is Dead". Notable episodes: S27E04.
Beverly Long — hailing from the season 8 installment "You Got F'd in the A". Notable episodes: S08E04.
The Big Bad Government Guy — a government official and the primary antagonist in South Park: The Stick of Truth.

Big Gay Al — a stereotypical homosexual man, debuting in the season 1 installment "Big Gay Al's Big Gay Boat Ride". He's renowned for his flamboyant and positive demeanor and typically responds to the greeting "How are you?" with an upbeat "I'm super! Thanks for asking!". Notable episodes: S01E04, SPECIAL.
Big Mesquite Murph — a hog wrestler who shows up in the season 23 installment "Shots!!!". Notable episodes: S24E02.
The Big Tobacco Employees — a large group of people who work at Big Tobacco Co. that series up in the season 7 installment "Butt Out". Notable episodes: S07E13, S12E02.

The Bigfoot Researchers — cryptozoologists (researchers of mythological beings) who series up in the season 16 installment "Jewpacabra", where they're spotted at their research station and at the location of the Easter Egg Hunt. Notable episodes: S16E04.

entries.n: Biggest Douche in the Universe Committee
entries.t: The Biggest Douche in the Universe Committee shows up in the season 6 installment "The Biggest Douche in the Universe". Notable episodes: S06E15.
k: biggest douche in the universe committee

entries.t: Christopher Wallace, aka Biggie Smalls / The Notorious B.I.G. — American rapper, frequent P. Diddy collaborator, behind East Coast hip-hop hits like "Juicy", "Hypnotize", "Mo' Money, Mo' Problems", and "I'm Goin' Back to Cali". He appears in "Hell on Earth 2006" as a Hell resident; per Butters, he can be summoned Bloody Mary-style by saying his stage name three times into a mirror. Notable episodes: S10E11.

Bill Allen — attends South Park Elementary, and is frequently seen with Fosse McDonald. Both lads are similar to Beavis and Butt-head, describing things as "gay" then laughing in a deep voice. Notable episodes: S01E04.

William Jefferson "Bill" Clinton — once the 42nd President of the United States, serving from 1993 to 2001. He has made occasional appearances on the series during his presidency, and later afterward as well. He's married to Hillary Clinton and belongs to the Democratic Party. Notable episodes: S02E02, S20E07.
Bill Clinton's Gentleman's Club — a group comprising Bill Clinton and Bill Cosby. They were featured in the season 20 installment "Oh, Jeez". Notable episodes: S20E07.

William Henry "Bill" Cosby Jr. — an African-American comedian, actor, and serial rapist. He debuted in the season 5 installment "Here Comes the Neighborhood", as one of the rich African-Americans who move to South Park. He came back as a hologram in the season 18 installment "#HappyHolograms", where he's shown attempting to molest pop star Taylor Swift during the Go Fuck Yourself Holiday Special. Notable episodes: S05E12.
Bill Cosby also known as BSM-471 — a cyborg from the future, specifically the year 2034. He shows up in the season 4 installment "Trapper Keeper". Notable episodes: S04E12.

Farmer Bill Denkins, also called Rancher Bob — a minor character who appeared frequently during the early Seasons. He was one of the first characters to appear on the series and owns a farm near South Park. Notable episodes: S05E04, S06E04, S01E01, S21E01.

Bill Donohue — an American author and the present-day president of the Catholic League for Religious and Civil Rights. He appears in the installment "Fantastic Easter Special" as the primary antagonist. Notable episodes: S11E05.
William Henry "Bill" Gates III — the founder and chairman of Microsoft. Notable episodes: MOVIE.

Bill Norman, formerly known as Bill Keegan — a news reporter and at times anchor for Channel 4 News. He debuted in the season 19 installment "Naughty Ninjas". He's the primary news anchorman in season 19 to Season 21 before returning to being a news reporter, although he was also seen as an anchor in season 24. Notable episodes: S19E07.
Bill O'Reilly shows up in the season 8 installment "Goobacks", hosting a debate about immigrants from the future on his series, The O'Reilly Factor. Notable episodes: S08E07.
William Forrester Owens — the ex-Governor of Colorado who shows up in the season 6 installment "Free Hat" and again in the season 9 installment "Follow That Egg!". Notable episodes: S06E09, S09E10.
Bill Stewart — an elderly man who appears as the president of the American Association of Retired Persons who shows up in the season 7 installment "Grey Dawn". Notable episodes: S07E10.
Bill Yellow Hawk — a Native American who Randy paid to make out with to sabotage his own DNA test. He debuted in the season 21 installment "Holiday Special.". Notable episodes: S21E03.
Billy — a minor characters who debut in the season 21 installment "Sons A Witches". Notable episodes: S21E06.
Billy — a kindergartner who debut in the season 4 installment "Trapper Keeper". Notable episodes: S04E12.
Billy Bob Thornton — an American actor, singer, songwriter, and musician who has appeared a few times on the series. Notable episodes: S14E01.

Billy Circlovich shows up in the season 4 installment "The Tooth Fairy Tats 2000". He appears again in "The Wacky Molestation Adventure", where he's spotted in the background waiting for his parents, along with other children. Notable episodes: S04E01, S04E16.
Billy Harris — a kindergartner who shows up in the season 4 installment "Trapper Keeper". Notable episodes: S04E12.

Billy Martin is only ever a background face, debuting in "Quest for Ratings". In "HUMANCENTiPAD", his father turns up, and in "200" he's spotted with a woman, possibly his mother. In "Dances with Smurfs", he's spotted in a different classroom. His name is revealed in "Bass to Mouth" in an Eavesdropper story about his hand getting stuck in his locker — and his conviction that it despises him. Notable episodes: S07E05, S08E11, S15E01, S14E05, S13E13, S15E10.

William Darrell "Billy" Mays Jr. — once an American salesman who was spotted in the season 13 installment "Dead Celebrities". He was renowned for his loud, impassioned sales pitches, which numerous people held to be incredibly annoying. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Billy Miller shows up in the season 14 installment "Medicinal Fried Chicken". Notable episodes: S14E03.
Mackey when they — once children. He made his only appearance in the season 14 installment "Insheeption". Notable episodes: S14E10.

Billy Turner — a 3rd-grader at South Park Elementary. He made his only appearance in the season 9 installment "Erection Day", and was later referenced in "Tsst", as a victim of Eric Cartman's torment. Notable episodes: S09E07, S10E07.
The Birthday Party Parents organize a birthday bash for their daughter in the season 18 installment "Cock Magic". Notable episodes: S18E08.

T' Challa, better known as Black Panther — a Marvel character who headlines the film of the same name. He was first referenced in the season 22 installment "Dead Kids", but first physically shows up in the season 23 installment "Band in China". Notable episodes: S23E02, S22E01.
The Black-Haired Scientist — an unnamed minor character who debut in the season 11 installment "Imaginationland, Episode II". Notable episodes: S11E11.

Blaintology — the cult from "Super Best Friends", founded by magician David Blaine. His followers, the Blaintologists, shave their heads regardless of gender, which confuses onlookers who can't tell anyone apart; the faith accepts all backgrounds and treats Blaine's book "David Blaine: Teachings" as scripture. After the government denies the cult tax-exempt status, Blaine orders a mass suicide in protest — until the Super Best Friends (Jesus, Buddha, Moses, Muhammad, Seaman, Joseph Smith, Krishna, and Lao Tse) break his hold and the followers abandon him. Notable episodes: S05E03.

Prince Michael Jackson II, known as Blanket Jackson — seen in "The Jeffersons" after he and his father Michael (alias "Mr. Jefferson") move into the neighborhood. He wears a mask constantly until his father lets him remove it at the episode's end; he reveals he's a test-tube baby who never knew his mother. Notable episodes: S08E06.

Blaze — a stripper who works at The Peppermint Hippo. She's well renowned for her catchphrases "Would you like a dance?", and "Dance?! Anybody like a dance?". She debuts in the season 7 installment "Lil' Crime Stoppers". She's later seen working in South Park Elementary's Administration Office in "Tegridy Farms". Notable episodes: S07E06, S22E04.
Blink-182 — an American pop-punk band seen in the season 7 installment "Christian Rock Hard". Notable episodes: S07E09.
Bluey Christine Heeler — the primary protagonist of the eponymous children's series Bluey. She shows up in the season 28 installment "Sora Not Sorry". Notable episodes: S28E03.
Robert Osbourne Denver — once an American actor who was spotted in the season 2 installment "The Mexican Staring Frog of Southern Sri Lanka". Notable episodes: S02E06.

Bob Dole — American politician: U.S. Senator from 1969 to 1996, Representative from 1961 to 1969, and the 1996 Republican presidential nominee, losing to Bill Clinton. In retirement he became a TV pitchman, most famously for Viagra. On the show he's heard only as a voice in a commercial in "Spontaneous Combustion". Notable episodes: S03E02.
Bob Ferrin — a representative of the Make-a-Wish Foundation. He shows up in the season 5 installment "Kenny Dies". Notable episodes: S05E13.
Robert "Bob" Allan Iger — the incumbent CEO of The Walt Disney Company, having served as the company's CEO since 2005, appearing in South Park: Joining the Panderverse. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.

Bob Johnson — one of Mayor McDaniels' aides. He and Janson help the mayor run South Park and serve on the City Council, and she's frequently known to claim his ideas as her own. Although he's briefly fired in "Volcano", he appears to be rehired in later episodes. Notable episodes: S01E02, S01E03.

Bob Saget — once an American actor and comedian. He was most renowned for his role as Danny Tanner on the sitcom, Full House and hosting America's Funniest Home Videos from 1989 to 1997. He was spotted in the season 1 installment "Cartman's Mom is a Dirty Slut" as the host of America's Stupidest Home Videos. He later reshowed up in "200" and "201". Notable episodes: S01E13, S14E06, S14E05.
Bob Summers — an elderly man who debut in the season 12 installment "Britney's New Look". Notable episodes: S12E02.
Bob Thomas — a dodgeball coach for a school in Denver. He shows up in "Conjoined Fetus Lady", where they faced the South Park Cows. Notable episodes: S02E05.

Robert "Bob" White — husband of Mrs. White, father of Jason and Crystal. He and his wife were die-hard Garrison supporters, earning the family a terrible reputation around town. He debuted as co-main villain of the season 21 finale "Splatty Tomato". Notable episodes: S24E02, S21E10.
Bobby shows up in the season 16 installment "Faith Hilling". Notable episodes: S16E03.
Bobby — an operator for the John Denver Experience ride in North Park Funland. He shows up in the season 4 installment "Cartman Joins NAMBLA". Notable episodes: S04E05.
Robert William Flay — an American celebrity chef who shows up in the season 14 installment "Crème Fraiche". Notable episodes: S14E14.
Bobby Palmer — a male student at South Park Elementary who first shows up in "Breast Cancer Show Ever" along with a few other students. Notable episodes: S12E09, S26E04.
The Body Language Expert — a guest speaker in Fox and Friends for Fox News. He shows up in the season 27 installment "Wok is Dead". Notable episodes: S27E04.

Paul David Hewson, aka Bono — the lead singer of the Irish rock band U2 and a renowned activist for assorted causes. He appears in the installment "More Crap", where he serves as the primary antagonist. After Mr. Hankey and his family, Bono ranks as South Park's second talking piece of fecal matter. Still, he's the first to take on a human form. Notable episodes: S11E09.
Bono's Butler — a butler who shows up in the season 11 installment "More Crap". Notable episodes: S11E09.
Boots — a character in the kids' animated TV series Dora the Explorer, who shows up in "Taming Strange". Notable episodes: S17E05.
Alexander Boris de Pfeffel Johnson — British politician, author, and journalist: UK Prime Minister 2019–2022, London Mayor 2008–2016. Seen in season 20's "Members Only". Notable episodes: S20E08.

Boston — an American rock band formed by Tom Scholz in 1975. They're renowned for songs like "More Than a Feeling" and "Smokin'". The band made a brief appearance in the season 20 installment "Skank Hunt". Notable episodes: S20E02.
Brad The "PC Arizona State" — one of the PC Bros, debuting in the season 19 installment "Stunning and Brave". Notable episodes: S19E01.
Brad Davis — a professional thief who shows up in the season 12 installment "About Last Night...". Notable episodes: S12E12.
Brad Morgan — a CNN news reporter that shows up in the season 8 installment "Goobacks". Notable episodes: S08E07.

Brad Paisley — American country singer-songwriter known for humorous, pop-culture-laced songs. He sings the national anthem before a Clippers–Nuggets game and duets "I Swear" with Cartman in "Cartman Finds Love"; a poster of him hangs in the WXFU lobby in "Buddha Box" (his song "Today" closes the episode); and he wrote and performed the original "We Are South America" for "South American Biker Gangs". Notable episodes: S16E07, S22E08, S29E01.

Bradley ("Cartman Sucks") — Butters' "Acountabilibuddy" at Camp New Grace. He lands them both in trouble over a men's underwear catalog in his room; after Butters innocently says he "like-likes" him, Bradley confesses to "bad thoughts" and, believing himself incurable, tries to jump off a bridge — but climbs down safely after Butters' speech. He's later glimpsed fishing off that bridge with the camp director in the season 17 intro. Notable episodes: S11E02.

Bradley Biggle (born Gok'zarah, aka Mintberry Crunch) — one of the lads' classmates. He's depicted as a background character until his first key appearance in the Superheroes Saga, beginning with "Coon 2: Hindsight". Notable episodes: S14E13, S03E15, S03E01, S14E11.

Brandon Carlile — a reporter for SPIN magazine who shows up in the season 18 installment "The Cissy". He's inspired by SPIN magazine reporter Brennan Carley, who wrote a widely criticized article about the installment "Gluten Free Ebola", and its supposed implication that a middle-aged man, Randy Marsh, could pass as the singer Lorde. Notable episodes: S18E03, S18E02.
Brandy — a contestant for the Little Miss Pageant in Denver. She's shown in the season 13 installment "Dead Celebrities". Notable episodes: S13E08.
Brandy's Mother — a the mother of Brandy who attends a beauty pageant in Denver in the season 13 installment "Dead Celebrities". Notable episodes: S13E08.

Brendan Carr — an American lawyer who has been serving as chair of the Federal Communications Commission since 2025. He debuts in the season 27 installment "Conflict of Interest". Notable episodes: S27E05.
Brent Woody Musburger — an American sportscaster who shows up in the season 2 installment "City on the Edge of Forever (Flashbacks)".
Brett — a clerk who works the front desk of the EvGames video game store who shows up in the season 11 installment "Guitar Queer-O". Notable episodes: S11E13.

Brett Lorenzo Favre — an American retired NFL Quarterback who primarily played for the Green Bay Packers from 1992 to 2007. He shows up in the season 2 installment "Summer Sucks". Notable episodes: S02E08.
Brian — the television executive of the Canada Channel, the sole TV channel in Canada. Notable episodes: S10E04.
Brian — one of the announcers at Denver Sea Park in "Free Willzyx". Notable episodes: S09E13.
Brian — a employee for Wolf Home Security who shows up in the season 16 installment "Insecurity". Notable episodes: S16E10.
Brian — a character residing in San Francisco. He appears in the season 10 installment "Smug Alert!". Notable episodes: S10E02, S13E05.
Brian — a 5th grade little league batter for the Greeley baseball squad. He shows up in the season 9 installment "The Losing Edge". Notable episodes: S09E05.

Brian Boitano — an Olympic gold-medalist figure skater, whose professional career has spanned two decades. He has been repeatedly referenced in South Park, typically preceded by the catchphrase "What would Brian Boitano do?" He's a fictionalized version of the celebrity, one of few to be depicted in a positive light. Notable episodes: S14E06.
Brian Boyant — an insurance salesman for GEICO who was spotted in the season 19 installment "Sponsored Content". Notable episodes: S19E08.

Brian Dennehy — American actor (Sheriff Will Teasle in First Blood, Walter in Cocoon, Big Tom Callahan in Tommy Boy). He appears in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut during "What Would Brian Boitano Do?", with lines spoofing Brian Boitano's from the original Jesus vs. Santa short; he later reappears in the background of "200" as one of the celebrities suing South Park. Notable episodes: MOVIE, S14E06, S14E05.
H. Brian Griffin — a primary character from the animated sitcom Family Guy. He's the talking pet of the Griffin family and appears in both Cartoon Wars episodes. Notable episodes: S10E03.
Brian Jeffries — once an aide to Hillary Clinton who was spotted in the season 11 installment "The Snuke". Notable episodes: S11E04.
Brian Thompson-Jarvis — a character who shows up in the season 10 installment "Smug Alert!". Notable episodes: S10E02.

Bridon Gueermo — a 3rd grade student who debuts in the season 12 installment "Elementary School Musical". He's a parody of Zac Efron's character Troy Bolton from High School Musical. Notable episodes: S12E13.

Brimmy — a 4th grader at South Park Elementary. He has remained a background character since the first season and still appears frequently in the series, although he has almost never spoken within the series and has no known personality.

Britney Jean Spears — an American singer and songwriter. Dubbed the "Princess of Pop", she most renowned for her songs like "...Baby One More Time" and "Womanizer". She first appeared as an animated character in the season 7 installment "Christian Rock Hard", and had a much larger role in "Britney's New Look". Notable episodes: S12E02, S03E03, S07E09.

Broadway Bros — Sondheim, Schwartz, Andrew Lloyd Webber, and Elton John as hard-partying Broadway writers who hang out at Hooters and secretly plant subliminal messaging in theater productions to get men oral sex. In "Broadway Bro Down" they panic when Randy's blatant "Splooge-Drenched Blowjob Queen" threatens to expose the scheme; after a "bro-down" between Randy and Sondheim, the writers befriend Randy and help him retool the show into "The Woman in White" — all subtext, no explicit mentions. Notable episodes: S15E11.
Brooke Shields — American actress and model, famed for The Blue Lagoon, Pretty Baby, and Suddenly Susan. First seen in the film South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. Notable episodes: MOVIE.

The Brooklyn Nets — a professional basketball squad, with the Barclays Center in New York City as their home base. They series up in the season 26 installment "The Worldwide Privacy Tour". Notable episodes: S26E02.

Bruce — an audio engineer who records audio for the lads, Britney Spears and the PC Babies. He first shows up in "A Very Crappy Christmas". He later shows up in "Britney's New Look" with an updated design. Notable episodes: S04E17, S12E02.

Walter Bruce Willis — a retired American actor and musician. He, famed for his role as Detective John McClane in the 1988 action film, Die Hard. He shows up in the season 2 installment "Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls" as a background character. Notable episodes: S02E09.
The Bruisers — an enemy faction in South Park: Snow Day!.

Bryan Adams — a Canadian singer and songwriter who is first referenced in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. He later shows up in the season 15 installment "Royal Pudding". Notable episodes: S15E03, MOVIE.

Lynell Griffin, better known as Bubb Rubb, shows up in the season 12 installment "Canada on Strike", as one of the internet celebrities waiting for their theoretical payments. He may or may not be deceased since he was not seen fighting or dead. Notable episodes: S12E04.
Buck — Leslie's husband and the father of Buck Jr. and Calvin. He shows up in the season 2 installment "Prehistoric Ice Man". Notable episodes: S02E18.
Buck Jr. — a 13-year-old boy and the son of Larry's ex-wife, Leslie. He shows up in the season 2 installment "Prehistoric Ice Man". Notable episodes: S02E18.
Bucky Bailey — a counselor, and the founder of Bucky Bailey's Bully Buckers. He shows up in the season 16 installment "Butterballs". Notable episodes: S16E05.

Bud 'Uncle' Stotch — Butters' uncle, who is first seen in the season 8 installment "AWESOM-O". He was later referenced in the season 10 installment "The Return of Chef". Notable episodes: SPECIAL, S16E05, S08E05, S10E01.
Buddha (शाक्यमुनि) — the founder of Buddhism and a member of the Super Best Friends, debuting in the season 5 installment "Super Best Friends". Notable episodes: S05E03.

Buddy Ebsen — once an American actor renowned for his role as Barnaby Jones in the eponymous detective drama. He was spotted in the season 2 installment "Roger Ebert Should Lay off the Fatty Foods". Notable episodes: S02E11.

Burgess Meredith — once an American actor and filmmaker. He, famed for his roles as The Penguin in the Batman television series and boxing trainer Mickey Goldmill from the Rocky film series. He shows up in the season 9 installment "The Losing Edge". Notable episodes: S09E05.
Butt Out! is an anti-smoking group that appears in the eponymous Season 7 installment "Butt Out". Notable episodes: S07E13.

Leopold "Butters" Stotch — a key character in the series. He's a fourth-grader in South Park Elementary. Butters' role gradually grew after he replaced Kenny during his temporary absence in season 6. This gave Butters more screen time with his character developing further. He's the "innocent child" in the crew and Cartman's most exploited and possibly best "friend". Butters is loosely inspired by Eric Stough, an animation director/producer that works on the series. Notable episodes: S09E09, S15E09, S06E06, S06E03, S13E10, S08E05, S01E01, S02E12.
Butters Stotch (Universe 216-B) — an alternate form of Butters Stotch who shows up in South Park: Joining the Panderverse. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Butters' Friends — a crew of students, debuting in the season 13 installment "Dances with Smurfs". Notable episodes: S13E13.
Butters' Kissing Company — once an organization founded by Butters seen in the season 13 installment "Butters' Bottom Bitch". Notable episodes: S13E09.
Buzz Lightyear — a Disney character who is a primary character of the movies Toy Story and Lightyear. He shows up in the season 23 installment "Band in China". Notable episodes: S23E02.

The Cafeteria Servers — characters who debut in the season 15 installment titled "Funnybot", although they have their most notable appearances in the season 23 installment "Let Them Eat Goo". Notable episodes: S15E02, S23E04.
Caine shows up in the season 13 installment "Margaritaville", where he — once seen as the cashier for the Sur la Table store. Notable episodes: S13E03.

Caitlyn Marie Jenner, formerly William Bruce Jenner or just Bruce Jenner — a retired American athlete and the 48th U.S. vice president, serving under Herbert Garrison. She transitioned after feeling female inside her whole life. The primary focus of the installment "Stunning and Brave" is how Kyle does not believe she's a hero for coming out as transgender. Notable episodes: S14E02, S19E02, S19E01.
The Cajun Shrimp Merchant shows up in the season 14 installment "Coon 2: Hindsight". Notable episodes: S14E11.
Calvin — an 8-year-old boy and the son of Larry's ex-wife, Leslie. He shows up in the season 2 installment "Prehistoric Ice Man". Notable episodes: S02E18.

Cameron has different roles during the series, he — once seen as a Toss-A-Ball operator in "Cow Days", and appears to be one of Jimbo's pals in "Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub". Notable episodes: S02E13, S03E08.

The Camp New Grace Counselors — counselors at Camp New Grace, a religious camp that aims to turn gay and bi-curious children straight. They debut in the season 11 installment "Cartman Sucks". Notable episodes: S11E02.
The Canadian Banker — a minor South Park character: The Stick of Truth.
The Canadian Gynecologist — a minor character who shows up in the season 13 installment "Eat, Pray, Queef". Notable episodes: S13E04.
The Canadian Minister of Sports — a minor character that shows up in the season 18 installment "Freemium Isn't Free". Notable episodes: S18E06.

The Canadian Minister of Streaming (formerly the Canadian Minister of Movies) shows up in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut, where he's spotted debating Sheila Broflovski at the U.N. Building. He previously went by the Canadian Minister of Movies. He later showed up in "SUPER HARD PCness" as The Canadian Minister of Streaming. Notable episodes: MOVIE, S21E09.
The Canadian Prime Minister — a minor character featured in season 15 installment "Royal Pudding". Notable episodes: S15E03, S07E15, S27E01.
The Canadian Prime Minister — a minor character featured in season 27 installment "Sermon on the 'Mount". Notable episodes: S27E01.
Canadians — citizens of Canada. Notable episodes: S01E06.
Candice — a flight attendant who shows up in the season 12 installment "Tonsil Trouble". Notable episodes: S12E01.
The Cannabis Farmers Panelist — a speaker for the Cannabis Cultivators Expo who shows up in the season 25 installment "The Big Fix". Notable episodes: S25E02.
Steve Rogers, better known as Captain America — a Marvel character who stars on the film with the same name. He shows up in the season 23 installment "Band in China". Notable episodes: S23E02.
Captain Horatio Magellan Crunch — the mascot of the Cap'n Crunch cereal, physically appearing in South Park: The End of Obesity. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Captain Diabetes — the superhero alter-ego of Scott Malkinson. He shows up in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Jack Brolin, better known by his identity Captain Hindsight — a news reporter and former superhero who debuts in the season 14 installment "Coon 2: Hindsight". Notable episodes: S14E11.
Captain James Bartholomew Hook — a Disney character who is the primary antagonist of the film, Peter Pan. He shows up in the season 23 installment "Band in China". Notable episodes: S11E12, S23E02.

Carol Danvers, better known as Captain Marvel — a Marvel Character who headlines the MCU film of the same name played by actress Brie Larson. She shows up in the season 23 installment "Band in China". Notable episodes: S23E02.
Captain Taylor and Captain Gabriel — two pilots for Homeland Security who play a minor role in season 12's Pandemic duology. Notable episodes: S12E11, S12E10.

Cardinal Roger Mahony — the former prelate of the Roman Catholic Church who served as Archbishop for the Los Angeles Catholic Archdiocese from 1985 to 2011. He's shown in the season 10 installment "Hell on Earth 2006". Notable episodes: S10E11.
Carl — an explosives expert who was spotted in the season 1 installment "Big Gay Al's Big Gay Boat Ride". Notable episodes: S01E04.
Carl — once a character in the season 7 installment "Grey Dawn". Notable episodes: S07E10.
Carlos — a boy Eric Cartman hires as part of his squad to smear poop all over Butters' home in the season 6 installment "My Future Self n' Me". Notable episodes: S06E16.

Carlos Mencia — a Honduran-born American comedian. He, famed for creating and starring in the comedy sketch series, Mind of Mencia on Comedy Central from 2005 to 2008. He was spotted in the season 13 installment "Fishsticks", where he asserted to be the creator of the Fishsticks Joke. Notable episodes: S13E05.
Carol McCormick — the wife to Stuart McCormick, as well as the mother of Kenny, Kevin, and Karen. She debuted in the season 1 installment "Starvin' Marvin". Notable episodes: S01E08.

Caroline Manzo — an American television personality most renowned for starring in the reality TV series, The Real Housewives of New Jersey, who shows up in "It's a Jersey Thing". Notable episodes: S14E09.

Scott Thompson, stage name Carrot Top — American prop comedian (Chairman of the Board). He plays a comic called "Carrot Ass" in "City on the Edge of Forever (Flashbacks)", wetting himself and fleeing the stage in embarrassment after Veronica Crabtree heckles him, to the audience's delight. He also appears in Cartman's "Gingervitus" presentation in "Ginger Kids". Notable episodes: S09E11.
The Cartman Impostor — once an unidentified young boy who was spotted in the season 4 installment "Fat Camp". Notable episodes: S04E15.
Cartman's Father — a deleted character from the unaired pilot, spotted at the Cartman family dinner — motionless and silent, like Cartman's Sister.

Cartman's New Bros — a friend group consisting of Jimmy Valmer, Clyde Donovan, Eric Cartman, and a Hispanic Boy. It's founded in "South ParQ Vaccination Special" after Cartman officially ends his broship with The Boys. Notable episodes: S24E02.

Cartman's Sister — a deleted character who appears in the pilot installment "The Unaired Pilot". She was spotted in the scene where the Cartman family is having dinner in the dining room but does not move or speak during the scene.

Casey Miller — a third-grader at South Park Elementary who competes with Cartman to become the new morning announcer in "Dances with Smurfs". Friends describe his voice as "butter to their ears" and "audible chocolate". Cartman tricks him out of the running by claiming Casey insulted Mr. Mackey's toupee — but Casey ends the episode as the new announcer, reading a letter that savages Cartman's management of the school. Notable episodes: S13E13.

The Cash For Gold Sign Holders series up in the season 16 installment "Cash For Gold", where they're spotted holding their signs outside of their place of employment, the Cash For Gold shops. Notable episodes: S16E02.

The Catamount Pictures Producers — a crew of television and film producers. They're first employed under the HBC Network in the season 5 installment "It Hits the Fan", and later under Catamount Pictures in the season 8 installment "AWESOM-O". Notable episodes: S05E01, S08E05.
Catatafish debuted in the season 6 installment "The Death Camp of Tolerance". He aided Lemmiwinks and presumably Paris Hilton escape Mr. Slave's digestive system. Notable episodes: S06E14.

entries.n: Cave of the Winds Tour Guide
entries.t: The Cave of the Winds Tour Guide — a tour guide from the season 10 installment "ManBearPig". Notable episodes: S10E06.
k: cave of the winds tour guide

entries.t: Cee Lo Green, aka CeeLo Green — an American singer-songwriter and rapper. He shows up in the season 16 installment "Sarcastaball", where he sings the "I Love Sarcastaball" before the Denver Broncos and Oakland Raiders sarcastaball game. Notable episodes: S16E08.

Celine Dion — a Canadian pop singer who is renowned for her songs like "Because You Loved Me" and "My Heart Will Go On". She shows up in the season 2 installment "Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus". She's revealed to be the ex-wife of Terrance, and the mother of their daughter Sally Dion. Notable episodes: S02E01.
Cesar Millan — a Mexican-American dog trainer. He shows up in the season 10 installment "Tsst". Notable episodes: S10E07.
Chad — a character that was spotted in the season 4 installment "Fat Camp". Notable episodes: S04E15.
Chad Handler — a male fourth grader with disabilities who appears in a few episodes with other handicapped children. Notable episodes: S08E02.

Chad's Parents ("Fat Camp") — appear at the end of "Fat Camp", pulling Chad out because he isn't losing weight, with his father demanding a refund from the counselors. Chad then admits he was eating the sweets Cartman sold campers at bedtime. Notable episodes: S04E15.
The Chamber of Commerce Representative — a minor character who shows up in the season 8 installment "Stupid Spoiled Whore Video Playset". Notable episodes: S08E12.
Chantal — a 4-month old baby girl seen in the season 6 installment "Freak Strike". Notable episodes: S06E03.
Chaos Hamsters — Butters Stotch's pets and serve as Professor Chaos's minions. Notable episodes: S06E06.
Chaos Kids — an enemy faction in South Park: The Fractured But Whole. Notable episodes: S21E04.

Chaos Minions — employees of Professor Chaos, appearing in South Park: The Fractured But Whole. The faction is composed of four distinct groups; schoolchildren, Mexican men, hamsters, and dogs. Notable episodes: S06E06.
Charles Biggens — a culinary expert who shows up in the season 15 installment "A History Channel Thanksgiving". Notable episodes: S15E13.
Charles Kincade — the manager for the Kincade Talent Agency and represents Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, and then Thad Jarvis in the season 11 installment "Guitar Queer-O". Notable episodes: S11E13.

Charles Milles Manson (né Maddox) — once an American criminal and cult leader, renowned for his followers murder of actress Sharon Tate on his orders in 1969. He was spotted in the season 2 installment "Merry Christmas Charlie Manson!". Notable episodes: S02E16.
Charlie — a pitchman for the Dyno Might Firework Company who shows up in the season 2 installment "Summer Sucks". Notable episodes: S02E08.
Charlie Brown — a primary character on the comic strip Peanuts by Charles M. Schulz who debuted in the season 4 installment "A Very Crappy Christmas". Notable episodes: S04E17.

Charles Peete Rose Jr. — an American journalist and former talk series host. He most renowned for hosting the PBS talk series, The Charlie Rose Show from 1991 to 2017. He shows up in the season 4 installment "Timmy 2000" and later reshows up in the season 16 installment "A Scause For Applause". Notable episodes: S04E03, S16E13.

Charlie Sheen — an American actor. He, famed for his starring role in films like Platoon, Wall Street and Major League, as well as the CBS sitcom, Two and a Half Men. He first showed up in "Sexual Healing". Notable episodes: S14E01.

entries.n: Charlie/Marcus Andrews and his Superior Officer
entries.t: The U.S. Border Patrol series up in the season 15 installment "The Last of the Meheecans". Notable episodes: S15E09.
k: charlie/marcus andrews and his superior officer

entries.t: Charlotte — a Canadian girl, debuting in the season 19 installment "Where My Country Gone?", where she's spotted dating Butters Stotch. Notable episodes: S19E02, S20E04.
Charlotte's Brother shows up in the season 19 installment "Where My Country Gone?". Notable episodes: S19E02.
Charlotte's Grandmother shows up in the season 19 installment "Where My Country Gone?". It's unclear whether she's the mother of Thomas or Charlotte's Mother. Notable episodes: S19E02.
Charlotte's Mother shows up in the season 19 installment "Where My Country Gone?". Notable episodes: S19E02.
Charlotte's Sister shows up in the season 19 installment "Where My Country Gone?". Notable episodes: S19E02.
Chase — a character who shows up in the season 15 installment "T.M.I.". Notable episodes: S15E04.

ChatGPT — a generative-AI chatbot, first seen in season 26's "Deep Learning". Users type prompts and it generates text, audio, or images; it can also serve as a personal assistant and hold real-time conversations. Notable episodes: S26E04.

Cheech Marin and Tommy Chong, the Cheech & Chong comedy duo — appearing as fictionalized versions of themselves posing as Cherokee herbalists in season 4's "Cherokee Hair Tampons". Notable episodes: S04E06.
The Cheesing King shows up in the season 12 installment "Major Boobage". Notable episodes: S12E03.
The Chef Aid host — a character that is spotted for the first time in the season 2 installment "Chef Aid". He emcees the Chef Aid concert. Notable episodes: S02E14.

Cherilynn Sarkisian, better known as Cher — an American singer, actress, and television personality, commonly referred to as the "Goddess of Pop". She was first referenced in the season 3 installment "Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub", where her song "Believe" was featured. She made a physical appearance in the season 20 installment "Members Only" as one of the people wishing to leave for Mars. Notable episodes: S05E05, S03E08, S20E08.
Chet — a minor South Park character, debuting in the season 8 installment "Goobacks". He's one of the community's numerous redneck residents. Notable episodes: S08E07.
Chief Joe — the head of the National Security Agency (NSA). He shows up in the season 17 premiere installment "Let Go, Let Gov". Notable episodes: S17E01.

Chief Running Water — a Native American chief of the Ute Tribe. He was spotted in the season 1 installment "Cartman's Mom is a Dirty Slut", and had a non-speaking role in "Cartman's Mom is Still a Dirty Slut". He also had a non-speaking background role in "201", present when Cartman discovers the true identity of his father. Notable episodes: S01E13, S02E02, S14E06.
Chief Runs With Premise — a Native American chief and the owner of the Three Feathers Indian Casino. He shows up in the season 7 installment "Red Man's Greed". Notable episodes: S07E07.
Chief Runs With Premise's Wife shows up in the season 7 installment "Red Man's Greed". Notable episodes: S07E07.
The Chief Scientist — once the scientist in charge of investigating COVID-19 in the season 24 installment "The Pandemic Special". Notable episodes: S24E01.
Chief Stevens — a police chief, debuting in the season 2 installment "Merry Christmas Charlie Manson!". Notable episodes: S02E16.
The Chinese Book Reader — a minor character from Season 14 installment "The Tale of Scrotie McBoogerballs". Notable episodes: S14E02.
The Chinese Clubbers appear in Randy's flashback to his time in Wuhan in "The Pandemic Special". Notable episodes: S24E01.

The Chinese Commentators — two Chinese men who commentate over the dodge ball game between the South Park Cows and the Chinese dodgeball squad in the season 2 installment "Conjoined Fetus Lady". Notable episodes: S02E05.

The Chinese Court Judges — a trio of high-ranking Chinese officials who came to judge Randy Marsh's crime of illegal possession of marijuana into China. They series up in the season 23 installment "Band in China". They rewas seen in the season 24's installment "The Pandemic Special". Notable episodes: S23E02, S24E01.

The Chinese Customs Officers — a duo of airport customs officers who stumbled upon Randy Marsh's baggage to find out it was marijuana inside. They series up in the season 23 installment "Band in China" and resurfaced as a flashback in the season 24 installment "The Pandemic Special". Notable episodes: S23E02, S24E01.
The Chinese Dodgeball Players — a crew of children from China that are specialized in dodgeball. They series up in the season 2 installment "Conjoined Fetus Lady". Notable episodes: S02E05.
The Chinese Mafia — an organized crime organization that shows up in the season 9 installment "Wing". Notable episodes: S09E03.
The Chinese Shopkeeper — the manager of a tea shop in China. She shows up in the season 23 installment "Band in China". Notable episodes: S23E02.
Chip Duncan — once a townsperson in South Park who appeared in the installment "Sons A Witches". Notable episodes: S21E06.
Chiquita — a costumed character at Casa Bonita, appearing in From Dusk till Casa Bonita DLC of South Park: The Fractured But Whole. Notable episodes: S07E11.

Chris — one of Satan's boyfriends who shows up in the season 4 installment "Do the Handicapped Go to Hell?", and its sequel "Probably". He's referenced in the season 6 installment "A Ladder to Heaven". Notable episodes: S04E09, S04E10, S06E12.
Chris — a news reporter who shows up in the season 12 installment "Britney's New Look". Notable episodes: S12E02.
Chris — the father of The New Kid, appearing in South Park: The Stick of Truth and South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Chris Allen — once a real estate agent employed under South Park Realtors. He debuted in the season 25 installment "Pajama Day". Notable episodes: SPECIAL, S25E01.
Christopher James Christie — an American politician who served as the Governor of New Jersey. He shows up in the season 20 installment "Member Berries". Notable episodes: S20E01.

Cara Cunningham, formerly Christopher Darren Cunningham and better known by her stage name Chris Crocker, is an American internet celebrity notable for her "Leave Britney Alone" video who was spotted in the season 12 installment "Canada on Strike". Notable episodes: S12E04.
Chris Donnely — a minor face in the season 17 "Black Friday" trilogy with the Sony Fighters of Zaron; also in South Park: The Stick of Truth as part of the Elven Kingdom. Notable episodes: S17E07.
Christopher Cross "Chris" Griffin — the middle child of the Griffin Family and a primary character on Family Guy, he's 13 years old. Notable episodes: S10E03, S12E04.

Chris Hansen — an American journalist and television presenter. He, famed for being the host of Dateline's To Catch a Predator which involves the catching of child molesters. He appeared in the installment "Le Petit Tourette". Notable episodes: S11E08.
Chris Holt — a news reporter working for the SNN network. Notable episodes: S05E08, S05E09.
Chris Martin — a guest speaker for The Charlie Rose Show. He shows up in the season 16 installment "A Scause For Applause". Notable episodes: S16E13.

Chris Peterson — a South Park townsfolk recognizable by his unusual haircut; similar to the hair of Butters. He first shows up in "Mr. Hankey, the Christmas Poo" and appears briefly in the season 3 installment "Spontaneous Combustion" when Kenny spontaneously combusts at the start of the installment. Notable episodes: S02E02, S01E09, S03E02.
Chris Swollenballs — a news reporter who was the lead reporter for Channel 4 News from Season 5 to Season 9, working with anchor Tom Pusslicker. Notable episodes: S02E14.
Christian Wilhelm Walter Wulff — a German politician, formerly the President of Germany. He shows up in the season 15 installment "Funnybot". Notable episodes: S15E02.

Christina María Aguilera — an American singer who appears as a pink monster in season 4 installment "Timmy 2000". She, famed for her songs like "Genie in a Bottle", "Come on Over Baby (All I Want Is You)", and "Beautiful". Notable episodes: S04E03.
Christina Nylon — a CNN news reporter that shows up in the season 8 installment "Goobacks". Notable episodes: S08E07.
Christine — a woman from Evergreen who was spotted in the season 11 installment "Night of the Living Homeless". Notable episodes: S11E07.
Christine Jonez — once Jared Fogle's fiancé who shows up in the season 6 installment "Jared Has Aides". Notable episodes: S06E01.
Christophe, aka the Mole — a bitter nine-year-old French kid, expert in covert ops with an intense hatred of God. Seen in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. Notable episodes: MOVIE, S03E08.

Christophe's Mother — seen in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. After her son speaks ill of God she grounds him — suggesting Christian or Catholic faith; both speak with French accents, implying they're from France. Notable episodes: MOVIE.

Christopher D'Olier Reeve — American actor and stem-cell-research activist, famed as Superman in the original Warner Bros. film series. Seen in "Krazy Kripples" (as its main villain) and "200". Notable episodes: S07E02, S14E05.
Chuck Chuck — the child of ManBearPig and PigBearGirl. Notable episodes: S10E06, SPECIAL.

Charles Entertainment Cheese, aka Chuck E. Cheese — the mouse mascot of the Chuck E. Cheese’s chain of American family restaurants. He was spotted in the season 21 installment "Hummels & Heroin". Notable episodes: S21E05.

The Central Intelligence Agency, known simply as CIA — a civilian foreign intelligence service of the United States, tasked with gathering, processing, and analyzing national security information from around the world. They debut in the season 3 installment "Starvin' Marvin in Space". Notable episodes: S03E13.

Cinderella — Disney's fictional princess from the classic fairy tale: star of the 1950 film, its sequels, the 2015 live-action remake, and the Disney Princess lineup. She appears in the season 11 Imaginationland trilogy. Notable episodes: S11E12.
Cindy McCain — the widow of John McCain who was spotted in the season 12 installment "About Last Night...". Notable episodes: S12E12.

entries.n: Citizen with Blond Hair and Blue Shirt
entries.t: The Citizen with Blond Hair and Blue Shirt — an unnamed citizen of South Park who has remained a background character since the first season and still appears frequently in the series, naturally, as a background character. He debuts in the season 1 installment "Death". Notable episodes: S02E15, S10E11, S01E06, S03E02.
k: citizen with blond hair and blue shirt

entries.n: Citizen with Brown Hair and Blue Suit
entries.t: Mr. Petuski (first name Bob or Rick) — DogPoo's father and a South Park citizen, first seen in season 1's "Mr. Hankey, the Christmas Poo": he's among the adults at the school's Non-Denominational Holiday Play, complaining that the star above the stage offends non-Christians. Later spotted in "Cherokee Hair Tampons" buying "all-natural ball juice" at Miss Information's shop, claiming his balls hurt whenever he watches VH1. Notable episodes: S04E10, S10E11, S01E09, S04E06.
k: citizen with brown hair and blue suit

entries.t: The City Ninjas — an enemy faction led by Tuong Lu Kim in South Park: The Fractured But Whole. They had earlier appeared in the installment "Fantastic Easter Special". Notable episodes: S11E05.
The City Pho Workers show up in South Park: Post Covid: The Return of Covid. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Clarence Thomas — an American jurist and associate chief justice of the Supreme Court of the United States who shows up in "Imaginationland, Episode III". Notable episodes: S11E12.
Clark — a 5th-grader at South Park Elementary. He shows up in the season 9 installment "Erection Day". Notable episodes: S09E07.
Clark Malkinson — the father of Scott Malkinson who appears on Season 23 installment "Basic Cable". Notable episodes: S20E02, S23E09.
Classi — a prostitute-for-hire. She debuted in the season 19 installment "PC Principal Final Justice" as Nathan's girlfriend. Notable episodes: S19E10.
Cleo Broflovski — Sheila Broflovski's late mother, who unusually shares her daughter's married name — implying Gerald took Sheila's surname. Notable episodes: S03E10.
Cliff Barackman — a recurring citizen of South Park first seen in "Jewpacabra" as part of the Bigfoot Researchers of community. Notable episodes: S16E04, S17E08.
Clone Stan Marsh — once Terrance Mephesto's Science Project. He was crafted by Dr. Mephesto, who also killed him after it demolished the community of South Park. Notable episodes: S01E05.
Clucky — once a rooster who plays Magic: The Gathering in the season 18 installment "Cock Magic". Notable episodes: S18E08.

Clyde Donovan (earlier Goodman and Harris) — one of the lads' classmates, born April 10 (per his Facebook profile in "You Have 0 Friends"). "Crack Baby Athletic Association" reveals his mother is Dutch, giving him some Dutch ancestry. He's in Craig's Gang. Notable episodes: S06E13, S11E03, S14E04, S01E01, S01E02, S15E05.
Clyde's Fortress Shopkeeper — a merchant in Clyde's Fortress.
Clyde's Sister — referenced in the season 16 installment "Reverse Cowgirl", but still has yet to have a speaking role. Notable episodes: S16E01.
Coach Miles — a coach who works at South Park Elementary. He debuted in the season 17 installment "Goth Kids 3: Dawn of the Posers". Notable episodes: S17E04.

The Cock Magic Promoter — a promoter for Magic: The Gathering, "Cock Magic" games, who shows up in the season 18 installment "Cock Magic". He invited the lads and McNuggets to compete in the big leagues, in the basement of Panda Express. Notable episodes: S18E08.
Cody — once an IntelliLink engineer, or "smartnician", that was spotted in the season 17 installment "Taming Strange". Notable episodes: S17E05.

Colette Francis — a student of South Park Elementary, who is spotted in numerous episodes with other handicapped children. She was first introduced in season 8 installment "Up the Down Steroid". Colette Francis shows up in South Park: The Fractured But Whole DLC, "Bring the Crunch" where she can snap a selfie with the player. Notable episodes: S08E02.

Colin Kaepernick — civil-rights activist and 49ers quarterback who knelt during the 2016 national anthem to protest racial inequality. "Member Berries" references the protest, with Herbert Garrison trying to sit out the anthem so nobody will want him as president. Notable episodes: S20E01.

Colonel Harland Sanders — once the creator and owner of the Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC) fast-food franchise. He appeared in the installment "Medicinal Fried Chicken", although his fast-food restaurants are referenced in three prior episodes. Notable episodes: S14E03.

The Colorado Avalanche — NHL pro hockey squad, seen in "Stanley's Cup". They let the Park County Pee-Wee squad take their place for the second half of their game against the Detroit Red Wings; the pee-wees are easily beaten and badly hurt, and Nelson Brown dies afterward — his last hope having been a win for his team. Notable episodes: S10E14.
Commander Miller — a military officer from the season 23 installment "Mexican Joker". Notable episodes: S23E01.

Conan O'Brien — American talk-show host, comedian, and writer: host of NBC's Late Night and TBS' Conan, plus a 1990s writer for Saturday Night Live and The Simpsons. He cameos in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. Notable episodes: MOVIE, S13E05.
Condoleezza Rice — 66th U.S. Secretary of State, the second to serve under George Bush (second term); previously his National Security Advisor in his first term. Notable episodes: S06E12.
Conner Davis — one of Ike Broflovski's pals who shows up in the season 18 installment "#HappyHolograms", where he's spotted watching videos on his iPad. Notable episodes: S18E08.
