Connor — a 4th Grade boy who shows up in the season 7 installment "South Park is Gay!". Notable episodes: S07E08.
The Construction Workers — a squad of minor characters who debuted in the season 3 installment "Rainforest Shmainforest". Notable episodes: S03E01.

Coon and Friends — the superhero team the Coon assembles to fight crime in South Park, mainly to build a franchise. The original lineup debuted across "Coon 2: Hindsight", "Mysterion Rises", and "Coon vs. Coon & Friends", later expanding in "Franchise Prequel" before splitting over competing franchise plans — the core conflict of The Fractured But Whole. The final roster (the Coon, Human Kite, Mosquito, Fastpass, Super Craig, and Captain Diabetes) merges with the Freedom Pals alongside Call Girl and Professor Chaos. Notable episodes: S13E02, S06E06, S14E11, S14E12, S14E13, S21E04.

Corey Hart — a Canadian singer and songwriter. He, famed for his hit singles, "Sunglasses at Night", "It Ain't Enough", and "Never Surrender". He shows up in the season 15 installment "Royal Pudding". Notable episodes: S15E03.
Corey Lanskin — a boy that pretends to be English, teaching Minecraft to adults for a fee in the season 17 installment "Informative Murder Porn". Notable episodes: S17E02.

Cornwallis Hankey — one of Mr. Hankey's children. He's presumed really clever, but he's conflicted with being a poo. He shows up in the season 4 installment "A Very Crappy Christmas" and South Park: The Stick of Truth. Notable episodes: S04E17.

Cosette — a poverty-stricken girl who shows up in the season 2 installment "Roger Ebert Should Lay off the Fatty Foods". She's inspired by the character of the same name from Les Misérables. Notable episodes: S02E11.
Cosette's Mother — the mother of Cosette, who shows up in the season 2 installment "Roger Ebert Should Lay off the Fatty Foods". Notable episodes: S02E11.

The Council of Nine — the ruling body over the world of Imaginationland. It was featured in the season 11 story arc "Imaginationland, Episode II and "Imaginationland, Episode III". Notable episodes: S11E11, S11E12.

Count Ravyncrowe — belongs to the South Park Vampire Society who debut in the season 12 installment "The Ungroundable". His name was revealed in the removed vampire children quest in South Park: The Stick of Truth. Notable episodes: S12E14.
The Cowboy Doctors — medical professionals who series up in the season 23 installment "Shots!!!".

Cows — Bill Denkins' herd of cattle, recurring background animals with several spotlight episodes ("Cartman Gets an Anal Probe", "Cow Days", "Prehistoric Ice Man", "Fun with Veal", "Ginger Cow", "Let Them Eat Goo"). They serve as the mascot for South Park Elementary's sports teams, a status PETA protested in "Douche and Turd". Notable episodes: S01E01, S02E13, S02E18, S06E04, S17E06, S23E04, S08E08.
Coyote Brown — a stand-up comedian who shows up in the season 11 installment "With Apologies to Jesse Jackson". Notable episodes: S11E01.
The CPS Agents — agents for the Child Protective Services. Notable episodes: S12E13.
The Crab King — the leader of the Crab People. It first showed up in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
The Crack Babies — crack-addicted babies who series up in the season 15 installment "Crack Baby Athletic Association". Notable episodes: S15E05.

Craig Tucker — a fourth-grade classmate of the boys, instantly recognizable by his blue chullo hat topped with a yellow puffball. Known for flipping people off for no apparent reason, leading his own crew ("Craig's Gang"), and speaking in an unusually deep voice for a kid. He was eight in the first three seasons, nine by "Fourth Grade", and ten by "Pandemic 2: The Startling". Notable episodes: S12E11, S01E09, S03E01, S04E11.
Creamy Goodness — a reporter for Channel 4 News, he appears in the installment "Summer Sucks". Notable episodes: S02E08.

Crimson Dawn — Stan's death-metal band from season 23's "Band in China": Stan on lead vocals, Butters on guitar and backup vocals, Kenny on bass, Jimmy on drums, with Kyle and Cartman joining later in the installment. Notable episodes: S23E02.
Crystal White — the fretful little sister of Jason White and the daughter of Bob and Mrs. White. She debuts in the season 21 finale installment "Splatty Tomato". Notable episodes: S21E10.

Cthulhu — a Great Old One (inter-dimensional god), created by H.P. Lovecraft in "The Call of Cthulhu". He debuts in "Coon 2: Hindsight", returning for "Mysterion Rises" and "Coon vs. Coon & Friends". He crosses into the human realm causing mass destruction, teams up with Cartman, and turns out to be the reason Kenny can't die. Notable episodes: S14E11, S14E12, S14E13.

Cupid Cartman, more commonly referred to as "Cupid Me" — an imaginary friend of Eric Cartman, who is the sole person who can see him. He debuts in the season 16 installment "Cartman Finds Love". Notable episodes: S26E01, S16E07.
Ralph Dale Earnhardt Jr. — an American professional racing driver who shows up in the season 14 installment "Poor and Stupid". Notable episodes: S14E08.
The Dallas Cowboys — once the NFL squad of the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. They series up in the season 18 installment "Go Fund Yourself". Notable episodes: S18E01.

Damien Thorn — the son of Satan. He says he comes from the seventh layer of hell. His only two speaking appearances to date were in the eponymous installment "Damien" and in The Stick of Truth but he makes infrequent background appearances. Notable episodes: S01E10.
Damla Jones — a girl born without a midsection who shows up in the season 6 installment "Freak Strike". Notable episodes: S06E03.
Dan — a sports commentator who shows up in the season 16 installment "Sarcastaball". Notable episodes: S16E08.
Dan Banks — once a news reporter who was spotted in the season 13 installment "Margaritaville". Notable episodes: S13E03.

Daniel Joseph Scavino Jr. — an American political advisor and former golf club manager, who at present serves as the Deputy Chief of Staff under Donald Trump. He shows up in the season 28 installment "The Woman In The Hat". Notable episodes: S28E02.

Daniel Snyder — an American businessman and the former owner of the Washington Redskins American football squad from 1999 to 2023. He shows up in the season 18 installment "Go Fund Yourself". Notable episodes: S18E01.

Dane Jeffrey Cook — American actor-comedian. As a comedian, he's renowned for his vulgar observational humor and long form storytelling, while as an actor he's renowned for his roles in films like Employee of the Month and Good Luck Chuck. He shows up in the season 15 installment "Funnybot". Notable episodes: S15E02.
Danica Sue Patrick — an American entrepreneur and retired professional racing driver who was featured in season 14 installment "Poor and Stupid". Notable episodes: S14E08.
Daniel — a character who shows up in the season 15 installment "T.M.I.". Notable episodes: S15E04.
Daniel Smith — Will Smith's younger son, appearing in the season 5 installment "Here Comes the Neighborhood". Notable episodes: S05E12.

Daniel Tanner (Andre in The Fractured But Whole) — a South Park Elementary pupil, first seen in "Breast Cancer Show Ever". Usually a background face in big crowds, parties, or hallways; in "Skank Hunt" his ex-girlfriend Annie Knitts dumps him at the episode's end. Notable episodes: S12E09, S20E02.

Danielle Staub — an American television personality most renowned for being a primary cast member of The Real Housewives of New Jersey, who shows up in "It's a Jersey Thing". Notable episodes: S14E09.
Danny Ganz — an ATF Commander who debut in the season 3 installment "Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub". Notable episodes: S03E08.
Danny Ray Johnson — a male 4th grader who shows up in the season 23 installment "Shots".

Darryl Weathers — a construction worker debuting in season 8's "Goobacks" as a laborer furious at losing his job to immigrants from the future. Since then a frequent background/minor face, often leading redneck and working-class crowds in the "They took our jobs!" chant. Notable episodes: S08E07.
Darwin — a minor character who shows up in South Park: Post Covid and South Park: Post Covid: The Return of Covid. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Dave — a character who was spotted in the season 23 installment "Mexican Joker". Notable episodes: S23E01.
Dave Beckett — an elderly man who resides in Boca Raton, Florida. He shows up in the season 20 installment "The End of Serialization as We Know It". Notable episodes: S20E10.
Dave Fitzsimmons — a minor character who debut in the season 21 installment "White People Renovating Houses". Notable episodes: S21E01, S23E02.
Dave Harrison — the son of Mr. and Mrs. Harrison and the sibling of Mark, Jenny, Gary, and Amanda Harrison. He shows up in the season 7 installment "All About Mormons". Notable episodes: S07E12.
Davey Solokov — a Russian dressage rider who shows up in the season 25 installment "Back To The Cold War". Notable episodes: S25E04.
David Blaine — an American illusionist, debuting in the season 5 installment "Super Best Friends", where he's the primary antagonist. Notable episodes: S05E03, S24E02.
John Arthur Carradine — once an American actor who was spotted in the season 13 installment "Dead Celebrities". Notable episodes: S13E08.

David Duchovny — American actor famed as Fox Mulder on The X-Files. On the show he's a sex addict at the Karne Institute in "Sexual Healing", told his addiction stems from a "Wizard Alien"; he also appears among the celebrities in "200" and "201". He was name-dropped earlier in "Chickenpox", where Dr. Doctor warns Stan's parents that untreated pox could make Stan think he's Duchovny. Notable episodes: S14E01, S14E05, S14E06, S02E10.

David Hasselhoff — an American actor who is well-liked for his role as Michael Knight in the 1980s TV series Knight Rider, as well as his role in the series Baywatch. He debuted in the season 1 installment "Tom's Rhinoplasty". Notable episodes: S01E11.
David Hemmings — English actor, director, and producer, seen in the short "The Gauntlet" playing his Gladiator character — a fictionalized take on Roman senator Cassius.

David Letterman — American TV host: Late Night with David Letterman (1982–1992), leaving NBC after Jay Leno was picked as Johnny Carson's Tonight Show successor; he launched CBS's Late Show the next year, hosting with Paul Shaffer from August 30, 1993 to May 20, 2015. Notable episodes: S13E05.
David Palmer, aka "Ol' Smithy" — once an employee at Pioneer Village, playing the blacksmith. He was spotted in the season 12 installment "Super Fun Time". Notable episodes: S12E07.
David Perry — a sports commentator who shows up in the season 23 installment "Board Girls". Notable episodes: S23E07.
David Quincy — a professional thief who shows up in the season 12 installment "About Last Night...". Notable episodes: S12E12.
David Rodriguez — a male fourth grader at South Park Elementary. His first appearance in the installment "The Last of the Meheecans",. Notable episodes: S15E09, S19E04.
David Satcher — an American physician and served as a Surgeon General of the United States. He shows up in the season 6 installment "Red Hot Catholic Love". Notable episodes: S06E08.
David "Running Horse" Sawitzky — once seen in the season 15 installment "A History Channel Thanksgiving". Notable episodes: S15E13.

David Wayne Spade — American actor-comedian. He, famed for his tenure on NBC's Saturday Night Live in the 1990s and starring in film and television shows like Just Shoot Me, Tommy Boy, and Joe Dirt. He shows up in the season 15 installment "Funnybot". Notable episodes: S15E02.

David Weatherhead — one of the numerous foster children under the care of the Weatherheads. He attends Greeley Elementary and shows up in the season 15 installment "The Poor Kid". Notable episodes: S15E14.
Davin Miller — a fourth-grader at South Park Elementary who shows up in the season 17 installment "Ginger Cow". Notable episodes: S17E06.

entries.n: Dawson's Creek Trapper Keeper Ultra Keeper Futura S 2000
entries.t: The Dawson's Creek Trapper Keeper Ultra Keeper Futura S 2000, typically referred to as "Trapper Keeper", is the primary antagonist in the eponymous Season 4 installment "Trapper Keeper". Notable episodes: S04E12.

entries.t: The DEA Agents — agents for the Drug Enforcement Administration. They series up in the season 12 installment "Major Boobage". Notable episodes: S12E03.

Dean — once the host of J&G Shopping Network who was spotted in the season 16 installment "Cash For Gold". In the installment, he sold overpriced jewelry on his television series. Notable episodes: S16E02, S23E09.
Dean Howland — the dean of the University of Colorado Boulder who shows up in the season 15 installment "Crack Baby Athletic Association". Notable episodes: S15E05.
Dean Martin — once an American singer, actor, and comedian who was spotted in the season 4 installment "Do the Handicapped Go to Hell?" as a Hell resident. Notable episodes: S04E09.
Death — the personification of death itself, debuting in the season 1 installment "Death". Notable episodes: S01E06, S24E02.
Deborah Carroll (also known as Nanny Deb) — a professional nanny seen in the season 10 installment "Tsst". Notable episodes: S10E07.
Demetria Devonne Lovato, aka Demi Lovato — an American singer-songwriter and part-time actor. She shows up in the season 19 installment "Safe Space". Notable episodes: S19E05.
Demonius — a demon from Hell who shows up in the season 10 installment "Hell on Earth 2006". Notable episodes: S10E11.
The Demons — creatures that inhabit Hell that appear numerous times in the series, the first being "Damien". Notable episodes: S03E15, S01E10.

Dennis — a mechanic, first seen in season 13's "W.T.F."; his biggest outing is "You're Not Yelping", where the local mascot throws him and his family out of Whistlin' Willy's. He later appears in The Fractured But Whole, where he and three other rednecks meet the New Kid on the street and pick a fight. Notable episodes: S13E10, S19E04.
Dennis — a resident of Evergreen who was spotted in the season 11 installment "Night of the Living Homeless". Notable episodes: S11E07.

Dennis Murray — a South Park Elementary pupil, spotted across multiple episodes with other handicapped kids. Debuted in season 8's "Up the Down Steroid"; his biggest appearance is in The Fractured But Whole's Bring the Crunch DLC, where the New Kid can take a selfie with him. Notable episodes: S08E02.
Dental Floss — an alter-ego of an unnamed kindergartener. He shows up in the season 15 installment "Royal Pudding". Notable episodes: S15E03.
The Denver Archbishop — a minor character who shows up in the season 22 installment "A Boy And A Priest". Notable episodes: S22E02.

The Denver Broncos — the NFL squad of Denver. They're the overall favored squad of the whole community of South Park and are as such, referenced numerous times. John Elway, ex-star quarterback, is a hero to most of the South Park characters. Notable episodes: S01E13.
The Denver Broncos Cheerleaders — a crew of cheerleaders for the Denver Broncos NFL squad. They series up in the season 16 installment "Sarcastaball". Notable episodes: S16E08.

The Denver Cougars — a squad of dodgeball players from Denver Elementary that series up in the season 2 installment "Conjoined Fetus Lady". Bob Thomas serves as the coach for the dodgeball squad. Notable episodes: S02E05.
The Denver Nuggets — a professional basketball squad, with Pepsi Center in Denver as their home base. Notable episodes: S16E07.
The Denver Sea Park Boss shows up in the season 9 installment "Free Willzyx". Notable episodes: S09E13.
The Denver Sea Park Employees — minor characters that was spotted in the season 9 installment "Free Willzyx". They're called Brian and Mike. Notable episodes: S09E13.

Derek Smalls (formerly Kevin McCarthy) — a reporter that appears in some episodes of the first seasons. He debuts in the season 2 installment "Summer Sucks". Derek didn't appear with the other reporters in "Sponsored Content". Notable episodes: S02E08, S19E08.

Detective Jarvis — seen in season 10's "The Return of Chef". He visits South Park Elementary to question kids about Chef's recent pedophilic behavior — later revealed as Super Adventure Club brainwashing — claiming to gather testimony, but only demonstrating how a pedophile would act toward them. Notable episodes: S10E01.
Detectives Hyde and Richardson — police officers from the Special Gang unit based in Denver. They series up in the season 7 installment "Krazy Kripples". Notable episodes: S07E02.

The Detroit Red Wings — NHL pro hockey squad, seen in season 10's "Stanley's Cup". The Avalanche players let the Park County pee-wees take their place against the Red Wings after the opposing pee-wee squad no-showed; the Red Wings showed no mercy, winning by a landslide and badly injuring the pee-wee players. Notable episodes: S10E14.

Diana, Princess of Wales — once an immensely well-liked member of the British Royal Family, married to Charles III and mother of Princes William and Harry. She debuted in the season 3 installment "Mr. Hankey's Christmas Classics". Notable episodes: S03E15.

Diane Choksondik — a fourth-grade teacher, introduced in season 4's "Fourth Grade" (her name riffs on "chokes on dick"). She taught the fourth grade at South Park Elementary until dying in "The Simpsons Already Did It" — her death spoiled the episode before. Notable episodes: S06E07, S04E11, S06E06.

Richard "Dick" Bruce Cheney — once the 46th U.S. vice president, serving under George Bush from 2001 to 2009. He handed the vice presidency to Joe Biden. Cheney had also served as White House chief of staff under Gerald Ford and defense secretary under the elder Bush. Cheney is also remembered for accidentally shooting Harry Whittington, a Texas attorney friend, while out hunting. The incident became a media punchline and a staple of criticism of Cheney. Notable episodes: S06E12.
Dick Dastardly and Muttley — a villainous duo who series up in the season 18 installment "Handicar", where they drive their Mean Machine in the TV series Wacky Races. Notable episodes: S18E04.
Diego — a Mexican day laborer. He debuted in the season 11 installment "D-Yikes!". Notable episodes: S11E06.
Diego Márquez — a character in the kids' animated TV series Dora the Explorer, who shows up in the season 19 installment "Hummels & Heroin". Notable episodes: S27E02, S21E05.
Dig 'Em Frog — the mascot of Honey Smacks, appearing in South Park: The End of Obesity. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Dildo Shwaggins, who also refers to himself as Dick Slapperman — an internet troll, debuting in the season 20 installment "Wieners Out". Notable episodes: S20E04, S24E02.
Dileep Rao — an American actor who shows up in the season 14 installment "Insheeption", portraying his character from Inception, Yusuf. Notable episodes: S14E10.

Dio — the metal band, seen in season 3's "Hooked on Monkey Fonics" playing their hit "Holy Diver" at South Park Elementary's Bay of Pigs Memorial Dance, with the Fonics Monkey joining on drums. Notable episodes: S03E12.
A dire wolf — a wolf found only in Canada, along with Dire Bears and Dire Snakes.

The Distracted Driving Awareness Group — a group that appears in the installment "Put It Down", promoting distracted driving awareness. They're one-sided rivals of Cartman who tried to get more attention than them by promoting awareness of his own "suicidal" behavior. Notable episodes: S21E02.

Adam Michael Goldstein, better known by his stage name DJ AM — once an American disc jockey who was spotted in the season 13 installment "Dead Celebrities". He was most renowned for being in the band Crazy Town as well as his collaboration with Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker. Notable episodes: S13E08.
DJ Hippo — the DJ who works at The Peppermint Hippo. Notable episodes: S07E06, S24E02.
The Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Workers series up in the season 17 installment "Let Go, Let Gov". Notable episodes: S17E01.
Doctor Lindsay — a spiritual medium who shows up in the season 9 installment "The Death of Eric Cartman". Notable episodes: S09E06.
Doctor Lout — a South Park eye doctor who loves fat jokes at Eric Cartman's expense, calling him "his little piggy". Seen once, in season 3's "The Succubus". Notable episodes: S03E03.
Doctor Timothy — the superhero alter-ego of Timmy Burch. He debuted in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Doctor Tom — a rhinologist and surgeon who owns the commonly-seen business, Tom's Rhinoplasty. He was first seen in the season 1 installment "Tom's Rhinoplasty". Notable episodes: S01E11, S20E08.

Doctor Vosknocker — seen in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. He introduces the V-Chip and implants it in Cartman's head to stop his swearing. His name is a deliberate double entendre on "Balls Knocker". Notable episodes: MOVIE.
DogPoo Petuski — attends South Park Elementary, and is constantly seen covered in dirt. Notable episodes: S06E06, S01E01.
The DOI Agents — representatives of the United States Department of Interior who series up in the season 3 installment "Jakovasaurs". Notable episodes: S03E04.
Dominick DeLuise — once an American actor and director who was spotted in the season 13 installment "Dead Celebrities". Notable episodes: S13E08.

Domino — a member of the Burger King Bandits, seen only in "Super Fun Time". During the gang's shootout with police he hides in the Pioneer Village saloon, firing on officers and hostages alike — until he pokes his head out a window and the police shoot him dead. Notable episodes: S12E07.
Don Heisman — a talent agent from the Creative Arts Agency (CAA) based in Los Angeles. He debuts in the season 9 installment "Wing". Notable episodes: S09E03, S13E09.
Donald King — a professional boxing promoter who appears promoting Satan in his fight against Jesus in the season 1 installment "Damien". Notable episodes: S01E10, S12E08.

Donald Henry Rumsfeld — once the United States Secretary Of Defense from 1975 to 1977 and again from 2001 to 2006, under Presidents Ford and Bush respectively. He shows up in "A Ladder to Heaven" and later in "Mystery of the Urinal Deuce", as a member of George Bush's inner circle. Notable episodes: S06E12, S10E09.

Donald Trump — businessman, TV personality, and politician, first seen in "The Entity". During his first presidency the show parodied him through President Garrison rather than depicting him directly; after losing the 2020 election (mirrored by Garrison's return in "South ParQ Vaccination Special"), he was re-elected in 2024 and appeared as himself in "Sermon on the 'Mount" — rendered Canadian-looking from real photos, in the style of Saddam Hussein's portrayal. Notable episodes: S28E01, S05E11, S27E01, S24E02.
Donald John Trump Jr. — an American businessman and activist, the eldest child of Donald Trump. He debuts in the season 27 installment "Conflict of Interest". Notable episodes: S27E05.
Donda West — Kanye West's deceased mother. She showed up in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Donna Reed — once an American actress, notable for portraying Mary Hatch Bailey in It's a Wonderful Life, which can be spotted in "Merry Christmas Charlie Manson!". Notable episodes: S02E16.
Dora Márquez — the primary protagonist of the kids' animated TV series Dora the Explorer, who shows up in "Taming Strange". Notable episodes: S17E05.
Ms. Dotty Applegate debuts in the season 18 installment "Handicar", where she's the passenger that the Wacky Racers need to pick up and deliver to her destination. Notable episodes: S18E04.

Dougie O'Connell — a second-grader at South Park Elementary, debuting in season 3's "Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub" playing with Butters, Pip, and briefly Stan. He started in first grade and moved up to second in season 4's "Fourth Grade"; he often appears as Professor Chaos's sidekick General Disarray. Notable episodes: S03E08, S06E06, S21E05, S04E11.
Douglas — a 4th-grader at South Park Elementary and debuts in the season 12 installment "Breast Cancer Show Ever". Notable episodes: S12E09, S13E13.

Dr. Alphonse Mephesto — a supporting character in the early Seasons introduced in "An Elephant Makes Love to a Pig". He's an eccentric geneticist and stereotypical mad scientist who resides and works at South Park Genetic Engineering Ranch. Notable episodes: S03E02, S01E05, SPECIAL.

Dr. Arnie Apesacrappin — a scientist who never appears on screen; he's known only from the Chef Aid album song "Mephesto and Kevin". Per the song, he genetically engineered Kevin Mephesto using Michael Jackson's DNA, aiming to build the greatest musical entertainer the world had ever seen. After exposure, Kevin was taken into state custody and adopted by Dr. Alphonse Mephesto; no charges were filed since no laws covered it, but the medical board stripped Apesacrappin of his credentials, and his name became slang for failure.
Dr. Biber — a plastic surgeon who shows up in the season 9 premiere installment "Mr. Garrison's Fancy New Vagina". Notable episodes: S09E01.
Dr. Carroll — a physician at Hells Pass Hospital and a pediatrics specialist who also makes private house calls. First seen in "Tonsil Trouble". Notable episodes: S12E01.

Dr. Chinstrap — once a psychiatrist who specialized in the mental illness of hoarding. Wendy asked for his help to make Stan confront his own hoarding. During his investigation, Chinstrap also found Mr. Mackey to be a hoarder, and tried hypnotizing the two (plus a luckless shepherd) back into their childhoods to uncover the roots of their hoarding. When Mackey's memories proved vivid enough to pull Stan and the shepherd into his reality, Chinstrap called on the world's greatest dream infiltrator, Freddy Krueger, to help them out. Notable episodes: S14E10.
Dr. Cornwallis — a goat character who shows up in the season 8 installment "Douche and Turd". Notable episodes: S08E08.

Dr. David Nelson — a man with dwarfism who comes to the South Park Elementary to give a talk about his experience in the season 11 installment "With Apologies to Jesse Jackson". Notable episodes: S11E01.

Dr. Doctor (Dr. Horatio Gauche in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut and Dr. Kels in "Cartman's Incredible Gift") — a doctor in South Park renowned for his unusual diagnoses. He practiced at Hells Pass Hospital, although as of "Medicinal Fried Chicken", he appears to own his own practice. Notable episodes: S02E02, S24E02, MOVIE, S08E13, S14E03.

Dr. Gary Gauche — physician at Hell's Pass Hospital; a poster by his office notes he also works for the Saint Penmar Department of Medicine (seen in "Shots!!!"). Since season 21 he's effectively replaced Dr. Doctor as the show's main doctor, treating Cartman, Stan, Sheila Broflovski, and PC Principal as their personal physician. Notable episodes: S21E09, SPECIAL.
Dr. Hallis — a plastic surgeon who works in Hell's Pass Hospital who shows up in the season 6 installment "Bebe's Boobs Destroy Society". Notable episodes: S06E10.

Dr. Jonathan Katz — the therapist from Comedy Central's Dr. Katz, Professional Therapist, cameoing in "Summer Sucks" to give Mr. Garrison psychotherapy in New York. Katz suggests Mr. Hat embodies Garrison's homosexuality, enraging him — moments before a giant charcoal snake levels part of the city and crushes Katz in his office; Garrison, emerging unharmed, figures he had it coming. Notable episodes: S02E08.
Dr. Kronberg — a child psychologist who shows up in South Park: Joining the Panderverse. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Dr. Land — A mental-health physician and Ike Broflovski's counselor. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Dr. Larry — A physician who is employed at the Alder Research Group. Notable episodes: S05E13.
Dr. Matlock — A physician who is employed at Hells Pass Hospital and doubles as a specialist. Notable episodes: S12E01.

Dr. Mehmet Oz — Dr. Mehmet Cengiz Oz, also called Dr. Oz is an American heart surgeon, writer, ex-talk-show emcee and the 17th head of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services during Donald Trump's second administration. From 2009 to 2022, most renowned for emceeing the daytime talk show, The Dr. Oz Show. Seen interviewing Stan Marsh and Butters Stotch about. After angering Butters by forcing him to speak out against bullying, he's attacked and beaten up by Butters on his TV show. Notable episodes: S16E05.
Dr. Neeland — A mental-health physician. Notable episodes: S10E01.
Dr. Pal — A physician that showed up to help discuss his erections with Jimmy. Notable episodes: S09E07.

Dr. Phil — An American TV personality who hosted his self-titled talk show. He assisted Eric Cartman by discussing his problem with Eric and rewarding him. Managed to give Eric the inaugural HUMANCENTiPAD. Notable episodes: S15E01.
Dr. Phillips — A kids' physician. Based on Zelda Rubinstein's figure Tangina Barrons from the Poltergeist film series. Her name tag reads 'Dr. Tangina'. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Dr. Pinkerton — Dr's assistant. Chinstrap. Often charged with explaining complex ideas and concepts to people while Chinstrap provided. Notable episodes: S14E10.
Dr. Poonlover — An abortion physician who initially showed up in the video game South Park: The Stick of Truth.
Dr. Roberts — Eric Cartman's dentist. Notable episodes: S04E01.
Dr. Sandra Lee — An American skin physician and YouTuber. Notable episodes: S29E02.
Dr. Schwartz — A good-natured Jewish rabbi who debuts who conducted Ike's bris. Notable episodes: S02E03.
Dr. Shay — A figure. Notable episodes: S04E03.
Dr. Sheltair — A proctologist. Notable episodes: S26E03.
Dr. Spookalot — The guide for Spooky Laboratory. Notable episodes: S03E10.
Dr. Stevens — A cosmetic surgeon who shows up in South Park: The Streaming Wars. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Dr. Tristan Adams — The proprietor of the Tantalus V. Observatory. He shows up as the central villain. Notable episodes: S02E11.
Dr. Wayne Schroeder — A psychologist shows up, spotted delivering a discuss internet trolls and Skankhunt42 with parents. Notable episodes: S20E02.
Dr. Zonder — A physician at the Colorado Neurology Center. Notable episodes: S11E08.
Dramatic Look Gopher — Dramatic Look Gopher showed up among the internet celebrities awaiting their theoretical payments. Notable episodes: S12E04.

Drew Carey — An American performer, comic, and game-show emcee. Most renowned for headlining the ABC comedy series, The Drew Carey Show and emceeing Whose Line Is It Anyway? and The Price is Right. Notable episodes: S05E01.

Droopy Dog — An imaginary cartoon figure who cameoed as a disabled camper at Lake Tardicaca. Droopy Dog himself as an actual figure initially shows up on the show in season 28's. Notable episodes: S14E07, S28E03.

Duck President — Thought to be an imaginary creature. However Duck President is revealed to be real. Duck President also briefly showed up, where he was recognized as Barack Obama's opponent in the 2012 presidential election. Seen in at the end celebrating the close of the pandemic. Notable episodes: S15E07, S15E08, S16E14, S24E02.
Duke of Vancouver — A figure from South Park: The Stick of Truth.

Dumb Donald — In a spoof of the program called The Fat Abbott Show, an imaginary figure from the Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids cartoon created by Bill Cosby, who shows up as a figure. Notable episodes: S02E12.
Duncan Everton — A history professor. Notable episodes: S15E13.
Dwight Schultz — An American performer. Notable episodes: S02E03.
Dylan and Sarah — A married pair. Notable episodes: S10E03.
E.T. — The titular central protagonist of the American 1982 sci-fi film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, who also briefly turns up multiple other times in the series. Notable episodes: S06E09.
Earl of Halifax — A figure featured. Notable episodes: S26E02.
Earl of Winnipeg — A figure from South Park: The Stick of Truth.

Ed McMahon — An American announcer, game-show emcee, comic, performer, vocalist, and combat aviator. Most renowned for serving as the announcer and co-host for The Tonight Show with Johnny Carson plus emceeing the talent contest show, Star Search. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Ed Sullivan — A TV personality. Notable episodes: S05E05.
Edgar Allan Poe — An American writer and poet who showed up as a ghost when he was pictured on Stan Marsh's shirt, as he'd briefly gone goth. Notable episodes: S17E04, S07E14.
Edge — Adam Joseph Copeland, better known as Edge is a Canadian WWE pro wrestler and Hall of Famer. Notable episodes: S13E10.
Eduardo Hernandez — A grocery shop attendant, originally from Guatemala. Notable episodes: S20E08.
El Pollo Loco Workers — The El Pollo Loco workers. Notable episodes: S15E09.
Elaine — An airport attendant for Denver International Airport. Notable episodes: S05E11.
Elin Nordegren — Tiger Woods's ex-wife. Notable episodes: S14E01.
Eliot Spitzer — An American elected official and was New York's 54th governor who made his only appearance. Notable episodes: S14E01.
Elise Garrett — A South Park citizen. She looks a lot like Mrs. Anderson. Notable episodes: S03E10, S05E06, S08E03.

Ellen DeGeneres — An American performer, comic, and TV talk-show emcee. She welcomed Eric Cartman and Jimmy Valmer to her talk show, The Ellen DeGeneres Show. She also shows up among the comedians. Notable episodes: S13E05, S15E02.
Ellen Malkinson — Scott Malkinson's mother. Notable episodes: S23E09, SPECIAL.
Elmer Fudd — An imaginary cartoon figure who cameoed as a disabled camper at Lake Tardicaca. Notable episodes: S14E07.

Elon Musk — The creator and chief executive of Tesla Motors and SpaceX. He takes part in Wacky Races, driving his Tesla D car. He also shows up, and in which he makes a guest appearance. Notable episodes: S18E04, S20E08, S20E10, S20E09.
Elsa — A Disney figure who headlines the animated musical film Frozen, alongside its sequel Frozen II. She. Notable episodes: S23E02.

Elton John — An English vocalist, songwriter and pianist. Collaborating with songwriter Bernie Taupin since 1967 on over 30 albums, Elton has moved over 300 million records,, which has made him among the best-selling music artists of all time. He has shown up in South Park in multiple cameo roles. Notable episodes: S02E14, S01E05.

Elvin Cartman — One of Cartman's kin. The younger cousin of Eric Cartman and Liane's nephew, plus Uncle Stinky and Lisa Cartman's son, and Alexandra Cartman's brother. He goes by 'Cousin Elvin'. Notable episodes: S02E16, S19E06.

Elvis Presley — Elvis 'The King' Presley was an American vocalist, performer, and pop-culture icon who showed up as a ghost though he's been referenced multiple times throughout the series. He later showed up as a hologram. Notable episodes: S16E11.
Elvis Presley Hologram — Featured. Modeled after deceased vocalist-performer Elvis Presley.
Emily Marx — A pupil at South Park Elementary who initially shows up. Notable episodes: S09E09, S15E10.
Emir Hadi — An American of Persian heritage who works as Xerxes' messenger. Notable episodes: S11E06.
Emmanuel Lewis — An American ex-performer who was most renowned for playing the titular role in the TV comedy series Webster as a youngster. Notable episodes: S13E12.

Emmett Hollis — A competitor in the Pinewood Derby competition in the self-titled season 13 episode. He has the best car, but loses because Randy ends up cheating. In front of him, his father, unable to bear the loss, commits suicide. Notable episodes: S13E06.
Emo Kids — A group. The group was briefly referenced earlier. Notable episodes: S17E04, S12E09.

Emperor Akihito — The former Emperor of Japan. In real life, he took the throne in 1989, upon his father's death, Emperor Hirohito. He relinquished the throne on 30 April 2019, because of his age and declining health with his son Naruhito succeeding him. Notable episodes: S13E11.
Emperor Hirohito — A South Park character. Notable episodes: S03E11.

Enchorito Mark — One living in South Park, who usually shows up as a background extra. At present, Mark's best-known appearances came in the game South Park: The Stick of Truth. Notable episodes: S06E14, S10E02, S19E04.
Enrique — The mascot of the Middle Park Elementary that only. Notable episodes: S01E04.
Enrique Iglesias — A Spanish vocalist. Notable episodes: S05E11.

Eric Cartman — One of the central characters, alongside Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, and Kenny McCormick. Cartman is sometimes the central villain of an episode, for example. None of the other three central kids really count Cartman as a friend and don't know why they started spending time with him in the inaugural place, but a kind of unstable friendship develops between them. However he's usually Kyle's first choice when he breaks his friendship with Stan. In earlier episodes, Kenny was his closest pal, however, in later seasons, Butters Stotch is usually depicted as such. Cartman was the inaugural one of the boys to be shown without his hat, as seen. He also weighs 90 pounds, as revealed. Notable episodes: S13E02, S10E12, S02E13, S13E10, S10E10, S01E01, S04E12, S02E16.

Eric Cartman — A variant of Eric Cartman from Universe 216-B. She shows up in South Park: Joining the Panderverse, having swapped places with Eric, and attempts to persuade his friends to return her to her universe. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Eric Roberts — An American performer who shows up as a performer in an America's Most Wanted re-creation, portraying Kevin Mephesto. Notable episodes: S02E02, S14E05.

Escaped Convict — A convict. A spoof of the figure Abel Magwitch from the Charles Dickens novel Great Expectations. Fresh out of prison, he threatens Pip in a graveyard, but Pip gives him a sandwich and cuts off his handcuffs. Touched by Pip's display of unconditional kindness, he moves to Wales and becomes a millionaire. Afterwards, he repays Pip's favor by sending him to become a gentleman in London. He later attempts to help Pip stop Miss Havisham, but is killed when she spits acid on his face. Notable episodes: S04E14.

Estella Havisham — A figure. A literary parallel from Charles Dickens's classic tale, Great Expectations. Estella is Miss Havisham's daughter, she was brought up to break men's hearts for her. Notable episodes: S04E14.
Estella's Boyfriends — Characters. Category:Characters Category:Male Characters. Notable episodes: S04E14.
Esther — A female fourth-grade pupil at South Park Elementary. One of the well-liked girls at South Park Elementary. Notable episodes: S03E01, S06E10.
Eugene — A figure. Notable episodes: S13E14.

Eugene Levy — A Canadian performer and comic. Most renowned for serving as an ensemble member on SCTV in the 1970s and 1980s plus for parts like Noah Levenstein (a.k.a. Jim's dad) in the American Pie film series and Johnny Rose in Schitt$ Creek. Notable episodes: S15E02.
Eugene's Wife — Eugene's wife, she. Notable episodes: S13E14.

entries.t: European Fecal Standards and Measurements Board — An organization. Notable episodes: S11E09.
k: european fecal standards and measurements board

entries.t: Excalibur Barker — An unidentified worker of the Excalibur Casino. Notable episodes: S05E01.
Excalibur Sorcerer — An elderly sorcerer who is employed at the Inner Sanctum of the Excalibur Casino. Notable episodes: S05E01.
Fabio Lanzoni — An Italian-American performer and fashion model who shows up as a background extra. Notable episodes: S02E09.

Faith + 1 — Faith + 1 played Christian rock put together by Eric Cartman, after being expelled from the boys' group, Moop. Cartman formed the band to win a bet he had made with Kyle Broflovski over who could get an album to go platinum first. Notable episodes: S07E09.
Faith Records CEO — Faith Records chief executive. Notable episodes: S07E09.

Farmer Fred — An old man who sometimes counsels South Park locals on their problems, though seldom involved in them himself. Based on the figure Jud Crandall from the 1989 horror film Pet Sematary, based on Stephen King's novel of the same name. Notable episodes: S05E14, S24E02.
Farrah Fawcett — An American performer. Renowned for her looks and was broadly seen as America's foremost sex symbol through much of the 1970s. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Farty O'Cool — The proprietor of the namesake Irish pub. Notable episodes: S25E06.
Fast Food Executives — A crew of executives repping various fast-food chains. Notable episodes: S15E08.
Fastpass — The superhero alias of Jimmy Valmer. He debuted. Notable episodes: S21E04.

Fat Abbott — The central figure of the TV show, The Fat Abbott Show, who was. A spoof of Fat Albert, the central figure from Bill Cosby's cartoon Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids. Notable episodes: S02E12.
Fat Bob — Bob Cartman, referred to as Fat Bob belongs to the Cartman family who initially showed up. Notable episodes: S02E16, S05E06.
Father and Handicapped Daughter — The father and Disabled Daughter. Notable episodes: S20E06.
Father Maxi — Father Maxi (Also frequently referred to as Priest Maxi) is a Roman Catholic priest who acts as the mouthpiece for South Park's Christian community. Notable episodes: S01E09.

FBI Kids — A rival group of kids to the boys playing FBI. They dress identically in all black while playing with more expensive toys versus the boys, which were presumably bought by their wealthier parents. In the episode, they attempt to take over Sarah Peterson's doll case, on which the South Park Junior Detectives had been working, by pulling over them. However, the South Park Junior Detectives are the ones who end up solving the case, getting the boys promoted to the South Park Crime Unit. Notable episodes: S07E06.

Federal Bureau of Investigation — Federal Bureau of Investigation, also called the F.B.I. is an United States law enforcement agency. The F.B.I. deals with incidents on a national level, unlike local police agencies, who only handle incidents on a city and county level. The F.B.I. has been appearing in many episodes, first appearing. Notable episodes: S01E08.

Federation Kids — A crew of Star Trek enthusiasts who initially show up as a group. The group is made up of Kevin Stoley, Dougie O'Connell, an unidentified Asian kid, and another unidentified member, alongside multiple other unidentified kids. They only show up as a group throughout the Black Friday Trilogy. Notable episodes: S17E07.

Feldspar the Thief — An honorable thief hailing from Zaron and the fantasy alias of Craig Tucker. Felipe Calderón — Acted as Mexico's 56th president. Notable episodes: S13E06, S15E09.
Female QAnon Tutor — A part of QAnon and its private tutoring branch Tutornon. Notable episodes: S24E02.
Fenton Hardly — A detective. Notable episodes: S10E09.

Ferrari — A worker at Raisins. She debuted as the most recent worker. As with all the other Raisins workers, she takes its name from a luxury sports car manufacturer. Notable episodes: S07E14, S16E05.

Fidel Castro — The former First Secretary of the Republic of Cuba. During the night of November 25, 2016, Castro died of natural causes. In the United States, Cuban Exiles joyfully celebrated his death. Notable episodes: S04E16.
Fifi — A female gray poodle. Notable episodes: S01E04.
Filmore Anderson — A minor returning figure. A pupil in kindergarten at South Park Elementary and the supposed rival of Ike Broflovski. Notable episodes: S04E12.

Firkle Smith — Georgie 'Firkle' Smith goes to kindergarten. The youngest part of the Goth Kids. Notable episodes: S07E14.
Fleetwood Mac — A British-American rock group. Renowned for popular songs. Notable episodes: S05E09.
Flo Kimble — Flo Kimble, also called Aunt Flo. Her real name is Florence Kimble, who also served as the aunt of Sharon and Jimbo. Notable episodes: S02E15.

Flora Larsen — A kindergartner girl. She debuted. In the kindergarten class elections she couldn't decide who to vote for class president, but ultimately chose Ike Broflovski against Filmore Anderson. Notable episodes: S04E12.

Florence Cartman — Eric Cartman's great-grandma; she's also Mabel Cartman's mother and maternal grandmother of Liane and Howard Cartman. Not seen at her daughter's funeral. Notable episodes: S02E16, S05E06.
Fluffy — Cartman's pet pig. Notable episodes: S01E05, S04E06.
Fluffy — A rooster who plays Magic: The Gathering. Notable episodes: S18E08.

Fosse McDonald — A male pupil at South Park Elementary who was frequently seen in the inaugural seasons with Bill Allen. In a deep voice, similar to Beavis and Butthead, Fosse often calls things followed by laughing. Notable episodes: S01E04.
Four-Assed Monkey — A genetically engineered monkey and one of Dr. Alphonse Mephesto's most prized creations. Notable episodes: S01E05.
Fox and Friends Hosts — A trio of newscasters who host the morning news program Fox and Friends on Fox News. Notable episodes: S27E04.
Frances Velman — The front-desk attendant for the sperm bank. Notable episodes: S06E07.

Francis — A male 4th-grader at South Park Elementary. Formerly voiced by Matt Stone, and then by Trey Parker. Francis — A female 4th-grader with disabilities who initially showed up. Notable episodes: S08E02, S21E08.

Francis Ford Coppola — An American filmmaker. Coppola is among the directors who is asked to attend the premiere of the remastered Raiders of the Lost Ark by George Lucas and Steven Spielberg. In the same manner as Colonel Herman Dietrich in Raiders of the Lost Ark, however, the truly terrible opening scenes of the film cause his head to shrivel up and implode. He also shows up in the episodes among the many celebrities suing South Park. Notable episodes: S06E09, S14E06, S14E05.

The crew is officially lead by Physician Timothy, with founding members Mysterion, Toolshed, Tupperware, and Wonder Tweek, who all left the ex-superhero team Coon and Friends because of disagreements regarding the original franchise plan. Freja Ollegard — A female Olympic 4-time gold medalist in volleyball and ran a Danish website for breast cancer. A breast cancer survivor, too. She initially showed up, spotted on the news discussing Skankhunt42. Notable episodes: S20E03, S20E02.
Frida — An old prostitute with herpes. Notable episodes: S02E10.
Frog King — Frog King (sometimes mistakenly Frog Prince) is a creature ghost. Notable episodes: S06E14, S15E10.

Frosty — A figure that showed up in Trey Parker and Matt Stone's pupil short film Jesus vs. Frosty. The boys' prototype accidentally animated a snowman with a magic hat, parodying the Rankin/Bass special Frosty the Snowman. Instead of being kind, the snowman is evil and murders Cartman, the only figure with a name. The film features four kids who are very similar of the four central characters of South Park, including a figure resembling Cartman, but called and three nameless boys resembling Kyle, Stan, and Kenny.

Funnybot — A robotic comic created and manufactured in Germany for entertaining people and proving Germans aren't the least funny people in the world. In which he acted as the central villain, funnybot shows up in the episode of the same name. After exhausting standard comedy routines, Funnybot decided to start slaughtering audiences to create situations. He eventually concluded that the would be the destruction of all biological life on Earth, which would be incredibly awkward. However, this plan was stopped by Jimmy and the boys. Funnybot later had a change of heart, understanding that comedy is about over simple logic. Notable episodes: S15E02.

Future Butters — A performer enlisted by Motivation Corp. Meant to play as a future Butters Stotch, whose life deteriorated after doing drugs and alcohol. However, Butters found out that he was being deceived, with the help of Stan Marsh. Notable episodes: S06E16.
Future Humans — Future Humans show up as Americans from the year 3045 who travel to present-day South Park seeking work. Notable episodes: S08E07.
Future Kyle's Kids — Adult Kyle Broflovski's kids who show up in South Park: Post Covid: The Return of Covid. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Future Shooter — A shooter who shows up in the South Park movie called South Park: Post Covid. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.

Future Stan — Played by a performer enlisted by Motivation Corp. From a future in which Stan Marsh was addicted to drugs to dissuade Stan from getting involved in drugs, his goal was to act as if he was. The plan completely failed as Stan quickly found out that Future Stan was actually a performer. Notable episodes: S06E16.

Notable episodes: S05E14.
Gary Harrison — Mr's son. Harrison and Mrs. Harrison. Notable episodes: S07E12.

Gavin Throttle — The coach for the Adams County Pee-Wee Hockey Team. Notable episodes: S10E14.
Gay Cowboys — The central characters of A Bunch of Gay Cowboys Eating Pudding. Notable episodes: S02E09.

Geeky Computer Guys — Geeky Computer Guys (also called the Star Trek Nerds) are two male college pupils who sometimes help out the boys in times of trouble. In Star Trek: The Original Series, they have shown to be useful and talented in both science plus special effects, but also to get into squabbles with each other over trivial things, such as the number of episodes. Notable episodes: S04E11.

Geldon — A dragon who will rise when the is spoken enough times to give him power, it is then that the world is to be destroyed. Defeated by Kyle using the Rune Stone of Undoing. Notable episodes: S05E01.

Gelgameks — An alien species and represent the Roman Catholic Church on their planet. Seen at the Vatican protesting Priest Maxi's request to change the Holy Law to stop molesting little boys. Notable episodes: S06E08.
Gems Wholesale Clerks — Three Asian women who run the Gems Wholesale jewelry shop. Notable episodes: S16E02.
Gene Hackman — A former American performer. Among other roles, he played Lex Luthor opposite Christopher Reeve as Superman in the Superman film series. Notable episodes: S07E02.
Gene Siskel — An American movie critic and journalist. Seen as a denizen of Hell. He showed up once in and again. Notable episodes: S03E15, S04E09.
General Davis — A military general who acted as an aide to Michael Chertoff. Notable episodes: S12E10.
General Deckter — A military general serving under the U.S. Department of Defense. He shows up in season 11's Imaginationland trilogy.
General Disarray — Professor Chaos' sidekick and the alter ego of Dougie O'Connell. He debuted. Notable episodes: S06E06.

General Tso — A Chinese general. Notable episodes: S16E14.
Genghis Khan — The creator of the Mongol Empire. Notable episodes: S03E15.
Genie — A Disney figure from the movie, Aladdin. Notable episodes: S23E02.

Geoffrey Maynard — A drama performer. Notable episodes: S04E13.
Geological Survey Supervisor — The boss of the United States Geology Survey in Colorado, the ex-workplace of Randy Marsh. Notable episodes: S12E12.

George Burns — George Burns, born Nathan Birnbaum was a renowned comic and performer. Burns showed up in the episode, among the forms Najix took to show up more familiar to the boys. He also showed up as one living in Hell. Kenny sees George Burns as he falls into Hell in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. Notable episodes: MOVIE, S07E01, S04E09, S10E11.
George Clooney — An American performer and filmmaker who was appearing in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. Notable episodes: S01E04, MOVIE, S10E02, S24E02.
George Lucas — The creator of the Star Wars franchise and the producer and writer of the Indiana Jones movies. Notable episodes: S06E09.
George Peppard — An American performer. Notable episodes: S02E03.

George R. R. Martin — An American writer best known as the writer of the fantasy series A Song of Ice and Fire, which is the basis of the TV series Game of Thrones. Featured. Notable episodes: S17E08, S17E09.

George W. Bush — From 2001 until 2009's 43rd president, acted as the United States, serving. A part of the American Republican Party alongside his vice president Dick Cheney. He has made multiple prominent and cameo appearances. Notable episodes: S10E09, S05E03.
George Washington — Acted as the United States who showed up in the short's 1st president. Notable episodes: S22E04.

George Zimmerman — An American, most renowned for his trial for the second-degree murder and manslaughter of African-American teenager, Trayvon Martin, which ended in acquittal. Notable episodes: S17E03.

Gerald Broflovski — Sheila Broflovski's husband, Kyle Broflovski's father and the adoptive father of Ike Broflovski. An Attorney at Law, currently operating at the Law Offices of Taylor, Broflovski & Swift and sometimes acting as the town's City Attorney. Operating under the alias of Skankhunt42, he plays a key antagonistic role throughout season 20. Named after Matt Stone's late father, Gerald W. Stone. Notable episodes: S01E01, S01E09.

Gerald Ford — An American lawyer, elected official and naval officer. He hold the distinction of being both the president and vice president of the United States without being elected into office. In 1974 upon the resignation of Richard Nixon, he acted as the 40th Vice-president following the resignation of Spiro Agnew in 1973, and then the 38th president. He ran for a full term on the Republican Party ticket in 1976 but lost the election to Jimmy Carter. Notable episodes: S05E05.
Geraldo Rivera — An ex-talk-show emcee and later news journalist for Fox News. He debuted in and later shows up. Notable episodes: S01E02, S10E05.

Getting Gay With Kids — Getting Gay With Kids (GGWK) is a choir organization featured. The group's central goal is to promote rainforest awareness and conservation through choir concerts. School counselor Mr. Mackey is revealed to be a GGWK board member. Notable episodes: S03E01.
Ghost Hunters — Ghost Hunters. Ghost Hunters is a real TV show on the Syfy Network. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Giada De Laurentiis — An Italian-American celebrity chef. Notable episodes: S14E14.
Giant Douche — One of the candidates for the South Park Elementary school mascot. Seen competing against Turd Sandwich. Notable episodes: S08E08.
Giant Nazi Zombie Fetus — A boss in South Park: The Stick of Truth.
Giant Reptilian Bird — A giant monstrous creature. Notable episodes: S15E14.
Gigi Hadid — Jelena Noura 'Gigi' Hadid is an American fashion model and TV personality. Notable episodes: S19E05.
Gil T — A figure. One of five members of the dance group, the Orange County Crew, who ended up being killed off at the end of the episode. Notable episodes: S08E04.
Ginger Cow — A cow. Notable episodes: S17E06.

Ginger Separatist Movement — An organization that was created by Eric Cartman to promote Ginger supremacy. Later brought back by Scott Tenorman in and where it is revealed that they're enemies of the Super Best Friends. Multiple kids are seen in during Stan's anti-bullying video. Notable episodes: S09E11, S14E05, S14E06, S05E03, S16E05.
Gingerbots — A returning foe in South Park: Tenorman's Revenge. In the show itself, exclusive to the game and have not made any appearances.
Gino — A crime boss and drug dealer who showed up as the proprietor of The Peppermint Hippo. A figure in the South Park criminal underworld. Notable episodes: S07E06.
Glee Club Kids — Unknown characters who are mentioned in a few episodes, but show up physically in and are also seen in South Park: The Stick of Truth. Notable episodes: S13E13, S17E09, S22E01.

Glen — One living in South Park who was also Head of Safety on the City Council. He debuted in the season 10 episodes as a background extra and made his first speaking appearance. He died from a shotgun blast to the face in the same episode by Randy Marsh. Notable episodes: S11E07, S10E03.
Glen Dumont — A F.B.I. negotiator. Notable episodes: S06E04.
Glinda the Good Witch — A figure from the Wizard of Oz film and the Oz franchise. She shows up as a part of the Council of Nine. Notable episodes: S11E12.
Gloria Allred — An attorney and human rights activist. Notable episodes: S05E02.
Gnome Warlock — A boss in South Park: The Stick of Truth.

God — God (real name Yahweh) is a supernatural celestial being and Jesus's father. Notable episodes: S03E16, S24E02.
Good Morning Canada Host — A presenter of the talk show Good Morning Canada. Notable episodes: S26E02.
Gordon Brown — From 2007 to 2010, a Scottish elected official who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. Notable episodes: S12E04, S13E06.
Gordon Ramsay — A British celebrity chef. Notable episodes: S14E14.

Gordon Stoltski — Gordon 'Jody' Stoltski was a bit-part figure who was first. A 3rd grade pupil at South Park Elementary who was in charge of giving the morning announcements, until his death. Notable episodes: S09E11, S13E13.

Goth Kids — The group of goth kids at South Park Elementary. Introduced in the episodes, they became regular background characters with occasional big roles including one episode where they even took over the title sequence and sung their own original version with new lyrics, the inaugural characters to have done so. Usually seen hanging around the café Benny's and the Village Inn. They also hang out behind the school, near the loading bay and parking lot and in Henrietta's Bedroom. They all wear black clothes and eyeliner and have black hair and pale skin plus being heavy smokers. Notable episodes: S07E14.

Grand Wizard King — The Grand Wizard King and leader of the humans at Kupa Keep. One of the six playable party members in South Park: The Stick of Truth,, who also serves as the last one to be unlocked. Notable episodes: S06E13, S17E09, S13E02.

Grandma Marsh — Randy Marsh's mother, plus Stan and Shelley Marsh's paternal grandmother. In although she has been mentioned in dialog in other episodes, she only made one on-screen appearance which was. Notable episodes: S04E08, S14E04.
Grandma Stotch — Butters' paternal grandmother, and Stephen Stotch's mother. Notable episodes: SPECIAL, S16E05.

Grandma Testaburger — Wendy Testaburger's grandmother. In the Testaburger family home, she has not showed up in the series outside of a photograph with her granddaughter, seen. She has been deceased since the season 1 episodes, when Principal Victoria told Wendy that she had died. Unknown whether she was her maternal or paternal grandmother. Notable episodes: S01E11, S12E09.
Grandma Tucker — The grandmother of Tricia and Craig Tucker. First mentioned in and later pictured. Notable episodes: S12E11, S12E10.

Grandma Tweak — Tweek Tweak's grandmother. The mother of either Tweek's mother or father and lives with the family sometimes; her bedroom is used as an office when she's not present. Notable episodes: S25E03.

Grandpa McCormick — From his grandson Kenny, he didn't have any speaking lines but he received a full body sensual massage. Laying on a heart-shaped bed in front of a studio audience when Kenny films this stunt. Notable episodes: S04E15.
Great-Great-Grandpa Marsh — The grandfather of Marvin Marsh and the great-great-grandpa of Stan Marsh. Notable episodes: S01E06.
Greeley Father — A parent who shows up watching the baseball game between South Park Little League Baseball Team and the Greeley Little League Baseball Team. Notable episodes: S09E05.

Gregory — A male fourth-grade pupil at South Park Elementary, who showed up only in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. He transferred to South Park from Yardale, where he purportedly maintained a 4.0-grade point average. Notable episodes: MOVIE.
Gretchen — Gretchen (formerly Linda) is a lesbian woman. Notable episodes: S11E06.
GS-401 — A weaponized, prototype clever towel, who was developed by Tynacorp. Notable episodes: S05E08.
Guinea Creatures — Giant guinea pigs that show up. Notable episodes: S12E10, S12E11.
Guy Fieri — An American celebrity chef. Notable episodes: S14E14.
Gwyneth Paltrow — An American performer who shows up in South Park: The Streaming Wars Part 2. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Hackelm Cartman — In South Park: Post Covid, the infant son of Eric and Yentl Cartman who shows up. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Hakeem Korashki — An Iraqi officer. He arrested Ms. Ellen. Notable episodes: S01E11.
Halfy — Halfy, pronounced is an amputee. Notable episodes: S01E09, S01E13, S24E02.
Hallway Monitor Boss — A boss in South Park: The Stick of Truth.

Haman — A former 5th Century BC Persian anti-Semitic chief official in the Ancient Persian Empire who attempted to annihilate the Jews and failed. Past his death he became a religious figure in the South Park universe who showed up as the secondary villain, where he shows up worshiped by the anti-Semitic sect of Judaism. Notable episodes: S03E09.
Han Seung-soo — The tenth prime minister of South Korea. Notable episodes: S13E06.

Hannah Williams — A first grader at South Park Elementary. Hannah's largest role was in when she conducted at the school talent show after Tweek. She sang while crying because Tweek's performance before her had scared her. Notable episodes: S09E07, S21E02.
Hansen — A SWAT member. Notable episodes: S04E11.
Hardly Boys — Private investigators, show up where they parody the Hardy Boys, a literary duo. Notable episodes: S10E09.
Hare Club for Men — An organization. Notable episodes: S11E05.
Harley Riders — Overly noisy motorcyclists. Notable episodes: S13E12.

Harold Cartman — A part of the Cartman family. The grandfather of Eric, Elvin, Fred and Alexandra and father of Liane, Uncle Stinky, and Howard Cartman, plus the husband and widower of Mabel. Notable episodes: S02E16, S07E04.

Harriet Biggle — Bradley Biggle and Henrietta Biggle's mother. She made brief appearances. On both occasions, she walks in on Henrietta in her room, for which she both praises Henrietta and is berated verbally. A secondary villain, too. Notable episodes: S07E14, S14E13, S23E08.
Harrison Moore — A CNN news reporter. Notable episodes: S08E07.

Harrison Yates — Sergeant Harrison Yates (often called Detective Harris) is the lead detective of the Park County Police Force and presumably, the highest-ranked officer in Park County. Usually accompanied by his partner Mitch Murphy or generic police officers. In the series since then, he initially shows up as a part of the FBI, but has since been seen as part of the Park County Police, a role he has consistently kept. Notable episodes: S07E09.
Harry — A part of Alcoholics Anonymous (AA). Notable episodes: S09E14.

Harry and Elise Gintz — Ike's biological parents. They named Ike. They took Ike away from The Broflovskis, because of the new law by the Canadian prime minister of every adopted Canadian must return home. The Canadian Prime minister was revealed to be Saddam Hussein, making the law not official. They saw how much Kyle cared about Ike, and gave him back to the Broflovskis. Notable episodes: S07E15.
Harry Potter Kids — From the Harry Potter universe, a crew of pupils roleplaying as characters. Notable episodes: S06E13.

Harvey Brown — The president and co-creator of Wall-Mart. The Boys found him brooding in a bar near the Wall-Mart headquarters in Bentonville, Arkansas. He told the boys that the only way to kill a Wall-Mart was to destroy its heart (a glass mirror near the TV department). His guilt got the best of him, and he then committed suicide, asking the boys to tell the world that he was sorry. Thanks to his help, Randy, Kyle and Stan were able to destroy the Wall-Mart in South Park. Notable episodes: S08E09.
Hat McCullough — A kid murderer. He also shows up as a background extra in the season 7 episode. Notable episodes: S06E09, S07E04, S08E07, S21E01.
Hazel — Ted's wife. Notable episodes: S22E02.
Hazmat Workers — Hazmat Workers. Notable episodes: S18E02.
HBC Head of Programming — A worker of the HBC Network. Notable episodes: S07E08.

Heather — A woman who shows up as Tad Mikowski's girlfriend. Notable episodes: S06E02.

Heather Conduct — The head of human resources at South Park Elementary. From showing romantic interest in their coworkers, called in by Mr. Mackey to help keep the school faculty, specifically PC Principal. Almost immediately after she introduces herself during a meeting with the school staff and the human resources department, Mr. Mackey ironically develops romantic feelings towards her. In a conversation with each other, after an attempt at demonstrating a healthy, platonic co-worker relationship with Mr. Mackey, Heather generates the same feelings, and the two become invested. Similarly to Mackey, Heather says at the end of most of her sentences. Notable episodes: S21E09.
Heather Swanson — Heather Swanson, formerly Blade Jaggart is a figure that showed up as the central villain. The ex-boyfriend of Strong Woman. Notable episodes: S23E07.

Heather Williams — A female pupil at South Park Elementary who initially shows up in South Park: Post Covid: The Return of Covid. Since season 25 she has made multiple minor appearances. Notable episodes: SPECIAL, S25E01.

Hebrews — Hebrews or Israelites are the ancestors of the Jews and Samaritans and the eponym of Israel - where they've lived since at least the 13th Century BC. The Hebrews are the source of the Biblical stories that led to the creation of the other Abrahamic monotheistic religions. For Jews while Eric Cartman disses Kyle Broflovski, they're usually used as a synonym.
Heidi — One of the contestants of the. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Heidi — The emcee of her own show, Simply Heidi, and is first seen where she has Freja Ollegard on her show as a guest. Notable episodes: S20E03.

Heidi Turner — A female fourth-grade pupil at South Park Elementary. She initially shows up as a background extra, and made her first speaking role in the 1999 film, South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut. Heidi is played among the in the fourth grade. Usually seen with Wendy, Bebe, Red, Nichole, Annie, Nelly, Jenny, Lola, and many other fourth grade girls. She hosted a sleepover in the season 9 episode, at which most of the attended, once again illustrating her popularity. She has been shown with different parents in four separate instances, most likely continuity errors. She acts as the primary female figure in Seasons Twenty and Twenty-One. Notable episodes: S04E10, MOVIE, S03E01, S09E09.
Heidi's Mother — Heidi's mother, one of the contestants of the. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Helen — A South Park character. Notable episodes: S03E02.
Helen Burch — Timmy's mom. Notable episodes: S04E03.

Henrietta Biggle — A 4th grader. The central female part of the Goth Kids, a group comprised of herself, Michael, Pete Thelman and Firkle Smith. The inaugural goth to have their name revealed. She speaks with a soft Valley Girl accent. Henrietta's Bedroom is among the Goth Kids' central hang-out spots and remains the only bedroom of the Goth Kids to be seen in the show. Notable episodes: S07E14.
Henry Gibson — An American performer and comic. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Henry Kline — A pupil at South Park Elementary. Notable episodes: S21E02.

Henry Winkler — An American performer and director. Most renowned for playing Arthur Fonzarelli (commonly referred to as Fonzie or ) on the 1970s' comedy series, Happy Days. He made an appearance as in the season 2 episode, plus providing the snarls of the Big Black Scary Beast. Notable episodes: S04E10.

Herbert Garrison — At South Park Elementary, mr. Herbert Garrison (briefly Mrs. Janet Garrison; after a sex-change operation that was later reversed) is a 4th grade educator. Voiced by Trey Parker. He ran for President in season 19, eventually gaining the Republican nomination. Lionel Barrymore — The classic Hollywood actor and director, famed as It's a Wonderful Life's Mr. Potter; he turns up in "Merry Christmas Charlie Manson!". Notable episodes: S02E16.
Lisa Berger — A shy-looking girl, previously called Lorraine, who first appears at the school assembly in "Butterballs" with Bucky Bailey's Bully Buckers. Notable episodes: S16E05.

Lisa Cartman — Extended Cartman family: Eric and Fred's aunt, Uncle Stinky's wife, Elvin and Alexandra's mom, and Liane's sister-in-law. Introduced in "Merry Christmas Charlie Manson!". Notable episodes: S02E16, S07E04.
Lisa Smith — Will Smith's daughter, seen in the season five episode "Here Comes the Neighborhood". Notable episodes: S05E12.
