entries.t: Little Debbie — The snack-cake brand mascot, appearing in the "End of Obesity" special. (Also: SPECIAL).
Liza Minnelli — The American actress and singer Liza Minnelli, seen in a season six episode. Notable episodes: S06E03.
Liza Nelson — A fourth-grade girl at South Park Elementary, first seen in the season nineteen episode "The City Part of Town". Notable episodes: S19E03.
Lizzy — A fourth-grade girl at South Park Elementary, first appearing in the season three episode "Hooked on Monkey Fonics". Notable episodes: S04E02, S03E05, S03E12, S12E04.
LoganLeDouche — An online influencer in the "Not Suitable for Children" special, constantly hyping Cred in his videos; he's based on influencer-wrestler Logan Paul.
Logger with Blue Overalls — A background construction worker in South Park, debuting in the season three episode "Rainforest Shmainforest". Notable episodes: S03E01.
Logger with Blue Pants — A background construction worker in South Park, debuting in the season eight episode "Goobacks". Notable episodes: S08E07.
Logger with Brown Coat — A background construction worker in South Park, debuting in the season three episode "Rainforest Shmainforest". Notable episodes: S03E01.
Lois Griffin — Lois Griffin, the matriarch of the Family Guy household, appearing in the two-part "Cartoon Wars" story. Notable episodes: S12E04, S10E03, S10E04.
Lola Paxton — A fourth-grade girl at South Park Elementary, first seen in the season three episode "Chinpokomon". Notable episodes: S03E11, S06E10, S11E14.

Lolly the Candy Man — He runs Lolly's Candy Factory. In "A Ladder to Heaven" he stages a candy shopping-spree contest the boys win, then refuses to honor it unless they produce the winning ticket stub within a week. In "The Scoots", a candy-desperate Mr. Mackey finds the shelves bare and gets turned away at gunpoint. Notable episodes: S06E12, S22E05.
Lonelygirl15 — The YouTube personality Jessica Rose, famous as Lonelygirl15, the fictional homeschooled vlogger Bree. She appears in a season twelve episode. Notable episodes: S12E04.

Loogie — Loogie, also called Luigi, a South Park Elementary student who runs a mob-style tooth-trading racket out of Loogie's Ristorante, an eatery that shares his name. He debuts in "The Tooth Fairy Tats 2000". Notable episodes: S04E01, S15E02.
Loogie's Associates — A trio of boys who work Loogie's tooth-trading operation in "The Tooth Fairy Tats 2000". Only one is named: Kolovski, the kid in the green jacket. Notable episodes: S04E01.
Lorde — Randy Marsh's secret musical alter ego, performing throughout season eighteen. Notable episodes: S18E02.
Los Angeles Clippers — The professional basketball team, appearing in a season sixteen episode. Notable episodes: S16E07.
Louis C.K. — The stand-up comedian Louis C.K., appearing in the season fifteen episode "Funnybot". Notable episodes: S15E02.
Louis Handler — A background student at South Park Elementary, first seen watching Tweek and Craig's fight in "Tweek vs. Craig". Notable episodes: S03E05, S03E11.
Lucky the Leprechaun — The Lucky Charms cereal mascot, appearing in the "End of Obesity" special. (Also: SPECIAL).
Lucy Harris — Martin Harris' wife and a witness to the golden plates, appearing in "All About Mormons". Notable episodes: S07E12.
Lucy van Pelt — The Peanuts comic-strip character, appearing in the season four episode "A Very Crappy Christmas". Notable episodes: S04E17.
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva — The Brazilian politician known as Lula, appearing in the season thirteen episode "Pinewood Derby". Notable episodes: S13E06.
Luke Covina — A fourth grader at South Park Elementary, appearing in the season sixteen episode "Cartman Finds Love". Notable episodes: S16E07.
Luke Skywalker — The Star Wars hero, sitting on the Council of Nine during the Imaginationland trilogy and backing Butters and the good imaginary characters against the evil ones.
M. Night Shyamalan — The filmmaker known for supernatural twists, appearing in the Imaginationland trilogy.
Mabel Cartman — Eric Cartman's maternal grandmother, married to Harold Cartman. She first appears in "Roger Ebert Should Lay off the Fatty Foods". Notable episodes: S05E06, S02E11, S02E16.
Mabel Gonzalez — Tom Brady's maid, appearing in the season twenty-three episode "Turd Burglars". Notable episodes: S23E08.
Mackey's Neighbor — A background South Park resident. His biggest moment comes in "The Scoots", where he informs Mr. Mackey that no one knows the scooters' origin. Notable episodes: S22E05.
Madelyn Dunham — The maternal grandmother of Barack Obama, making a brief appearance in "About Last Night...". Notable episodes: S12E12.
Madonna — The pop singer Madonna, appearing in the episode "Kenny Dies". Notable episodes: S05E13.
Maga Store Salesman — He works at the Myrtle Beach, South Carolina Maga Store, appearing in the season twenty-six episode "Spring Break". Notable episodes: S26E06.

Maggie Yates — The wife of Park County head detective Harrison Yates. She backs his police work despite worrying about his safety, and in "The Jeffersons" she talks him out of quitting the force. Notable episodes: S08E06.

Magi — The Three Wise Men, the biblical visitors who brought gold, frankincense, and myrrh to the newborn Jesus. They appear in "Jesus vs. Frosty" and "Mr. Hankey's Christmas Classics". Notable episodes: S03E15.
Magic Johnson — The former NBA star Earvin "Magic" Johnson, appearing in "Tonsil Trouble". Notable episodes: S12E01.

Mahatma Gandhi — The leader of India's independence movement, cameoing during Kenny's hellbound trip in the South Park movie, and again briefly in "Hell on Earth 2006". Notable episodes: S10E11. (Also: MOVIE).
Mailman — A character who introduces the season three episode "Mr. Hankey's Christmas Classics". Notable episodes: S03E15.
Malcolm McDowell — The English actor, serving as narrator of the season four episode "Pip". Notable episodes: S04E14.
Male St. Patrick's Day Offender — A criminal locked up at the county jail during the season twenty-five "Credigree Weed St. Patrick's Day Special". Notable episodes: S25E06.
Mall Madman — A character in the season four episode "Something You Can Do with Your Finger". Notable episodes: S04E08.

Manatees — The manatees who secretly write Family Guy: Gretchen, Flubber, Tigger, Pete, and Lucy. They live in a tank of "idea balls" — nouns, verbs, adjectives, celebrities — and assemble cutaway gags from random draws. Remove one ball and they stop working entirely. Seen in "Cartoon Wars Part II". Notable episodes: S04E15, S10E04.

ManBearPig — A demon from Hell who feeds on temptation, striking bargains that unleash carnage on the next generation once the debt comes due. Usually feral-looking, he is actually sentient and smart, sometimes donning clothes or chasing specific goals. Long dismissed as Al Gore's fictional career prop, he proves real in "Time to Get Cereal" when he starts menacing South Park. Notable episodes: S10E06, S11E11, S22E06. (Also: SPECIAL).
Mandy — A South Park Elementary cheerleader alongside Bebe, Red, Annie, Heidi, and Esther, debuting in the season eight episode "Douche and Turd". Notable episodes: S08E08.
Mannuel — An employee of MASA, the Mexican aeronautics and space agency, first seen in "Free Willzyx". Notable episodes: S09E13.
Manny Martinez — A sixth-grade background student at South Park Elementary, first seen in "Breast Cancer Show Ever". Notable episodes: S12E09.
Mantequilla — Butters Stotch's Mexican alter ego in the season fifteen episode "The Last of the Meheecans". Notable episodes: S15E09.
Manuelo Furnanda — A boxer from Del Fuego, Mexico, nicknamed "The Destructor", appearing in the season nine episode "Wing". Notable episodes: S09E03.
Many-Assed 6th Graders — Mutant sixth graders from the Genetic Engineering Ranch's experiments, appearing in the game The Fractured But Whole.
Many-Assed Cats — Mutant cats from the Genetic Engineering Ranch's experiments, appearing in the game The Fractured But Whole.
Mao Zedong — The Chinese revolutionary leader, appearing in the season three episode "Mr. Hankey's Christmas Classics". Notable episodes: S03E15.
Marc — Big Gay Al's pianist, debuting in the South Park movie. (Also: MOVIE).
Marcia Wallace — A non-speaking background character in "Super Best Friends", where she plays George Bush's maid Maggie. She has not appeared since. Notable episodes: S05E03.
Marcus — Ms. Crabtree's boyfriend inside Stan's dream in "City on the Edge of Forever (Flashbacks)".
Marcus Preston — A fourth grader at South Park Elementary, appearing in the season twenty-one episode "Hummels & Heroin". Notable episodes: S21E05.

Margaret Nelson — The substitute fourth-grade teacher who fills in after Garrison leaves to run for President, until he takes the job back. She debuts in "The City Part of Town" and dies of COVID-19 in "South ParQ Vaccination Special". Notable episodes: S24E02, S19E03. (Also: SPECIAL).
Maria Sanchez — A fourth grader at South Park Elementary, first seen in the season sixteen episode "Cartman Finds Love". Notable episodes: S16E07.
Marilyn Chambers — The adult-film actress and exotic dancer Marilyn Chambers, appearing in "Dead Celebrities". Notable episodes: S13E08.
Marilyn Manson — The shock-rock singer, appearing in "Prehistoric Ice Man" and singing "Stinky Britches" on a TV screen in "Chef Aid". Notable episodes: S02E18, S02E14.
Mario Batali — The celebrity chef, featured in the season fourteen episode "Crème Fraiche". Notable episodes: S14E14.
Marjorine — Butters Stotch in a girl disguise, in the season nine episode "Marjorine". Notable episodes: S09E09.
Mark — A pharmacist at the South Park Pharmacy, first seen in the season four episode "Timmy 2000". Notable episodes: S04E03.

Mark — A musician with Skyler Morse's group The Lords of the Underworld, appearing in "Cat Orgy" and "Timmy 2000", with a band cameo in "Christian Rock Hard". Notable episodes: S03E07, S07E09, S04E03.
Mark Cotner — His vehicle dies in South Park during "The Wacky Molestation Adventure", stranding him before a job interview. Notable episodes: S04E16.
Mark Cotswolds — A home-schooled kid who wins South Park's 15th annual spelling bee in "Hooked on Monkey Fonics". Notable episodes: S03E12.
Mark Fuhrman — The former LAPD detective known for his role in the O.J. Simpson trial, appearing in the season eleven episode "With Apologies to Jesse Jackson". Notable episodes: S11E01.
Mark Harrison — The eldest Harrison child, sibling to Jenny, Gary, Dave, and Amanda, appearing only in "All About Mormons". Notable episodes: S07E12.
Mark McGwire — The baseball player, presenting an award at the Special Olympics alongside Barry Bonds and Jason Giambi in "Up the Down Steroid". Notable episodes: S08E02.
Mark the Security Guard — A security guard who usually works with Alan, first seen in "Korn's Groovy Pirate Ghost Mystery" and "Trapper Keeper". Notable episodes: S03E10, S04E12.
Mark Wahlberg — The actor Mark Wahlberg, briefly appearing in "A Nightmare on Face Time". Notable episodes: S16E12.
Mark Zuckerberg — The Facebook founder and CEO, making his first appearance in the season twenty-one episode "Franchise Prequel". Notable episodes: S21E04.
Mark's Wife — A South Park resident, often seen alongside her husband Enchorito Mark. Notable episodes: S12E08.

Marklar — An intelligent alien species whose members all look identical and call every person, place, and thing "Marklar" — yet somehow understand each other without any confusion. Notable episodes: S03E13.
Martha — A South Park resident whose first notable appearance comes in the season twenty episode "The Damned". Notable episodes: S13E06, S20E03, S26E06.
Martha Stewart — The lifestyle businesswoman and TV personality, first appearing in the season six episode "Red Hot Catholic Love". Notable episodes: S06E08.
Martin Harris — In "All About Mormons", he aids Joseph Smith in rendering the golden plates as the Book of Mormon. Notable episodes: S07E12.
Martinez — An immigrant kid in the season twenty-three episode "Mexican Joker". Notable episodes: S23E01.
Marty — A USPS postmaster in the season fifteen episode "Crack Baby Athletic Association". Notable episodes: S15E05.
Marty — A film director in the season two episode "Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls". Notable episodes: S02E09.
Marty Jonus — The CEO of an unnamed Denver talent agency, appearing in "City on the Edge of Forever (Flashbacks)".

Marvin Marsh — Stan's paternal grandfather and Hare Club for Men member, regularly begging Stan to kill him. He has dementia and calls Stan "Billy". He debuted in the season one episode "Death". Notable episodes: S01E06.
Mary, Mother of Jesus — The biblical mother of Jesus, appearing in "Jesus vs. Frosty" and "Mr. Hankey's Christmas Classics". Notable episodes: S03E15.
MASA Workers — The employees of Mexicano Aeronáutico y Spacio Administración, first seen in "Free Willzyx". Notable episodes: S09E13.
Master P — The rapper, who performed "Kenny's Dead" for the Chef Aid album and joined the boys' band Moop in their anti-piracy strike in "Christian Rock Hard". Notable episodes: S07E09.
Matt — Nelly's father and Nelly's Mom's husband, a recurring background character with no major role yet. Notable episodes: S12E10, S15E06.
Matt Damon — The actor Matt Damon, first mentioned in "Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls" and first appearing in "The Streaming Wars Part 2". Notable episodes: S02E09. (Also: SPECIAL).
Matt Hasselbeck — The NFL quarterback, appearing in "Insheeption" as the gridiron player who enters Mr. Mackey's dream, with only a few lines. Notable episodes: S14E10.
Matt Kenseth — The professional race car driver, featured in the season fourteen episode "Poor and Stupid". Notable episodes: S14E08.
Matt Lauer — The former Today Show host, mentioned in "Something You Can Do with Your Finger" and appearing in "The Tale of Scrotie McBoogerballs". Notable episodes: S04E08, S14E02.
Matthew Broderick — The actor, appearing alongside his wife Sarah Jessica Parker in "The Tale of Scrotie McBoogerballs". Notable episodes: S14E02.
Matthew Klinner — Winner of a "Become a South Park Citizen" sweepstakes, shown during the closing title sequence of the season fourteen premiere "Sexual Healing". Notable episodes: S14E01.
Matthew McConaughey — The actor, driving and promoting the Handicar and ZipCar in the season eighteen episode "Handicar", spoofing his real Lincoln commercials. Notable episodes: S18E04.
Matti Vanhanen — The former Prime Minister of Finland, featured in "Pinewood Derby". He is presumed dead after the other nations nuke Finland. Notable episodes: S13E06.
Maury — The bouncer for the Raisins Girls, first appearing in the season seven episode "Raisins". Notable episodes: S07E14.
Maury Povich — The talk-show host, appearing in "Freak Strike" with Cartman and Liane as guests on his show. Notable episodes: S06E03, S02E15.
Max Weinberg — The Late Night bandleader and E Street Band drummer, appearing in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut when Terrance bursts through his bass drum. (Also: MOVIE).
Mayor McDaniels — The mayor of South Park, debuting in the season one episode "Weight Gain 4000" and remaining a prominent recurring figure. Notable episodes: S01E02.
Mayor of Imaginationland — The mayor of Imaginationland, modeled on Dreamfinder from Disney's Journey Into Imagination attraction. Notable episodes: S11E11.
Mayor of Weenietown — He governs Billionaire Weenietown — a data center sitting in Butters' backyard — debuting in the season twenty-nine episode "Billionaire Weenietown". Notable episodes: S29E02.
Mayor's Rival — Mayor McDaniels' unnamed rival, glimpsed in the season thirteen episode "The F Word". Notable episodes: S13E12.
McNuggets — A young Cornish rooster who plays Magic: The Gathering, appearing in the season eighteen episode "Cock Magic". Notable episodes: S18E08.
Meagan Ridley — A fourth-grade girl at South Park Elementary, previously called Riley, first appearing in "The List". Notable episodes: S15E08, S11E14, S15E04.
Meat Loaf — The rock musician and actor, appearing in "Chef Aid" in support of Chef's cause. Notable episodes: S02E14, S07E09.
Megan — One of the girls in Butters' kissing business in the season thirteen episode "Butters' Bottom Bitch". Notable episodes: S13E09.
Mel Gibson — The actor and director, depicted as completely and violently deranged in South Park. He debuts in the season eight episode "The Passion of the Jew". Notable episodes: S08E03.
Melancholy — Butters' dressage horse at the Park County Equestrian Facility championship, debuting in "Back to the Cold War". Notable episodes: S25E04.
Melania Trump — Donald Trump's wife, appearing in the season twenty-eight episode "The Woman in the Hat". Notable episodes: S28E02.
Melissa Weatherhead — One of the Weatherheads' many foster children, attending Greeley Elementary, appearing in "The Poor Kid". Notable episodes: S15E14.
Melita — She attends Jim Davis High School, appearing in the season twelve episode "Eek, A Penis!". Notable episodes: S12E05.
Memberberries — Sentient super-fruit debuting in the season twenty premiere "Member Berries". Notable episodes: S20E01, S21E07.
Menorah Cartman — Eric and Yentl Cartman's daughter, appearing in South Park: Post Covid. (Also: SPECIAL).
Mental House Doctors — Two doctors who briefly appear in "Mr. Hankey, the Christmas Poo", putting Kyle in a straightjacket. Notable episodes: S01E09.
Mercedes — A background figure debuting in the season seven episode "Raisins". Notable episodes: S07E14.
Meredith Vieira — The television personality, appearing in the season fourteen episode "The Tale of Scrotie McBoogerballs". Notable episodes: S14E02.

Metallica — The thrash metal band, joining the boys' anti-piracy strike in "Christian Rock Hard". Drummer Lars Ulrich also appears, disappointed he can't afford a shark tank. Notable episodes: S07E09.
Meth Heads — A group of drug dealers in the season seven episode "Lil' Crime Stoppers". Notable episodes: S07E06.
Mexican Joker — A puppet appearing in the season twenty-three episode "Mexican Joker". Notable episodes: S23E01.
Mexican Laborers — Day laborers making their first appearance in the season eleven episode "D-Yikes!". Notable episodes: S11E06.
Mexicans — Citizens of Mexico.
Miami Dolphins — The Miami NFL team, appearing in the season thirteen episode "Whale Whores". Notable episodes: S13E11.

Michael — The most prominent of the Goth Kids — Pete, Henrietta, and Firkle — often appearing in storylines without the other three. He debuts in the season seven episode "Raisins". Notable episodes: S07E14.
Michael — The unofficial head of Alcoholics Anonymous, appearing in the season nine episode "Bloody Mary". Notable episodes: S09E14.
Michael — A store clerk at Bed, Bath & Beyond, appearing in the season fourteen episode "Crème Fraiche". Notable episodes: S14E14.
Michael — A shopkeeper at Ur Da Star, appearing in the season seven episode "Fat Butt and Pancake Head". Notable episodes: S07E05.
Michael — He works at Wolf Home Security, appearing in the season sixteen episode "Insecurity". Notable episodes: S16E10.

Michael — A background character first seen in "Pandemic". His most notable appearances are in the season twenty episodes "The Damned" and "Wieners Out". Notable episodes: S17E03, S12E10, S13E02, S20E03, S20E04.
Michael — A disabled male fourth grader seen with the other handicapped children. He goes to Tardicaca Camp on the Red Team. Notable episodes: S08E02.
Michael — A Backcountry Adventures employee who hosts the ziplining tour group the boys join in "I Should Have Never Gone Ziplining". Notable episodes: S16E06.

Project Imagination Doorway Lead Scientist — A Pentagon scientist who worked under General Deckter for 40 years. Notable episodes: S09E08.
Psychiatrist — An unnamed psychiatrist who gives Cartman anger therapy in "T.M.I.". Notable episodes: S15E04.
Public Defender — He defends Butters in the season twenty-five episode "Credigree Weed St. Patrick's Day Special". Notable episodes: S25E06.
Pueblo Father — A parent in the baseball audience in "The Losing Edge". Notable episodes: S09E05. (Also: SPECIAL).
Purity Ring Kids — Children wearing purity rings in the season thirteen episode "The Ring". Notable episodes: S13E01.
PurpleHeadedQueefLicker — An internet troll of unknown real name, first appearing in "Wieners Out". Notable episodes: S20E04.

Q-Money — Nut Gobbler's pimp in "Erection Day". He kidnaps her from Jimmy, chases them to a rooftop, and gets clobbered with a metal pipe after Jimmy distracts him with jokes. Notable episodes: S09E07.
QAnon — The conspiracy group led by Bob White, the main villains of "South ParQ Vaccination Special". Notable episodes: S24E02.
Qatari Dignitary — A Middle Eastern businessman in the season twenty-seven episode "Sickofancy". Notable episodes: S27E03.
Quaid — A minor recurring kindergartner at South Park Elementary who debuted in Trapper Keeper. He is the best friend of Filmore Anderson, the rival of Ike Broflovski. Notable episodes: S04E12.

Queen Elizabeth II — The British monarch who makes a brief appearance attempting to invade the United States with a fleet of archaic warships. When her fleet is sunk, she shoots herself with a handgun. Notable episodes: S11E04.
Queen of Canada — A minor figure seen in Royal Pudding and later posthumously in The Worldwide Privacy Tour. Notable episodes: S15E03, S26E02.
Queen of Hearts — The tyrannical ruler from Alice in Wonderland who shows up in the South Park universe in Band in China. Notable episodes: S23E02.

entries.n: Queer Eye for the Straight Guy
entries.t: Queer Eye for the Straight Guy — The five-man makeover crew, the Fab Five, who help straight men with style but are secretly Crab People in disguise. Notable episodes: S07E08.
k: queer eye for the straight guy

entries.t: Quintuplets — Five Romanian contortionist sisters who perform at the Cirque Du Cheville. They are orphans with an absent father, and their grandmother dies of a heart attack during the episode; they briefly live with the Marsh family. Four are named Glacas, Nadia, Natalia, and Baltania; the fifth is never named. Notable episodes: S04E04.
R. Kelly — The R&B singer and songwriter behind hits like I Believe I Can Fly, who appears in the show in Trapped in the Closet. Notable episodes: S09E12.
Rachel — A sales representative for Quality Curtains who appears once, in Marjorine. Notable episodes: S09E09.
Radiohead — The English rock band that appears in Scott Tenorman Must Die. Notable episodes: S05E04.
Raila Odinga — The Prime Minister of Kenya, shown as one of the world leaders in Pinewood Derby. Notable episodes: S13E06.
Raisins Girls — Preteen waitresses who staff the Raisins restaurant. Notable episodes: S07E14.
Ralph — A mailman from Topeka who appears in The Red Badge of Gayness. Notable episodes: S03E14.

Ranae Holland — A recurring South Park citizen and Bigfoot researcher, first seen with the city's Bigfoot research group in Jewpacabra; she later turns up in background roles. Notable episodes: S16E04, S17E09, S23E10.
Rancid — A punk rock band from Berkeley, California, featured among the performers in Chef Aid. Notable episodes: S02E14.

Randy Marsh — Stan and Shelley's father and Sharon's husband, a geologist with a doctorate whose antics drive many later-season plots; he was calmer and more level-headed in earlier seasons, often advising the boys. His erratic behavior is later tied to unhappiness in his marriage, and he briefly divorces Sharon and moves away. Notable episodes: S01E03 (debut, Volcano), S04E08, S09E08, S11E01, S15E07, S18E03, S18E08.

Randy Newman — Tolkien Black hires this American singer-songwriter, pianist, and film composer — famed for I Love L.A. and You've Got a Friend in Me — to write a theme song for Here Comes Fatty Doo Doo in Raising the Bar. Notable episodes: S16E09.
Randy's Friends — A group of four local men who first appear in Spontaneous Combustion, dressed up as the boys. Notable episodes: S03E02.
Ranger McFriendly — A park ranger who appears in Smug Alert!. Notable episodes: S10E02.

Ranger Pete — A forest ranger who greets Mr. Mackey's class on their field trip to Frisco Woods and introduces them to Woodsy Owl, not knowing Woodsy is a child molester, unknowingly setting young Mackey's abuse in motion. Notable episodes: S14E10.

Ranger Stan Marshwalker — Stan Marsh's ranger alter ego, appearing through the Season Seventeen Black Friday trilogy, and the protecting warrior of the Elven Kingdom in The Stick of Truth game. Notable episodes: S17E07, S17E08, S17E09.
Rauf Xerxes — The owner of Club Persh in South Park who tries to shut down the Les Bos bar but is stopped by Mrs. Garrison. Notable episodes: S11E06.
Reality — A physical embodiment of the harsh truths that Safe Space advocates want to ignore, appearing in Safe Space. Notable episodes: S19E05.
Rebecca (Raisins Girl) — A waitress at Raisins who appears in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Rebecca (Towelie's Ex-girlfriend) — Towelie's former girlfriend and the mother of his son Washcloth, seen in Crippled Summer. Notable episodes: S05E08, S14E07.
Rebecca and Her Mother — Two customers at the South Park Mall in Titties and Dragons. Notable episodes: S17E09.
Rebecca Cotswolds — A home-schooled girl who competes alongside her brother and wins the 15th Annual South Park Spelling Bee in Hooked on Monkey Fonics. Notable episodes: S03E12.
Rebecca Turnod — The Surgeon General of the United States, seen in T.M.I. Notable episodes: S15E04.
Recess Supervisor — The woman who dismisses and supervises recess at the school, seen in Damien and Butters' Bottom Bitch. Notable episodes: S01E10, S13E09.
Recorder Concert Coordinator — The organizer of the recorder concert in World Wide Recorder Concert. Notable episodes: S03E17.
Red Harris — The owner of Luau's Toys, first appearing in Chinpokomon. Notable episodes: S03E11, S05E08.

Red McArthur — A female fourth-grade student at South Park Elementary, arguably the fifth-most prominent girl in the grade behind Wendy, Heidi, Bebe, and Nichole. She debuts in Cartman Gets an Anal Probe. Notable episodes: S01E01, S01E10.
Reese Witherspoon — This American actress — Laura Jeanne Reese Witherspoon — shows up in South Park: The Streaming Wars Part 2.
Reggie Burke — A student at South Park Elementary who turns up in episodes alongside the other handicapped children. Notable episodes: S08E02.
Regis Philbin — The American talk show host who appears in Eat, Pray, Queef. Notable episodes: S13E04.
Reince Priebus — The American politician and former White House Chief of Staff, seen in Members Only. Notable episodes: S20E08.
René Dif — The Danish singer-songwriter and lead male vocalist of the Eurodance group Aqua, appearing in Cock Magic. Notable episodes: S18E08.
Retarded Fish — A character who appears in A Scause For Applause. Notable episodes: S16E13.
Rex — Clyde's dog, seen in Big Gay Al's Big Gay Boat Ride. Notable episodes: S01E04.

Ricardo Montalban — The American actor shown as his Fantasy Island character Mr. Roarke in Cancelled as one of Najix's forms; his Star Trek character Khan turns up in the Imaginationland trilogy, and he is among the dead celebrities in Dead Celebrities. Notable episodes: S02E11, S07E01, S13E08.

Richard Adler — The shop class teacher at South Park Elementary, first seen in Tweek vs. Craig. He regularly tells students to stop screwing around and fills in wherever school faculty are needed. Notable episodes: S03E05.
Richard Burch — Timmy's father, appearing in Timmy 2000. Notable episodes: S04E03.
Richard Dawkins — The English scientist known for his work on evolution, appearing in the Go God Go two-parter and mentioned in Faith Hilling. Notable episodes: S10E12, S10E13, S16E03.
Richard Stamos — The fictional brother of John Stamos, featured in Big Gay Al's Big Gay Boat Ride. Notable episodes: S01E04.
Richard Tweak — Mrs. Tweak's husband and Tweek Tweak's father, making his first appearance in Gnomes. Notable episodes: S02E17.
Rick — The former ticket salesman for the Bijou Cinema, now the manager of the local Burger King.
Rick (Black Friday) — A security guard who appears in the Season Seventeen episodes Black Friday, A Song of Ass and Fire, and Titties and Dragons. Notable episodes: S17E07, S17E08, S17E09.
Rick (Japanese Toilet) — An employee of The Home Depot, seen in Japanese Toilet. Notable episodes: S26E03.
Rick (Pajama Day) — Herbert Garrison's boyfriend, first seen in Pajama Day; the two live together in what seems to be a serious relationship. Notable episodes: S25E01.
Rick (Taming Strange) — A friend of Terry's who appears in Taming Strange. Notable episodes: S17E05.
Rick (Field Reporter) — A field reporter for the South Park News. Notable episodes: S09E08.
Rick and Susan Tyler — The camp counselors at Hopeful Hills, seen in Fat Camp. Notable episodes: S04E15.

Rick James — The American singer, songwriter, and producer behind late-70s and early-80s hits like Super Freak. He gives the boys money to help Chef in Chef Aid, protests alongside other musicians in Christian Rock Hard, and sits in the back row at the MTV Music Awards in Britney's New Look. Notable episodes: S02E14, S07E09, S12E02.

Rick Santorum — In Faith Hilling he attends the Colorado Republican Presidential Debate beside Ron Paul, Newt Gingrich, and Mitt Romney; by the end, he, Gingrich, and Romney are debating the Talking Cat, which has replaced Paul. Notable episodes: S16E03.
Rick Tellmore — During Titties and Dragons he camps outside the South Park Mall, waiting for the Black Friday sales to begin. Notable episodes: S17E09.
Rick the Mountie — A member of the Canadian Mounted Police, seen in It's Christmas in Canada. Notable episodes: S07E15.
Rick Watts — A news reporter for Channel 4 News. Notable episodes: S04E11, S05E01, S05E02.
Rita Struthers — A nurse who appears in Lice Capades as a lice screener. Notable episodes: S11E03.
Rob Reiner — The American actor and director who debuts as the primary antagonist of Butt Out, leading a sinister anti-smoking campaign. Notable episodes: S07E13.

Rob Reiner's Smoke Stoppers — A sinister anti-smoking group led by Rob Reiner that wants smoking banned from bars and public places. They plan to kill Eric Cartman after filming a commercial to make it more realistic; ironically, their overweight leader gorges on junk food. Notable episodes: S07E13.
Rob Schneider — The American actor and comedian who appears in The Biggest Douche in the Universe. Notable episodes: S06E15.
Robby — Heidi Turner's dog, found dead in Helen Keller! The Musical after Timmy frees Gobbles and lets him loose on the street. Notable episodes: S04E13.
Robby (The Entity) — A baby seen in the Season Five episode The Entity. Notable episodes: S05E11.

Robert Redford — The former actor and director who founded the Sundance Film Festival. He appears in Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls and later returns in 200 and 201. Notable episodes: S02E09, S14E05, S14E06.
Robert Smith — The English musician and lead singer of the goth rock band The Cure, appearing in Mecha-Streisand. Notable episodes: S01E12.
Robert T. Pooner — A Nebraska news field reporter seen in Merry Christmas Charlie Manson! and Britney's New Look. Notable episodes: S02E16, S12E02.
Robin Meade — The American news anchor who appears in Go Fund Yourself. Notable episodes: S18E01.
Robin Williams Hologram — A hologram modeled on the famous comedian, featured in a cameo in #HappyHolograms, the only celebrity hologram with just a cameo appearance.
Robot Monkeys — Robotic primates that appear in Pip. Notable episodes: S04E14.
Rod Stewart — The British rock and pop singer, songwriter, and record producer who makes his first appearance in Are You There God? It's Me, Jesus. Notable episodes: S03E16.
Rodriguez — A Jim Davis High School student in Eek, A Penis! who serves as one of Eric Cartman's pupils while Cartman poses as Eric Cartmanez. Notable episodes: S12E05.
Roger — The owner of an East Asian weapon stall, seen in Good Times with Weapons. Notable episodes: S08E01.

Roger Donovan — Clyde's widowed father, mentioned in Terrance and Phillip: Behind the Blow and first appearing at the book meeting in Red Hot Catholic Love. He was usually seen with his wife Betsy until her death in Reverse Cowgirl, when his name was revealed; he now dates a new woman. Notable episodes: S05E05, S06E08, S16E01.
Roger Goodell — The commissioner of the NFL, first appearing in Sarcastaball, where he is sarcastic and rude to Randy Marsh like nearly everyone else in the episode. Notable episodes: S16E08.
Romanian Father — In Quintuplets 2000, a gun is held to his head while he is made to demand that the U.S. government return the quintuplets to Romania. Notable episodes: S04E04.
Romanian Guards — Seen in Quintuplets 2000 trying to bring the Quintuplets and their grandmother home; a later boating accident presumably kills them. Notable episodes: S04E04.
Romper Stomper — A prisoner who appears in Cartman's Silly Hate Crime 2000. Notable episodes: S04E02.
Ron — A record producer who appears in The Cissy. Notable episodes: S18E03.

Ron Paul — The former U.S. Representative for Texas's 14th district, shown as a Republican presidential candidate at the Colorado Republican Debate with Romney, Gingrich, and Santorum in Faith Hilling; by the episode's end he has been replaced by a Talking Cat for the debate. Notable episodes: S16E03.
Ron Silver — The American actor, activist, and director who appears in Dead Celebrities. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Ron Zappolo — He retired from news and sports broadcasting after leading Denver's FOX affiliate KDVR as anchor from 2000 to 2013. Notable episodes: S11E13.
Rosemary — A hotel maid who appears in Crème Fraiche. Notable episodes: S14E14, S20E05.
Rosie O'Donnell — The American actress, talk show host, and comedienne best known for hosting The Rosie O'Donnell Show, who appears in Trapper Keeper. Notable episodes: S04E12.
Roy — Sharon Marsh's boyfriend in the Season Two episode Clubhouses. Notable episodes: S02E12.
Rudolph — The fictional reindeer, often described as the youngest of Santa's reindeer and famous for his shiny red nose. Notable episodes: S02E16.
Rudy — Within Clubhouses, a parody of the Bill Cosby cartoon Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids called The Fat Abbott Show features Rudolph Rudy Davis. Notable episodes: S02E12.

Rudy Giuliani — The former mayor of New York City, appearing as an attorney for President Garrison in Season Finale, where he helps the arrested Randy Marsh, who donated bombs to end home weed-growing and protect his business. Notable episodes: S23E06.
Ruffian's Couple — A gay couple who appears in Tweek x Craig. Notable episodes: S19E06.
Ruhollah Khomeini — Iran's first Supreme Leader, a political and religious figure who held the post from 1979 until dying in 1989; Ali Khamenei succeeded him. Notable episodes: S02E01.

Runaway Girls — Two sixteen-year-old high schoolers, one blonde and one brunette, who debut in Clubhouses with a major role though their names are never given; they later pop up in the background among other teenagers. Notable episodes: S02E12.
Rush — The Canadian prog rock band that appears in Royal Pudding. Notable episodes: S15E03.
Russell — The Fat Abbott Show, a parody of Bill Cosby's Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids seen in Clubhouses, includes him as a character. Notable episodes: S02E12.
Russell Brand — The English actor and comedian best known as Aldous Snow in Forgetting Sarah Marshall, who appears in Funnybot. Notable episodes: S15E02.

Russell Crowe — The New Zealand-Australian actor known for Gladiator, first seen on a poster in Chef Goes Nanners and later in person in The New Terrance and Phillip Movie Trailer. Notable episodes: S04E07, S06E05, S14E06.

Russell Crowe Editor — An editor for the show Russell Crowe Fightin' Around The World, seen in The New Terrance and Phillip Movie Trailer with a background appearance in Erection Day. Notable episodes: S06E05, S09E07.
Ryan (Cartman Sucks) — A boy seen only in Cartman Sucks at Camp New Grace, where he was supposed to be Butters's Accountabilibuddy but is found hanged in his room. Notable episodes: S11E02.
Ryan (Faith Hilling) — A teenager who appears in Faith Hilling. Notable episodes: S16E03.
Ryan (Taming Strange) — A character who makes a brief appearance in Taming Strange. Notable episodes: S17E05.
Ryan Ellis — A male fourth grader who first appears in The Ungroundable as a member of the South Park Vampire Society. Notable episodes: S12E14.

Ryan Valmer — Jimmy Valmer's father and Sarah Valmer's husband, chief of South Park's Fire Department on the City Council. He first appears with Mrs. Valmer in Krazy Kripples, suspecting Jimmy has joined a gang. Notable episodes: S07E02, S07E08.

Saddam Hussein — Iraq's former president and dictator, who recurs on the show and anchors South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut as its main villain. A pack of wild boars kills him before the American-Canadian War, after which he dates — then splits from — Satan as his jealous, abusive, manipulative boyfriend. Notable episodes: S01E11 (Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus), S02E01, S04E10, S07E15.
Saddam Hussein's Parents — Ibrahim al-Hassan Muhammad and Subha Talfah, who briefly appear in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut.
Saint Joseph — The legal father of Jesus Christ, glimpsed in the background beside Mary, Mother of Jesus, during O Holy Night in Mr. Hankey's Christmas Classics. Notable episodes: S03E15.

Saint Patrick — The Romano-British Christian missionary and primary patron saint of Ireland, proclaimed a saint by popular acclaim rather than canonization. He appears in the Credigree Weed St. Patrick's Day Special. Notable episodes: S25E06.
Saint Peter — Born Shimon Bar-Yona in Bethsaida, Judea, this Christian saint numbers among Jesus Christ's Twelve Apostles. Notable episodes: S09E04, S11E05.
Sally (Douche and Turd) — This ostrich is married to Gary, who belongs to the People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals; she is seen in Douche and Turd. Notable episodes: S08E08.
Sally Bands — A kindergartner girl who debuts in Trapper Keeper, where she votes for and supports Ike Broflovski against Filmore Anderson in the class president election. Notable episodes: S04E12.

Sally Darson — A female fourth-grade student at South Park Elementary who debuts in Butters' Bottom Bitch. She runs a schoolyard kiss-for-money operation, is the only known member of the school swim team, and is seen checking out Larry's bike in Bike Parade. Notable episodes: S13E09, S22E10, S23E07.
Sally Dion — The daughter of Terrance and Celine Dion, appearing in Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus. Notable episodes: S02E01.
Sally Struthers — This American actress played Gloria — Archie and Edith's daughter — on All in the Family, and first appears in Starvin' Marvin. Notable episodes: S01E08, S14E06.
Sally Turner — A female fourth-grade student at South Park Elementary, also called Powder. She first appears in Rainforest Shmainforest. Notable episodes: S03E01, S08E12, S09E10.
Sam, David, and Chris — Three geologist friends of Randy Marsh who appear in the Season Five premiere It Hits the Fan. Notable episodes: S05E01.

Samantha Dunskin — A South Park Elementary student in Eat, Pray, Queef who can queef at will; she demonstrates on Butters Stotch's face, enraging the town's fathers, who try to get her expelled. Notable episodes: S13E04.

Samaritans — An ethnoreligious group descended from a mix of Israelites and exiled Middle Eastern peoples, with a long love-hate history with the Jews until they gained a common enemy in the Roman and later Byzantine empires. Notable episodes: S02E02.
Samuel Alito — The American jurist and associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court who appears in Imaginationland, Episode III. Notable episodes: S11E12.
San Diego Singers — Three male characters who appear in Butterballs. Notable episodes: S16E05.
Sanctified — A Christian metal band that appears in Christian Rock Hard. Notable episodes: S07E09.
Sandy Cervix — The host of The Hollywood Minute in Funnybot, one of the show's many reporters with strange-sounding names. Notable episodes: S15E02.

Santa Claus — The world-renowned holiday symbol in his trademark red and white suit, a friend and ally of the boys who shows up for their Christmas adventures. In Imaginationland he is said to be an imaginary character, and he is a friend and rival of Jesus Christ.
Sarah — In Pajama Day, she works at the International House of Pancakes. Notable episodes: S25E01.
Sarah (The Ring) — A character who appears with her boyfriend in The Ring. Notable episodes: S13E01.
Sarah Flannigan — The wife of Howard Flannigan, appearing in Goth Kids 3: Dawn of the Posers. Notable episodes: S17E04.
Sarah Jessica Parker — The American actress best known as Carrie in Sex and the City, seen in a non-speaking role in The Tale of Scrotie McBoogerballs. Notable episodes: S14E02.

Sarah McLachlan — The Canadian singer-songwriter known for 90s hits like Possession, Building a Mystery, Sweet Surrender, and Angel, and for founding the Lilith Fair music festival. She appears in Crack Baby Athletic Association. Notable episodes: S15E05.
Sarah Palin — The former Alaska governor and Republican vice-presidential candidate in 2008, who appears prominently in About Last Night... Notable episodes: S12E12.
Sarah Peterson — A character whose only appearance is in Lil' Crime Stoppers. Notable episodes: S07E06.
Sarah Valmer — Jimmy Valmer's mother and Ryan Valmer's wife, first appearing in Krazy Kripples, where she suspects Jimmy has joined a gang. Notable episodes: S07E02.

Satan — Hell's ruler, who often surfaces in South Park for plots ranging from nefarious to harmless. He is openly gay, and though evil itself, he is compassionate and vulnerable; he is the big bad of South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut yet gets sympathetic turns in Probably, Hell on Earth 2006, and Freemium Isn't Free. In Nobody Got Cereal? he fights ManBearPig, is beaten and slain, and rises to Heaven — ironic for a fallen angel. Notable episodes: S01E10, S04E10, S10E06, S10E11, S18E06, S22E07.
Saudi Royals — Two Saudi Arabian princes, including Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud, acting as representatives for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in Turkey Trot. Notable episodes: S28E04.

Scary Assistant — A member of Rob Reiner's Smoke Stoppers in Butt Out, seen offering Eric Cartman a presumably poisoned cupcake to kill him after the anti-smoking commercial, pinning his death on lung cancer from smoking. Notable episodes: S07E13.
Schlomo — A Squirt leader who appears in Jewbilee. Notable episodes: S03E09.
School Advisory Board Technician — A minor character appearing only in Deep Learning. Notable episodes: S26E04.
School Librarian — A background character who works at South Park Elementary. Notable episodes: S13E13.
Schroeder — The pianist from the Peanuts comic strip, appearing in three Season Four episodes, usually whenever music auditions are held. Notable episodes: S04E08, S04E10, S04E17.
Science Expert — A guest speaker on Fox and Friends for Fox News, appearing in Wok is Dead. Notable episodes: S27E04.
Scott (Clubhouses) — A minor character first seen in Clubhouses. Notable episodes: S02E12.
Scott and Tyler — Two HBC Network employees first seen in It Hits the Fan, later appearing as Jared Fogle's aides in Jared Has Aides. Notable episodes: S05E01, S06E01.
Scott Evans — This counselor handles prison rehabilitation at the Canyon City Maximum Security Prison in The Wacky Molestation Adventure. Notable episodes: S04E16.
Scott Malkinson — A character introduced in Elementary School Musical, who has a lisp and diabetes, which Cartman mocks him for. Notable episodes: S08E06, S12E13.

Scott Tenorman — A ninth-grader and self-proclaimed Head Ginger who becomes Eric Cartman's nemesis and, unbeknownst to him, half-brother. He debuts in Scott Tenorman Must Die. Notable episodes: S05E04, S24E02.

Scott the Dick — A character who first appears in Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus, cameos on the Asses of Fire movie poster, and later shows up in It's Christmas in Canada and Royal Pudding, where he is seen as a giant dick. Notable episodes: S02E01, S07E15, S15E03.
Scrambles (Cock Magic) — A rooster who plays Magic: The Gathering in Cock Magic. Notable episodes: S18E08.
Scrambles (Major Boobage) — A gray tabby cat who appears in Major Boobage. Notable episodes: S12E03.
Scrambles (The Fractured But Whole) — A brown tabby cat who appears in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.

Scuzzlebutt — A basket-weaving monster living atop a mountain in South Park, with a piece of celery for an arm and Patrick Duffy for a leg. He features prominently in Volcano and has made several cameos since. Notable episodes: S01E03.

Seaman — A member of the Super Best Friends whose name is constantly mispronounced as semen by the other members and the episode narrator, much to the superhero's dismay. Notable episodes: S05E03, S24E02.
Sean Hannity — The American television presenter and host of Hannity on Fox News, first seen in Wok is Dead. Notable episodes: S27E04.

Secret Service Agents — Federal officers of the U.S. Secret Service who protect political leaders, candidates, and families, and investigate financial crimes like counterfeiting and bank fraud. First seen in Mystery of the Urinal Deuce. Notable episodes: S10E09, S24E02.

Secret Society of Cynics — A band of freedom fighters in Ass Burgers who set out to destroy the illusory world, headquartered at the Asperger's Research Center. Its leader and patients echo Morpheus and other Matrix figures, and they recruit Stan into group therapy to teach him their coping secret. Notable episodes: S15E08.

Sef Furman — Josef Saul Sef Furman, an 18-year-old South Park fan from Plano, Texas who made a guest appearance in The Pandemic Special with the help of the Make-A-Wish Foundation. Notable episodes: S24E01.
Selena Gomez — The American actress, singer, and animal rights activist who appears in Bass to Mouth. Notable episodes: S15E10.
Senior AIDS Researcher — An AIDS researcher first seen in Tonsil Trouble, in charge of Mitch and his cohort. Notable episodes: S12E01.
Sergei Shoigu — The Russian military general and politician serving as Russia's Minister of Defence, appearing in Back To The Cold War. Notable episodes: S25E04.

Sex Pistols — The British punk band known for Anarchy in the U.K. and God Save the Queen, pictured with Chef in his photo album in Chef Aid; one of their songs, Pretty Vacant, is played by Stan and Kyle on Guitar Hero in Guitar Queer-O. Notable episodes: S02E14, S11E13.
Señor Lopez — He turns up in a dream sequence during Pee, the Season Thirteen finale. Notable episodes: S13E14.
Sgt. Snetzl — A sergeant with the Santa Barbara Police Department, seen in The Jeffersons. Notable episodes: S08E06.
Shadowbane — An eagle serving as assistant to the School Advisory Board Technician in Deep Learning. Notable episodes: S26E04.

Shari Lewis — The entertainer and her puppet Lambchop, seen on Mr. Garrison's television in Summer Sucks, where Garrison fantasizes about severing Lambchop from her hand and grilling it. Notable episodes: S02E08.
Sharon Marsh — Stan and Shelley Marsh's mother and Randy Marsh's wife, first appearing in An Elephant Makes Love to a Pig. Notable episodes: S01E05, S01E06, S01E11, S06E16.
Shauna — A South Park Elementary student who debuts in Erection Day and later appears as a background character in Board Girls. Notable episodes: S09E07, S23E07.
Shauna's Mother — The parent of Shauna, making a minor appearance in Erection Day. Notable episodes: S09E07.

Sheila Broflovski — Kyle's mom and Ike's adoptive mother, married to Gerald Broflovski. Cartman constantly insults her, branding her a bitch who ruins his fun — he even wrote Kyle's Mom's a Bitch about her — and she drives the plot of South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut as its central villain. Notable episodes: S01E06, S14E09.

Shelley Marsh — Randy and Sharon's daughter and Stan's older sister. She is vindictive, aggressive, and ill-tempered, calling those around her turds and beating or torturing Stan and his friends when adults are absent, though she has a compassionate side; later seasons show her as assertive and focus on her bond with her father. She first appears in An Elephant Makes Love to a Pig. Notable episodes: S01E05, S16E02.
Sheriff McLawdog — The town sheriff of Pioneer Village, played by an unnamed employee, appearing in Super Fun Time. Notable episodes: S12E07.
Shinzo Abe — The former Japanese prime minister, whose image appears in Handicar when news of the Wacky Races breaks out. Notable episodes: S18E04.
Shoe Saver Salesman — A salesman who appears in Insecurity. Notable episodes: S16E10.
Shoe Store Mother — An actor who appears in Insecurity. Notable episodes: S16E10.
Shub-Niggurath — An Elder God from the Cthulhu Mythos who debuts in South Park: The Fractured But Whole and cameos in the South ParQ Vaccination Special. Notable episodes: S24E02.
Sia — A student at South Park Elementary who appears only in The Cissy; no other character speaks her name in the episode. Notable episodes: S18E03.
Sid — A guest speaker on the Larry King Live show in Whale Whores. Notable episodes: S13E11.
Sid Greenfield — A Los Angeles director for America's Most Wanted, appearing in Cartman's Mom is Still a Dirty Slut. Notable episodes: S02E02.

Sidney Poitier — The American actor who helps South Park battle Barbra Streisand in Mecha-Streisand by transforming into a Japanese kaiju; he and Leonard Maltin fail, and Robert Smith destroys Streisand in the end. Notable episodes: S01E12.

Silvio Berlusconi — The former Italian prime minister, one of the world leaders in Pinewood Derby whose residence is later blown up by Baby Fark McGee-zax; he reappears when Lorde is replaced by her hologram on live TV. Notable episodes: S13E06, S18E01.
Simon — A fourth grader at South Park Elementary who is sometimes confused with the Boy with Blond Hair.
Simon Hankey — One of Mr. Hankey's children, born with a peanut in his head and of low intelligence. He appears in A Very Crappy Christmas and The Stick of Truth game. Notable episodes: S04E17.
Simon McCoy — A British newsreader who appears in Wieners Out. Notable episodes: S20E04.
Sinéad O'Connor — The Irish singer and songwriter who appears in Taming Strange. Notable episodes: S17E05.

Sir John Harington — A writer who invented the modern flush toilet, dubbing it his porcelain toilet machine. In Reverse Cowgirl he crashes the courtroom while the Hoffman and Turk Law Offices perform their sue-ance. Notable episodes: S16E01.
Sister Anne — A Roman Catholic nun. Notable episodes: S04E09.
Sister Hollis — A Christian missionary seen in Starvin' Marvin in Space. Notable episodes: S03E13.
Sixth Grader Swarmer — Groups of sixth graders who debut as recurring enemies in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Skankhunt42 — This internet troll and cyberbully is the big bad of Season Twenty's first half. Notable episodes: S20E01.

Skeeter — He owns and tends bar at Skeeter's Wine Bar, and ranks among the town's notable citizens. His cameo debut is Cartman's Mom is a Dirty Slut, with his first real showcase in Sexual Harassment Panda. Usually found at his bar or heading protests, he reads as a stereotypical redneck with a thick Southern accent and conservative activist politics, though his views shift episode to episode. Notable episodes: S01E13, S03E06.

Skeeter's Friends — Two minor hillbilly-side characters who debut in Sexual Harassment Panda and are often seen with Skeeter until Follow That Egg!; a prototype pair appears in Chef's band in Weight Gain 4000. Notable episodes: S01E02, S03E06, S09E10.
Skyler Morse — A 22-year-old musician who is still in high school because of low grades, first appearing in Cat Orgy. Notable episodes: S03E07, S07E09.

Slash — Born Saul Slash Hudson and also called Vünter Slauche, this English-American musician and songwriter — famed lead guitarist of the hard rock band Guns N' Roses — turns out to be a made-up figure from a Dutch legend. Notable episodes: S07E04.
Slaughterhouse — A teenager who faces Kenny as his Magic: The Gathering opponent in Cock Magic. Notable episodes: S18E08.
Sloth — Lotney Sloth Fratelli, the character from the 1985 adventure film The Goonies, who appears in Freak Strike. Notable episodes: S06E03.
Smelly John — A Canadian singer and pianist seen in The Worldwide Privacy Tour, where he performs Goodbye, Queefy Queen at the Queen of Canada's funeral. Notable episodes: S26E02.
Smitty — A minor character seen in World Wide Recorder Concert and one of several cut from The Stick of Truth game. Notable episodes: S03E17.
Smoking Boys — Three fifth graders who appear in Chef's flashback in The Tooth Fairy Tats 2000. Notable episodes: S04E01.

Smurfs — A species of small blue creatures living in Smurf Village in the woods near South Park. They appear in the background of the Imaginationland episodes and take a prominent role in Dances with Smurfs. Notable episodes: S11E12, S13E13.

Snarf — The ThunderCats character who, in the Imaginationland trilogy, escorts Butters to Castle Sunshine with the Lollipop King at the Mayor of Imaginationland's request, ending most sentences by saying Snarf once or twice until an annoyed Butters asks him to shut up for five minutes. Notable episodes: S11E11.
Sneezing Panda — An internet celebrity who appears in Canada on Strike, waiting for his theoretical payment. Notable episodes: S12E04.
Snooki — A parody of Jersey Shore's Nicole Snooki Polizzi, seen in It's a Jersey Thing terrorizing Skeeter's Bar. Notable episodes: S14E09.

Snoop Dogg — The American rapper, singer, producer, and actor, a key figure in West Coast hip-hop known for hits like What's My Name?, Gin and Juice, and Drop It Like It's Hot. He appears in Here Comes the Neighborhood as one of the rich newcomers to South Park. Notable episodes: S05E12.
Snoopy — The main character of Charles M. Schulz's Peanuts comic strip, who first appears in A Very Crappy Christmas. Notable episodes: S04E17.
Snow White — The Disney character starring in Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, based on the German fairytale, who appears in Band in China. Notable episodes: S23E02.
Snowball — Pope Snowball, a white rabbit who becomes the leader of the worldwide Roman Catholic Church in Fantastic Easter Special. Notable episodes: S11E05.

SoDoSoPa Ninjas — A ninja faction created by the boys in Naughty Ninjas. According to Jimmy, they believe in something greater than themselves, follow a strict warrior code, and stay united to defeat all enemies. Notable episodes: S19E07.
Soleil Moon Frye — The American actress, director, producer, and screenwriter best known as Punky Brewster, who appears in Terrance and Phillip: Behind the Blow. Notable episodes: S05E05.
Somali Pirates — A group of pirates based in Somalia who appear in Fatbeard. Notable episodes: S13E07.
Some Puerto Rican Guy — An entirely fabricated criminal mentioned in Butters' Very Own Episode. Notable episodes: S05E14.
Sonny Bono — The American singer, actor, and politician who appears in Terrance and Phillip: Behind the Blow. Notable episodes: S05E05.
Sonny the Cuckoo Bird — Cocoa Puffs' mascot, seen in South Park: The End of Obesity.

Sophie Gray — A female fourth-grade student at South Park Elementary who debuts in Basic Cable as the new girl, recently moved from Scottsdale, Arizona. Like Scott Malkinson, she has diabetes, and from Season Twenty-Six she continues as a background character. Notable episodes: S23E09.
Sounderoos — A local country music duo formed by musicians Earl and Kate, appearing in Band in China. Notable episodes: S23E02.
South Park Committee — The South Park-based town committee organization that appears in Gnomes. Notable episodes: S02E17.

South Park Compounding Pharmacy — A business formed by the Boys in South Park: The End of Obesity to make obesity drugs for Eric Cartman, letting him lose weight after his insurance refuses to cover weight-loss drugs like Ozempic.

South Park Crime Unit — The South Park Junior Detectives, a crime-solving group founded by Stan Marsh in Lil' Crime Stoppers so the boys' playtime would mean something and they could protect and serve South Park. The uncorrupted unit consists of Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny, with Liane Cartman as secretary; it operates first from Cartman's basement, then from a park. Notable episodes: S07E06.
South Park Express Conductor — A minor character who first appears in Cartman Gets an Anal Probe. Notable episodes: S01E01.

South Park Vampire Society — A group of South Park Elementary students who dress up and act like vampires, featured prominently in The Ungroundable and Goth Kids 3: Dawn of the Posers. Notable episodes: S12E14, S17E04.
South Park: Phone Destroyer/Characters — A roster page listing the characters that appear in the game South Park: Phone Destroyer.

Sparky — Stan Marsh's pet dog, claimed to be part Doberman and part wolf and the toughest dog on the mountain. That claim is challenged when Sparky's homosexual nature emerges, first with Sylvester and then with Clyde's dog Rex; he has made sporadic cameos since. Notable episodes: S01E04, S20E10.
Sparrow Prince — A sparrow-ghost who first appears in The Death Camp of Tolerance. Notable episodes: S06E14.
Special Ed Kids — A group of children who appear across several episodes and in The Fractured But Whole DLC Bring the Crunch. Notable episodes: S03E17.
Special Olympics Volunteers — Volunteers who appear in Up the Down Steroid. Notable episodes: S08E02.
Special Weapons and Tactics — SWAT, police tactical units specially trained and equipped for high-risk situations, featured in multiple episodes.
Spencer Hollis — He attends South Park Elementary and appears in South Park (Not Suitable For Children).
Spider-Man — The Marvel character starring in several Marvel Cinematic Universe films, who first appears in Hell on Earth 2006. Notable episodes: S10E11.

Spike Lee — The American film director and actor known for Jungle Fever, Do the Right Thing, Malcolm X, and BlacKkKlansman, appearing as a background character in Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls. Notable episodes: S02E09.

Spontaneous Bootay — This obese stripper dances at The Peppermint Hippo. Her appearances include The Return of Chef, The Fractured But Whole, and a brief shot at the end of the South ParQ Vaccination Special. Notable episodes: S10E01, S24E02.
Spookyfish — An evil goldfish that Stan Marsh receives as a gift from his aunt Flo Kimble, serving as the main antagonist of Spookyfish. Notable episodes: S02E15.
Stacy — A background character and sixth-grade student at South Park Elementary, first seen in Breast Cancer Show Ever. Notable episodes: S12E09.
Stacy Muleburg — The poster child for Halitosis Kidz!, an organization fighting bad breath, appearing in Cartman Finds Love. Notable episodes: S16E07.
Stan Marsh — Stanley Stan Marsh, one of South Park's four main characters alongside Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, and Kenny McCormick. Notable episodes: S01E01, S14E04.
Stan Marsh (Universe 216-B) — This alternate-timeline Stan Marsh turns up in South Park: Joining the Panderverse.
Star Wars Kid — Ghyslain Raza, the Canadian internet celebrity popularly known as the Star Wars Kid, appearing in Canada on Strike. Notable episodes: S12E04.
Starvin' Marvin — A thin little boy from Ethiopia who first appears in Starvin' Marvin. Notable episodes: S01E08.
Steamy Nicks — A female singer who appears in You're Getting Old, whose name and look riff on Stevie Nicks, lead vocalist and songwriter of Fleetwood Mac. Notable episodes: S15E07.

Stella Reid — One of the nannies on the TV show Nanny 911 in Tsst, alongside Yvonne Finnerty and Deborah Carroll; she is chosen to help Liane at the Cartmans' house but fails in her task. Notable episodes: S10E07.
Stephen Abootman — The head of the World Canadian Bureau (WGA) in Canada on Strike. Notable episodes: S12E04.
Stephen Abootman's Aides — Assistants to Stephen Abootman at the World Canadian Bureau in Canada on Strike. Notable episodes: S12E04.

Stephen and Martha Thompson — A couple with a deformity called Reverse Polarity Syndrome (or Torsonic Polarity Syndrome, TPS) that makes their faces resemble buttocks, appearing in How to Eat with Your Butt. Notable episodes: S05E10.

Stephen Hopkins — Seen during Cartman's flashback in I'm a Little Bit Country, he governed the Colony of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations and sat in the 1776 Continental Congress. Notable episodes: S07E04.

Stephen Miller — This American political adviser serves as Senior Adviser to the President on immigration and domestic policy in Donald Trump's second administration, featured in The Woman In The Hat. Notable episodes: S28E02.
Stephen Stotch — Stephen Willis Stotch, also known as Chris, Butters' father and Linda Stotch's husband. Notable episodes: S02E04, S04E04, S05E14, S18E05.
Stephen Tamill — A fifth-grade boy who appears in 1%. Notable episodes: S15E12.
Stephen Tamill's Friends — Two fifth-grade boys seen protesting the 99% alongside Stephen Tamill in 1%. Notable episodes: S15E12.
Steve — The lead counselor at Tardicaca Camp and a teacher at South Park Elementary working with special education students, first seen in Crippled Summer. Notable episodes: S14E07, S21E08.
Steve (Grounded Vindaloop) — He works customer service in Grounded Vindaloop, fielding calls for Korean Airlines, Best Buy, El Pollo Loco, Oculus Rift, and more. Notable episodes: S18E07.
Steve (Pip) — This teenager dates Estella Havisham in Pip. Notable episodes: S04E14.
Steve (Canadian) — A Canadian fisherman from Newfoundland who appears in It's Christmas in Canada. Notable episodes: S07E15.
Steve Ballmer — The former Microsoft CEO and current owner of the Los Angeles Clippers, seen in A Song of Ass and Fire. Notable episodes: S17E08.

Steve Bannon — The American political strategist and media executive who served as Donald Trump's Chief Strategist, acting as President Garrison's strategist in Members Only. Notable episodes: S20E08.
Steve Bisciotti — The owner of the Baltimore Ravens who appears in Go Fund Yourself. Notable episodes: S18E01.

Steve Black — Steven Steve Black, the father of Tolkien and husband of Linda Black. Very wealthy, with a large house and expensive SUV, he is a diehard fan of author J.R.R. Tolkien; he previously worked as a lawyer and financial consulting executive before entering marijuana farming. He debuts in Cartman's Silly Hate Crime 2000. Notable episodes: S04E02, S06E13, S25E02.

Steve Forbes — The American publisher and businessman, editor-in-chief of Forbes magazine, who first appears in The Entity as one of the rich and famous people Mr. Garrison invites to view his creation, IT. Notable episodes: S05E11.
Steve Irwin — The Australian TV personality known as the Crocodile Hunter, parodied in Prehistoric Ice Man. Notable episodes: S02E18, S14E05.
Steve Jobs — The former CEO of Apple Inc., who died on October 5, 2011. Notable episodes: S05E11, S15E01.
Steve McNair — The American NFL football quarterback who appears in Dead Celebrities. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Steve Nelson — An endorsement management worker who appears in A Scause For Applause. Notable episodes: S16E13.
Steven (Super Best Friends) — A Blaintologist and the henchman and spokesman for cult leader David Blaine in Super Best Friends. Notable episodes: S05E03.
Steven (News Anchor) — Also known as Chris Swollenballs, a news anchor for Channel 4 News during Seasons Eleven and Twelve. Notable episodes: S04E11, S12E10.
Steven Seagal — The American actor who appears in Safe Space. Notable episodes: S19E05.

Steven Spielberg — The American film director behind the Indiana Jones series, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, and many more, known for collaborating with George Lucas. He first appears in Cripple Fight. Notable episodes: S05E02, S06E09.
Stevens Family (Volcano) — A family of four first seen in the Lava and You segment of Volcano, who occasionally reappear as background characters in Seasons One and Two. Notable episodes: S01E03.

Stevie Wonder — The American singer-songwriter known for Superstition, Part-Time Lover, and That's What Friends Are For. He is first mentioned in Damien and physically appears as a background character in Chef Aid. Notable episodes: S01E10, S02E14, S03E01.
Stewie Griffin — The one-year-old Griffin infant — flamboyant, eccentric Stewart Stewie Gilligan Griffin — and a Family Guy lead. Notable episodes: S10E03, S12E04.
Storehand — An unnamed employee plays this owner of Pioneer Village's general store in Super Fun Time. Notable episodes: S12E07.
Stormtroopers — Soldiers and guards of the Star Wars universe, typically serving the Galactic Empire. Notable episodes: S11E11.
Stormtroopers (First Order) — The First Order's stormtroopers, tasked with guarding and defending the First Order, seen in Band in China. Notable episodes: S23E02.

Stormy Weathers — A Park County district attorney in The China Probrem, whose name puns on stormy weather, referring both to literal storms and to dramatic personal situations needing an attorney. Notable episodes: S12E08.

Strawberry Shortcake — The American Greetings character from cards, dolls, and animation who appears in the Imaginationland trilogy, where she is tortured and killed by evil fictional characters, then revived with all the other slain imagination characters when Butters re-imagines Imaginationland. Notable episodes: S11E12.
Street Skater Boys — Characters who appear briefly in With Apologies to Jesse Jackson. Notable episodes: S11E01.
Streibel Daughters — The twin daughters of Mr. and Mrs. Streibel, playing a minor role in Toilet Paper. Notable episodes: S07E03.
Stripe — Craig Tucker's pet guinea pig, first seen on screen in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Strippers — The strippers of The Peppermint Hippo, featured in Lil' Crime Stoppers, The Return of Chef, and The Fractured But Whole. Notable episodes: S07E06, S10E01.

Strong Woman — South Park Elementary's vice-principal and mom to the PC Babies. True to her name, she is strong and independent, aiming to be a role model for little girls. She first shows up in SUPER HARD PCness, where PC Principal's conflicted romantic feelings for her turn out to be mutual. Notable episodes: S21E09, S28E01.
Stu — The salesman and owner of Stu's Firework Shack, appearing in Summer Sucks. Notable episodes: S02E08.

Stuart McCormick — Carol McCormick's husband and the father of Kenny, Karen, and Kevin McCormick. He debuts in Starvin' Marvin and his first name is revealed in Chickenpox. Notable episodes: S01E08, S02E10.
Studio Ghibli Executives — A trio of representatives from Studio Ghibli who appear in Sora Not Sorry. Notable episodes: S28E03.
Stupid Spoiled Whore Teenage Girls — Two teenage girls who first appear in Stupid Spoiled Whore Video Playset. Notable episodes: S08E12, S23E02.
Sue Preston — The mother of Marcus Preston and wife of Mr. Preston, seen at her son's birthday party in Hummels & Heroin. Notable episodes: S21E05.
Sugar Bear — Golden Crisp's mascot, seen in South Park: The End of Obesity.
Suicidal Canadian — A resident of Canada who appears in Where My Country Gone? Notable episodes: S19E02.

Summons — Combat abilities in The Stick of Truth and The Fractured But Whole, earned by completing side quests for selected characters. Each character has a unique summon drawn from their earlier appearances in South Park continuity, used to aid the player in battle.
Sundar Pichai — The American-Indian businessman and CEO of Google, appearing in Sickofancy. Notable episodes: S27E03.

Super Adventure Club — A pedophilic travel group that serves as the main antagonist of The Return of Chef. The club tours the world to molest the native children of the countries it visits, and parodies the Church of Scientology with its bizarre beliefs and brainwashing of new members. Notable episodes: S10E01.

Super Awesome Talent Agency — A talent company in Wing, founded by Eric Cartman on the theory that even the untalented can succeed by taking 20% off those who are. He starts it with Stan, Kyle, and Kenny to become Tolkien Black's management team, decking out his basement as an office complete with a water fountain, big desk, and telephone. Notable episodes: S09E03.

Super Best Friends (Group) — A superhero organization made up of the leading figures of the world's major religions, plus Seaman. A parody of the Superfriends cartoon and DC's Justice League, they debut in Super Best Friends. Notable episodes: S05E03.
Super Craig — The superhero alter ego of Craig Tucker, debuting in Franchise Prequel. Notable episodes: S21E04.
SuperSexyLisa18 — An internet troll of unknown real name who first appears in Wieners Out. Notable episodes: S20E04.
Susan — A background character, referred to as Kate in Christmas Snow, most notable in Time To Get Cereal. Notable episodes: S21E02, S22E06, S23E10.

Susan Boyle — The Scottish singer mentioned in Fatbeard, where Ike Broflovski says he would vomit his balls out through his mouth if he heard one more thing about her Britain's Got Talent performance of I Dreamed a Dream from Les Misérables. Notable episodes: S13E07.
Susan's Husband — The husband of Susan, appearing in Time To Get Cereal. Notable episodes: S22E06.
Suzanne Somers — The American actress and singer best known for Three's Company, She's the Sheriff, and Step by Step, who appears in Death. Notable episodes: S01E06.
Suzette — The female mascot for the alcoholic drink brand S'more Schnapps, appearing in The Red Badge of Gayness. Notable episodes: S03E14.
Swallow — A member of the Super Best Friends and Seaman's bird sidekick, first appearing in Super Best Friends. Notable episodes: S05E03.
Swimming Instructor — An unnamed woman who appears in Summer Sucks as Eric Cartman's swimming teacher. Notable episodes: S02E08.
Swiper — The character from the children's animated series Dora the Explorer, who first appears in Hummels & Heroin. Notable episodes: S21E05.
Sylvester — A street dog who appears in Big Gay Al's Big Gay Boat Ride, billed as the toughest dog in South Park. Notable episodes: S01E04, S02E03.
Sylvester (Crippled Summer) — A fictional cartoon character who cameos as a handicapped camper at Lake Tardicaca in Crippled Summer. Notable episodes: S14E07.

Sylvester Stallone — The American actor, director, and screenwriter known for Rocky Balboa in the Rocky films and John Rambo in the Rambo films. He appears in Wing as the host of the reality show The Contender. Notable episodes: S09E03.
Tad Mikowski — The skier Stan Marsh battles in a competition in Asspen, who mockingly calls Stan Stan Darsh. Notable episodes: S06E02, S26E02.
Talnua Cussler — A golf course owner who appears in South Park: The Streaming Wars.

Tammy Nelson — A student at South Park Elementary, usually seen in the school corridors. Her first speaking role is in Bass to Mouth, where she tells Emily her mother is an alcoholic; her name is confirmed there. Notable episodes: S08E11, S15E10.

Tammy Thompson — A television news reporter and anchor for Channel 4 News alongside her brother Tom Thompson, first appearing in Black Friday. She and her brother are later revealed to secretly be lovers. Notable episodes: S17E07.
Tammy Warner — A fifth-grade girl introduced in The Ring, who serves as Kenny McCormick's love interest during her screen time. Notable episodes: S13E01.
Tardicaca Camp Counselors — Counselors at Lake Tardicaca, a summer camp for disabled children, first seen in Crippled Summer. Notable episodes: S14E07.
Tardicaca Indians — A Native American tribe living on a reservation around Lake Tardicaca in Crippled Summer. Notable episodes: S14E07.
Taro Aso — The 92nd Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister of Japan, first seen in Canada on Strike and later in Pinewood Derby. Notable episodes: S12E04, S13E06.
Tasmanian Devil — The fictional cartoon character, also spelled Tazmanian Devil, who cameos as a handicapped camper at Lake Tardicaca in Crippled Summer. Notable episodes: S14E07.
Tauntaun — The fictional Star Wars creature used as a mount, first seen in Obama Wins! Notable episodes: S16E14.

Tay Zonday — Adam Nyerere Bahner, better known as Tay Zonday, the internet celebrity famous for singing Chocolate Rain, a song about racism toward African Americans, seen in Canada on Strike. Notable episodes: S12E04.

Taylor Swift — Taylor Alison Swift, the American Grammy-winning singer-songwriter and occasional actress, featured in #HappyHolograms, where she performs a duet of Baby It's Cold Outside with Bill Cosby.
Teabag — A character who appears in Medicinal Fried Chicken. Notable episodes: S11E05, S14E03.
Ted — An aide to Mayor McDaniels who works with her to help improve South Park. Notable episodes: S01E03, S11E07, S14E01.
Ted (A Boy And A Priest) — The husband of Hazel, appearing in A Boy And A Priest. Notable episodes: S22E02.
Ted (A Nightmare on Face Time) — The titular character of the 2012 movie, briefly appearing in A Nightmare on Face Time. Notable episodes: S16E12.
Ted (Planned Parenthood Doctor) — First seen in Cartmanland as the proctologist treating Kyle's hemorrhoid; in later appearances he serves as a regular abortion doctor. Notable episodes: S05E06.
Ted Bundy — Theodore Robert Ted Bundy, the American serial killer, seen in Hell on Earth 2006 as a resident of Hell. Notable episodes: S10E11.

Ted Kennedy — Edward Ted Moore Kennedy, the U.S. Senator from Massachusetts, seen in Dead Celebrities aboard a plane bound for Purgatory with Billy Mays, Natasha Richardson, and many other deceased celebrities. Notable episodes: S13E08.

Ted Koppel — The news anchor who hosts Nightline in Free Hat, where the boys appear to promote their movement against directors revising Hollywood classics and to free Hat McCullough, the convicted serial killer guilty of murdering twenty-three babies. Notable episodes: S06E09.
Ted Turner — The American media tycoon and founder of CNN, one of the rich and famous people Mr. Garrison invites to view IT in The Entity, his only appearance to date. Notable episodes: S05E11.
Teenage Hippies — Hippies who first appear in Ike's Wee Wee. Notable episodes: S02E03.
Teenagers — Frequent minor characters who debut in Clubhouses. Notable episodes: S02E12.
Teresa — A llama housed at the PETA Compound, appearing in Douche and Turd. Notable episodes: S08E08.
Terrance and Phillip — These two Canadians form a comedy duo headlining The Terrance and Phillip Show; Terrance was born October 20th and Phillip November 12th. Notable episodes: S01E06.

Terrance Mephesto — A South Park Elementary student and the son of Dr. Alphonse Mephesto, owner of the South Park Genetic Engineering Ranch. He makes his only speaking appearance in An Elephant Makes Love to a Pig as a rival and antagonist to the boys, leading Bill Allen and Fosse McDonald. Notable episodes: S01E05, S01E12.

Terri Irwin — The Australian-American naturalist and television personality best known for co-starring with Steve Irwin in The Crocodile Hunter, appearing in Prehistoric Ice Man. Notable episodes: S02E18.
Terry — The Canadian Minister of Health, appearing in Taming Strange. Notable episodes: S17E05.
Terry Gilliam — A filmmaker belonging to Monty Python, the acclaimed British comedy troupe.
Terry's Wife — A minor character who appears in Taming Strange. Notable episodes: S17E05.
Thad (Insecurity) — A UPS truck driver and deliverer in Insecurity, bringing Amazon.com packages to the townsfolk of South Park. Notable episodes: S16E10.

Thad Jarvis — A Guitar Hero expert tapped by a talent agency to hit one million points alongside Stan Marsh in Guitar Queer-O. He walks out once Stan gets hooked on Heroin Hero and grows crabby, and dismisses Cheap Trick as bubblegum crap. His party trick: playing John the Fisherman and Jordan on a bare controller so cleanly that onlookers hear the music and praise him. He also cameos in Stan's anti-bullying video in Butterballs. Notable episodes: S11E13, S16E05.
The FAGS Boys — Two brothers who first appear in W.T.F. Notable episodes: S13E10.

The 4th Grade — Since the episode of the same name, most characters sit in this class grade. It holds most of the child cast, though a second fourth-grade classroom likely exists, since plenty of fourth graders never appear in the main room. Notable episodes: S04E11.
The 6th Graders — Students at South Park Elementary who recurred in the early seasons and now appear as background characters. Notable episodes: S02E12.

The 9th Graders — Ninth-grade teens including Scott Tenorman and his crew. They bake the pube-laced chili for Cartman in Scott Tenorman Must Die and rejoin Scott for the Fellowship of the Ring sequel episode. Notable episodes: S05E04, S06E13.
The Afghan Boys — The Afghan counterparts of the South Park boys, appearing in Osama bin Laden Has Farty Pants. Notable episodes: S05E09.

The Back Dorm Boys — Wei Wei and Huang Yixin, web-famous for lip-syncing the Backstreet Boys' I Want It That Way. In Canada on Strike they linger in the background among internet celebrities awaiting theoretical payments; whether they lived is unknown. Notable episodes: S12E04.
The Baldwins — The acting family of Alec, Daniel, William (Billy), and Stephen Baldwin, appearing in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut.
The Bard (Character) — Jimmy Valmer's alter ego in The Stick of Truth, the singing bard of the Drow Elves and one of the game's six playable partners. Notable episodes: S17E07, S17E09.
The Beatles — The English rock band, mentioned in numerous South Park episodes. Notable episodes: S02E14.

The Boys — Also known as the Broship, the group of the show's four main characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, and Kenny McCormick. Early episodes usually open with them standing at the bus stop; Chef calls them Children. Notable episodes: S01E01.

The Clitoris — In South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut, Stan begs Chef for a way to make Wendy Testaburger like him again, and Chef answers: just find the Clitoris. Stan hunts everywhere — asking Kyle (clueless), Shelley (who chairs him in the head), and the internet (useless) — before learning the Clitoris is a giant glowing, talking reproductive organ.

The Coon (Character) — Eric Cartman's costumed superhero and eventual supervillain alter ego, debuting in the self-titled episode The Coon. He leads Coon and Friends in Coon 2: Hindsight but is kicked out for beating up and blackmailing the other heroes. He goes fully evil in Mysterion Rises, allying with Cthulhu and embarking on a killing spree that levels San Francisco, continuing in Coon vs. Coon & Friends as Cthulhu destroys the Burning Man festival. Notable episodes: S13E02, S14E11, S14E12, S14E13.
The Evil Boys — The boys' counterparts from a parallel universe, seen in Spookyfish. Notable episodes: S02E15.
The Fat Abbott Show — An animated TV show seen in Clubhouses. Notable episodes: S02E12.
The Foley Kids — Three red-haired siblings who first appear in Ginger Kids. Notable episodes: S09E11.
The Ghetto Avenue Boys — A fictional boy band Randy Marsh joined in the 1980s; Randy recounts his whole experience to Stan in Something You Can Do with Your Finger. Notable episodes: S04E08.
The Hobbit (Character) — The secondary protagonist of the South Park short Cartman and the Hobbit.

entries.n: The Knights of Standards and Practices
entries.t: The Knights of Standards and Practices — Medieval knights sworn to keep cursing to a minimum, set to return whenever a swear word is used excessively. A rune was made for each of the eight words that so offended God; they appear only in It Hits the Fan. Notable episodes: S05E01.
k: the knights of standards and practices

entries.t: The Llama Brothers — The Boys and Craig Tucker form this Peruvian flute band, heard in Pandemic and Pandemic 2: The Startling. Notable episodes: S12E10, S12E11.
