The Lollipop King — An imaginary character from the Imaginationland trilogy, seen with Snarf escorting Butters to Castle Sunshine at the request of the Mayor of Imaginationland.
The Lords of the Underworld — A band made up of Skyler Morse, Jonesy, and Mark, later joined by Timmy. Notable episodes: S03E07.
The Melvins — A group of boys considered the lamest kids in all of South Park Elementary, seen in Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub. Notable episodes: S03E08.
The Muppets — The puppets made by Jim Henson, mentioned many times across the show.

The New Kid — Canon also calls them Butthole, Buttstuff, and Douchebag. They headline The Stick of Truth, The Fractured But Whole, Phone Destroyer, and Snow Day! — games only, never the show. They speak exactly once, at the end of The Stick of Truth: Screw you guys. I'm going home. The Big Bad Government Guy outs their real name as Dovahkiin.
The Other 4th Grade — Children known to be in the larger fourth-grade class at South Park Elementary who are not regularly seen in Mr. Garrison's classroom.
The Redbox Killers — A gang seen in A Nightmare on Face Time. Notable episodes: S16E12.

The Rockettes — The Radio City Rockettes, the American precision dance company performing at Radio City Music Hall in New York, best known for the annual Radio City Christmas Spectacular and the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.
The South Park Diggities — Stan Marsh assembles this dance troupe, which the Orange County Crew challenges to a dance-off in You Got F'd in the A. Notable episodes: S08E04.

entries.n: The Stick of Truth Combatants (The Fractured But Whole)
entries.t: The Stick of Truth Combatants (The Fractured But Whole) — Also called the Fighters of Zaron, the kids playing the fantasy game from The Stick of Truth, appearing in The Fractured But Whole.
k: the stick of truth combatants (the fractured but whole)

entries.t: The Ugly Kids — Students in The List who are ostracized for their ugliness, shunned by the community and forced to sit together at one lunch table, apart from the other children. Notable episodes: S11E14.
Therapy Kids — A group of students in The Fractured But Whole who act as manifestations of negative relationship issues, fought during the Therapy Wars mission.
Theresa — A female fourth-grade student at South Park Elementary who first appears in The List. Notable episodes: S11E14, S15E04.
Thomas — A boy with Tourette's syndrome who appears in Le Petit Tourette. Notable episodes: S11E08.
Thomas (Blizzard Staff) — One of the directors of Blizzard Entertainment, the company behind World of Warcraft, appearing in Make Love, Not Warcraft. Notable episodes: S10E08.
Thomas (Charlotte's Father) — Charlotte's father, appearing in Where My Country Gone? Notable episodes: S19E02.
Thomas Jefferson — The third President of the United States, serving 1801 to 1809, a founding father who wrote the Declaration of Independence in 1776. Notable episodes: S07E04.
Thomas McElroy — Chef's father, who lives in Scotland. He first appears in The Succubus, traveling to South Park with his wife for Chef's wedding. Notable episodes: S03E03, S06E17.
Thomas Tucker — Laura Tucker's husband and the father of Craig and Tricia, considered one of the town's rednecks. Notable episodes: S03E05.

Thomas Turner — Heidi Turner's father, a very muscular and stereotypically over-protective dad who keeps his daughter out of trouble. Three different versions of him appeared in Probably, Two Days Before the Day After Tomorrow, and Marjorine. Notable episodes: S04E10, S09E08, S09E09, S24E01.
Thomas' Mother — Thomas's mother, first appearing in Le Petit Tourette alongside her son. Notable episodes: S11E08.
Thompson — An old man who owns the Garden of Betrayal, first appearing through the Season Seventeen Black Friday trilogy. Notable episodes: S17E07, S17E08, S17E09, S24E02.
Thompson (Pandemic) — An interpreter who appears in Pandemic. Notable episodes: S12E10.
Thor — Thor Odinson, the Marvel character starring in several Marvel Cinematic Universe films, appearing in Band in China. Notable episodes: S23E02.
Thumper — A skiing instructor who appears in Asspen. Notable episodes: S06E02.
Thumper (Cat) — Bebe Stevens' pet cat, first mentioned in Bebe's Boobs Destroy Society and first seen in Major Boobage. Notable episodes: S06E02, S06E10, S12E03.
Tiger Woods — Eldrick Tont Tiger Woods, the professional golfer and World Golf Hall of Fame inductee, appearing in Sexual Healing. Notable episodes: S14E01.

Tim Burton — Timothy Walter Tim Burton, the famous movie director, featured in 200 as one of the celebrities in the class-action lawsuit against South Park after Tom Cruise is called a fudge packer. He is mocked for casting Johnny Depp in all his lead roles and for using the same crappy music in his films. Notable episodes: S14E05.
Tim Cook — The American businessman and CEO of Apple Inc., appearing in Sickofancy. Notable episodes: S27E03.

Timmy Burch — Timothy Timmy Burch, a male fourth-grader at South Park Elementary who debuts in The Tooth Fairy Tats 2000. Handicapped and using a wheelchair, he has a limited vocabulary of mostly his own name and a few phrases. His full name is revealed in T.M.I. on a poster of the kids' growth differentials. Notable episodes: S04E01, S15E04.
Timothy Neely — A professional thief who appears in About Last Night... Notable episodes: S12E12.
Tina Yothers — The former child actress and musician best known as Jennifer Keaton on Family Ties, appearing in the Season One Halloween episode Pinkeye. Notable episodes: S01E07.
Tinkerbell — Paris Hilton's pet chihuahua, making her only appearance in Stupid Spoiled Whore Video Playset. Notable episodes: S08E12.
Tiny Miss Pageant Judges — The judges of the Tiny Miss Pageant in Dead Celebrities. Notable episodes: S13E08.

Tiny Tim — Herbert Butros Khaury, known professionally as Tiny Tim, the American musician, songwriter, and musical archivist, appearing as a resident of Hell in Do the Handicapped Go to Hell? Notable episodes: S04E09.
Todd — A budtender in Medicinal Fried Chicken who appears in The Fractured But Whole. Notable episodes: S14E03, S25E01.
Todd Palin — The ex-husband of Sarah Palin who served as Alaska's First Gentleman from 2006 to 2009, appearing in About Last Night... Notable episodes: S12E12.

Toilet Safety Administration — The TSA, a fictional government agency parodying the Transportation Security Administration, seen in Reverse Cowgirl providing excessive security around every toilet. Notable episodes: S16E01.

Tolkien Black — A male fourth grader at South Park Elementary, formerly known as Token Black and Token Williams. In The Big Fix his real name is revealed to be Tolkien, named after the writer J.R.R. Tolkien. Notable episodes: S01E01, S03E05, S09E03, S13E10, S25E02.

Tom (Ike's Wee Wee) — A local journalist and the father of Kevin, the boy thawed from ice in Summer Sucks. He reappears in Helen Keller! The Musical, explaining to his son how his mother died, and is spotted in the movie while Stan sings his way through town. Notable episodes: S02E03, S02E08, S02E13, S03E10, S04E13.

Tom (Newsman) — A news anchor and reporter for Channel 4 News, first seen in Pinewood Derby covering an alien ship preparing to land. He was the primary anchor from Season Twenty-Two to Season Twenty-Four and still appears as a field reporter. Notable episodes: S13E06.
Tom and Mary — A married couple who appear in Cow Days. Notable episodes: S02E13.
Tom Brady — The Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback who has made a few appearances on the show. Notable episodes: S16E03, S17E05.
Tom Brady Publicist — Tom Brady's publicist, appearing in Turd Burglars. Notable episodes: S23E08.

Tom Cruise — Thomas Tom Cruise Mapother IV, the Hollywood actor and vocal supporter of the Church of Scientology. He is the focus, along with Scientology, of Trapped in the Closet, and the lead celebrity suing South Park in 200 and 201. Notable episodes: S09E12, S14E05, S14E06, S14E11.
Tom Davis — A character from You Have 0 Friends. Notable episodes: S14E04.
Tom Foley — The dentist who confronts Loogie in The Tooth Fairy Tats 2000. Notable episodes: S04E01.

Tom Green — The Canadian actor and comedian known for the shock comedy of his MTV series The Tom Green Show and films like Freddie Got Fingered. He appears in Fat Camp, being interviewed by Howard Stern alongside Kenny McCormick and Johnny Knoxville, with whom he bids low to give Howard a hummer. Notable episodes: S04E15.
Tom Hanks — Thomas Jeffrey Hanks, the American actor and filmmaker who has made a few South Park appearances, starting with Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls. Notable episodes: S02E09.
Tom Hardy — The English actor who appears in Insheeption as Eames, his character from Inception. Notable episodes: S14E10.
Tom Johannsen — An ice cream and candy shop owner who appears in Cartman's Incredible Gift. Notable episodes: S08E13.
Tom Nelson — Better known as Bat Dad, a trash-talking parent in The Losing Edge. Notable episodes: S09E05.

Tom Pusslicker — A news anchor who served as the main Channel 4 News television anchor and reporter for the first ten seasons, often seen covering large-scale bizarre events; episodes' news reports would sometimes follow the tail end of an unheard story about Hillary Clinton's ass. He stopped reporting after Season Eleven, replaced by other anchors, but briefly returns in Sponsored Content as one of the former anchors introducing Jimmy Valmer to Leslie Meyers. Notable episodes: S01E03, S19E08.

Tom Shane — The president and spokesperson for The Shane Company, a Colorado fine jewelry retailer, seen as a local celebrity at Charles Kincade's party in Guitar Queer-O alongside Jay Cutler and Jake Jabs. Notable episodes: S11E13.

Tom Thompson — Channel 4 News' former lead television reporter and anchor. Starting in Season Thirteen he takes over from Tom Pusslicker as the town's top anchor, still doing field reporting at times. Notable episodes: S12E02.

Tom Vilsack — The U.S. Secretary of Agriculture and head of the USDA, who appears in Gluten Free Ebola leading the effort to solve the anti-gluten panic in America sparked by South Park. Notable episodes: S18E02.

Tommy (Faith Hilling) — This teen debuts in Faith Hilling via the short Bloody Sunday: The Dangers of Memeing: with his car parked on train tracks, he scrambles to photograph his girlfriend's Tebowing as a train closes in, and it plows through her and the car. He is later spotted in the crowd in The Scoots. Notable episodes: S16E03, S22E05.
Tommy (Medicinal Fried Chicken) — A Kentucky Fried Chicken dealer working under Billy Miller in Medicinal Fried Chicken. Notable episodes: S14E03.
Tommy Edwards — A student at South Park Elementary who appears in Bass to Mouth. Notable episodes: S15E10.

Tommy Fritz — A boy seen briefly in Roger Ebert Should Lay off the Fatty Foods, singing the Cheesy Poofs Theme Song for the Cheesy Poofs Talent Ship; though praised, he is not made a finalist. Notable episodes: S02E11.
Tommy Turner — Also known as Petey, a student at South Park Elementary who first appears in The Succubus. Notable episodes: S03E03.

Tommy's Girlfriend — A teenager who first appears in Faith Hilling in the short film Bloody Sunday: The Dangers of Memeing: parked on train tracks with Tommy, she asks him to photograph her Tebowing, and the train runs over her and his car as he panics. She later appears among the crowd in The Scoots. Notable episodes: S16E03, S22E05.
Tony — A character seen in Fat Camp. Notable episodes: S04E15.
Tony (Cartman Joins NAMBLA) — Also known online as Tony316, a pedophile who meets with Eric Cartman in Cartman Joins NAMBLA. Notable episodes: S04E05.
Tony and Toby — Male nurses for the Shady Acres retirement home, seen in Hummels & Heroin and Post Covid: The Return of Covid. Notable episodes: S21E05, S28E05.
Tony Bennett — Anthony Dominick Benedetto, known professionally as Tony Bennett, the American singer known for Because of You and I Left My Heart in San Francisco, appearing in #HappyHolograms.
Tony Danza — The actor best known for the long-running 80s-90s sitcom Who's the Boss?, seen in Rainforest Shmainforest. Notable episodes: S03E01.

Tony Hayward — The president of BP (later DP), appearing in Coon 2: Hindsight and Mysterion Rises. He bears much of the blame for the Gulf of Mexico oil spill and the resulting leak of other-dimensional creatures including Cthulhu, and his string of apology videos grows increasingly, disturbingly erotic. Notable episodes: S14E11, S14E12.
Tony Kornheiser — Anthony Irwin Kornheiser, the American television sports talk show host, appearing in Poor and Stupid. Notable episodes: S14E08.

Tony Orlando and Dawn — The 1970s American pop group of singer Tony Orlando and backing vocalists Dawn (Telma Hopkins and Joyce Vincent Wilson), appearing briefly in a photo with Terrance and Phillip in Terrance and Phillip: Behind the Blow. Notable episodes: S05E05.
Tony Stewart — Anthony Wayne Stewart, the American professional racing driver, appearing in Poor and Stupid. Notable episodes: S14E08.
Tony the Tiger — Frosted Flakes' mascot, seen in South Park: The End of Obesity.
Toolshed — An original member of Coon and Friends who debuts in Coon 2: Hindsight. Named after an actual tool shed, referencing his tool-based powers and attire. Notable episodes: S14E11.
Tooth Decay — A monstrous beast and the main antagonist of Royal Pudding, a monstrous personification of tooth decay, the breakdown of teeth by bacterial acids. Notable episodes: S15E03.
Topher — He studies at the University of Massachusetts and belongs to the PC Bros, debuting in Stunning and Brave. Notable episodes: S19E01.
Toto — The American rock band, styled TOTO, that appears in Gnomes. Notable episodes: S02E17.

Totoro — The title character of the Japanese animated film My Neighbor Totoro. He first appears in the Imaginationland trilogy on the good side of the battle, and later in Sora Not Sorry. Notable episodes: S28E03.
Tourette's Tolerance and Understanding Foundation — A support group for people with Tourette's syndrome, seen in Le Petit Tourette. Notable episodes: S11E08.

Towelie (Character) — A talking towel genetically engineered by Tynacorp to dry people as situations require, debuting in the episode Towelie. He pops up out of nowhere to dispense towel advice, gets high often (the Popeye theme plays whenever he does), is a friend of Randy Marsh, and served as the agricultural inspector for Tegridy Farms. Notable episodes: S05E08, S06E06, S14E03, S22E04, S28E05.
Townsfolk — South Park's assorted residents, mostly background filler — yet at least one gets a line in most episodes. Notable episodes: S01E02.
Trashman — A South Park worker who appears only briefly in Jakovasaurs. Notable episodes: S03E04.
Travis Mayfield — A head louse who lives in Clyde's hair in Lice Capades. Notable episodes: S11E03.
Trent Boyett — A bully and former preschool classmate of the boys, the main antagonist of Pre-School. Notable episodes: S08E10.
Trevor — A teenager and airsoft player who appears in Help, My Teenager Hates Me! Notable episodes: S25E05.
Trevor's Mother — Trevor's mother, appearing in Help, My Teenager Hates Me! Notable episodes: S25E05.
Tricia Tucker — The daughter of Thomas and Laura Tucker and Craig Tucker's younger sister, first appearing in Tweek vs. Craig. Notable episodes: S03E05, S12E03.
Trinity — A religious-based band that appears in Christian Rock Hard. Notable episodes: S07E09.
Trix Rabbit — Trix cereal's mascot, seen in South Park: The End of Obesity.
Tron Guy — Jay Maynard, also known as the Tron Guy, the American computer programmer and internet celebrity, appearing in Canada on Strike. Notable episodes: S12E04.

True Freaks Union — An organization of people born as or accidentally become freaks, seen in Freak Strike singing a same-named song in a public service video parodying the real ILGWU PSA. Notable episodes: S06E03.
Tucker Rae — Tucker Cleetus Rae, an anti-Alexa protester in the Season Twenty-One premiere White People Renovating Houses. Notable episodes: S21E01.
Tugger — The nickname of Russell Crowe's tugboat, seen in The New Terrance and Phillip Movie Trailer. Notable episodes: S06E05.

Tuong Lu Kim — An alter ego of Dr. William Janus and owner of the City Wok restaurant and City Airlines, whose stereotypical Chinese accent turns city into shitty. He debuts in Jared Has Aides and stays recurring; his true identity is only revealed in City Sushi. Notable episodes: S06E01, S15E06.

Tupac Shakur Hologram — The late rapper 2Pac, rendered by the Syntech Hologram Company in #REHASH to hunt the escaped Michael Jackson hologram; he also beds Sharon Marsh. Come #HappyHolograms, he strolls into the Park County Police Station, joins forces with Michael Jackson, and helps murder the Record Producer.
Tupperware — An original member of Coon and Friends, debuting in Coon 2: Hindsight. Notable episodes: S14E11.

Turd Sandwich — One of the candidates for South Park Elementary's school mascot, running against Giant Douche in Douche and Turd. Cartman invents the Turd Sandwich idea to oppose Kyle's Giant Douche. The Douche and Turd concept returns in Member Berries, where Garrison is the Giant Douche and Hillary Clinton the Turd Sandwich, and the Turd Sandwich loses. Notable episodes: S08E08, S20E01.
Tutornon — A private tutoring organization founded by Bob White and staffed by QAnon members as tutors, featured in the South ParQ Vaccination Special. Notable episodes: S24E02.

Tweek Tweak — A fourth-grade student at South Park Elementary who drinks lots of coffee, laced with meth, leaving him paranoid with jittery muscle spasms. He debuts in Gnomes. Notable episodes: S02E17.
Tween Wave Fans — Fans of the Tween Wave music genre who appear in You're Getting Old. Notable episodes: S15E07.
Twinkie the Kid — The Twinkies snack cake's mascot, seen in South Park: The End of Obesity.
Two Astronauts — Two unnamed men who appear in Bebe's Boobs Destroy Society. Notable episodes: S06E10.
Two Farmers — Two rednecks who constantly gripe about new trends, working as janitors, ranchers, and more. Notable episodes: S15E07, S23E06.

Tyler Perry — The American actor, director, producer, and screenwriter best known for creating and playing Mabel Madea Simmons in the Madea films and shows like Tyler Perry's House of Payne. He appears in Funnybot. Notable episodes: S15E02.
U2 — The Irish rock band that appears in #HappyHolograms.
Ugly Bob — A Canadian who debuts in Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus. Hideously ugly, he wears a paper bag over his face at all times. Notable episodes: S02E01.
Uncle Sam — The personification of the United States government, seen briefly in a newsreel recruiting American soldiers for the American-Canadian War in South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut.

Uncle Stinky — Stinky Cartman, a member of Cartman's family introduced in Merry Christmas Charlie Manson!. He is the father of Elvin and Alexandra, the husband of Lisa Cartman, and the uncle of Eric and Fred, as well as the brother of Liane and Howard. Notable episodes: S02E16, S05E06.
Underpants Gnomes — Small humanoid creatures that travel the world stealing underpants, first appearing in Gnomes. Notable episodes: S02E17.
Unified Atheist League (UAL) — The UAL: a mid-21st-century organization from an alternate timeline. Notable episodes: S10E12.

United Atheist Alliance (UAA) — The UAA: a mid-21st-century organization from an alternate timeline whose members insist their answer to what atheists should call themselves beats the rival groups'. Cartman mostly sides with the Alliance even though the Unified Atheist League unfroze him and he spends off-screen time with the Allied Atheist Alliance. Notable episodes: S10E12.

United Nations — The UN, the real-life international organization founded October 24, 1945 to keep peace and security between nations. It appears several times in South Park, first in the film South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut.

United States Border Patrol — The U.S.B.P., the federal law enforcement agency tasked with stopping illegal aliens and terrorists and preventing trafficking of contraband and people. Their only major role is in The Last of the Meheecans. Notable episodes: S15E09.
Unplanned Parenthood Counselor — A counselor who appears in Cartman's Mom is Still a Dirty Slut. Notable episodes: S02E02.
Van Gelder — A volunteer worker for the Tantalus V. Observatory in Roger Ebert Should Lay off the Fatty Foods. Notable episodes: S02E11.
Van Halen — The American hard rock band formed in the mid-1970s and active until Eddie Van Halen's death in 2020, seen in Ginger Cow. Notable episodes: S17E06.
Vanessa — A woman who appears in Freak Strike as the mother of the out-of-control teen Vanity. Notable episodes: S06E03.
Vanity — This supposedly out-of-control teen appears on Maury Povich's show in Freak Strike. Notable episodes: S06E03.
Vanna White — The co-host of Wheel of Fortune, appearing in With Apologies to Jesse Jackson. Notable episodes: S11E01.
Varashnu — An employee at Wolf Home Security seen in Insecurity. Notable episodes: S16E10.

Vernon Trumski — An overweight child resembling Cartman in looks and behavior, even bossing around his mother. He somehow comes to possess Lemmiwinks after the creature escapes Mr. Slave's rectum; the boys take Lemmiwinks from him to stop Wikileaks in Bass to Mouth. Notable episodes: S15E10.
Veronica — Chef's former girlfriend and fiancee, revealed to be a succubus, a demon that visits dreams in the form of a woman to seduce men, in The Succubus. Notable episodes: S03E03.
Veronica Crabtree — Ms. Veronica Crabtree, South Park Elementary's main bus driver until her death in Season Eight. Notable episodes: S01E01, S08E13.
Vice President Greg — A louse living in Clyde's hair in Lice Capades, serving as the episode's main antagonist. Notable episodes: S11E03.
Vin Diesel — The actor who appears in Safe Space. Notable episodes: S19E05.
Vince McMahon — The American businessman and former pro wrestling promoter, Chairman and CEO of WWE from 1982 until his 2022 retirement, seen briefly in W.T.F. Notable episodes: S13E10.
VIP Johns — During The Bowels of the Beast mission in The Fractured But Whole, players meet Brad and Roger — two drunks collectively called the VIP Johns.

Visitors — The aliens who give Eric Cartman an anal probe in the pilot Cartman Gets an Anal Probe and kidnap Ike Broflovski in the same episode. After observing Earth, they conclude cows are the planet's most intelligent species. Notable episodes: S01E01.
Vladimir — A male fourth grader who first appears in The Ungroundable as a member of the South Park Vampire Society. Notable episodes: S12E14.

Vladimir Putin — The incumbent President of Russia, leading the country since 1999, known for his adversarial stance toward the United States and authoritarianism. He first appears in Free Willzyx. Notable episodes: S09E13.

Vladimir Stolfsky — The British Royal family hires this Russian terrorist to pull America's attention elsewhere while the UK invades to reclaim its former colonies; he appears in The Snuke. Notable episodes: S11E04.
Volleyball Girls — First seen in Cock Magic, these female South Park Elementary students have popped up in later episodes too. Notable episodes: S18E08.
Vosky — A member of the Burger King Bandits who appears in Super Fun Time. Notable episodes: S12E07.
Walgreens Pharmacist — A healthcare worker for Walgreens who appears in the South ParQ Vaccination Special. Notable episodes: S24E02.

Wall-Mart — The superstore that acts as the main antagonist of Something Wall-Mart This Way Comes and returns in Raising the Bar. It sells virtually everything, using bulk purchasing to create bargains nobody can resist. Notable episodes: S08E09, S16E09.
Walter Cronkite — The famous American CBS anchorman, appearing in purgatory in Dead Celebrities. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Walter Matthau — This American actor often teamed with Jack Lemmon for comedies like The Odd Couple and Grumpy Old Men. He resides in Hell in Do the Handicapped Go to Hell? Notable episodes: S04E09.
Wario — The Mario franchise character and star of his own series, featured in the Imaginationland trilogy as an antagonist on the villains' side, prominent in the battle of Imaginationland.
Washcloth — Towelie and Rebecca's son, making his first and only appearance in Crippled Summer. Notable episodes: S05E08, S14E07.
Washington Dodgeball Players — A group of dodgeball players who appear in Conjoined Fetus Lady. Notable episodes: S02E05.
Water Bears — Tardigrades, also called moss piglets, water-dwelling micro-animals among the hardiest creatures on Earth, surviving the vacuum of space and high radiation. Notable episodes: S21E08.
Water Commissioner — An agent of the Colorado Division of Water Resources, appearing in South Park: The Streaming Wars.

Wayne D — A character in T.M.I., a stereotypical white guy acting like a stereotypical black guy; he also appears as one of the mall security guards in the Black Friday trilogy. Notable episodes: S15E04, S17E07, S24E02.
Weasel — A character in the Season Four premiere The Tooth Fairy Tats 2000. Notable episodes: S04E01.
Weatherhead Kids — A group of foster children who appear in The Poor Kid. Notable episodes: S15E14.
Weathers — A USAF officer who appears in PC Principal Final Justice. Notable episodes: S19E10.
Ween — The American experimental rock band that appears in Chef Aid, playing the concert to help Chef pay his legal bills. Notable episodes: S02E14.
Wellington Bear — The commercial and promotional mascot for Snacky Cakes and many other items owned by Eric Cartman across the series. Notable episodes: S01E06.

Wendy Testaburger — A major supporting character and the most prominent female on South Park. She is the leading girl among Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny's classmates, a fourth-grader at South Park Elementary, and Stan's on-and-off girlfriend. She debuts with her first speaking role in Cartman Gets an Anal Probe. Notable episodes: S01E01, S01E07.
Wendy Williams — The American retired talk show host, actress, and author best known for her radio shock-jock career and The Wendy Williams Show, appearing in #REHASH.
Whistlin' Willy (Mascot) — The mascot for Whistlin' Willy's, first seen in Quest for Ratings. Notable episodes: S08E11.
White House Artist — An artist who appears in Sermon on the Mount. Notable episodes: S27E01.
Whole Foods Representative — A representative of the Whole Foods Market, appearing in The City Part of Town. Notable episodes: S19E03.

Whoopi Goldberg — The comedienne, actress, and talk show host known for The Color Purple, Ghost, and Sister Act, and for playing Guinan on Star Trek. She appears in Spontaneous Combustion as the host of the Nobel Prize Awards ceremony. Notable episodes: S03E02.
Wieners Out (Movement) — A movement founded by Butters Stotch in the episode Wieners Out. Notable episodes: S20E04.
Wikileaks — A rat who serves as the main antagonist of Bass to Mouth. Notable episodes: S15E10.
Wild Dogs — Wild animals in The Stick of Truth, usually found in the Lost Forest.
Will Barton — William Denard Barton III, the professional basketball player for the Denver Nuggets, appearing in Band in China. Notable episodes: S23E02.

Will Smith — Willard Carroll Will Smith II, the American actor, rapper, and film producer known for The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, Independence Day, and Men in Black, and for songs like Summertime and Gettin' Jiggy wit It. He first appears with his wife Jada Pinkett Smith in Here Comes the Neighborhood. Notable episodes: S05E12.
William Daniels — Nichole's father, first appearing in Cartman Finds Love. Notable episodes: S16E07.
William Janus — Dr. William Janus counsels patients as a therapist in City Sushi — and secretly runs the City Wok as Tuong Lu Kim. Notable episodes: S15E06.

William P. Connelly — William P. Connelly, Esquire, the leader of the Super Adventure Club and the main antagonist of The Return of Chef. Despite his menace, he prefers having security guards escort people off his property to hurting them; like every club member, he is a child molester. Notable episodes: S10E01.
William P. Phineas — An adventurer and the founder of the pedophilic Super Adventure Club, appearing in The Return of Chef. Notable episodes: S10E01.
William Shatner — Star Trek's Captain Kirk. Spookyfish name-drops him first; he later shows up on Family Guy in Cartoon Wars Part I. Notable episodes: S02E15, S10E03.

Wilson Aubry — A first-grader at South Park Elementary in Franchise Prequel. Coon and Friends visit him to help, but he turns them down, believing they did all the horrible things Professor Chaos accused them of on Facebook. Notable episodes: S06E06, S21E04.
Wing Han Tsang — A New Zealand singer born in Hong Kong, appearing in Wing as the wife of Tuong Lu Kim. Notable episodes: S09E03, S27E04.

Winnie the Pooh — The fictional character from the 1926 book, appearing in Band in China, where Randy kills him after he is released from Chinese prison. He returns in the Tegridy Farms Halloween Special as a zombie trying to kill Randy for revenge, though Randy is hallucinating at the time. Notable episodes: S23E02, S23E05.
Winona Ryder — Winona Laura Horowitz, better known as Winona Ryder, the American actress most famous for Beetlejuice, Stranger Things, Heathers, Edward Scissorhands, and Girl, Interrupted.
Wolf Blitzer — The CNN reporter who appears in Obama Wins! Notable episodes: S16E14.

Wolf Home Security — A business in Insecurity selling security packages that automatically alert an operator during emergencies like burglaries. Cartman hires them to guard against the UPS delivery man, an apparent mass rapist. Notable episodes: S16E10.
Women With Fake Titties — A group of women who have undergone artificial breast implants, appearing in South Park: The Streaming Wars Part 2.
Wonder Tweek — The superhero alter ego of Tweek Tweak, debuting in Franchise Prequel. Notable episodes: S21E04.
Wonder Woman — This DC superheroine sits on the Council of Nine in the Imaginationland trilogy.

Woodland Critters — Deceptively cute but truly evil Satanic animals who commit ritual sacrifice and acts of physical, psychological, and sexual violence. Though they celebrate Christmas, they worship Satan and await the birth of the Anti-Christ; they dote on Stan Marsh, calling him Stanny. Eric Cartman originally invented them for his story in Woodland Critter Christmas, and they are treated as imaginary until they manifest in reality. Notable episodes: S08E14, S28E05.

Yamal — A South Park Elementary student in The List, part of the group of ugly kids. Notable episodes: S11E14.

Yasmine Bleeth — The Baywatch actress, hand-picked by Mr. Garrison to view IT in The Entity. Notable episodes: S05E11.

Yukio Hatoyama — The Japanese politician who formerly served as prime minister of Japan, appearing in Whale Whores. Notable episodes: S13E11.
Yvonne Finnerty — One of the nannies on the TV show Nanny 911 in Tsst who attempt to fix Eric Cartman's behavior. Notable episodes: S10E07.

American Dental Association — The ADA's headquarters building in Chicago. Notable episodes: S04E01.

Stan and Kyle usually stand side by side, Kenny at the far right, Cartman nearest the sign, though the lineup shifts from episode to episode. It is the show's most iconic location — the four kids at the sign is so recognizable that the boys themselves use it to audition a replacement fourth friend. The stop anchored many scenes through the first nine seasons before school hallways and cafeterias took over; by the Streaming Wars, Kyle and Kenny alone still line up there. Notable episodes: S01E01 (series premiere debut), S06E06 (auditioning a new fourth friend), SPECIAL (Streaming Wars return).

EvGames — A video game store in the South Park Mall, parodying EB Games. Notable episodes: S10E12, S17E09.
Ewok Village 2000 — Cartman and Kenny's clubhouse in Cartman's backyard. Notable episodes: S02E12.
Excalibur — A casino in Las Vegas, Nevada. Notable episodes: S05E01.
F.E. Warren Missile Base — A military base in Cheyenne, Wyoming. Notable episodes: S15E02.
Faith Records — A music record studio. Notable episodes: S07E09.
Family Medical — A clinic.
Farnickle Residence — The home of Mrs. and Mr. Farnickle. Notable episodes: S07E06, S09E02.
Farty O'Cool's Irish Pub — An Irish pub in South Park. Notable episodes: S25E06.

Federation of Planets — A benevolent interstellar federation governing many species and worlds. New species become eligible to join upon discovering warp speed, but must pass the "space money test": those who pocket the space cash get sealed off from the universe in a force field around their homeworld. Randy Marsh stumbles into warp speed using a stolen Swiss particle accelerator in Stan's pinewood derby car, drawing the Federation's attention. Notable episodes: S13E06.
FedEx Office — A Federal Express office and print-services shop. Notable episodes: S15E04.
Feed The Children Foundation — A charitable organization operating in Ethiopia. Notable episodes: S03E13.
Feegan Residence — The Feegan family house, where Stan and Shelly Marsh stay for a weekend while their parents are in New York. Notable episodes: S15E11.
Finland — A country that accepted the space cash. Notable episodes: S13E06.
First Lady's Symposium on Obesity — An obesity symposium presented by Michelle Obama. Notable episodes: S16E09.
First National Bank of Chicago — A bank branch in Chicago, Illinois. Notable episodes: S10E05.
Flex Gym Fitness Club — A public gymnasium in South Park. Notable episodes: S06E01.
Food 4 Little — A local grocery store in South Park. Notable episodes: S12E05.
Fort Collins — A Colorado city in Larimer County, 65 miles from Denver, featured prominently in a Season 20 arc. Notable episodes: S05E04, S20E06, S20E07.
Fort Collins Hotel — A hotel in Fort Collins, labeled "Ft. Collins Hotel". Notable episodes: S05E04, S20E06.
Fort Sumter — A historic sea fort in Charleston, South Carolina. Notable episodes: S03E14.
Fortress of Tooth Decay — A large castle used as the base of the monster Tooth Decay. Notable episodes: S15E03.
Fountains of Varnov — An imaginary pool visited by people while "cheesing". Notable episodes: S12E03.
Fran's National Bank — A drive-thru bank in South Park, seen once. Notable episodes: S02E04.

France — A Western European country. Episodes featuring it usually show the Eiffel Tower in Paris with a little restaurant called "Café Grenouille" in front; kids also tease Pip for supposedly being French. Notable episodes: S03E04, S26E02.
Freedom Pals HQ — The Freedom Pals faction's home base, in Tolkien's basement.
Freeman's Tacos — A Mexican restaurant run by Morgan Freeman.
Freemont Bridge — A bridge in or near South Park, Colorado. Notable episodes: S11E02.
Frisco Woods — A Colorado state park where Mr. Mackey took his class on a childhood field trip. Notable episodes: S14E10.
Gamecraft Arcade — An arcade in South Park. Notable episodes: S11E13.

Garden of Betrayal — A garden Wizard Cartman calls "the Garden of Andros," running through the Season 17 Black Friday arc as a Game of Thrones-style spot for plotting betrayals. Notable episodes: S17E07, S17E08, S17E09.
Garrison & Son Gas Station — A gas station. Notable episodes: S03E17.
Garrison Residence — Herbert Garrison's home; the interior changes often while the exterior stays consistent. Notable episodes: S01E02.
Garrison Senior Residence — Mr. Garrison Senior and his wife's Arkansas home, probably Herbert Garrison's childhood home. Notable episodes: S03E17.
Gems Wholesale — A jewelry store. Notable episodes: S16E02.
General Store — A general-purpose shop on South Park's main street, a plain brown building with two windows. Notable episodes: S03E02.
Germany — A Central European country. Notable episodes: S13E06.
Get Cable Company — The Park County cable TV provider, later renamed Park County Cable. Notable episodes: S17E02, S23E09.
Girls' Stronghold — A one-off location. Notable episodes: S05E07.
Government Desalinization Plant — A desalination plant run by the US Geological Survey. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Gramercy Lanes — A fairly standard but dilapidated, dirty bowling alley with a bar and arcade cabinets. Notable episodes: S22E06.
Great Cuts — A barbershop in South Park, seen once. Notable episodes: S23E09.
Great Hall of the People — A Chinese government building in Beijing. Notable episodes: S23E02, S24E01.
Greeley — A Colorado city where the Weatherheads foster Kenny, Kevin, Karen McCormick, and Eric Cartman. Notable episodes: S09E05, S15E14.

Greeley Elementary — An elementary school in Greeley, Colorado, attended by Cartman and the McCormick kids while in foster care; the students are friendly and the faculty enforces a strict no-bullying policy. Notable episodes: S15E14.
Green Bay — A city in Wisconsin. Notable episodes: S02E08.
Grocery Mart — A supermarket. Notable episodes: S09E08.
Gueermo Residence — Where the Gueermo family lives. Notable episodes: S12E13.
Guinness Book of World Records — The record-keeping organization's office. Notable episodes: S11E09.
Gulf of Mexico — The body of water off Mexico and the southern US coast. Notable episodes: S14E11, S14E13.
Hagen Residence — The Hagen family's house. Notable episodes: S17E02.
Hakeem Residence — The house where the Hakeem family briefly lived. Notable episodes: S11E04.
Hall of Super Best Friends — The headquarters of the Super Best Friends. Notable episodes: S05E03, S14E06.
Halloween Outlet — A South Park store selling costumes and Halloween goods. Notable episodes: S22E03.
Hankey Residence — The Hankey family home in the sewers beneath South Park. Notable episodes: S04E17.
Happy Burger — A burger restaurant. Notable episodes: S01E02.
Haps Bar — A bar in Nebraska. Notable episodes: S02E03.
Harbor Hospital — A medical center. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Harbucks — A coffee shop franchise with a South Park branch; despite being a corporation, its coffee is very good. Parodies Starbucks. Notable episodes: S02E17.
Harequin Romance Book Publishing — A publishing house for romance books. Notable episodes: S04E06.
Harris Residence — The home of Martin Harris and his wife. Notable episodes: S07E12.
Harrison Residence — The home of the Harrison family, seen once. Notable episodes: S07E12.
Havisham Estate — The UK home of Miss Havisham and Estella Havisham, known in Great Expectations as Satis House. Notable episodes: S04E14.
Hawaii — The 50th US state; Butters turns out to be a Kauai native. Notable episodes: S16E11.
Heartbreak Falls — A miniature waterfall in the South Park wilderness. Notable episodes: S16E06.

Heaven — The afterlife where God lives. It once admitted only Mormons, but opened its gates wider to build an army for a coming war. Kenny has been there at least twice, and Saddam Hussein took up residence there for a time, even developing chemical weapons until he left to take over Canada. Notable episodes: MOVIE, S09E04, S04E10, S06E12.

Hell — The afterlife ruled by Satan, where nearly everyone ends up. It is nothing like the traditional fiery torment: Satan is a laid-back, fun-loving ruler who throws Christmas parties and luaus, and the damned build homes, eat, and run businesses — dying in Hell just means waking up the next day, as Saddam Hussein and Chris learned fighting over Satan. Notable episodes: S02E06 (first proper look), S13E08, MOVIE, S09E04.
Hell's Pass Hospital — South Park's main hospital, with several doctors and nurses. Notable episodes: S02E02.

Henrietta's Bedroom — Inside the Biggle Residence, the Goth Kids' main hangout: a fading dark-blue room decked out with skulls, crucifixes, melting red candles, band posters, and scattered books, where they sit in the dark listening to music, smoking, writing poems about pain, and dabbling in the occult. It later fills with Cthulhu posters and gets a redesign when Henrietta goes emo. Notable episodes: S07E14, S14E13, S17E04.
Henry's Supermarket — A local supermarket in South Park. Notable episodes: S04E07.
Hillvale Farm — A fruit and vegetable farm run by the Old Farmer, seen once. Notable episodes: S20E03.
Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum — A Japanese museum documenting the WWII atomic bombing of Hiroshima, seen once. Notable episodes: S13E11.
Ho-Tel — A hotel in South Park's red-light district, seen once. Notable episodes: S09E07.
Hoffman and Turk Law Offices — A law firm specializing in suing the dead. Notable episodes: S16E01.
Holiday Inn — A hotel chain. Notable episodes: SPECIAL, S13E08.
Holiday Inn Select — A hotel brand; one appears in the city of Lynchburg. Notable episodes: S13E08.
Hollywood Planet — A South Park restaurant opened by Robert Redford. Notable episodes: S02E09.
Hooters — An American restaurant chain. Notable episodes: S15E11.
Hopeful Hills — A camp for overweight kids. Notable episodes: S04E15.
Horse Stables — Stables in the South Park wilderness. Notable episodes: S16E06.
Hot Topic — A store. Notable episodes: S12E14.
I Am Siam Thai Cuisine — A Thai restaurant. Notable episodes: S05E14.
ICE Detention Center — Where ICE detains immigrant kids. Notable episodes: S23E01.
ICE Recruitment Center — An office branch of Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Notable episodes: S27E02.
Ichi Ban Karate Dojo — A Japanese martial arts training center. Notable episodes: S09E14.
Imaginationland — Another dimension, reachable only with the "Imagination Song". Notable episodes: S11E12.
Incredible Meats — A company and factory making "goo" as a meat substitute. Notable episodes: S23E04.
Independence Hall — The historic Philadelphia building the Philadelphia hall where America's founding documents were adopted. Notable episodes: S07E04, S14E01.
Indi — A planet. Notable episodes: S15E13.
India — A South Asian country. Notable episodes: S02E03.
India Manufacturing Inc. — A factory. Notable episodes: S16E02.
Indian Burial Ground — A burial ground first seen in Season 2. Notable episodes: S02E15.
Indian Burial Ground Pet Store — A South Park pet store selling evil animals; Flo Kimble purchases a fish for Stan there. Notable episodes: S02E15.
International House of Pancakes — The IHOP restaurant chain. Notable episodes: S16E01.
Internet Refugee Camp — A temporary refugee camp just outside Silicon Valley, California. Notable episodes: S12E06.
Iran — A Middle Eastern country; its residents were first drawn like Canadians because of the episode's focus, later redesigned to match other characters. Notable episodes: S02E01, S11E06, S17E06.
Iraq — A Western Asian republic, mostly known through Saddam Hussein, its former leader, who appears across several episodes and the film. Notable episodes: S01E11, S06E17, MOVIE.
Island of Misfit Mascots — A rehabilitation camp for mascots. Notable episodes: S03E06.
Israel — A Middle Eastern country, homeland of the Jews and of Jesus. Notable episodes: S17E06.
IT Dealership — Herbert Garrison's dealership for the IT vehicle he invented. Notable episodes: S05E11.

Italy — A Southern European country; Father Maxi is seen arriving by taxi in Rome against the Colosseum, and a presidential palace is destroyed there in another episode. Notable episodes: S06E08, S13E06.
J-Mart — A South Park department store popular with lower-income families, shunned by the well-off. Notable episodes: S05E11.
J. Brown Elementary School — An elementary school. Notable episodes: S12E03.
J. Prewitt Law Office — A law firm Mr. Hankey visits. Notable episodes: S22E03.
Jakov Residence — Where Jakov and his family live. Notable episodes: S03E04.
Jamba — A restaurant chain serving juices and smoothies. Notable episodes: S29E01.
Janus Residence — William Janus's mansion. Notable episodes: S15E06.
Japan — An East Asian island nation of four main islands, neighboring China and the Koreas. Notable episodes: S03E11.
Jared: The Galleria Of Jewelry — A jewelry store chain. Notable episodes: S22E07.
Jefferson Lake Recreation Area — A recreational area along Beaverton Lake. Notable episodes: S09E08.
Jefferson Residence — Michael Jackson (as Michael Jefferson) and his son Blanket's home; the Donovan family previously lived there. Notable episodes: S08E06.
Jerusalem — The capital of Israel, sacred to Jews since Biblical times and holy to Christians through Jesus' time there. Notable episodes: S17E06.
Jesus' Residence — Jesus Christ's home in South Park. Notable episodes: S03E16, S05E03.
Jewbilee Camp — Where the Jew Scouts hold the Jewbilee. Notable episodes: S03E09.
Jewleeard — A Jewish Yeshiva school parodying Juilliard. Notable episodes: S06E15.
Jim Davis High School — A fictional inner-city school. Notable episodes: S12E05.
Jim's Drugs RX — Mr. Farkle's pharmacy. Notable episodes: S08E09.
Jimbo and Ned's Residence — The house Jimbo Kern and Ned Gerblanski share. Notable episodes: S02E06.
Jimbo's Cabin — A small forest cabin owned by Stan's uncle Jimbo Kern. Notable episodes: S20E02.
Jimbo's Guns — Jimbo's gun store, seen and mentioned across several episodes. Notable episodes: S01E02, S17E03.
John Edward's Residence — The home of psychic medium John Edward. Notable episodes: S06E15.
Joozineks — A strip club on Planet Fognl, called a "hekmabah" by the Joozian aliens. Notable episodes: S07E01.
Joseph Smith's Residence — The home of Joseph Smith. Notable episodes: S07E12.
K-13 — Aspen's most dangerous ski mountain, referencing K-2; Stan kills a mountain lion there. Notable episodes: S06E02, S08E14.
Karl's Kroff Dinner Palace — A restaurant. Notable episodes: S02E01.
Karne Institute for Sex Addiction — A fictional rehab clinic for sex addiction. Notable episodes: S14E01.
Keller's Bike Shop — A bike shop selling regular and electric bikes. Notable episodes: S29E01.
Kentucky Fried Chicken — The KFC fast-food chain, famous for its fried chicken and a favorite of the boys. Notable episodes: S08E13.
Kenya — An East African country, featured once. Notable episodes: S13E06.
Kickstarter — The crowdfunding platform, headquartered in the US. Notable episodes: S18E01.
Kidzone Roller Rink — A roller rink with food, drink, and air hockey, reserved for Clyde's birthday party. Notable episodes: S22E02.
King Jimmy's Buffet — South Park's all-you-can-eat buffet restaurant, also written KJ's Buffet. Notable episodes: S01E08, S03E13.
Kokujon — An extraterrestrial planet, mentioned once. Notable episodes: S14E13.
Komfort Inn — A motel seen across three episodes. Notable episodes: S10E06, S12E05, S12E02.
Kum & Go — A convenience store modeled on a real chain, a near-identical lookalike of 7-11. Notable episodes: S16E12, S23E01.
Kupa Keep — Cartman's backyard base of his Kingdom of Kupa Keep.
Kuwahara Saimin — A drive-thru restaurant in Hawaii serving traditional Hawaiian food, seen once. Notable episodes: S16E11.

entries.n: L. Ron Hubbard's Scientology Celebrity Center
entries.t: L. Ron Hubbard's Scientology Celebrity Center — The head office of the Church of Scientology for celebrities and members. Notable episodes: S09E12.
k: l. ron hubbard's scientology celebrity center
l. ron hubbards scientology celebrity center

entries.t: La Taco — A taco restaurant where Jennifer Lopez ends up working after Mitch Conner steals her success. Notable episodes: S07E05.
Lake George — A reservoir. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Lake Tardicaca — A camp for handicapped kids, parodying Lake Titicaca. Notable episodes: S14E07.
Lamont's Dance Studio — A dance studio. Notable episodes: S08E04.
Lanskin Residence — The home of Corey Lanskin. Notable episodes: S17E02.
Las Vegas — The most populous city in Nevada. Notable episodes: S03E16.
Last Vista Life Care Center — A retirement home in South Park. Notable episodes: S24E02.
Laugh Factory — A chain of comedy clubs, seen once. Notable episodes: S11E01.
Law Office, pa — A business seen once. Notable episodes: S18E01.

entries.n: Law Offices of Mayer, Schulz & Tate
entries.t: Law Offices of Mayer, Schulz & Tate — A law firm handling criminal, corporate, intellectual property, and personal injury cases, visited by Mr. Hankey to sue the town council. Notable episodes: S22E03.
k: law offices of mayer, schulz & tate

entries.n: Law Offices of Taylor, Broflovski & Swift
entries.t: Law Offices of Taylor, Broflovski & Swift — A law firm and Gerald Broflovski's current workplace. Notable episodes: S27E01.
k: law offices of taylor, broflovski & swift

entries.t: Le Catamount Bistró — A restaurant in the film studio commissary inside Catamount Pictures. Notable episodes: S08E05.
Le Place Restaurant — A fine-dining restaurant in South Park. Notable episodes: S06E01.
Les Bos — A lesbian bar in South Park, which Allison calls a "girl bar". Notable episodes: S11E06.
Lihue Airport — The primary airport on the Hawaiian island of Kauai. Notable episodes: S16E11.
Lincoln Memorial — The national memorial hall in Washington, D.C. Notable episodes: S05E03.
Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — The landmark reflecting pool in Washington, D.C. Notable episodes: S05E03.
Little Future — A South Park district inhabited by future immigrants. Notable episodes: S08E07.
Loading and Unloading Dock — A dock outside South Park Elementary and a common Goth Kids hangout. Notable episodes: S07E13.
Lolly's Candy Factory — A South Park confectionery run by Lolly the Candy Man. Notable episodes: S06E12, S22E05.
London Recording Studio — A London-based recording studio, seen once. Notable episodes: S05E04.
Loogie's Ristorante — Loogie's family's Italian restaurant in South Park, where the Tooth Trade conducts its business. Notable episodes: S04E01.
Looming Sunset Assisted Living — A nursing home. Notable episodes: S16E02.
Loomis Gasoline — The Old Farmer's former workplace, a gas station. Notable episodes: S05E14.
Los Angeles — California's biggest city, second-biggest in the US, mentioned or visited across several episodes. Notable episodes: S08E05.
Lost Forest — A forest marking the boundary between South Park and Canada.
Luau's Toys — A toy store on South Park's Main Street. Notable episodes: S03E11.
Lucky Penny — A store in the South Park Mall. Notable episodes: S04E04.
M. Ingalls Vista — A lookout point in South Park.
Mabel Cartman's Residence — Grandma Cartman's house, later owned by Uncle Stinky. Notable episodes: S02E16, S05E06.
Macintosh Residence — The home of Betsy MacIntosh. Notable episodes: S15E05.
Mackey Residence — Mr. Mackey's home, leased from Mr. Freely; later redecorated in navy with a new interior. Notable episodes: S02E03, S03E08, S22E04, S22E05, S22E09.
Maga Store — A Myrtle Beach accessory shop selling flags, shirts, stickers, and novelty goods. Notable episodes: S26E06.
Main St. Pharmacy — A pharmacy. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.

Main Street — South Park's main thoroughfare, home to most of the town's businesses and shops. Early seasons used it as a stock shot of the whole town with the town sign; later it gets more detailed views, with building positions shifting as new shops like the Bijou Cinema appear. Notable episodes: S01E01.
Main Street Business Services — An office building on South Park's Main Street.
Main Street Office — An office block on Main Street, next to Tom's Rhinoplasty. Notable episodes: S01E11.
Mala Vista Middle School — A fictional middle school, scene of a school shooting. Notable episodes: S22E01.
Malkinson Residence — Where the Malkinson family lives. Notable episodes: S12E13.
Mall of Nebraska — A shopping mall. Notable episodes: S02E16.
Mar-a-Lago — Donald Trump's resort residence in Palm Beach, Florida, with a members-only club. Notable episodes: S27E02.
Marklar — An Earth-like world home to the Marklar aliens, and Starvin' Marvin's current home. Notable episodes: S03E13, S01E08.
Marryot Hotel — A hotel. Notable episodes: S10E05.
Mars — The fourth planet of the solar system, featured prominently in Season 20. Notable episodes: S20E04.

Marsh Residence — The Marsh family house on Avenue de Los Mexicanos, home to Randy, Sharon, Stan, and Shelley. First seen in Season 1, the family has moved out twice, including from Season 22 to Season 28 when they lived at Tegridy Farms. Notable episodes: S01E04 (first appearance), S22E04 (Tegridy era), S16E01, S05E09, S02E10.
McArthur Residence — The McArthur family home, painted beige-brown. Notable episodes: S04E16.
McCormick Residence — The home of the McCormicks. Notable episodes: S01E08.
McCormick Science Wing — A science laboratory in South Park Elementary Plus. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
McDonald Residence — The home of Fosse McDonald. Notable episodes: S07E06.
McDonald's — The fast-food chain; its South Park restaurant's sign reads "M Burgers" out front. Notable episodes: S18E08, S15E05.
McKemicks — A bar and nightclub in South Park. Notable episodes: S03E15.
Medicinal Fried Chicken — A medical marijuana store in South Park that replaced the town's KFC. Notable episodes: S14E03.
Mel Gibson's Residence — The Malibu, California home of actor and director Mel Gibson. Notable episodes: S08E03.
Mel's Buffet — A buffet restaurant in South Park. Notable episodes: S04E05.
Methadone Clinic — A drug rehabilitation clinic. Notable episodes: S14E03.
Mexicano Aeronáutico y Spacio Administración — MASA, a fictional Mexican spaceport. Notable episodes: S09E13.
Mexico — The North American country south of the US; prominent cities include Tijuana and Ensenada in Baja California. Notable episodes: S02E08, S15E09.
Michael Deets' Residence — The home of serial killer Michael Deets. Notable episodes: S08E13.
Mick's Bowling — A tenpin bowling alley and bar in South Park. Notable episodes: S11E13, S23E09.
Microsoft HQ — The headquarters of the multinational tech giant co-founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen. Notable episodes: S17E08.
Middle Park — South Park's neighboring town in Park County, Colorado. Notable episodes: S01E04.

Middle Park Elementary — The elementary school in Middle Park, with a layout matching South Park Elementary in different colors; its sports team is the Middle Park Cowboys. Notable episodes: S01E04, S08E11.
MIR Space Station — The first modular space station ever built, run by Russia. Notable episodes: S01E07.
Miss Information's New Age Shop — A spiritual shop. Notable episodes: S04E06.
Moderna Center — A public theater in New York City. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Moon — Earth's natural satellite. Notable episodes: S09E13.
Moovit! — A moving company in South Park. Notable episodes: S09E08.
Motel 2½ — An accommodation in Pueblo.

Motivation Corp. — A fictional organization keeping kids off drugs by hiring actors to pose as their drug-addled future selves; its motto is that lying to children about drugs is okay. Its clients included Stan's, Butters', and Kevin Stoley's parents. Notable episodes: S06E16.
Mount Evanston — The dormant volcano near South Park that Scuzzlebutt calls home. Notable episodes: S01E03.
Mouse Holes — Tiny holes in the New Kid's room and the Unplanned Parenthood Clinic; the New Kid uses Gnome Dust to shrink and enter them.
Mr. Mackey's Childhood Residence — The house Mr. Mackey grew up in during the 1970s and 80s, now home to his mother. Notable episodes: S14E10.
Mr. Slave's Residence — Where Mr. Slave lives with his husband Big Gay Al. Notable episodes: S09E10.
Mt. Peaceful Cemetery — A cemetery in South Park. Notable episodes: S03E10.
Musa Van Kleef Mustard Farm — A mustard farm. Notable episodes: S26E05.
Museum of Tolerance — A tolerance museum. Notable episodes: S06E14.
Music Lab Recording Studio — A music recording studio. Notable episodes: S07E05.
Myrtle Beach — A city in South Carolina. Notable episodes: S26E06.
Myrtle Beach International Airport — The public airport serving Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. Notable episodes: S26E06.
Nashville — The capital and most populous city of Tennessee. Notable episodes: S29E02.
Nebraska State Penitentiary — A prison. Notable episodes: S02E16.
Nebraska Train Station — Nebraska's railway station linking it to other cities and towns. Notable episodes: S02E03.
New New Hampshire — A future dystopian version of New Hampshire. Notable episodes: S10E13, S10E12.
New York City — The largest city in the US, in southern New York State. Notable episodes: S01E06.
NFL HQ — National Football League headquarters, home of commissioner Roger Goodell. Notable episodes: S18E01.
Niagara Falls National Park — The trio of waterfalls on the Ontario–New York border. Notable episodes: S19E02.
Nigeria — A West African country, featured once. Notable episodes: S12E01.
Nishimura School of Martial Arts — A Japanese martial arts academy. Notable episodes: S03E05.
North Korea — The East Asian country on the northern Korean Peninsula. Notable episodes: S21E02.
North Park — The town north of South Park in Park County, Colorado. Notable episodes: S02E08.

North Park Funland — An amusement park in North Park that Cartman buys: he first keeps everyone out, then has to sell tickets to cover costs, grows miserable, and sells it back to Frank Fun. Notable episodes: S04E05, S05E06 (Cartmanland), S06E06, S09E04, S10E10.
Nueva Familia — A Mexican restaurant arriving with the town's Whole Foods-driven gentrification wave. Notable episodes: S19E04.
O'Connell Residence — The O'Connell family home. Notable episodes: S06E07.
Ocean View Terrace Treatment Center — A drug rehab center in Rancho Palos Verdes, California. Notable episodes: S14E07.
Olive Garden — An Italian restaurant chain. Notable episodes: S14E12, S22E06.
Oprah Winfrey's Residence — A mansion in South Park. Notable episodes: S05E12.
Optometrist — An optometrist clinic. Notable episodes: S03E03.
Ottawa — The capital city of Canada. Notable episodes: S07E15.

P.F. Chang's — A Chinese-themed restaurant chain that originated in America despite the cuisine. Towelie briefly works there and gets fired for being too high; Cartman and Butters hold the place hostage hunting a rumored Chinese invasion; Randy credits its General Tso's Chicken for his record-sized crap, photographed on the news; and Kyle wins a $5,000 gift certificate there. Notable episodes: S10E05 (Towelie's job), S12E08 (the hostage standoff), S11E09 (Randy's record), S05E08, S16E14.
P.F. Pityef Bracelet Factory — A bracelet factory drawn in a Dr. Seuss-like style. Notable episodes: S16E13.
Pakistan — A South Asian country; capital Islamabad, biggest city Karachi. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.
Panda Express — A restaurant chain; its South Park location hosts underground rooster fights run through Magic: The Gathering. Notable episodes: S18E08.
Papa John's — A fast pizza chain. Notable episodes: S18E02.
Paradise Bar — A small outdoor bar in Hawaii, seen briefly during Kenny's letter montage. Notable episodes: S16E11.
Parental Revenge Center — Eric Cartman's fictional company for exacting revenge on parents who anger their kids. Notable episodes: S06E16.
Park County Airfield — An aerodrome. Notable episodes: S07E15.
Park County Community Center — A public building in South Park, also called the South Park Community Center. Notable episodes: S01E06, S22E05.
Park County Coroner — A coroner's office in South Park. Notable episodes: S21E05.
Park County Courthouse — A courthouse. Notable episodes: S21E01.
Park County Courts — A law firm. Notable episodes: S12E08.

entries.n: Park County Drug and Alcohol Rehabilitation Center
entries.t: Park County Drug and Alcohol Rehabilitation Center — An institution treating drug addiction and alcoholism. Notable episodes: S10E10.
k: park county drug and alcohol rehabilitation center

entries.t: Park County Equestrian Facility — South Park's horse riding arena. Notable episodes: S25E04.
Park County Government Center — A government center in South Park. Notable episodes: S10E14.
Park County Hockey Rink — An indoor ice hockey rink. Notable episodes: S10E14.

Park County Police Station — The three-story building used by the Park County Police and the FBI. Sergeant Yates is its most prominent officer, having framed Michael Jackson and lectured the boys on music piracy; the detectives brag about shooting suspects. Notable episodes: S07E06, S10E10, S08E13.
Park County Shoes — A shoe store in South Park. Notable episodes: S24E01.
Park County Television Studio — A TV broadcasting studio for Channel 4 News. Notable episodes: S11E08.
Park County Trash Dump — A local garbage dump in South Park. Notable episodes: S07E11.
PC Delta — A fraternity house and the PC Bros' home base through Season 19. Notable episodes: S19E01.
Pebble Beach Hotel and Resort — A hotel in Florida. Notable episodes: S21E05.
Pentagon — The headquarters of the US Department of Defense in Arlington, Virginia, one of the world's largest office buildings. Notable episodes: S06E12.

Smithsonian Natural History Museum — The National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C. Notable episodes: S12E12.
SoDoSoPa — An entertainment and shopping district in South Park. Notable episodes: S19E03.
Solokov Residence — Where the Solokov family lives. Notable episodes: S25E04.

United States Capitol — The home of the US Congress in Washington, D.C. Notable episodes: S03E14.
United States Geological Survey — The Colorado branch of the government scientific facility; a former workplace of Randy Marsh. Notable episodes: S18E03.
United States Post Office — The national post office chain; the building itself appears once. Notable episodes: S15E05.

Walgreens — A retail store appearing across several episodes. Notable episodes: S13E02, S16E10, S16E13, S23E09, S24E02.

Whole Foods Market — A supermarket chain selling "natural" foods without artificial additives, central to a Season 19 arc. Notable episodes: S19E03, S19E10, S19E05.
Will Smith's Residence — The South Park house of Will Smith's family. Notable episodes: S05E12.
Willy's Chilly Ice Cream Parlor — An ice cream parlor in South Park. Notable episodes: S26E04, S26E05.
Wingstreet — A fast-food restaurant, seen once. Notable episodes: S16E04.
Winnipeg — The capital and largest city of Manitoba, Canada; its players perform at the Canadian Royal Wedding. Notable episodes: S15E03.
Winter Rink — An ice-skating rink. Notable episodes: S23E10.
WSPIC 88.3 FM — A radio station. Notable episodes: S18E02.
Wuhan — A large city in Hubei Province, China. Notable episodes: S24E01.
Yates Residence — Where the Yates family lives. Notable episodes: S08E06.
Zeebod's Toys — A South Park toy store seen in the year 2546, appearing once. Notable episodes: S10E13.
Zhongnanhai — A former imperial compound in Beijing serving as the office of China's top leaders. Notable episodes: S19E06.
Zimmerman Residence — The home of George Zimmerman's family. Notable episodes: S17E03.
Zoom — A communications technology company. Notable episodes: SPECIAL.

entries.n: S01E01 — Cartman Gets an Anal Probe
entries.t:
Cartman insists the alien abduction he remembers was only a bad dream, but everything in South Park suggests otherwise. While the boys wait for the school bus, Chef pulls up wearing a shirt that reads 'Believe' beneath a picture of a grey alien and asks whether anyone has seen a visitor ship. Soon after, Kyle spots his baby brother Ike being carried off by two of the visitors, and the search is on. Officer Barbrady, meanwhile, is busy on a local farm investigating cows that have been turned inside out, which he treats as perfectly normal, and he mistakes passing helicopters for pigeons. At school, Mr. Garrison refuses to excuse Kyle unless his hand puppet Mr. Hat agrees, and Cartman keeps blasting gouts of fire from his backside, singeing Pip. Wendy Testaburger slips Stan a note asking to meet at Stark's Pond, and Stan throws up on her from nerves. At lunch the boys ask Chef for advice, and Chef answers with one of his off-topic love songs before snapping out of it and ordering them to go find Ike. After school, Cartman still claims mind control is nonsense — right before a beam from the sky makes him burst into 'I Love to Singa.' When a visitor ship descends, the aliens blast Kenny with a star-shaped object, setting off the town's soon-famous ritual: 'Oh my God, they killed Kenny!' 'You bastards!' Kenny survives the blast, survives being trampled by fleeing cattle, and is finally finished off when Barbrady runs him over chasing the herd. Wendy suggests using Cartman as bait, so the boys tie him to a tree. His flaming flatulence summons the ship, and an eighty-foot satellite dish unfolds from his rear. Ike is returned, the visitors explain the inside-out cows were the new guy Carl's mistake, declare cows the most intelligent life on Earth, hand them a device that forces people to sing, and abduct Cartman a second time. Barbrady is made to sing while the cows dance. The next morning Cartman drops from the sky with one red eye and describes a new 'dream' about catching pinkeye from Scott Baio aboard the ship.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Chef, Wendy Testaburger, Mr. Garrison and Mr. Hat, Officer Barbrady, Ms. Crabtree (the bus driver, introduced shouting 'Sit down and shut up!'), Ike Broflovski, Pip Pirrip, and the alien visitors.

Locations: the school bus stop, South Park Elementary (classroom and cafeteria), Stark's Pond, the Denkins farm, and the tree where Cartman is staked out as bait.

Key events & continuity: the first appearance of the visitors and their anal probe; the debut of Ms. Crabtree, Ike, and the Garrison/Mr. Hat catchphrase 'You go to hell! You go to hell and you die!'; the first 'Oh my God, they killed Kenny!' / 'You bastards!' exchange; the first 'Screw you guys, I'm going home!'; the start of Stan vomiting whenever Wendy talks to him; and the visitors' standing judgment that cows are Earth's smartest species.

Cartman wins the national 'Save Our Fragile Planet' essay contest, and America's sweetheart Kathie Lee Gifford is coming to South Park to hand him the award in person. Wendy is furious, convinced he cheated, and the whole town throws itself into preparations, with Mayor McDaniels turning the visit into a showcase for herself. Chef is booked to sing at the ceremony and spends the whole time scheming to seduce Kathie Lee. Mr. Garrison is put in charge of a pioneer-and-Indian pageant meant to honor her, but the rehearsal turns into a bloodbath, the townspeople are horrified, and Garrison gets fired as director. That is the last straw for him: he has hated Kathie Lee since childhood, when she upstaged him and Mr. Hat in a talent show, and Mr. Hat talks him into settling it with a rifle bought from Jimbo's gun shop. Meanwhile Cartman, told to get in shape for the big day, starts chugging the bodybuilding supplement Weight Gain 4000 without doing any exercise, and balloons into a morbidly obese wreck. Wendy digs through Garrison's files to prove Cartman cheated and discovers his essay was just a copy of Walden with his name written on it. On the day, Kathie Lee arrives sealed inside a bubble of bulletproof glass. Garrison lines up his shot from the book depository, Wendy talks him down, but Stan clumsily reopens the old talent-show wound and Mr. Hat fires anyway. At the same instant the stage collapses under Cartman's weight, flinging Kathie Lee clear and dropping Kenny into the bullet's path; he is sent flying into a flagpole and impaled through the head. Kathie Lee is rushed out of town, Garrison ends up in a mental hospital with Mr. Hat in a straitjacket, Chef finally gets his night with Kathie Lee (and is startled by her appetites), and Cartman appears on Geraldo as a living monument to following your dreams, chanting 'Beefcake! Beefcake!'

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Wendy Testaburger, Mr. Garrison and Mr. Hat, Chef, Mayor McDaniels, Jimbo Kern, Kathie Lee Gifford.

Locations: South Park Elementary, Jimbo's gun shop, the award ceremony stage, the book depository, the mental hospital.

Key events & continuity: Cartman's essay fraud is exposed (Walden with his name on it); Mr. Hat is established as a violent, murderous influence on Garrison; Chef's womanizing lands him Kathie Lee; Cartman's 'Beefcake' chant becomes a signature; Garrison's childhood talent-show humiliation becomes a running grievance.

Stan's uncle Jimbo and his war buddy Ned take the four boys on a hunting trip in the mountains, handing each kid a rifle, a beer, and a pack of cigarettes. Jimbo and Ned's style of hunting is to gun down anything that moves and yell 'It's coming right for us!' to make it self-defense. Stan proves to be a terrible hunter — he cannot bring himself to shoot a living target — while Kenny impresses Jimbo by drinking gasoline straight from the can. Back in town, Stan's father Randy, the town geologist, detects at the seismic center that the mountain they are on is about to erupt. On the mountain, Jimbo accidentally sets Ned on fire during a hot-dog roast, and Cartman spins a campfire tale about Scuzzlebutt, a deformed mountain monster with a celery stalk for a hand and a piece of Patrick Duffy for a leg, who weaves wicker baskets and kills climbers. Nobody believes him, so Cartman dresses up as Scuzzlebutt the next morning to scare them; the prank backfires when Jimbo and Ned try to shoot him for the fame. The townspeople below, unaware of the volcano, organize a search party while Randy has them dig a trench to divert the lava. The mountain blows, the hunting party is trapped on the wrong side of the trench, and then the real Scuzzlebutt appears and ferries everyone to safety in a giant wicker basket. Randy's miscalculated trench sends the lava flow straight into Denver. Desperate to prove himself to Jimbo, Stan shoots the real Scuzzlebutt dead — and Jimbo is unimpressed, lecturing him that some things you kill and some things you don't. The boys conclude that hunting sucks and go home to watch cartoons.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Jimbo Kern, Ned Gerblansky, Randy Marsh, Scuzzlebutt.

Locations: the mountain hunting camp, the South Park Center for Seismic Activity, the lava-diversion trench, Denver (destroyed off-screen).

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Jimbo and Ned and their 'It's coming right for us!' loophole; first appearance of Randy Marsh as the town geologist; the debut of Scuzzlebutt; Stan's inability to kill becomes a character beat; Denver is wiped out by lava and nobody much cares.

entries.n: S01E04 — Big Gay Al's Big Gay Boat Ride
entries.t:
Stan's new dog Sparky turns out to be gay — he humps Sylvester, then Rex, sending both dogs fleeing — and Stan is mortified. Mr. Garrison's classroom definition of homosexuality ('evil right down to their cold black hearts') only confuses him further, though Garrison is really just masking his own feelings. Stan tries to butch Sparky up, even presenting him with Fifi, a female poodle; Sparky steals her diamond collar instead. A call to the TV show Jesus and Pals for moral guidance gets cut off before Jesus can answer. Feeling rejected, Sparky runs away to Big Gay Al's Big Gay Animal Sanctuary, a refuge for gay animals run by the flamboyant Big Gay Al. Stan tracks him down, and Big Gay Al gently teaches him that homosexuality has always existed and is nothing to be ashamed of. Stan accepts his dog just in time for the big homecoming football game against Middle Park. Meanwhile Jimbo and Ned have bet five hundred dollars on the South Park Cows to beat the spread, and their backup plan is pure sabotage: a bomb strapped to the Middle Park mascot, rigged to detonate when halftime singer Richard Stamos hits the high note in 'Lovin' You.' Stamos flubs the note, the bomb survives, and Stan — stepping in at quarterback — throws a last-second touchdown pass to Kyle that beats the spread. Stan tries to lead the townspeople to the sanctuary to preach tolerance, but the sanctuary has mysteriously vanished, though everyone's lost pets come home. Big Gay Al thanks Stan and disappears. Moments later, Richard Stamos returns to prove he can hit the note after all — and the bomb finally goes off.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Sparky, Big Gay Al, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Jimbo Kern, Ned Gerblansky, Mr. Garrison, Chef, Richard Stamos, Jesus (on TV).

Locations: the bus stop, South Park Elementary, the football field, Big Gay Al's Big Gay Animal Sanctuary.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Big Gay Al and Sparky; Stan's acceptance of his gay dog becomes one of his defining moral moments; Jimbo and Ned's gambling and bomb plots become a running pattern; the sanctuary's unexplained disappearance is never explained.
k: big gay al's big gay boat ride

entries.n: S01E05 — An Elephant Makes Love to a Pig
entries.t:
Kyle gets a new pet elephant, but his mother refuses to let him keep it because the animal is simply too enormous for the house. Unwilling to give the elephant up, the boys turn to the town's resident mad scientist, Dr. Alphonse Mephesto, hoping he can use genetic engineering to shrink the elephant down to a manageable size. (Note: the surviving source material for this story is unusually thin — the extract preserves only the premise above plus notes about an edited scene — so this entry sticks to what is actually documented rather than inventing plot beats.)

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski, Stan Marsh, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Sheila Broflovski, Dr. Alphonse Mephesto.

Locations: the Broflovski home, Dr. Mephesto's genetics lab.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Dr. Mephesto, who becomes the town's go-to geneticist for every bizarre creature plot to follow.
k: an elephant makes love to a pig

entries.t:
It is Grandpa Marvin Marsh's 102nd birthday, and his only wish is to die — he tries to shoot himself, misses, and then offers Stan a dollar to do the job for him, noting that he shot his own grandfather at Stan's age. Stan refuses and spends the day asking adults whether he should help, but nobody will discuss it. Meanwhile Sheila Broflovski catches Kyle and Ike watching the boys' favorite show, Terrance and Phillip, and is so disgusted by the fart jokes that she organizes a parent boycott, marching on the Cartoon Central headquarters in New York. Back home, Kenny comes down with violently explosive diarrhea that spreads through the whole town, including the protesting parents, who laugh at real-life toilet humor even as they denounce the cartoon. Left unsupervised, the boys watch Terrance and Phillip freely while Grandpa keeps scheming: he tricks a distracted Stan into holding a noose, then locks Stan in a room blasting Enya to show him what old age feels like. The boys finally agree to help and rig a cow to drop from a tree onto Grandpa — but Death, when he arrives, ignores the old man ('I'm over here, you son-of-a-whore!') and comes for Kenny instead. Death pauses to watch Terrance and Phillip through a TV-store window, and the network, stunk out by the protest's tactics, pulls the show in favor of reruns of She's the Sheriff. One touch from Death kills Kenny, and the ghost of Grandpa's own grandfather appears to warn that suicide lands you in limbo — he knows, because he asked his grandson to kill him. Grandpa mishears the moral entirely and starts planning a trip to Africa, where hundreds of people are eaten 'naturally' by lions every year. Sheila returns home and marches the boys toward their next boycott, while the boys, bored without their show, start discussing drugs and porn.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Grandpa Marvin Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Sheila Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Death, Terrance and Phillip.

Locations: the Marsh home, the Broflovski home, South Park Elementary, Cartoon Central HQ in New York, the TV store.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Grandpa Marsh, Sheila Broflovski, and Death; first appearance of Terrance and Phillip, the boys' favorite show and the town's favorite moral panic; establishes Sheila as the leader of every future parent crusade.

The night before Halloween, the MIR space station crashes onto Kenny at the bus stop and kills him. At the morgue he is drained and refilled with embalming fluid — into which a coroner accidentally knocks a bottle of Worcestershire sauce — and Kenny rises as a zombie, biting the morgue staff on his way out. By morning he is shambling at the bus stop like nothing happened, and the town's school costume contest proceeds: Stan as Raggedy Andy, Wendy as Chewbacca (ruining Stan's planned couples costume), Kyle in a store-bought Chewbacca, Cartman in a Hitler costume his mother made, and zombie Kenny, whom everyone mistakes for a celebrity doing Edward James Olmos. Principal Victoria replaces Cartman's costume with a ghost outfit that looks exactly like a Klan robe. The doctor examines the bitten morgue workers and diagnoses pinkeye. Kyle, annoyed that half the school is Chewbacca, builds a working model of the solar system; Wendy still wins first place and the two tons of candy, which she donates to starving children in Nairobi, while Kenny takes second and Stan is judged worst-dressed. Zombie Clyde drowns Bebe during apple-bobbing, and by nightfall the 'pinkeye' has overrun South Park. Chef is the first to realize they are dealing with the living dead, but nobody believes him — the doctor gets eaten mid-disbelief. The boys ditch the candy-stealing zombie Kenny and hole up with Chef, who leads them to the morgue. There they find the Worcestershire sauce bottle — and a copy of Crack Whore Monthly featuring Cartman's mother on the cover. The zombies break in (aided by a zombified Pip, dubbed the 'little limey zombie') and turn Chef, who performs a Thriller-style musical number. Kyle calls the hotline on the sauce bottle and a British operator explains the cure: kill the original zombie and the rest revert. A zombified Wendy lunges at Stan and he cannot bring himself to strike her, so Kyle bisects Kenny with a chainsaw and the whole town turns human again. Cartman weeps at Kenny's grave, then leaves to count his candy. Kenny later claws out of his grave stitched together, only to be crushed by a falling tombstone statue and then a crashing jet.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Wendy Testaburger, Chef, Principal Victoria, the town doctor, Ms. Crabtree's bus-stop crew.

Locations: the bus stop, the morgue, South Park Elementary (classroom and gym), the doctor's office, Kenny's grave.

Key events & continuity: the Halloween tradition begins; Kenny's death-by-space-station is one of his most absurd; Wendy giving away her candy establishes her charitable streak; Cartman's mother's magazine cover feeds the long-running joke about Liane; Stan's refusal to hurt zombie Wendy shows how deep his feelings run.

While watching the Terrance and Phillip Thanksgiving special, the boys see a charity commercial starring Sally Struthers promising a Teiko digital sports watch to anyone who sponsors a starving African child. They call in, and through a misunderstanding the charity ships them an actual Ethiopian boy instead of a watch. They name him Starvin' Marvin and take turns housing him (everyone except Kenny, whose family is too poor). At school, Mr. Garrison launches a canned-food drive for the needy — pointedly including Kenny — just as Dr. Mephesto's genetically engineered turkeys escape and start attacking the town; Mayor McDaniels dismisses Mephesto as an insane crank and ignores the warning. At King Jimmy's All-You-Can-Eat Buffet, Cartman refuses to share his pot pie with Marvin and steals Marvin's peach cobbler instead. Secret-service agents arrive looking for a starving African child; Marvin points at Cartman, and Cartman is shipped to Ethiopia in his place. There he finds the Red Cross out of food and discovers Sally Struthers hoarding it all for herself; when she won't share her cake, he exposes her to the starving crowd.
