Back home, the mutant turkeys besiege the town square during the canned-food grab (Kenny scores a can of string beans), and the townspeople slaughter them in a battle staged like Braveheart — Kenny dies in the fighting. The agents retrieve Marvin and fly Cartman home, and Marvin takes the dead mutant turkeys back to Ethiopia to feed his people, who tie up Sally Struthers and spit on her. The episode closes on the McCormick dinner table, where the family cannot open Kenny's can of beans because they don't own a can opener.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Starvin' Marvin, Sally Struthers, Mr. Garrison, Dr. Mephesto, Mayor McDaniels, the McCormick family.

Locations: Cartman's house, South Park Elementary, King Jimmy's All-You-Can-Eat Buffet, the town square, Ethiopia.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Starvin' Marvin, who returns in later stories; first appearance of Dr. Mephesto's out-of-control genetic experiments as a town hazard; Cartman's selfishness at the buffet becomes a defining trait; Kenny's family's poverty is played for bleak comedy with the can opener.

entries.n: S01E09 — Mr. Hankey, the Christmas Poo
entries.t:
South Park Elementary rehearses its Christmas pageant — a traditional Nativity with Kyle, who is Jewish, cast as Joseph — until Sheila Broflovski storms in and demands every religious element be stripped out. Her crusade snowballs: the town decides that anything that offends anyone must go, so Santa, trees, wreaths, stars, lights, and candy canes are all banned. Kyle suggests replacing the religious content with Mr. Hankey, the Christmas Poo, a cheerful figure from his own family tradition, but nobody takes him seriously. Feeling like a lonely Jew at Christmas and humiliated by his mother, Kyle is sent to bed without a Hanukkah present — and that night, while brushing his teeth, he meets Mr. Hankey for real: a small, talking piece of poop who only appears to those with Christmas spirit. Kyle tries to show him to the town, but to everyone else Mr. Hankey looks like an ordinary turd, and after Kyle hurls him at Cartman and spikes Mr. Mackey's coffee, Mackey diagnoses Kyle as a 'clinically depressed fecalphiliac on Prozac' and has him committed to the asylum. Meanwhile the pageant, scrubbed of everything, becomes a minimalist Philip Glass song-and-dance that horrifies the parents into a screaming blame-fight. At the height of the chaos Mr. Hankey reveals himself to the whole town, Christmas spirit is restored, Kyle is released with a town-wide apology, and Mr. Hankey flies off into the night alongside Santa Claus. The boys notice something feels missing — Kenny, cheerfully waving, points out that he never died this time as 'The End' appears over him. Over the credits, Jesus sits alone singing 'Happy Birthday' to himself, since religion has been effectively outlawed.

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski, Stan Marsh, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Sheila and Gerald Broflovski, Mr. Hankey, Mr. Mackey, Jesus, Santa Claus.

Locations: South Park Elementary (pageant stage), the Broflovski home and bathroom, the mental asylum, the town square.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Mr. Hankey, who becomes the town's Christmas mascot; first time Kenny survives an entire story, which he celebrates; establishes Sheila's holiday moral crusades and Kyle's 'lonely Jew on Christmas' melancholy as recurring beats.

Cartman hands out birthday-party invitations in class, each one assigning the guest a specific Mega Man toy to buy him (Stan gets Green, Kyle gets Red, Kenny gets the cheap Yellow), and then Mr. Garrison introduces a new student: Damien Thorn, who announces he is from the seventh level of Hell and that his father Satan's reign is beginning. The boys mock him relentlessly until Damien's eyes burst into flame, he telekinetically hurls Cartman's desk out the window, turns Kenny into a duck-billed platypus, and levels the cafeteria with a whirlwind, demanding that Jesus be brought to him. Jesus arrives and challenges Satan to face him directly; Satan, speaking through Damien, agrees to a final battle the next day. The whole town descends on the bookie — Jimbo first — and the fight is booked as a pay-per-view boxing match at the South Park Forum for $49.95, which infuriates Cartman because it lands on his birthday. Everyone bets on Jesus until Satan shows up for the weigh-in looking enormous, and the town stampedes back to change its bets. The boys draft Chef to spar with Jesus and train him; Chef knocks Jesus out cold with one punch. At Cartman's party, Damien tries to fit in by opening a pit of fire and having black ghosts toss a flaming Pip into the air, which wins the boys over. During present-opening, Kyle gives Cartman Ants in the Pants instead of the Red Mega Man, Cartman attacks him and cancels the party outright, and everyone heads to the fight. Satan pummels a dispirited Jesus, who has lost heart at the town's lack of faith — until Stan's pep talk ('Don't try to be a great man, just be a man,' which Stan admits he stole from Star Trek) gets him back up. Jesus lands one punch, Satan takes an obvious dive, and the truth comes out: Satan was the only one who bet on Jesus, engineering the whole spectacle to get rich and buy real estate. The town begs forgiveness, Jesus shrugs it off, and Damien says goodbye to Stan and Kyle, agreeing that being happy is what matters for kids. Cartman ends the night sick and fatter than ever, asking his mother for more pie.

Featured characters: Damien Thorn, Satan, Jesus, Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Chef, Jimbo Kern, Pip Pirrip, Mr. Garrison.

Locations: South Park Elementary (classroom, cafeteria, playground), the South Park Forum, Cartman's birthday party.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Damien, and of Satan as an active character (a scheming, real-estate-hungry showman rather than a monster); Jesus is established as South Park's resident, slightly hapless savior with his own TV show; Cartman's Mega Man gift-grab shows his birthday extortion racket.

Stan and Wendy are planning a romantic Valentine's Day when Mr. Garrison leaves class for a nose job at Tom's Rhinoplasty, and Principal Victoria introduces the substitute: Ms. Ellen, a beautiful young teacher who instantly bewitches every boy in the room. Stan starts vomiting around her the way he always does around Wendy, which makes Wendy insanely jealous. The boys shower Ms. Ellen with gifts, and Chef — smitten himself — warns them she is a lesbian; not knowing what that means, the boys try to become lesbians too, licking carpet in Cartman's living room and gnawing on cardboard boxes on Liane's advice. Wendy tries to win Stan back with a Grease-style leather outfit, but Ms. Ellen shows up in a matching one and steals the spotlight again, then offers to take the spelling-test winner to dinner. Meanwhile Garrison's surgery is a triumph: he comes back looking like a movie star, quits teaching to enjoy being the most handsome man in South Park, and is soon mobbed by adoring women. With Garrison gone, Ms. Ellen is hired permanently. Pushed past her limit — her grandmother just died, Stan won the dinner date, and Ms. Ellen is untouchable — Wendy snaps and warns Ms. Ellen, 'Don't fuck with me.' The next day a squad of armed Iraqi men storms the classroom and exposes Ms. Ellen as a wanted fugitive who seduced their leader; she grabs a sword, accidentally kills Kenny, and is hauled off to be shot into the sun on a rocket. Terrified by his harem of admirers, Garrison has his old nose restored and returns to teaching. In the final scene Wendy hosts a pool party and, speaking fluent Arabic, pays off the Iraqi men with a huge stack of cash and a box aimed at the sun, watching Ms. Ellen's rocket burn up in the sky while Kyle looks on in horror. 'I told her: DON'T FUCK WITH WENDY TESTABURGER!'

Featured characters: Wendy Testaburger, Stan Marsh, Ms. Ellen, Mr. Garrison, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Chef, Principal Victoria, Bebe Stevens.

Locations: South Park Elementary, Tom's Rhinoplasty clinic, Cartman's living room, Wendy's pool party.

Key events & continuity: Wendy's jealousy turns genuinely dangerous for the first time — and Kyle learns she is capable of anything; Ms. Ellen's fate is one of the show's darkest punchlines; Garrison's brief handsomeness confirms his vanity; Kenny dies by stray sword during the classroom raid.

During a fossil dig, Cartman finds a strange stone triangle, tosses it aside, and Kyle picks it up. An archaeologist identifies the markings as Anasazi, Kyle ends up on television with the find, and Cartman immediately wants it back — he breaks into Kyle's bedroom at night to steal it, and Kyle finally just hands it over to end the squabble. Meanwhile film critic Leonard Maltin arrives in town asking Chef whether he has seen Barbra Streisand, warning that if she has seen the news report, the boys are in grave danger. At the bus stop, Streisand lands in her helicopter and demands the Triangle of Zinthar. Maltin explains the stakes to Chef on the drive: Streisand's mother was a jackal, her father an insurance salesman, and she is hunting an ancient relic called the Diamond of Pantheos, which was split into two triangles hidden across the Earth. She dug up one piece years ago; Cartman's triangle is the other. United, they would transform her into Mecha-Streisand, the most dangerous creature ever to walk the Earth. Disguised, Streisand lures the boys to her mountain condo with the promise of money, then ties them up and tortures them with medieval devices and her own singing until Cartman surrenders the triangle. She fuses the two halves into the Diamond of Pantheos and becomes a colossal mechanical dinosaur-songstress who starts leveling South Park. Maltin and Chef free the boys, and Maltin transforms into a giant Ultraman-style robot to fight her — and is quickly beaten. Kenny, fleeing, is strangled by a schoolyard tetherball. Sidney Poitier arrives as a giant Gamera-like turtle and also falls. All seems lost until Robert Smith of The Cure appears, guided by a wristwatch, and morphs into a giant moth. Spotting that Mecha-Streisand's weak point is her nose, Smith lands the Robot Punch, knocking the Diamond of Pantheos loose, then hurls the weakened monster into space, where she explodes. The town cheers its savior — Jesus himself hails Smith — and Kyle shouts that Disintegration is the best album ever. The boys agree the diamond must stay split, since no one should wield that power. It is promptly rediscovered, and the story closes on the boys cowering before a giant Ike Broflovski: Mecha-Ike.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Barbra Streisand (Mecha-Streisand), Leonard Maltin, Chef, Robert Smith, Sidney Poitier.

Locations: the fossil dig, Kyle's bedroom, the bus stop, Streisand's mountain condo, downtown South Park.

Key events & continuity: the Diamond of Pantheos saga — the triangle halves are separated again but already resurfacing; Robert Smith is canonized in-universe as a hero on par with religious figures; Kenny's tetherball death is one of his most random; the Mecha-Ike stinger keeps the threat alive.

entries.n: S01E13 — Cartman's Mom is a Dirty Slut
entries.t:
Stan, Kyle, and Kenny skip school to find Cartman, discover him in his backyard having a tea party with his dolls, and — at Mr. Mackey's request — film the whole thing. That night Cartman asks his mother whether he has a father, and Liane tells him she got pregnant at South Park's 12th Annual Drunken Barn Dance after sleeping with Chief Running Water. Cartman dresses as a Native American and treks to the Ute reservation, where the chief bluntly tells him he is not the father and that Liane is a slut — it was Chef she was with that night, not him. Cartman starts calling Chef 'pops,' but Chef is stunned: he and Liane only kissed, and he serenades the boy with a song about it. The man Liane left with that night, Chef recalls, was actually Mr. Garrison. Meanwhile the boys spot an ad for America's Stupidest Home Videos — Bob Saget is offering ten thousand dollars for the funniest tape — and enter their footage of Cartman's tea party. At the bar, Garrison admits he slept with Liane that night, then asks the room who didn't; only one patron claims innocence, confirming Liane's reputation. Despairing of ever learning the truth, Cartman is offered a way out by Dr. Mephesto: a DNA test that will name his real father, for three thousand dollars he doesn't have. At the bus stop the next day, the boys are tinkering with a go-kart; Kenny gets it running, gets yanked behind it, can't let go, and is dragged through town before landing upside down on train tracks and being hit by a train. That night the boys watch the home-video show: their Cartman tape airs, and the final entry — Kenny getting hit by the train — wins the ten thousand dollars. But the runner-up prize is three thousand, exactly the price of the DNA test. The story cuts to the genetics ranch, where Cartman, Mephesto, Liane, and every possible father are assembled — and just as Mephesto is about to read the name, the broadcast cuts away, promising the answer in four weeks.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Liane Cartman, Chef, Mr. Garrison, Dr. Mephesto, Chief Running Water, Bob Saget.

Locations: Cartman's backyard, the Ute reservation, the town bar, the South Park Genetic Engineering Ranch, the bus stop.

Key events & continuity: the first half of the two-part paternity mystery; Kenny's go-kart death wins the home-video prize; the tea-party tape becomes town legend; Liane's promiscuity is established as the engine of the whole mystery.
k: cartman's mom is a dirty slut

entries.n: S02E01 — Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus
entries.t:
After four weeks of waiting to learn who Cartman's father is, the audience gets no payoff at all: instead, the HBC movie of the week airs — a full-length Terrance and Phillip adventure, Not Without My Anus. It opens in a Canadian courtroom, where Scott, a furious Canadian, is testifying that Terrance murdered Dr. Jeffrey O'Dwyer by beating him repeatedly with a hammer. Phillip's closing argument consists largely of the duo farting so relentlessly that the jury can barely deliver its verdict; Terrance is found not guilty. Outside, Scott vows revenge and takes a call from Saddam Hussein, who proposes a deal: Scott helps him get rid of Terrance and Phillip, and Saddam gets to conquer Canada. Back home, Terrance and Phillip meet Ugly Bob — a Canadian so hideous that only other Canadians (and Iranians) can perceive it — and advise him to wear a paper bag over his head. Terrance receives a letter: his daughter Sally, his child with Celine Dion, has been captured in Tehran. The duo flies to Tehran, rescues Sally with suspicious ease, and returns to find Canada plastered with posters of Saddam. At Celine Dion's house they discover she is carrying on an affair with Ugly Bob, now calling himself Handsome Bob; they rip the bag off and she screams at the truth. The U.S. government gives Saddam three years to pull his troops out of Canada or face bombing, and Saddam starts plotting world domination from his new base. Scott hands Terrance and Phillip a bomb and tells them to strap it on at the big Roughriders-versus-Roughriders football game to stop Saddam — but Phillip counters with 'chemical warfare': mass farting. At halftime, while Celine Dion is forced to sing the Iranian national anthem, the entire stadium dons gas masks and unleashes a flatulence cloud so vast it kills Saddam and his Iranian guards. The Canadians dismember the body and close the film singing their national anthem.

Featured characters: Terrance, Phillip, Scott the Dick, Saddam Hussein, Celine Dion, Ugly Bob (Handsome Bob), Sally.

Locations: the Canadian courthouse, Terrance and Phillip's house, Tehran, the Roughriders football stadium, Karl's Kroff Dinner Palace.

Key events & continuity: the infamous April Fools' bait-and-switch that denied the Cartman paternity payoff; first major appearance of Saddam Hussein, whose ambitions foreshadow the film-era conflicts to come; first appearance of Scott the Dick, Terrance and Phillip's eternal nemesis; Ugly Bob's paper-bag solution becomes a running visual gag.
k: terrance and phillip in not without my anus

entries.n: S02E02 — Cartman's Mom is Still a Dirty Slut
entries.t:
Just as Dr. Mephesto is about to name Cartman's father, Kenny — dead since the previous story — walks back in as if nothing happened. The lights cut out, two gunshots ring through the dark, and when the lights return, Mephesto has been shot. Chef finds a pulse and rushes him to the hospital, where the only staff on duty are Dr. Doctor and Nurse Goodly, a nurse with no arms. A blizzard seals the town in, so no other doctors can get through. Meanwhile the crew of America's Most Wanted arrives to dramatize the shooting, holding auditions for Mephesto, Chef, Barbrady, Garrison, and Kevin. During the reenactment shoot the power fails again, trapping the adults in a small building, and after only a few hungry hours Jimbo proposes cannibalism — they eat Eric Roberts first, then devour the rest of the production crew, who had opposed the idea. Elsewhere, Liane decides she wants to abort Cartman, only to be told at the clinic that it is far too late. Back at the hospital, the generator dies and the only way to restore power is to send someone through a sewer, past possible velociraptors, to reconnect it — Team A (everyone) gets hot cocoa in the lounge while Team B (Kenny alone) does the work. Kenny finds a heated path only after suffering the whole route, discovers a missing wire, jury-rigs the connection himself, and is electrocuted for his trouble — but the power returns and Mephesto survives. At last, gathered in the emergency room, Mephesto reveals the truth: Cartman's father is Mrs. Cartman herself. Liane is a hermaphrodite, with both male and female anatomy, and she got another woman pregnant — which raises a brand-new question: who is Cartman's mother? Is it Ms. Crabtree, Sheila Broflovski, Mayor McDaniels? Cartman, broken by the evening, refuses to pursue it: 'OH, FORGET IT!'

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Liane Cartman, Dr. Mephesto, Chef, Dr. Doctor, Nurse Goodly, Jimbo Kern, Officer Barbrady, Mr. Garrison.

Locations: the genetics ranch, South Park Hospital, the snowbound reenactment building, the abortion clinic.

Key events & continuity: the paternity cliffhanger resolves with the hermaphrodite twist — though much later ('200'/'201') it is revealed the DNA test was tampered with and Cartman's real father is Jack Tenorman, Scott Tenorman's father, making Cartman half-ginger; Kenny's generator run is one of his most thankless deaths; the adults' instant resort to cannibalism becomes a signature town behavior.
k: cartman's mom is still a dirty slut

entries.t:
Mr. Mackey delivers his annual drug lecture — 'drugs are bad, you shouldn't do drugs' — and passes a bag of marijuana around the class so the kids can learn the smell. When the bag vanishes and a police search comes up empty, Mackey is fired on the spot, harassed in the street as a hippie, locked out by his landlord, and ends up drunk in an alley, then tripping on a hobo's spliff and a hippie's LSD until his head becomes a floating balloon. He marries a hippie woman, honeymoons in India, gets abducted by the A-Team, and is 'cured' at the Betty Ford Clinic before returning to class as if nothing happened. Meanwhile Kyle invites the boys to Ike's bris without knowing what a bris is; Stan checks with Chef and several others and bursts in with the news that they are going to 'chop off his wee-wee.' Horrified, Kyle smuggles Ike onto a train to Nebraska and builds a decoy doll, which is promptly eaten by a dog that is then run over by a truck in front of the house. At the dog's funeral, Kyle learns the real shock: Ike is not his biological brother at all — he was adopted from Canada. Kyle decides Ike isn't his 'real' brother and stops caring, then is forced by his grounded-by-parents trip to Nebraska, where they find Ike being used as a table leg in a bar. On the day of the bris, Ike flees to Kyle's room in terror, throws himself into Kyle's arms, and Kyle's heart melts — he defends his little brother fiercely until someone finally explains that a circumcision is just 'snipping the penis a little to make it look bigger.' Relieved, Stan and Cartman immediately decide they want to be circumcised too.

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski, Ike Broflovski, Stan Marsh, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Mr. Mackey, Sheila and Gerald Broflovski, Chef.

Locations: South Park Elementary, the Broflovski home, the alley, the woods, the Nebraska bar, the Betty Ford Clinic.

Key events & continuity: Ike is revealed as Kyle's adopted Canadian brother — a cornerstone of their relationship going forward; Mr. Mackey's drug spiral and rehab become his defining character arc; the boys' misunderstanding of the bris drives the whole plot and ends with Ike circumcised and safe.

When the third-grade class visits the Book Mobile, someone has assaulted a chicken outside it, and Officer Barbrady's investigation collapses the moment he cannot read the note the attacker left behind. Humiliated at a press conference, Barbrady resigns — and with no law enforcement at all, South Park instantly slides into anarchy, proving the town needs even its most incompetent cop. Mayor McDaniels enrolls Barbrady in the boys' class to learn to read, where Mr. Garrison and Mr. Hat mock him mercilessly. The attacker, politely dubbed the 'Chickenlover' since the adults won't say the real word, strikes again. Barbrady earns an A on a Go, Dog, Go! book report and starts enjoying school a little too much, so the mayor speeds up his education and makes the boys his deputies. Cartman takes to patrol on his Big Wheel, enforcing his own brutal justice — this is the first time he bellows 'Respect my authoritah!' — and, in a parody of the show Cops, beats Randy Marsh with a nightstick for alleged speeding. Barbrady pieces the clues together from children's books and predicts the Chickenlover will strike the petting zoo next. The culprit is caught in the act: the Book Mobile driver himself, who started assaulting chickens the moment he learned Barbrady couldn't read — his twisted plan was to force Barbrady to learn, so the officer could experience the magic of reading through the clues. He gifts Barbrady a copy of Atlas Shrugged, Barbrady demonstrates the proper nightstick technique on him, and the boys are relieved of duty. Barbrady closes the story by settling into a hot bath with a good book and giving the camera a long thumbs-up, while Kenny is flattened by a falling tree during the credits.

Featured characters: Officer Barbrady, Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Mayor McDaniels, Mr. Garrison and Mr. Hat, the Book Mobile driver, Randy Marsh.

Locations: the Book Mobile, South Park Elementary, the petting zoo, Barbrady's bathtub.

Key events & continuity: Cartman's 'Respect my authoritah!' debuts and becomes his signature; Barbrady learns to read (and promptly decides reading 'totally sucks ass'); the Book Mobile driver's scheme is one of the show's most deranged motives; Kenny's tree death plays out silently over the credits.

The boys meet the new school nurse, Nurse Gollum, and are horrified to find a dead fetus attached to the side of her head — the result of a fictional condition called Conjoined Twin Myslexia. When Sheila Broflovski hears the boys mocking her, she launches 'Conjoined Twin Myslexia Week,' a town-wide awareness celebration with an honoree population of one. The townspeople don hats that fake the fetus, throw Nurse Gollum a parade, and videotape her constantly. She finally explodes: she doesn't want special treatment or pity, she just wants to be harassed and ridiculed like everybody else in town, and she storms off. The adults call her ungrateful, but the kids are left wondering whether the fetus actually makes her smarter. Running alongside this, the school dodgeball team — with Pip, the British exchange student, as its secret weapon — storms through the state championships in Denver and the nationals in Washington (D.C. forfeits rather than face China) all the way to the world finals in China. Pip's power comes from pure rage: call him French and he becomes unstoppable. Kenny is crushed against a wall by a flying dodgeball and dies. In the final, every South Park player is eliminated until only Pip remains; after Kevin tricks the Chinese team into calling Pip French, Pip wipes out the entire opposing team with a single throw. Nobody cares — by then the whole team has decided dodgeball is stupid — and they head home, leaving Pip's triumph completely uncelebrated.

Featured characters: Nurse Gollum, Sheila Broflovski, Pip Pirrip, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Kevin.

Locations: South Park Elementary (nurse's office, dodgeball courts), Denver, Washington D.C., China.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Nurse Gollum, whose demand to be mocked like everyone else becomes her defining trait; Pip's French-triggered rage is established as his superpower; Kenny's dodgeball death is one of his most abrupt; the town's fetus hats show how fast South Park turns pity into pageantry.

entries.n: S02E06 — The Mexican Staring Frog of Southern Sri Lanka
entries.t:
Assigned to interview Vietnam veterans for a school project, the boys choose Jimbo and Ned, who now host the public-access hunting show Huntin' and Killin'. The two spin a wildly sanitized war story — American camps had amusement-park rides, and they personally defeated the entire Viet Cong — and the boys' report earns an F and detention, because Garrison and Mackey are sure the whole thing was invented. Furious at being lied to, the boys take revenge: they fabricate footage of the legendary Mexican Staring Frog of Southern Sri Lanka, a beast that supposedly kills with a glance, and mail it to Jimbo and Ned, who air it as genuine. Huntin' and Killin' gets a ratings bump — which starts draining viewers from the rival show, Jesus and Pals. Desperate, that show's producer retools it into trashy scandal TV over Jesus's objections. Jimbo and Ned head into the wild with a photographer veteran to hunt the frog, while the boys plant a fake one; Ned takes one look at it and collapses into a fear-induced coma. In the hospital, the guilt-ridden boys confess everything, and the producer arranges for all of them to appear on Jesus and Pals — where she secretly coaches them to lie on air for ratings, getting Jimbo to call Stan a drug-addicted Satan-worshipper and Stan to claim Jimbo molested him. The engineered screaming match finally makes Jesus snap: he roars 'Shut the fuck up!' at the entire studio, uncovers the producer's scheming, helps Jimbo and the boys make peace (Jimbo admits he embellished, but never meant to get them in trouble), and fires the producer — sending her straight to Hell, where she meets Satan and Saddam Hussein, a glimpse of conflicts to come.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Jimbo Kern, Ned Gerblansky, Jesus, the Jesus and Pals producer.

Locations: South Park Elementary, the Huntin' and Killin' studio, the wilderness, the hospital, the Jesus and Pals set.

Key events & continuity: the Staring Frog hoax becomes the boys' signature revenge scheme; Jesus's talk show is established as a ratings-chasing mess; the producer's damnation quietly foreshadows the Satan-and-Saddam storyline; Ned's coma-from-fright shows how fragile he is.
k: the mexican staring frog of southern sri lanka

entries.n: S02E07 — City on the Edge of Forever (Flashbacks)
entries.t:
A detour along a mountain pass leaves the school bus teetering on the edge of a cliff. Ms. Crabtree climbs out to find help, warning the kids not to leave the bus because a big scary monster will eat them, and the stranded children pass the time by reminiscing — except every memory is wrong. In their retellings, Stan kisses Wendy instead of vomiting on her, Kenny kills Death instead of the reverse, Scuzzlebutt's leg is played by Brent Musburger instead of Patrick Duffy, and Mr. Garrison guns down Kathie Lee Gifford as an alien. Every recollection ends with the characters eating ice cream, followed by the narrator's 'Now that's what I call a sticky situation!' and laughter — until someone points out what actually happened. Some memories aren't even from South Park: one kid recalls Fonzie jumping buses. When a boy in a red Starfleet uniform tries to leave, a genuine giant black monster bursts out, eats him, and lays siege to the bus, carrying off Kenny. Meanwhile Ms. Crabtree's rescue mission goes sideways: she falls in with Marcus (or Mitch — his name keeps changing), a roofie-peddling Elvis impersonator, who takes her to a comedy club where she heckles Carrot Top into stardom-by-insult, lands an agent, and becomes a stand-up comedian, appearing on The Tonight Show and completely forgetting the children. Back home, Mr. Mackey convinces the parents their kids ran away, and they humiliate themselves on television begging them to come home. In the final flashback, Cartman misremembers identifying his father as John Elway; Kyle corrects him ('I thought your father was your mother 'cause she had a penis'), Cartman lunges at him, and the bus tips over the cliff, splitting in two and landing in a gigantic tub of ice cream. Cartman wakes up in his own bed, tells his mother about the bizarre dream over a breakfast of beetles — and then Stan wakes up in his bed: it was his dream all along. He calls Kyle, who calls the dream messed up and invites him to Happy Burger. Ms. Crabtree and Marcus/Mitch are last seen sitting together by Stark's Pond, in no hurry to leave the dream.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Ms. Crabtree, Marcus/Mitch, Mr. Mackey, Craig.

Locations: the teetering school bus, the cliffside, the comedy club, The Tonight Show, Stark's Pond.

Key events & continuity: the clip-show-that-isn't — every flashback is deliberately misremembered; Cartman's John Elway father-memory quietly plants a seed paid off seasons later; the ice-cream tub landing becomes a surreal touchstone; the whole story is revealed as Stan's dream, with Ms. Crabtree seemingly choosing to stay inside it.
k: city on the edge of forever (flashbacks)

entries.t:
Summer arrives and Mr. Garrison refuses to dismiss class until someone returns Mr. Hat; the instant he turns his back, everyone bolts except Pip, who has summer school anyway. The boys set out to buy fireworks for the Fourth of July and learn that Colorado has banned everything — after a kid in North Park blew his hand off — except black snakes, which they consider incredibly lame. Jimbo and Ned volunteer to smuggle real fireworks in from Mexico, but at the border Jimbo forgets to answer 'no' when asked if he's carrying explosives, and both are arrested. Mayor McDaniels, desperate to salvage the town celebration, seizes on a loophole: snakes are legal, and no law says how big a snake can be. The town builds the world's largest black snake in a giant dish ringed with flamethrowers. Meanwhile Mr. Garrison visits a psychiatrist, Dr. Katz, who explains that Mr. Hat is the outlet for his repressed homosexuality — and is then killed when the giant snake smashes through his window. At a sauna, Brett Favre meets Mr. Hat, whose eyes move on their own, suggesting the puppet might be alive. On the Fourth, the snake is lit and grows out of control, rampaging through town. The boys call Chef for help, but he's vacationing in Aruba and tells them to fudge themselves. Jimbo and Ned arrive with the smuggled fireworks, which are set off into the snake, impaling it; it rains black ash over South Park. Cartman, at his swimming lesson, finally reaches the deep end just as the first-graders pile in and turn the whole pool yellow. With no snow, the town plays in the ash instead. Mr. Garrison returns with Mr. Hat's replacement — Mr. Twig — and Chef comes home to find everyone coated in black soot, assumes they're in blackface, and orders them to line up for a whipping.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Mr. Garrison, Mr. Hat, Mr. Twig, Jimbo Kern, Ned Gerblansky, Mayor McDaniels, Chef, Dr. Katz, Pip.

Locations: South Park Elementary, the Mexican border, the mayor's office, the Fourth of July fairground, the swimming pool, Aruba (phone call).

Key events & continuity: Mr. Hat is replaced by Mr. Twig (temporarily); Garrison's repressed homosexuality is named outright; the 'It's coming right for us' smugglers get arrested by their own forgetfulness; the ash-snow swap becomes a visual signature of the story.

Robert Redford decides the Sundance Film Festival has ruined Park City, Utah, and moves the whole thing to South Park. The quiet mountain town is overrun with pretentious, tofu-eating film lovers, and Mr. Garrison marches his class off to see an independent film and write about it. The festival's waste overwhelms the sewers, and Mr. Hankey — who lives down there — starts dying as his delicate ecosystem collapses. The boys climb into the sewer, run into Mr. Garrison snorkeling in the sewage ('just hanging out'), and find Mr. Hankey, who explains the corruption below mirrors the corruption above. Chef realizes his own recipe-selling has helped ruin the town. Kyle presents Mr. Hankey to the festival organizers, who mistake him for a movie pitch. Cartman starts selling Mr. Hankey T-shirts for a tidy profit. At the hospital, Mr. Hankey flatlines; Kyle wonders if he'll go to Heaven, Chef hopes not, and then revives him with one of his Chocolate Salty Balls. They confront Robert Redford, who hurls Mr. Hankey at a wall; a second Salty Ball brings him back. Donning a wizard hat, Mr. Hankey summons a tornado of sewage that flushes the entire festival out of town — Redford and his aide drown in it — leaving South Park saved but completely coated in waste. Wendy, who spent the festival begging Stan to watch films with her, apologizes. Cartman closes with his lesson: being a sellout is sweet, because money means never having to hang out with poor losers again. 'So screw you guys, I'm going home.'

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski, Stan Marsh, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Mr. Hankey, Chef, Mr. Garrison, Wendy Testaburger, Robert Redford, Mayor McDaniels.

Locations: the Sundance-turned-South-Park festival grounds, the sewers (Mr. Hankey's home), the hospital, the town square.

Key events & continuity: Mr. Hankey returns and his sewer ecosystem is established; Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls debut as a miraculous cure; Cartman's T-shirt hustle shows his sellout philosophy in action; Redford's drowning ends the festival for good.

When twelve-year-old Shelley Marsh comes down with chickenpox, the hospital warns that the disease is far more dangerous the older you get — and Randy and Sharon decide the younger boys should catch it now on purpose. Kenny gets sick first, so the parents stage a forced sleepover at the McCormicks' to expose Stan, Kyle, and Cartman. At the house, Carol McCormick lets slip that Stuart and Gerald used to be close friends until Gerald became a lawyer and climbed out of poverty while Stuart stayed poor; the friendship quietly died. After the sleepover, Stan and Cartman break out in spots but Kyle stays healthy, so his parents arrange a second sleepover and Sheila subjects him to a gauntlet of exposure tricks. Kyle overhears his mother on the phone with the doctor, realizes the whole thing was a setup, and runs away. Sheila secretly engineers a fishing trip to reunite Stuart and Gerald; it collapses into a screaming fight about money. The furious boys ask Chef how to get revenge and give their parents herpes; Chef points them to Frida, an elderly prostitute who, for a fee, contaminates the parents' belongings. Kyle finally catches chickenpox and collapses, waking up in the hospital. The parents explain they only wanted to protect them, the boys confess about the herpes, and everyone — including a reconciled Stuart and Gerald — laughs it off together. Then Kenny suddenly dies of the chickenpox.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Randy and Sharon Marsh, Gerald and Sheila Broflovski, Stuart and Carol McCormick, Shelley Marsh, Chef, Frida.

Locations: the McCormick home, the hospital, the fishing spot, Frida's corner of town.

Key events & continuity: the Stuart-Gerald friendship and class divide is established as a long-running thread; the boys weaponize herpes against their own parents and get away with it; Kenny's death from an ordinary childhood illness is one of his least spectacular — which is the joke.

entries.n: S02E11 — Roger Ebert Should Lay off the Fatty Foods
entries.t:
When Stan complains that they never do anything normal, Mr. Garrison announces a field trip to the new planetarium. Inside, the laser star show takes a strange turn and quietly hypnotizes the entire class — they all walk out desperate to go back. Cartman, meanwhile, spots the Cheesy Poofs van outside holding auditions for a TV commercial, makes the cut, and advances toward his one second of fame. The kids return to the planetarium again and again until they're volunteering there in a full trance. On the bus, an escaped, wild-eyed kid named Van Gelder rants about the planetarium and is hauled off to Nurse Gollum; Mr. Mackey tries a mind-to-mind technique on him and learns the truth about the hypnosis. Stan and Kyle sneak into the projection booth to test the machine on Kenny: low settings do nothing, but cranked to maximum, the hypnosis blows his head clean off. They take their findings to Officer Barbrady and ask him to arrest the planetarium's owner, Dr. Tristan Adams — but Barbrady wanders into the laser field himself and emerges convinced he is Elvis Presley. Cartman is briefly ecstatic to see himself on the Cheesy Poofs ad, then crushed to learn none of his friends watched it because they were all at the planetarium. Mr. Mackey arrives to investigate and is captured for hypnosis along with Stan and Kyle. Just as they're sinking into the light, Cartman storms in, furious about being ignored, and smashes the laser device — it swings around and blasts Dr. Adams point-blank, wiping his mind completely. Stan and Kyle marvel at the machine's power; Cartman is simply thrilled to be the hero for once.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Dr. Tristan Adams, Officer Barbrady, Mr. Mackey, Van Gelder, Nurse Gollum.

Locations: the planetarium, the school bus, the nurse's office, the Cheesy Poofs audition van.

Key events & continuity: Cartman's Cheesy Poofs commercial is his first brush with showbiz; Dr. Adams's mind-wipe ends the hypnosis scheme; Kenny's head-explosion is one of his most gruesome; Barbrady-as-Elvis becomes a running gag.
k: roger ebert should lay off the fatty foods

entries.t:
Wendy tells Stan to build a clubhouse so they can play Truth or Dare — and to set Kyle up with Bebe — so Stan recruits his dad Randy as construction help. In the kitchen, Sharon drops her wedding ring down the sink, Randy fishes for it, and after a small argument he accidentally calls her a terrible name; she walks out. At school, Bebe passes Kyle a note confessing her crush, but Stan is caught holding it and forced to read it aloud, so the whole class hears what sounds like Stan declaring his attraction to Kyle. Mr. Mackey summons both sets of parents, and Randy and Sharon's argument curdles into an actual separation. Sharon promptly introduces Stan to her new boyfriend Roy, an insufferable nuisance. Meanwhile Cartman and Kenny, shut out of the clubhouse, build their own — the Ewok Village 2000 — which is immediately overrun when Kenny lures in two teenage girls who invite all their friends; the party spirals into a mosh pit that tramples Kenny to death while Cartman shrieks that nobody will play Truth or Dare. Stan's clubhouse finally gets finished with Chef's coaching (play truth first, save dare for later), and Kyle is dared to kiss Bebe — he does, screams in horror, and flees. Fed up with Roy, Stan follows the wisdom of a Fat Abbott cartoon: leave a note luring the nuisance stepdad to a meeting spot, then set a bear trap. Roy takes the bait and is left dangling; Sharon and Randy follow the note too, and the clubhouse reminds them of playing Truth or Dare as kids — Sharon dares Randy to make love to her, and they reconcile. The next day at the bus stop, Bebe tells Kyle she's leaving Clyde for him, and the clubhouse hosts its first real game: Wendy, Bebe, Clyde, and Stan, where Stan's dare is shoving a twig up his urethra. Roy is still hanging in the trap as the credits roll.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Wendy Testaburger, Bebe Stevens, Randy and Sharon Marsh, Roy, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Chef, Mr. Mackey, Clyde.

Locations: the Marsh home, the half-built clubhouse, the Ewok Village 2000, South Park Elementary, the bus stop.

Key events & continuity: Randy and Sharon's separation-and-reconciliation becomes a template for their marriage; Roy's bear-trap fate is pure Fat Abbott justice; Kyle and Bebe's romance begins; Kenny's mosh-pit trampling is one of his most chaotic deaths.

The 14th Annual Cow Days carnival rolls into town, and the boys fixate on the grand prize at a ball-toss booth: Terrance and Phillip dolls. The game is flagrantly rigged — the balls are bigger than the hole, which is a picture of Jennifer Love Hewitt's open mouth — and Kyle burns through his money, cries shenanigans, and gets Officer Barbrady to inspect it. The stall owner hands Kyle a smaller ball that actually fits, then pays out in toothpicks: seven toothpicks trade up for the dolls. Broke, the boys enter Cartman in a bull-riding contest after he wastes their cash on joke rides like the Chamber of Farts. When Kyle pegs the practice bull's testicles with a snowball, the animal goes berserk and flings Cartman headfirst into the snow, giving him total amnesia — he wakes up convinced he's Ming Lee, a Vietnamese prostitute, and starts propositioning every adult man he meets. The boys enter him anyway; clinging on in a daze, he sets a new world record and wins the prize money, while Kenny is gored to death by the bull's horn. Meanwhile the town's cows steal the giant new cow clock, Jimbo blames two out-of-town game-show winners, Tom and Mary, and has them arrested — then everyone forgets them and they starve to skeletal death in their cell. Jimbo and Ned track the cows to a cliffside cult worshipping the clock; the FBI orders them to freeze, and the cows hurl themselves off the cliff one by one. The boys pour their winnings into the ball game, the owner 'generously' hands over the dolls for all of it, and Kyle realizes they're cheap rip-offs — the whole town cries shenanigans and riots. Cartman snaps out of it with only a hazy memory of a dream about romancing Leonardo DiCaprio, who pulls up in a limousine to thank Ming Lee personally.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman (as Ming Lee), Kenny McCormick, Jimbo Kern, Ned Gerblansky, Officer Barbrady, Mayor McDaniels, Tom and Mary, the cows.

Locations: the Cow Days carnival, the ball-toss booth, the bull-riding arena, the hospital, the cliffside, the jail.

Key events & continuity: Cartman's Ming Lee amnesia becomes one of his most quoted personas; the mass cow suicide is played as a cult tragedy; Tom and Mary's forgotten starvation is the town's darkest bureaucratic joke; 'shenanigans' enters the town lexicon.

Cartman can't get Alanis Morissette's new hit 'Stinky Britches' out of his head — until Chef hears it and recognizes it as a song he wrote twenty years ago. When Chef and the boys confront the record company, its executive has his lawyer, Johnnie Cochran, sue Chef for harassment instead. In court, Cochran deploys the infamous Chewbacca Defense, baffling the jury into ruling against Chef: he has twenty-four hours to pay up or serve four years in prison. Chef plans to earn the money and use it to hire Cochran to sue the label back. Meanwhile Mr. Garrison is being tormented by someone trying to murder his new puppet Mr. Twig — he catches Mr. Hat on a hidden camera, confronts him near-naked, hurls him out the door, and gets arrested by Barbrady for public nudity. Chef shows the boys his photo album: he personally mentored half the music industry. The boys hawk sweets to every famous musician who remembers Chef, but between Chef's own fundraising (which mostly involves propositioning the town's women) and the boys' candy money, they fall far short, and Chef is hauled off to prison — sharing a cell with Garrison — until Mr. Hat smashes through the wall driving a rescue vehicle. The boys organize 'Chef Aid' in the town square, with Cartman performing his German Dance to draw a crowd; at first nobody comes, but then every musician who bought the sweets shows up, and the concert explodes into a full-blown festival. Cochran, moved by the spectacle, takes Chef's case for free, and Chef finally gets his rightful credit on 'Stinky Britches.' Garrison, asked by Mr. Twig whether he still loves Mr. Hat, admits it — then ditches Twig and goes back to his original puppet.

Featured characters: Chef, Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Johnnie Cochran, Mr. Garrison, Mr. Hat, Mr. Twig, Alanis Morissette (song), the record executive.

Locations: the record company, the courtroom, the prison, the town square (Chef Aid stage), Chef's photo-album living room.

Key events & continuity: the Chewbacca Defense debuts and becomes the show's most famous legal joke; Chef's past as a music-industry mentor is established; Mr. Hat proves he can drive and stage prison breaks; Garrison definitively chooses Mr. Hat over Mr. Twig.

Sharon's Aunt Flo comes for her monthly visit, bringing Shelley a giant stereo and Stan a strange goldfish. Cartman, meanwhile, keeps showing up either with or without a beard and a wildly different personality — bearded Cartman is polite and helpful, beardless Cartman is extra hostile and says 'hella' constantly. At night, threatening messages appear on Stan's goldfish bowl; Stan covers it with a shirt, wakes screaming to find a corpse on his floor, and Sharon — convinced Stan is the killer — buries the body in the garden to cover it up. The bodies keep coming: the goldfish is murdering people. Sharon takes Officer Barbrady hostage in the basement when he starts asking questions. The boys try to return the fish to the pet store and discover a literal portal to a parallel universe behind it — the source of both the killer goldfish and the bearded, well-mannered Cartman. The fish kills Kenny and Aunt Flo before they can act. At the pumpkin-carving contest, which the boys win, an evil bearded Stan and Kyle appear and unleash all the parallel-world pets; the real Stan and Kyle wrestle the portal device away from their doubles and send them back. Then comes the hard choice: the bearded Cartman explains how awful his counterpart is, and the boys vote to banish the normal Cartman to the evil universe. He rips the beard off the other Cartman to prove which is which, gets shoved through anyway screaming 'Screw you guys!', and the good Cartman stays — immediately taunting the boys about how hella stupid they are. Randy frees Barbrady, and Sharon finally realizes the goldfish committed all the murders.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman (both versions), Kenny McCormick, Sharon Marsh, Randy Marsh, Aunt Flo, Officer Barbrady, the goldfish.

Locations: the Marsh home, the bus stop, the pet store (and its parallel-universe portal), the pumpkin-carving contest.

Key events & continuity: the parallel universe and its 'evil' bearded doubles are established; the good Cartman briefly replaces the real one; Sharon's willingness to bury bodies for Stan shows her maternal extremes; the goldfish is confirmed as the killer.

The boys are invited to Cartman's grandmother Mabel's house in Nebraska for Christmas. Stan's mother forbids him to go; he argues, gets sent to bed without supper, and sneaks out the window anyway. After an agonizing car ride sound tracked by Cartman and Liane's singalongs, they arrive to find Cartman's entire extended family: all overweight, all talking like Cartman, all using his catchphrases, all eating like pigs. At dinner, Uncle Howard appears via satellite from prison, and Stan declares his parents dead to him. That night the boys are woken by a break-in — it's Howard, escaped from prison with his cellmate, Charlie Manson. The next day the family won't take the boys to the mall, so Manson offers them a ride — he wants some action. At the mall, Kyle discovers the Mr. Hankey meet-and-greet is just a guy in a costume; enraged, he rips the head off, the kids riot, and the police arrive. Manson catches a Mr. Hankey Christmas special modeled on the Grinch — a nasty person becoming nice — and is genuinely moved by it. He returns having given Kenny a smiley-face tattoo. The police spot Manson and a car chase erupts back to Mabel's house. Stan's parents, learning he disobeyed them, drive to Nebraska to punish him. Cornered, Manson listens to a lecture about family, decides to turn himself in, and apologizes to every family he ever tore apart, hoping to prove crime never pays. Kenny is sent out waving a white flag of surrender and is gunned down. In prison, Manson finishes writing another book and turns out the light — which clicks back on as the entire Cartman clan and the boys surprise him with 'Hark! The Herald Angels Sing.' Stan turns to Kyle: that was the most messed-up chain of events ever.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Charlie Manson, Uncle Howard, Mabel Cartman, Liane Cartman, Sharon and Randy Marsh, the Cartman extended family.

Locations: Mabel Cartman's house in Nebraska, the prison, the mall, the highway car chase.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Cartman's extended family (all Cartman clones); Charlie Manson is portrayed as a goofy, redeemable oddball rather than a monster; Kenny's white-flag death is one of his most ironic; Stan's rebellion against his parents ends with him choosing family anyway.

Threatened with firing if he can't prove he teaches current events, Mr. Garrison assigns reports — and Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny get paired with Tweek, a jittery, over-caffeinated kid who swears gnomes are stealing his underpants. At the Tweek family coffeehouse, a Harbucks representative tries to buy out Mr. Tweak, first with a briefcase of crimsonite, then with half a million dollars; refused twice, he vows to open a Harbucks right next door and crush the little shop. The boys spend the night at Tweek's to write about the gnomes, but Mr. Tweak hands them a pre-written screed against big corporations instead — while the actual underpants gnomes sneak in and steal Tweek's underwear right under their noses. The boys present Mr. Tweak's report as their own; the town committee buys it, sides with the coffeehouse, and Garrison orders the boys to ride the lie to the end. They become poster children for the anti-corporate cause, doing talk shows and ads while Mrs. Tweak fumes about exploiting kids for politics. The mayor schedules a debate and a vote on Proposition 10. Desperate for material, the boys follow a gnome home to its village and ask how the gnome corporation works: Phase One, collect underpants; Phase Three, profit. There is no Phase Two. At the vote, the boys confess they didn't write the report — and then deliver the real lesson: big corporations aren't evil; without them there'd be no computers or cars, and Harbucks itself started as a tiny shop that simply made better coffee. Mrs. Tweak applauds, admits nobody ever actually tried the Harbucks coffee, and the whole crowd — including Mr. Tweak — tastes it and loves it. The Harbucks rep hires Mr. Tweak to run the new store on the spot.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Tweek Tweak, Mr. and Mrs. Tweak, the Underpants Gnomes, Mr. Garrison and Mr. Hat, Mayor McDaniels, the Harbucks rep.

Locations: Tweek Bros. Coffeehouse, the Harbucks construction site, the gnome village, the town debate hall.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Tweek and his parents; the Underpants Gnomes debut with their infamous missing Phase Two; the 'Phase One / Phase Three: profit' business plan becomes a cultural punchline; Harbucks wins on merit, not malice.

After watching the Crocodile Hunter, Cartman inspires the boys to hunt crocodiles in the mountains. Kyle falls down a hole, Stan rappels in to rescue him, and they spot a human figure frozen in the ice. Dr. Mephesto thaws him out in his lab: the man has been frozen since 1996. Kyle wants to name him Steve; Stan wants Gorak; Steve wins, infuriating Stan. The man — actually named Larry — is installed in a lovingly recreated 1996 habitat complete with Ace of Base, while federal agents circle, wanting to weaponize him. Sightseers pay to gawk at him like a caveman, though he's only two years out of date, and his loneliness curdles when he visits his wife and finds she has remarried and had children who are impossibly older than two years' absence allows. Stan hatches a rescue plan, breaks into the lab at night, and finds Kyle already there doing the same thing; they agree to settle their Steve-versus-Gorak feud with a fight at four o'clock the next day. Kyle tells Larry about Des Moines, Iowa — a town so behind the times it's practically still 1996 — and they smuggle him to the train station. Mephesto, the feds, and Steve Irwin himself give chase; the pursuers land a helicopter on the tracks, the train plows into it, and Irwin is killed in the crash, giving Larry his opening. He escapes in the helicopter and lectures the boys on the value of friendship; Stan and Kyle make up, united at last in their shared opinion that Cartman sucks as a best friend.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Larry (the 'prehistoric' ice man), Dr. Mephesto, Steve Irwin, the federal agents.

Locations: the mountain ice cave, Mephesto's lab, the 1996 habitat, the train station, Des Moines, Iowa (mentioned).

Key events & continuity: Stan and Kyle's friendship is tested and reaffirmed over the Steve/Gorak naming feud; Larry's two-year freeze is treated as prehistory by everyone; Steve Irwin dies in the train-helicopter crash; the closing consensus — Cartman sucks as a best friend — becomes canon.

Ms. Stevens recruits Mr. Garrison's class for 'Getting Gay With Kids,' a children's choir touring to save the rainforest. Only Kenny is interested — he's smitten with a choir girl named Kelly, who can't quite catch his name and calls him Lenny, Benny, and Johnny. The boys mouth off, and Mr. Mackey punishes them by signing them up for the tour. In San José, Costa Rica, Cartman is horrified to learn it's a poor country and insults everything in sight; Ms. Stevens bribes him quiet with promises of ice cream. The choir performs for the Costa Rican president (via Mackey's Spanish), with Kyle audibly off the beat. On the rainforest tour, Cartman whacks every wonder of nature with a stick to 'assert his authoritah,' the guide is eaten alive by a coral snake mid-lecture about how snakes fear humans, and Cartman barely escapes the same snake. Lost in the jungle, the group is menaced by revolutionaries ('We're not getting gay with any kids'), caught between rebels and government troops, and then captured by the Yanagopa tribe, who get stuck in quicksand with them and plan to sacrifice Ms. Stevens. Cartman, meanwhile, has wandered off and befriended a deforestation crew, demanding medium-spicy chicken wings. He arrives with the bulldozers just in time to save everyone. Back in San José, Kelly finally agrees to be Kenny's girlfriend despite the distance — and Kenny is immediately struck dead by lightning. Stan and Kyle deliver the traditional line, but Kelly asks who 'they' are, since lightning killed him, not people; the boys can only stammer, 'You know. They. They're bastards.' Kelly performs CPR and actually brings Kenny back, stunning them. The choir performs its song with rewritten lyrics denouncing the rainforest, Ms. Stevens now agreeing it's a horrible place. The story closes with a public-service message warning that rainforests produce cancer-causing compounds that kill hundreds yearly — and urging viewers to help destroy them.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Kelly, Ms. Stevens, Mr. Mackey, the Costa Rican president, the Yanagopa tribe.

Locations: South Park Elementary, San José (Costa Rica), the rainforest, the Yanagopa village.

Key events & continuity: Kenny's lightning death is undone by Kelly's CPR — a rare resurrection; Kelly becomes Kenny's first real girlfriend; Ms. Stevens's activist-to-anti-rainforest conversion is total; Cartman's deforestation alliance is peak Cartman.

While the boys are shopping for a 'nerection' for Kyle's dad — Kyle misheard the word 'resurrection' at church — Kenny spontaneously combusts on the sidewalk, reduced to a pile of ash. Panic spreads as more townspeople explode: Mayor McDaniels puts Randy Marsh, the town geologist, in charge of solving it, dangling the title of South Park's most beloved man. At Kenny's funeral, the priest closes with a prayer about the Denver Broncos, and Father Maxi ropes the boys into performing the Stations of the Cross. Kyle learns Jesus was resurrected, hears 'nerection,' and volunteers; Cartman plays Jesus in the performance and ends up crucified in the wilderness for real when Stan and Kyle abandon him there to fetch the 'nerection' for Gerald. Randy's investigation leads him to a breakthrough: spontaneous combustion is caused by holding in farts, and people in relationships are the most at risk because couples fart less. He orders the town to fart regularly, becomes a hero, and wins the Nobel Prize — infuriating Dr. Mephesto, who believes his seven-assed Galapagos turtle deserved it. But the town's constant farting tears a hole in the ozone layer, temperatures soar, and Mephesto goes on Jesus and Pals to blame Randy, turning the town against him. Meanwhile a group of prostitutes hires Gerald to sue Randy, and the stress gives Gerald skin problems — which somehow finally gives him an erection, letting him 'set things right' with Sheila. Randy refines his theory: farting is necessary, but only in moderation — at appropriate times, or when it's really funny. The town cheers him again. Stan and Kyle finally remember Cartman, still nailed up after three weeks, alive only because he survived on his own fat — and now shockingly thin. He swears revenge the moment he gets down.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Randy Marsh, Gerald Broflovski, Dr. Mephesto, Mayor McDaniels, Father Maxi.

Locations: the church, the Marsh home, the wilderness cross, the Nobel ceremony (mentioned), the Jesus and Pals studio.

Key events & continuity: Randy wins the Nobel Prize for fart science; Mephesto's seven-assed turtle becomes his eternal grievance; Cartman's three-week crucifixion leaves him emaciated and vengeful; the moderation doctrine becomes town policy.

Cartman visits the eye doctor, is mocked for his weight, and ends up in enormous glasses; a botched laser surgery lands him in bed. Meanwhile the boys' world collapses: Chef has quit the cafeteria, replaced by a skinny, illiterate oddball named Mr. Derp, and Chef himself is engaged to a woman named Veronica — dull, domesticated, and utterly changed. Veronica croons a hypnotic song the boys despise, and Chef stands them up for their after-school ball game. Desperate, they ask Mr. Garrison for advice; he declares Veronica is probably a succubus, a demoness from Hell who drains the life out of men. At Chef's house they meet his parents, Thomas and Nellie McElroy, visiting from Scotland and full of alleged encounters with the Loch Ness Monster. Veronica bakes Cartman a pie and sweet-talks the boys — until her face warps into a demon's and she hisses that nothing will stop the wedding. The boys research all night and learn the counter-ritual: sing her song ('The Morning After') backwards. At the wedding they stay quiet until the vows, then cue Cartman's tape recorder — but he dozes off from exhaustion, the tape jams, and when Kenny tries to fix it, the succubus drops on him and crushes him dead. The tape sputters back to life, the boys finish the reversed song, and Veronica is banished shrieking to the depths of Hell. Chef, seeing what he nearly married, thanks them sincerely. A groggy Cartman asks, 'Is Kenny OK?' — and later, at the eye clinic, gets his vision fixed with a transplant: Kenny's frozen head.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Chef, Veronica (the succubus), Thomas and Nellie McElroy, Mr. Garrison and Mr. Hat, Mr. Derp.

Locations: the eye doctor's office, Chef's house, the school cafeteria, the wedding chapel.

Key events & continuity: first appearance of Chef's parents and Mr. Derp; the succubus is genuinely defeated by reversed music; Kenny is crushed mid-ceremony and his frozen head becomes Cartman's eye donor — one of the show's most grotesque gags.

Camping at Stark's Pond, the boys chase a strange creature into Jimbo and Ned's yard and trap it in a cage. Inside the house, Ned has lost his voice box and Jimbo is ordering him a replacement. The creature turns out to be a female Jakovasaur, a supposedly near-extinct species, and City Hall — with the Department of the Interior looking on — decides the town must protect it. Then a male is found, and the town stages an elaborate mating campaign, building the pair a love nest, only to discover Jakovasaurs have no genitals at all. Dr. Mephesto improvises: he collects a sample from the male, Jakov, and artificially inseminates the female, Hope, who soon gives birth to an enormous, deafening litter. Everyone in town except Cartman finds the creatures unbearable. When the Department of the Interior prepares to leave, it deputizes Cartman as an official member with authority — 'authoritahh' — over all living things around South Park. The mayor's real plan surfaces on a televised game show: invite Jakov's family to compete against Officer Barbrady, declare Jakov the winner regardless (Barbrady actually wins on the creatures' stupidity), and ship all fifty-plus Jakovasaurs straight to France. Stan and Kyle are sent to distract Cartman by having him inspect a rare deer in the mountains — it's Kenny wearing antlers — and a bear promptly mauls Kenny to death. Cartman sees through the ruse and races to the airport, but he's too late. Ned finally receives his new voice box and addresses Cartman in a posh accent (after an Irish one), leaving everyone unsatisfied. In France, the Jakovasaurs settle in happily; Jakov trips into a café, and the French declare he reminds them of Jerry Lewis.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Jakov and Hope, Jimbo Kern, Ned Gerblansky, Dr. Mephesto, Mayor McDaniels, Officer Barbrady.

Locations: Stark's Pond, Jimbo and Ned's house, City Hall, Mephesto's lab, the airport, France.

Key events & continuity: the Jakovasaurs are exiled to France, removing them from town continuity; Cartman briefly wields real federal authority; Ned cycles through replacement voice boxes; Kenny's antler-deer disguise ends in a bear mauling.

In shop class, the boys can't agree whether Tweek or Craig is the bigger troublemaker, so they bet five dollars on a fight between them. Cartman tells Craig that Tweek called him a 'poop eater'; Stan and Kyle tell Tweek that Craig called him a chicken and challenged him. Both agree to fight after school — then both go home without fighting. The lies escalate: Craig is told Tweek called his guinea pig Stripe a sex toy. Meanwhile Kenny, the only boy in home economics, is doing well with the girls. The shop teacher, Mr. Adler, is falling apart: his fiancée died when her skywriter plane exploded and crashed into the ocean, and he copes with nicotine gum and staring at her photograph, refusing the home-ec teacher's advances. The boys stage a pre-fight press conference in the cafeteria; Cartman and Kyle start brawling with each other instead, and nobody notices because everyone's focused on the main event. Stan and Kyle train Tweek to box with Jimbo and Ned's help (Tweek flattens Ned); Cartman teaches Craig sumo wrestling and defeats him by shoving his backside into Craig's face. Out of nicotine gum and out of hope, Mr. Adler decides to end it all on the shop saw belt — just as Kenny, flunked out of home ec for poor performance, transfers into shop class and walks in. The Tweek-Craig fight finally erupts, crashes through the classroom wall, interrupts Adler's suicide attempt, and flings Kenny into a jigsaw and a pile of rusty nails, killing him. In the wreckage Kenny's face becomes a vision of Adler's dead fiancée, who tells him the happy times matter, not how someone left — and Adler, seeing his dead grandmother and uncle too, decides to live. Tweek and Craig end up hospitalized; the boys visit, apologize, admit the insults were all invented — then start the fight up again by claiming each boy's parents trash-talked the other.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Tweek Tweak, Craig Tucker, Mr. Adler, Jimbo Kern, Ned Gerblansky.

Locations: the shop classroom, the home-ec room, the cafeteria, the hospital.

Key events & continuity: first major appearance of Craig and of Mr. Adler, whose grief arc resolves here; Tweek and Craig's rivalry is born entirely from the boys' lies; Kenny's jigsaw death interrupts a suicide and accidentally saves a life.

Mr. Garrison introduces the class to Peetie the Sexual Harassment Panda, a mascot who lectures the kids on harassment law. Days later, Stan calls Cartman an 'ass-sucker'; Cartman learns that counts as sexual harassment and sues Stan, hiring Gerald Broflovski as his lawyer. In court, Cartman weeps that Stan wanted oral intercourse with his mouth, Gerald declares his client too traumatized to continue, and Stan's only defense is being eight — the judge rules for Cartman and orders him compensated from Stan's assets. Gerald smells bigger money: sue the school for failing to stop it. At trial, Garrison first claims ignorance, then admits under questioning that he heard the insult and did nothing because he agrees Cartman is an ass-sucker; Principal Victoria accidentally confesses to an unrelated killing while panicking on the stand. Peetie testifies the school is liable. Cartman wins $1.3 million and does a victory dance, Gerald expands his house into a mansion, and the school — gutted by the payout — downgrades to desks-less rooms where Garrison writes with a rusty nail. The lawsuit plague spreads: Bebe wins $1.6 million, Clyde $1.4 million, Pip sues Cartman for half his belongings, Craig sues Wendy for $2.1 million, Mr. Mackey sues Tweek for $2 million. The school hemorrhages $32 million and starts layoffs; Peetie — real name Tom Morris — is fired and washes up on the Island of Misfit Mascots. The boys visit him there, where a falcon mascot demonstrates his act by feeding Kenny to a giant magnet-and-fan contraption that shreds him. Convinced, Peetie changes his message: there's no such thing as free money — it gets taken from places that need it, like schools. Everyone, including Gerald (under threat of being sued himself), drops the cases.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, Stan Marsh, Gerald Broflovski, Peetie the Sexual Harassment Panda (Tom Morris), Mr. Garrison, Principal Victoria, Bebe Stevens, Clyde, Pip, Craig, Wendy, Mr. Mackey, Tweek, Kenny McCormick.

Locations: South Park Elementary (courtroom scenes in town), the courtroom, the Island of Misfit Mascots, Gerald's expanding mansion.

Key events & continuity: the lawsuit epidemic nearly bankrupts the school; Peetie's reformed message ends it; Gerald's greed is checked by his own son; Kenny's magnet-shredding is one of his most elaborate deaths.

On the night of the meteor shower, Liane leaves for Mr. Mackey's party and leaves Cartman with his babysitter: Shelly Marsh, Stan's older sister, who immediately establishes that she's in charge and invites her 22-year-old boyfriend Skyler over. Cartman, busy reenacting Wild Wild West with his toys, declares war — especially once he notices Mr. Kitty, his cat, is in heat and keeps presenting her backside. He doses Mr. Kitty with catnip, which only makes her wilder, and manages to photograph Shelly and Skyler kissing, then tapes the photo to the cat. Skyler's band, the Lords of the Underworld, shows up to rehearse; Shelly sings with them, critiques them, and they leave disliking her. Meanwhile Mr. Kitty prowls the streets, fails to seduce an obese orange tom, and finally finds a whole gang of toms. Outside watching the meteor shower, Skyler dumps Shelly because she won't get physical with him; she breaks down, admitting nobody at school will date her because she's ugly. Cartman — who agrees she's ugly but says Skyler's a gross jerk for dating twelve-year-olds — offers to help her get revenge. He lures Skyler out with a fake Selma Hayek distress tape, Shelly smashes Skyler's beloved guitar and mounts it on kitty litter labeled 'King Turd,' and Cartman throws catnip on Skyler so the aroused cat horde swarms him. Back home, Mr. Kitty has invited every tom in town inside for a full-blown cat orgy, trashing the house. Liane returns too drunk to notice the wreckage and passes out; Shelly admits Cartman's okay, Cartman admits she's okay, and the two sworn enemies clean the house together while Cartman sings his Wild Wild West song.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, Shelly Marsh, Skyler, Liane Cartman, Mr. Kitty, the Lords of the Underworld.

Locations: Cartman's house, the streets of South Park.

Key events & continuity: the first of three interlocking meteor-shower stories (with 'Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub' and 'Jewbilee'); Shelly and Cartman's mutual hatred cracks into genuine respect; Mr. Kitty's heat drives the entire feline subplot; Skyler's band connects to later music plots.

entries.n: S03E08 — Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub
entries.t:
On the same meteor-shower night, Stan's parents drag him to Mr. Mackey's party and stash him in the basement 'kids' room' with the school's three resident geeks: Pip, Butters, and Dougie. Stan is appalled. Upstairs, Mackey shows off his new hot tub; Sharon and Sheila decline for lack of swimsuits, while Randy and Gerald climb straight in. In the basement, the geeks rope Stan into games — he gets cast as Bosley in their Charlie's Angels dress-up — and he manipulates them with 'missions' to fetch him cookies and a TV. In the tub, Randy and Gerald decide to have a night of experimentation; Gerald confesses he's always wondered what it's like to watch another man masturbate, and then does exactly that. Randy spirals, seeing judgment in every glance, until all the men admit they've experimented too and it doesn't make anyone gay. Outside, the ATF has surrounded the house, convinced the meteor-shower party is a suicide cult, and prepares a full Waco-style assault: blasting Cher from giant speakers, failed negotiations, and finally a missile launcher. The boys film a mock news report exposing the truth, but can't get it outside — until Pip fires a plunger onto Officer Barbrady's head with his archery bow and Butters slides down the hill to deliver the tape. The ATF fires the missile anyway, obliterating three neighboring houses, then claims it was 'just a simulation' and leaves. Stan, humbled, tells the geeks he was wrong to mock them — right up until Kyle arrives with Ike from Jew Scouts and Stan starts mocking them again.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Pip, Butters Stotch, Dougie, Randy and Sharon Marsh, Gerald and Sheila Broflovski, Mr. Mackey, the ATF.

Locations: Mr. Mackey's house (hot tub, basement kids' room), the ATF siege line.

Key events & continuity: the second meteor-shower story, overlapping 'Cat Orgy' and 'Jewbilee'; Butters emerges as a central geek-trio member; the ATF's Waco parody ends with destroyed houses and zero accountability; Randy and Gerald's hot-tub experimentation becomes a bonding secret.
k: two guys naked in a hot tub

entries.t:
On meteor-shower night, Gerald and Sheila head to Mackey's party while Kyle and Ike go to Jewbilee, a camp for Jewish scouts. Kenny, with nowhere else to go, tags along; the Broflovskis reluctantly bring him, and Sheila lectures him on Judaism the whole drive. At camp, the older scouts go to the meeting hall while the little 'squirts' — including Ike — head to their own lair. New members are initiated by having a giant bell clanged over their heads; Kenny's attempts to dodge it only make it worse. The scouts sculpt soap art for the coming of Moses, who arrives as a giant glowing levitating dreidel — and promptly banishes Kenny for not being Jewish. Meanwhile the squirts are taken on a Chutzpah-badge bear hunt; the bear outsmarts them one by one until their leader quits. In the meeting hall, the Jewish council shuns a strange new sect that worships Haman as too weird to tolerate. That sect's leader then launches his real plan: he traps Moses in a shell, takes the whole camp hostage, and prepares to free Haman. Everything now depends on Kenny. Wandering the forest, Kenny is grabbed by the bear — but discovers the bear only took the squirts to her cub's birthday party. Kenny rallies the squirts, they form a living ladder to unlock the hall, and Kenny smashes Moses's shell open with his own head, dying in the process. Freed, Moses destroys Haman and his worshiper. Kyle admits they were wrong to shun Kenny, and Moses decrees that every year they shall gather and bring him soap sculptures, macaroni pictures, and paper-plate bean shakers.

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski, Kenny McCormick, Ike Broflovski, Gerald and Sheila Broflovski, Moses, the Haman worshiper, the Jew Scouts and squirts.

Locations: the Jewbilee camp (meeting hall, squirts' lair), the forest.

Key events & continuity: the third meteor-shower story, closing the trilogy; Moses appears as a giant dreidel and institutes an annual tribute; Kenny's sacrificial head-smash saves the camp; Kyle's guilt over shunning Kenny drives the moral.

entries.n: S03E10 — Korn's Groovy Pirate Ghost Mystery
entries.t:
At the docks, the boys dismiss the Halloween Haunt as lame — Cartman's already thinking about Christmas — until the older fifth-graders terrorize them with the legend of the Pirate Ghosts. For revenge, the boys dig up Kyle's dead grandmother, Cleo Broflovski, and stash her at the docks; a stray dog carries her off before they notice. The cemetery wardens report the desecration to Sheila as suspected necrophilia. Meanwhile the band Korn, driving to their South Park Halloween concert, spots the Pirate Ghosts on the road, panics, and drives their van off a cliff into town. They tell the boys what they saw; the boys suspect the fifth-graders. At a town meeting about the grave-robbing, a ghostly pirate ship materializes in the sky and three Pirate Ghosts slaughter members of the crowd, then vanish with a warning to stay away from the docks. Father Maxi declares the whole thing proves Korn are evil devil-worshippers, and the town votes to drive the band out. The boys arrive in costume — Stan a cowboy, Kyle a clown, Kenny a walking ED-209 from RoboCop, Cartman clutching his 'Christmas present,' an Antonio Banderas blow-up doll — and discover grandma's corpse is gone. Teaming with Korn, they split up: Cartman's team baits a trap with the blow-up doll, Fieldy loses his glasses and meets a real ghost, and the pirates blunder into the net. Korn unleashes their 'Korn powers' — transforming into giant ears of corn — which are completely useless but look cool. Just as the ghosts are about to be unmasked, they vanish for good, suggesting they were real all along; then Korn's pet Nibblet opens a trapdoor exposing the true villain: Father Maxi, who faked the haunting to frame the band. The dog returns and vomits up grandma's corpse. Maxi is arrested, the town begs Korn to stay, and they close the night playing 'Falling Away From Me.' The boys scare the fifth-graders with the corpse; Nibblet pops Cartman's doll (he chases the bird screaming about a 'son of a bitch chicken from outer space'); Wendy wins the costume contest in her recycled Chewbacca outfit from Pinkeye; and Kenny, still in his walker, is shot down by tiny Star Wars-style fighters.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman, Kenny McCormick, Korn, Nibblet, Father Maxi, Cleo Broflovski (corpse), the fifth-graders, Wendy Testaburger, Sheila Broflovski.

Locations: the docks, Mt. Peaceful Cemetery, the town hall, the Halloween concert stage.

Key events & continuity: Father Maxi is exposed as a fraud and arrested; the Pirate Ghosts are never fully debunked; Wendy's Pinkeye Chewbacca costume wins again; Kenny's ED-209 ends in a Star Wars homage.

A new Japanese cartoon, Chinpokomon, airs, followed instantly by ads for Chinpokomon dolls — and Cartman drags his mother to the toy store, only to find every other kid got there first. At the bus stop he tries to trade Kenny for his favorite doll; Kyle shows up with a Cyborg Bill figure and is told dolls are already out — it's all about the video game now, which involves bombing Pearl Harbor and gives Kenny a seizure. The toy-shop owner grows suspicious when a doll blurts out that the American government must be stopped; he flies to Japan to confront the creators, who flatter him about the size of his penis until he leaves satisfied. Randy and Sharon watch Stan's Chinpokomon tape and are disturbed enough to call a parents' meeting. The fad escalates to Chinpokomon Camp, where the cheerful leaders teach the kids Japanese and explain the real mission: destroy the evil power — the American government — starting with bombing Pearl Harbor. The adults panic at City Hall, where the Chinpokomon creators deploy the penis-flattery trick on the fathers (the mothers see through it). Realizing kids abandon anything adults like, Sharon has the parents stage a counter-fad: they all pretend to love Chinpokomon, roll out toy commercials for 'Wild Wacky Action Bike' and 'Alabama Man,' and President Clinton himself gets duped by the penis trick on national TV. At the airfield, as the brainwashed kids march to their planes, the sight of their parents loving Chinpokomon kills the cool instantly — the kids bail. Kyle, still in his plane, insists he'd follow the group even if he quit liking it; Stan argues you shouldn't follow a group blindly, then that groups can help you choose — Kyle, thoroughly confused, climbs out. The craze dies, the kids resolve to buy only toys they actually want, and Kenny finally succumbs to his seizure as a nest of rats bursts from his stomach.
