Butters escapes Hilton, hides in the party closet, and flees when the girl inside comes on to him. Hilton hears Mr. Slave call her a "thoughtless, talentless lowlife" and challenges him to a Whore-Off. Hilton performs escalating lewd acts, finishing with a whole pineapple inside herself. Mr. Slave counters by stripping, leaping, and jamming her entire body up his anus. The crowd applauds; he silences them and delivers the moral: girls shouldn't dress whorishly, and parents must teach kids that people like Paris Hilton are supposed to be despised. The girls apologize to Wendy; inside Mr. Slave, the Frog King sends Hilton on Lemmiwinks's quest.

Featured characters: Wendy Testaburger; Paris Hilton; Butters as "Mr. Biggles"; Mr. Slave; Bebe and the girls; Stan; Cartman; Clyde; the Stotch parents.

Locations: the South Park Mall, the Stupid Spoiled Whore store, Bebe's party, Hilton's limo.

Key events & continuity: Mr. Slave wins the Whore-Off with a moral about role models; all of Hilton's pets committed suicide; the Frog King sends Hilton on Lemmiwinks's quest.

Cartman tries to fly off his roof with cardboard wings, falls into a short coma, and wakes in a hospital room shared with a victim of a serial killer who cuts off left hands. When Cartman correctly guesses dinner and a few other obvious routine things, gullible detective Harrison Yates declares him a psychic "child wonderkid." At a murder scene, Cartman has "visions" of ice cream and Double Stuff Oreos; Yates arrests Tom Johannsen, the ice-cream store owner, brutally. More innocents follow, including rival "psychics" who threaten to sue Cartman over the psychic-detective ad and their 10% cut. The left-hand murders continue — including Mrs. Crabtree — but the cops dismiss them as copycat killings. At every crime scene, Michael Deets, a disturbed man in a blood-spattered rain slicker, tells the boys, "They're never gunna catch the killer, he's too smart," then addresses a female mannequin torso as his abusive mother. Kyle suspects Deets, but the detectives brush him off. He follows Deets home and obtains fingerprints and blood samples; the police dismiss his real evidence as unreliable.

Kyle imitates Cartman's flight, enters a coma, and wakes claiming psychic powers, feeding police his actual findings. Yates investigates; by now Deets has abducted Cartman, furious the fake psychic credited his work to others. Yates finds hands nailed to Deets's wall but dismisses them, insisting they are right hands — botching the thumb logic, since the palms face the wall and the thumbs point right. He cannot hear the gagged Cartman in the basement and leaves, then questions his own observation. After a montage of criminology tests and exercise, he realizes his mistake, returns, and kills Deets just before Deets kills Cartman. Back at the hospital, Johannsen and the psychics are freed, and Kyle is hailed as the real psychic. He declares there are no psychics and every psychic story has a logical explanation. Yates shrugs: good old-fashioned police work stopped the crime. The rival psychics reignite their feud with Cartman in a "final battle" — until Kyle yells at them to stop, and the room's light bulbs explode as devices topple off a shelf. Kyle insists there must be a logical explanation while everyone raises an eyebrow.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, the fake psychic; Kyle Broflovski, the real detective; Harrison Yates; Michael Deets; Tom Johannsen; Mrs. Crabtree; the rival psychics.

Locations: the hospital, the murder scenes, Deets's house, the police station.

Key events & continuity: Yates's thumb-logic blunder nearly gets Cartman killed; Kyle solves the case with fingerprints and blood while the police trust only "psychic" claims; Mrs. Crabtree is murdered; the episode ends on an ambiguous note as Kyle's outburst seemingly causes bulbs to explode, undercutting his no-psychics speech.

In rhyming narration, "the boy in the red poof-ball hat" — Stan — finds talking woodland critters decorating a Christmas tree and is talked into making their star. That night they wake him: Porcupiny the porcupine is pregnant with their Savior, and they need a manger. Every year one of them conceives the Savior, but an evil mountain lion kills it before birth, and only Stan can help. Stan kills the beast, then learns it was the mother of three cubs. Worse, the critters reveal themselves as Satanists: their Savior is the Anti-Christ. They sacrifice Rabbitty the rabbit and devour his entrails in a blood orgy. Stan tries to stop them but is rebuffed. Learning only a mountain lion can kill the Anti-Christ, he takes the orphaned cubs to an abortion doctor to teach them abortions — against his will. The critters need a human host — a non-baptized non-Christian — and kidnap Kyle, who is Jewish.

Stan arrives to find the Anti-Christ already born, with Kyle tied to a Satanic altar. Santa Claus suddenly appears, pulls out a SPAS-12 combat shotgun, and slaughters the critters. He is about to kill the Anti-Christ when the freed Kyle declares he wants it to possess him, to make the world better for the Jews. The demon enters him — when the story cuts to Mr. Garrison's class. It was all a Christmas story Eric Cartman was reading aloud. Kyle objects that Cartman is mocking him for being Jewish at Christmas; Garrison, fearing Sheila's complaints, makes Cartman stop. The class begs Kyle to let him finish; Kyle calls the ending obvious — Santa kills story-Kyle — but Cartman insists otherwise, and Kyle reluctantly relents. Back in the story, Kyle feels the Anti-Christ cold, dark, and evil inside him. "What did you expect, dude? It's the son of the Devil!" Stan says. Santa says they must kill Kyle before the Anti-Christ consumes his soul — so the cubs perform an abortion on Kyle's anus, and Santa smashes the Anti-Christ with a sledgehammer. Santa grants Stan one wish — the cubs' mother's resurrection. The narrator concludes: "they all lived happily ever after... except for Kyle, who died of AIDS two weeks later." Kyle: "Goddammit, Cartman!"

Featured characters: Stan Marsh; Kyle Broflovski, the possessed host; Eric Cartman, the narrator; the Satanist woodland critters; the mountain lion cubs; Santa Claus.

Locations: the forest, Stan's bedroom, the abortion clinic, the Satanic altar, the classroom.

Key events & continuity: the story is revealed as Cartman's Christmas tale mocking Kyle; Santa massacres the critters; the Anti-Christ is aborted from Kyle and smashed; Stan's wish resurrects the cubs' mother; the coda kills Kyle with AIDS two weeks later.

entries.n: S09E01 — Mr. Garrison's Fancy New Vagina
entries.t:
Mr. Garrison undergoes a sex change at the Trinidad Medical Center, realizing he has always been a woman trapped in a man's body. At the Colorado state basketball tryouts, Kyle is cut — the coach tells him Jews can't play basketball — while the rest of the team are all tall African-Americans. Stan and Kenny comfort him; Cartman mocks him. In town, the boys run into Mrs. Garrison buying tampons and accept their teacher's decision. At home, Kyle asks Gerald what a sex change is; Sheila explains that people get such surgeries because who they are outside doesn't reflect who they are inside. Kyle realizes he relates: he feels like a tall African-American trapped in a small Jewish body, given his love of basketball and rap. He decides to get surgery to become a tall African-American man. Gerald objects furiously and goes after Dr. Biber — but Biber spots Gerald's dolphin t-shirt and convinces him to get a "dolphinplasty," turning him into a half-man, half-dolphin humanoid. Convinced surgery is fine now, Gerald allows Kyle's "negroplasty" to proceed.

Meanwhile Garrison and Mr. Slave have a falling out: Slave is hurt that Garrison thought only of "herself," declares he hates vaginas, and is outraged when Garrison tells him to stop being gay. Garrison yells "Fag!" and the relationship ends. Then Garrison wonders why "she" hasn't had a period, concludes a missed period means pregnancy — blaming the truckers "she" slept with — and happily visits Planned Parenthood for an abortion, only to learn the surgery provided no reproductive system at all. Feeling cheated, "she" demands a reversal, but Biber reveals the old scrotum was made into Gerald's dorsal fin and the testicles into Kyle's kneecaps — reversal is impossible without those exact parts. They track Kyle to the basketball game — he made the team — where Biber warns that he only made Kyle look like a player, not be one: one jump could detonate his kneecaps. Fighting through security, they arrive just as Kyle scores — and his kneecaps explode on landing. "My balls!" Garrison cries. Gerald and Kyle are told their surgeries can be reversed; Garrison's cannot. Unbothered, "she" embraces the new gender: better a fake woman who can't have periods than a fag.

Featured characters: Mr./Mrs. Garrison; Kyle Broflovski; Gerald Broflovski, the dolphin-man; Dr. Biber; Mr. Slave; Stan, Kenny, and Cartman; Sheila Broflovski.

Locations: the Trinidad Medical Center, the basketball tryouts and game, the Broflovski home, Planned Parenthood.

Key events & continuity: Garrison's sex change becomes permanent, ending the relationship with Mr. Slave; Gerald's dolphinplasty and Kyle's negroplasty are reversible, but Kyle's kneecaps explode mid-game; the scrotum-to-dorsal-fin and testicles-to-kneecaps transfers make Garrison's reversal impossible.

In pest-control gear, Cartman warns a neighbor of a hippie infestation. Cartman — an avid hippie-hater — finds stoners in her attic and a drum circle in her backyard, rounding them into his basement with dozens more. Stan, Kyle, and Kenny, selling magazines door to door, meet "college know-it-all hippies" who convince them corporations tricked kids into selling out. The boys adopt the ideology and join the plan: a week-long music festival to change the world through music. Cartman warns the City Council the festival will let hippies consume the town; they kick him out. He finds his friends have joined the hippies and maces them in the square. Barbrady arrests Cartman for imprisoning sixty-three hippies. The Mayor admits she signed the festival permit to boost the economy. The festival draws thousands of hippies getting high; the boys grow confused — the hippies have done nothing — and realize their perfect world is exactly the one they already have. Randy is furious Stan is there, recalling when he and Sharon were hippies, then admits the old ones were just as bad; rushing to save Stan, he collapses from the stench. The festival swells past half a million hippies. Ashamed, the Mayor shoots herself — and survives. The desperate townsfolk beg Cartman for help; he agrees only for a new Tonka remote-controlled bulldozer, on the condition that Kyle must watch and may not play.

Cartman's plan: drill through the crowd in a drilling vehicle to the stage and insert a Slayer CD into the stereos, since hippies cannot stand heavy metal. His crew: scientist Randy, engineer Mrs. Stotch, and unwilling Chef as the black man to sacrifice. They drill through the crowd, killing hundreds of hippies. Stan denounces the hippies; the boys realize they are trapped by the crowd. The drill overheats; Cartman forces Chef to "sacrifice" himself, activating the emergency boosters. The Mayor suggests nuking the town; the townspeople protest. The crew storms the stage, killing the band; Cartman plays the Slayer CD. The hippies flee the city. Randy reunites with Stan; Chef survives. Cartman brandishes a knife at Kyle, who insists he is no longer a hippie; Cartman spares him, saying he has bigger plans. Cartman gets his bulldozer and forces Kyle to watch him play, taunting him.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, hippie exterminator; Stan, Kyle, and Kenny; Randy Marsh; Mayor McDaniels; Officer Barbrady; Chef; Mrs. Stotch.

Locations: South Park, Cartman's basement, the city square, the festival grounds.

Key events & continuity: Cartman imprisons sixty-three hippies; the Mayor's suicide attempt fails; the Slayer CD routs half a million hippies; Chef survives his "sacrifice"; Cartman's price — the bulldozer plus Kyle forced to watch — fuels his torment of Kyle.

When Tolkien wins a contest to sing at a beauty pageant for $200, the boys decide to mooch off his talent by becoming his agents. They promptly lose him to a rival talent agency — but land a replacement client: Wing, the wife of City Wok owner Tuong Lu Kim. Recently smuggled into the United States by the Chinese Mafia, Wing is set to audition for American Idol, and the boys' "Super Awesome Talent Agency" agrees to bring her to Los Angeles for the competition. The venture goes sideways fast: they enter Wing into The Contender, where she is beaten up by a boxer mid-song. Then a real gig lands — Wing is invited to sing at the wedding of Sylvester Stallone's son after Stallone says her voice impressed him. But the Chinese Mafia kidnaps Wing because Tuong never paid the $10,000 he owed them for smuggling her in. The boys, mistaking the Mafia for the agency that stole Tolkien, go after them to get their client back. In the end, both the Mafia and the boys realize their businesses are dirty and exploit the hopes of others — and all of them decide to quit. They gather to hear Wing sing at the wedding, where they find Tolkien waiting tables, trying to earn enough to get home, since the agency apparently does nothing for you. Cartman rubs Tolkien's bad luck in his face. The episode closes on a real-life portrait of Wing with a promotional ad for her website.

Featured characters: Wing, the smuggled singer; Tuong Lu Kim; Tolkien Black; Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny as the Super Awesome Talent Agency; the Chinese Mafia; Sylvester Stallone.

Locations: South Park, Los Angeles, The Contender ring, Stallone's son's wedding.

Key events & continuity: Wing is established as Tuong Lu Kim's wife, smuggled in by the Chinese Mafia for $10,000; the boys mistake the Mafia for Tolkien's poaching agency; both the Mafia and the boys quit their exploitative businesses; Tolkien is found waiting tables, the agency having done nothing for him; the episode ends with a real portrait of Wing.

Kenny is the first in town to get a PlayStation Portable and becomes inseparable from it. Cartman, who missed out by arriving late at the store, seethes with envy. Kenny climbs to level 59 of Heaven vs. Hell, but his parents' arguing drives him outside for level 60 — where an ice-cream van runs him over. He dies. In Heaven, Kenny learns God created the PSP to find the one who can command His legions against Hell: someone skilled enough to defeat 10 billion damned souls with 10,000 troops. He is, basically, "Keanu Reeves." Satan's spy warns him about Kenny; Satan wants to give up, but his advisor insists on attacking. Just as Hell's armies advance, Kenny is revived — brain-dead and vegetative, kept alive by a feeding tube. His will reading — Cartman gets the PSP out of pity, Stan and Kyle the rest — is interrupted: Kenny is alive. The lawyer mentions a passage about Kenny's wishes if ever vegetative, but the last page is missing.

With Satan's army closing in, the angels need Kenny dead to win the Apocalypse. Cartman takes his half of a BFF medallion to the Colorado Supreme Court, claims "best friend forever" status, wins an order to remove the feeding tube, and pulls it after finding the other half — implied planted by Cartman himself. Stan and Kyle, Kenny's parents, and protesters — including a food-smuggling Mrs. Garrison, who is arrested — wage a media war to restore the tube, while Cartman rallies BFF-rights supporters. On live TV, both sides argue in Kenny's suite until the lawyer announces the last page has been found. Kenny's wish: if he were ever in a vegetative state, "please, for the love of God... do not ever show me in that condition on national television." Both sides realize they turned a private matter into a public spectacle against his wishes, and leave him to die in peace. Kenny returns to Heaven just in time to command the angels to victory. The battle is never shown, only described — demon dragons, "TEN times bigger" than the Lord of the Rings finale — ending with battered angels cheering and Kenny receiving a golden Keanu Reeves statue.

Featured characters: Kenny McCormick, Heaven's commander; Eric Cartman, fighting for the PSP; Stan and Kyle, fighting for Kenny's life; Kenny's parents; Satan; God and the angels; Mrs. Garrison.

Locations: South Park, Heaven, Hell, the hospital.

Key events & continuity: Kenny dies by ice-cream van and is prophesied as Heaven's "Keanu Reeves"; Cartman manipulates the courts with a planted medallion half; Kenny's true will exposes both sides' media circus; he returns to Heaven to win the Apocalypse.

The boys play Little League only because their parents are enthusiastic; they hate baseball. After winning their final game, they celebrate the season being over — then learn they must continue into the state championship. Since the tournament is single elimination, they decide to throw the next game and win back their summer. Unfortunately, every other team hates baseball just as much and is trying to lose too. Despite their best efforts to fail, the boys keep winning, until only South Park and Denver remain. Throughout the games, Randy gets drunk and trash-talks the opposing teams, starting fights with other fathers at every game. Everyone finds it obnoxious; Randy considers the fights the most important part of baseball. He brawls his way through every drunk father until he meets Bat Dad — an overweight Denver father in a purple Batman cowl and cape — whose size and aggression intimidate Randy into skipping the Denver game entirely.

Fearing a win means baseball all summer on the national circuit, Cartman suggests recruiting the worst player possible to guarantee defeat: Kyle's cousin Kyle Schwartz, distinguished as "Kyle One," who is terrible at every sport. The scheme fails — Denver has practiced being bad, with players "batting themselves out" by hitting South Park's pitches straight into fielders' gloves. Just as South Park is about to win anyway, Randy shows up and starts harassing Bat Dad. The two brawl, and the announcers warn that continued fighting means disqualification. The team, desperate for that disqualification, chants for Randy. Egged on — plus motivational voices in his head, including Mickey Goldmill — Randy keeps fighting Bat Dad until South Park is disqualified and the kids' summer is saved. Led away in handcuffs wearing only his underwear, Randy hears Stan say, "You're the greatest." He leaps for joy as "You're the Best" plays over a freeze-frame.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh; Randy Marsh, the brawling dad; Bat Dad; Eric Cartman; Kyle Broflovski and cousin Kyle Schwartz ("Kyle One"); Kenny; the Little League teams; Mickey Goldmill (in Randy's head).

Locations: the Little League fields, the state championship game.

Key events & continuity: Kyle Schwartz returns as the team's ringer-for-defeat; Bat Dad becomes Randy's nemesis; Randy's brawl gets South Park disqualified on purpose; Stan's "You're the greatest" and the freeze-frame close the episode; the boys' shared hatred of baseball drives the entire plot.

entries.n: S09E06 — The Death of Eric Cartman
entries.t:
At Stan's house, the boys wait for Sharon to return with KFC. Cartman eats all the skin off the chicken, and the others are furious — Kenny bursts into tears. At the bus stop the next day, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny decide Cartman has gone too far. Since he thrives on being ripped on, they resolve to completely ignore him. Cartman, suddenly unseen and unheard, concludes he has died and become a ghost. It seems confirmed when he sees a casket-like box carried from his house — the men say it's full of chicken skins, though it's really the toilet he destroyed — and hears his mother "crying," actually having sex with a plumber. Soon most of South Park's kids join the ignoring. Butters, unaware of the movement, greets Cartman, and both conclude Butters can psychically see him. They set out to get Cartman into Heaven — he claims he can't go to Hell because he's not black. First Butters apologizes to everyone on Cartman's behalf; when that fails, he compiles a list of Cartman's sins and they deliver amends via gift baskets. That fails too. Cartman goes berserk, destroys Butters's room with a baseball bat, and gets Butters committed to the South Park Institute for Mental Health, where a machine anally probes him for over fourteen hours.

After breaking Butters out, they consult a psychic, Doctor Lindsay, who suggests God kept Cartman on Earth for some crisis. Hearing of a hostage situation at the Red Cross, they go; Cartman stops the criminals by moving things around, befuddling the robbers long enough for police to end the standoff. He is credited with saving the day, "armed only with the weapon of confusion." His classmates arrive, willing to be friends again, believing he has truly changed. Once they leave, Cartman — mortified and furious that he apologized to everyone and was fooled — goes berserk again, blames Butters, and vows revenge, only to be caught by his parents and an asylum doctor, still carrying the anal device, who says Butters needs more therapy.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, the "ghost"; Butters Stotch, his medium; Stan, Kyle, and Kenny, ignoring him; Liane Cartman; Doctor Lindsay; the Red Cross robbers.

Locations: Stan's house, the bus stop, Cartman's house, Butters's room, the South Park Institute for Mental Health, the Red Cross.

Key events & continuity: the KFC skin incident triggers the town-wide ignoring; Cartman's ghost delusion drives the amends campaign; Butters endures a fourteen-hour anal probing; Cartman's "weapon of confusion" heroism is genuine accident; the episode ends with Cartman vowing revenge on Butters once he learns he was never dead.

With the South Park Elementary Talent Show approaching, Jimmy faces a crisis: he gets spontaneous erections whenever he's the center of attention, and fears humiliation onstage. He consults Butters — the one kid unlikely to mock him. Butters explains that an erect penis needs to go into a woman's vagina, where it "sneezes milk," after which it weakens again. Jimmy concludes he should have intercourse before performing. With Cartman's help he arranges a date with a schoolgirl named Shauna — and ruins it by announcing, "I really wanna stick my penis in your vagina." On Officer Barbrady's suggestion, he heads for Colfax Point, the town's red-light district, to get laid, while the talent show begins back at school.

The show's acts are a disaster parade: Butters forgets the words to his apple song and wets himself, Cartman does a dead-on Tony Montana Scarface impression, and the Goth Kids perform "Talent Shows are for Fags." Meanwhile Jimmy picks up Nut Gobbler, an obese prostitute, and tries to woo her at a restaurant — until her pimp Q-Money storms in, assumes she's betraying him, and drags her off to kill her. Jimmy gives chase in a bizarre car pursuit, subdues the pimp with his comedy routine while Nut Gobbler clubs him from behind, then carries her into a hotel amid applause from the prostitutes. Jimmy races back and takes the stage at the last possible moment. He launches into his routine — and soon senses another erection coming on.

Featured characters: Jimmy Valmer; Butters Stotch, his advisor; Nut Gobbler; Q-Money, her pimp; Shauna; Officer Barbrady; Cartman; the Goth Kids.

Locations: South Park Elementary, Colfax Point, the restaurant, the hotel.

Key events & continuity: Jimmy's erection problem threatens his long-awaited talent-show set; Butters's birds-and-bees explanation ("sneezes milk") sets the plot in motion; Jimmy defeats a pimp with stand-up comedy; the episode ends on a cliffhanger as Jimmy feels another erection mid-routine.

entries.n: S09E08 — Two Days Before the Day After Tomorrow
entries.t:
At Jefferson's Lake, Cartman talks Stan into playing in his "uncle Roy's" speed boat. When Stan muses how cool driving for real would be, Cartman pulls the keys from the glove compartment, promising to take responsibility. Stan relents, loses control, and crashes into the world's largest beaver dam, breaking it. Beaverton floods. Cartman reneges: no uncle Roy — Stan's in trouble. They hide their involvement, but Stan is wrecked with guilt. The news shows Beaverton's residents stranded on rooftops while the reporter sensationalizes — a death toll bigger than the town's population, speculation about rape, murder, looting, cannibalism. Liberals blame Bush for not caring about beavers; conservatives blame terrorists. Stan's parents brush off rescue talk, preferring to blame Beaverton's mayor and FEMA.

At school, Cartman denies responsibility — the town shouldn't have built under a dam — and warns Stan not to confess to Kyle, a "Jew Rat" whose "Jew Ethics" and hoarded "Jew Gold" will "Jew" him out. Kyle arrives, Stan lies. Then Butters announces the cause: Global Warming. The Governor assembles Colorado's geologists — Randy Marsh alone — who warns worse disasters come "the day after tomorrow"; other scientists say the end comes two days before the day after tomorrow. A horrified Randy realizes: today. Panic erupts — "We didn't listen!" — and the town barricades in the community center. Stan confesses to Kyle; Cartman snaps, then suggests Kyle spend his Jew Gold on Beaverton. Randy, convinced the world has frozen, marks a map and inadvertently draws a penis. The boys steal a speed boat, crash into an oil factory, and burning oil spreads across the floodwater. Randy, Stephen, and Gerald rush out in winter gear despite the warmth, suffering heat stroke they mistake for hypothermia. The government first snubs Beaverton, then learns it wasn't global warming and rushes in. Fleeing to a roof, the boys are stopped by Cartman, who pulls a gun demanding Kyle's Jew Gold; Kyle drops the bag into the flaming water, and Cartman panics. Everyone is picked up and returned. The town declares global warming over — until soldiers announce the real cause was Crab People. Stan admits, "I broke the dam!" Everyone takes it as metaphor and repeats it proudly. Stan explains exactly how; nobody listens. "Aw, fuck it!"

Featured characters: Stan Marsh; Eric Cartman; Kyle Broflovski; Randy Marsh, the lone geologist; Butters Stotch; the Governor.

Locations: Jefferson's Lake, Beaverton, the Marsh home, the community center, the oil factory.

Key events & continuity: Stan and Cartman break the beaver dam and cover it up; the "two days before the day after tomorrow" panic; Randy's penis map; Crab People named the official cause; Stan's literal confession becomes the town's metaphorical slogan.
k: two days before the day after tomorrow

entries.t:
Cartman shows the boys a videotape: the girls using a cootie catcher to predict the future. Not realizing it's a game, he believes the girls possess a secret high-tech future-telling device. The boys build a containment center — bio suits, quarantine shower, housing unit — and plan to steal it at Heidi Turner's sleepover, sending one boy in disguised as a girl: Butters. To cover his absence, they fake his death: Butters stands atop a skyscraper threatening to jump while the boys drop a swine carcass dressed like him over the edge. At the funeral, with the pig's remains in the coffin, Linda Stotch throws herself on the coffin in hysterical grief as Stephen holds her back.

The next morning, Butters arrives at school as a new girl, "Marjorine." Heidi's mother got a call from "Marjorine's mother" — actually Cartman — claiming to be a governor's assistant who demands Mrs. Turner "respect her authoritah." Clueless about girls' parties, Butters screams during "light as a feather, stiff as a board," gets mocked, and locks himself in Heidi's bathroom crying. The gentler Wendy and Bebe decide they were too hard on the new kid; the girls give Marjorine a makeover and invite her to dance. Meanwhile a farmer warns Stephen not to dig up the corpse and rebury it in the old Indian burial ground — "Sometimes, what you take out of the ground ain't the same thing you put in!" Stephen does it anyway, hoping to resurrect Butters. When the boys peer through Heidi's window, they find Marjorine dancing to Justin Timberlake's "Rock Your Body," mission forgotten. Heidi's dad spots Craig watching with binoculars; thinking he's been found out, Butters snatches the device and flees. Heidi just asks for paper to make another one. Butters hands the device to the boys and goes home to prove he's alive. The boys deem its power too dangerous and have Kenny blow it up rather than defend it from the girls, the CIA, terrorists, and Russia — an explosion visible from space. Butters's parents, convinced he'll return as a demon, lock him in the basement. When he says he's hungry, they kill a curtain saleswoman and drop her at his feet. He asks for Spaghetti-O's.

Featured characters: Butters as Marjorine; Eric Cartman; Stan, Kyle, and Kenny; Heidi Turner; Wendy and Bebe; the Stotches; Craig.

Locations: Cartman's basement, the skyscraper, the funeral, Heidi's sleepover, the Indian burial ground, the Stotch basement.

Key events & continuity: Butters fakes his death with a pig carcass; Stephen reburies him in the Indian burial ground; the cootie catcher explodes visibly from space; his parents murder a saleswoman to feed their "demon" son, who wants Spaghetti-O's.

To teach parenting responsibility, Mrs. Garrison pairs the class off and hands each pair an egg to protect — everyone gets a white egg except Tolkien, who receives a brown one. Stan dreads partnering with ex Wendy, for whom he still has feelings; instead Wendy is paired with Kyle, and Stan gets Bebe. Stan grows convinced Kyle has feelings for Wendy, while Bebe tells Wendy she's furious at Stan's indifference to their egg. Stan calls Kyle sarcastically; when Kyle calls the project stupid, Stan snaps, "yeah, well so is your hat," deeply offending him.

Meanwhile Mrs. Garrison pines for her ex, Mr. Slave, who left her after her sex change — then learns he and Big Gay Al plan to marry once same-sex marriage is legalized. Jealous, she campaigns to block the union, hoping Slave will marry her instead. She petitions the governor to veto the gay marriage bill, claiming gay couples can't raise children; the governor demands a study proving gay families unstable. So Garrison reorganizes Stan, Kyle, Wendy, and Bebe into same-sex pairs, counting on Stan's poor parenting to destroy the egg. In a custody-battle parody, Wendy is upset that Stan and Kyle hold her original egg. Cartman breaks his egg and argues he deserves an F and his partner an A — earning a C- — but Garrison gives him a new egg, threatening to break his legs and burn his house down if he breaks it again, while strangling him. She schedules the final egg check at the governor's office and hires an assassin, who destroys Stan's egg.

Then the twist: fearing Stan's disinterest would fail them both, Kyle gave Stan a fake egg and safeguarded the real one — and he never had any interest in Wendy. Kyle asks if Stan really thinks his hat is stupid; Stan says no. Reconciled, they race to the governor's office through gunfire and bombs; Stan hoarsely presents the intact egg and faints. The governor verifies it, the bill passes, and same-sex marriage is legalized — which confuses Kyle. Mr. Slave and Big Gay Al marry with Father Maxi officiating. Randy congratulates Stan and Kyle for their gay-rights heroism, though neither knows what they actually did. Wendy apologizes for doubting Stan's parenting; Stan, no longer caring about her opinion, dismisses her, and she leaves upset.

Featured characters: Stan and Kyle; Wendy; Bebe; Mrs. Garrison; Mr. Slave and Big Gay Al; Tolkien; Cartman; the governor; Father Maxi; Randy.

Locations: South Park Elementary, the governor's office, the wedding.

Key events & continuity: Stan and Wendy's post-breakup tension ends with Stan dismissing her; Kyle secretly swaps the egg; the assassin fails; same-sex marriage is legalized and Mr. Slave marries Big Gay Al.

For a class presentation, Cartman delivers a hate speech declaring "Ginger Kids" — red hair, freckles, pale skin — creepy, evil, soulless sufferers of "gingervitus" who can't stand sunlight like vampires. He cites Kyle as a "Daywalker": auburn hair, no freckles, immune to the sun. The speech incites real discrimination — Tolkien, Craig, Clyde, and Jimmy shove a ginger boy in the hallway — infuriating Kyle. He counters with a presentation on ginger genetics, interviewing a ginger family; it reveals even the parents of three ginger kids share the public's bigoted hatred, though the gingers are depicted as genuinely creepy. Kyle's speech lands okay, but Cartman keeps undermining his Daywalker status. Fed up, Kyle and the others break into Cartman's house that night: Kyle knocks him out, then beats him in a rage until Stan pulls him off. They dye Cartman's hair red, bleach his skin lighter, and give him henna freckles, making him "a ginger." Liane is horrified; his doctor suggests putting him down. Liane considers it — with Cartman standing right there — but declines.

At school, Cartman endures his own discrimination but blames society, exempting himself. He assembles the "Ginger Separatist Movement," initially preaching equality and Ron Howard pride — but it turns violent, Cartman declaring the only way to fight hatred is with more hatred. Their first act: savagely beating a non-ginger actress for playing Annie. The movement grows; Cartman preaches gingers are the "chosen race" and orders the eradication of all non-gingers. The gingers abduct South Park's children — including Stan, Kyle, and Kenny — to the Sunset Room at the Airport Hilton, where a massive lava pit awaits their ritual murder. Kyle the Daywalker is chosen to die first, but whispers to Cartman that he's not really ginger — Stan, Kyle, and Kenny made him up. Cartman realizes his followers would kill him if they learned the truth, and announces a sudden epiphany: everyone must get along. The gingers are suspicious, but Cartman wins them over by singing "Hands in Hand," and the freed children join in. Kyle mutters that Cartman is a manipulative asshole; Cartman concedes it's true, but doesn't care — he's not going to die.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, ginger demagogue; Kyle, the Daywalker; Stan and Kenny; Liane; Mrs. Garrison; the ginger family.

Locations: South Park Elementary, Cartman's house, the Airport Hilton, the lava pit.

Key events & continuity: Cartman's speech invents "gingervitus" and Daywalkers; the boys transform him into a ginger; his doctor suggests euthanasia; the movement escalates from Ron Howard pride to genocide; his fake epiphany saves his life.

Stan skips laser-tag with his friends to save for a new bike and runs into some Scientologists, who talk him into a free personality test. The auditor declares him depressed — a perfect Scientology candidate. At dinner, Stan asks his parents for money for a "self-help program"; Randy tells him to use his bike money. After Stan's auditing, the shocked auditor sends the results to the home office, where the president concludes from Stan's thetan levels that he is the reincarnation of L. Ron Hubbard. The president visits the Marsh home with the news. Sent to his room, Stan meets Tom Cruise, who asks what he thought of his movies. Stan's callous opinion of his acting upsets Cruise, who locks himself in Stan's closet — giving the town its running joke: "Tom Cruise won't come out of the closet!" The president reveals Scientology's secrets to Stan — the Xenu story plays out on screen captioned "THIS IS WHAT SCIENTOLOGISTS ACTUALLY BELIEVE" — and assigns him to write a new doctrine for the church. Stan doesn't know where to start; the president notes Hubbard didn't either.

The town mobilizes to get Cruise out; John Travolta is called in and also ends up in the closet. On the news, R. Kelly sings in his "Trapped in the Closet" style, then pulls a gun. Nicole Kidman fails to coax Cruise out; R. Kelly is called in and joins them in the closet. Kyle, Kenny, and Cartman visit Stan; Kyle tries to tell him the truth about Hubbard, but Stan won't listen. Stan presents his doctrine: Scientologists shouldn't have to pay. The president drops the act — Scientology is a big scam. Stan tries to read his doctrine to the followers outside, can't go through with it, and tells everyone it's a scam instead. The president threatens to sue. Cruise, Travolta, and R. Kelly emerge from the closet; Cruise says Stan made him look stupid and threatens to sue in England. Stan shouts, "Go ahead! Sue me! I dare you!" The credits roll with every name listed as "John Smith" or "Jane Smith."

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, the reincarnated Hubbard; Tom Cruise, in the closet; the president of Scientology; John Travolta; R. Kelly; Nicole Kidman; Randy Marsh; Kyle, Kenny, and Cartman.

Locations: the Marsh home, Stan's closet, the Scientology testing center.

Key events & continuity: Stan is declared L. Ron Hubbard's reincarnation over his thetan levels; the Xenu story is presented as what Scientologists actually believe; the president admits Scientology is a scam; "Tom Cruise won't come out of the closet" becomes the episode's refrain; Stan dares them to sue him; the credits anonymize everyone as Smith.

At Denver Sea Park, the boys watch Jambu the orca perform. Kyle lingers — and the whale seems to speak to him. The voice comes through a loudspeaker, courtesy of Brian, one of the show's hosts; he and Mike play this prank for amusement. As Jambu, Brian tells Kyle the whale longs for outer space. Kyle fetches the group, and Brian reveals the whale's real name is "Willzyx" (pronounced "Willziak"), who must return to the moon — his "home" — or die. The boys rally the fourth grade to liberate Jambu and send him "home." They break into the park at night and stash the orca in Clyde's backyard pool. When the whale is reported missing, Brian and Mike realize what happened and start tracking the boys. Kyle calls the Russian government about a moon trip; they quote $20 million, then dismiss him as a George Bush prank call. The boys pivot to developing countries with cheap space programs. Animal Liberation Front protesters rally for the whale's freedom. Brian and Mike find Clyde's abandoned pool and whale feces — the boys have moved Jambu to Kyle's bedroom, keeping him wet with hoses. Kyle phones the Japanese while Jimmy, Timmy, and Tweek try the Chinese Embassy; everywhere the price is too high. Stan and Craig try Mexico, where MASA — the Mexican Aeronáutica y Spacial Administración — will fly their whale to the moon for $200. Brian and Mike learn from Sheila that the boys are headed for Tijuana.

Brian and Mike intercept the boys and try to tell them the truth, but police interrupt; the ALF provides cover fire, and Mike and one officer die in the gunfight. The ALF leader drives the van the rest of the way to the spaceport. The boys get the whale into the water just as the park owner, the police, and onlookers arrive. The ALF celebrates — briefly. Everyone but the boys watches in horror as the Mexican rocket launches with the whale tethered to it. The boys celebrate back home. The asphyxiated whale lies dead on the moon's surface as the credits roll in silence.

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski; Stan, Cartman, Kenny, and Craig; Brian and Mike; Jimmy, Timmy, and Tweek; the ALF; Sheila; the park owner.

Locations: Denver Sea Park, Clyde's pool, Kyle's bedroom, the Chinese Embassy (via Jimmy, Timmy, Tweek), Tijuana, the MASA spaceport, the moon.

Key events & continuity: the "talking whale" is a loudspeaker prank; the Russians quote $20 million; MASA flies whales to the moon for $200; Mike and an officer die in the shootout; the whale asphyxiates on the moon as the boys celebrate.

In karate class, the instructor fumes at Cartman because he "racks disciprine." After class, a drunk Randy picks the boys up; caught peeing in a beer bottle, he's arrested for drunk driving and loses his license. The next day, a mortified Stan begs Kyle and Cartman to keep quiet — but Randy, ordered by the state, gives a drunk-driving speech at school, and Mrs. Garrison humiliates him for lecturing elementary kids about how pathetic he is. Randy must attend Alcoholics Anonymous for two weeks. The meetings preach powerlessness: alcoholism is a "disease" only a higher power can cure. Soon convinced, Randy starts drinking more at home, from a wheelchair. Stan argues he just needs to drink less; Randy insists only "a miracle" can cure him.

Then a Virgin Mary statue in the next town starts bleeding from a hole in its "ass," astounding a passing priest. Crowds gather hoping for cures; watching the news, Randy believes it can cure him too. Stan crashes an AA meeting to demand why they told his dad he has a disease; he sees through them, but preaching "disciprine" gets him thrown out. Stan finds Randy trying to drive to St. Peter's Church and warns him a second DUI means ten years in jail — so Randy makes Stan drive him. They join a long line of the hopeful, brain cancer and elephantiasis sufferers among them. Randy, sure his disease is worst, cuts the line until an officer whose brother is an alcoholic intervenes. The statue spouts a long stream of blood over Randy. Convinced he's cured, he rises from his wheelchair and vows never to drink again. The next day at Whistlin' Willy's, the news shows Pope Benedict XVI investigating: the statue bled from its vagina, not its ass — and "chicks bleed out their vaginas all the time," so no miracle. Randy declares himself powerless again, and the alcoholics raid the bar. Randy flees with drinks; Stan catches him and, after a long speech, convinces him he was in control all along. Randy vows never to drink again — but Stan counters that quitting entirely still lets drinking control his life; true discipline is moderation. Randy piggybacks Stan home into the sunset.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh; Randy Marsh; Kyle and Cartman; Mrs. Garrison; the AA group; Pope Benedict XVI.

Locations: karate class, the school, AA meetings, St. Peter's Church, Whistlin' Willy's.

Key events & continuity: Randy's DUI costs him his license; AA convinces him he's diseased and he takes to a wheelchair; the Virgin Mary bleeds from her "ass" — then, per the Pope, her vagina, voiding the miracle; Stan's closing argument lands on moderation; the piggyback ride closes the season.

A fake "Previously on South Park" shows Chef leaving to join the Super Adventure Club; the boys give him a tearful farewell. Three months later the doorbell rings: "It's Chef!" — "Hello there children!" — and the boys hug him. The town is delighted; Chef stays at Jimbo and Ned's. The boys notice his voice changed but shrug it off. In the lunch line, Clyde says Chef wants to have sex with him; they dismiss it. Then Chef asks the boys to meet up and make love. Horrified, they warn him to stop; he ignores them. Police question the pupils, a cop using a doll to demonstrate possible molestation.

The boys visit the club's headquarters and learn the truth: the club "adventures" around the world having sex with children. Chef is brainwashed. A psychiatrist prescribes a cure — return Chef to his old pastime of women — and takes them to the Peppermint Hippo strip club. Chef is uninterested until a large black pole dancer catches his eye; he snaps out of it, but the club tranquilizes him. At headquarters, leader William Connelly explains: the founder, always beaten to new discoveries, settled for being first to have sex with native children at each destination, believing it granted immortality. The boys call it ridiculous; Connelly says it's no more ridiculous than any religious parable. The boys refuse to leave without Chef; thanks to a Kenny attack move, they escape across a rope bridge. The club reminds Chef he sought adventure from a dull life; Stan reminds him they love him. Chef apologizes and crosses to the club. Lightning strikes the bridge; Chef catches fire, falls, smashes into rocks, and is impaled on a branch. A mountain lion and a grizzly attack; a wild club shot hits Chef. The beasts rip his face off and tear him apart. Stan cries, "Oh my God, they killed Chef!" and Kyle snarls, "You bastards! You bastards!" — in Kenny's style. Cartman notes your last act before dying is crapping your pants — and Chef's body voids its bowels. At the funeral, the coffin holds Chef's spatula. Kyle says to blame "that fruity little club, for scrambling his brains." At the club, Chef's corpse is fitted into a Darth Vader-like suit with a glowing red spatula.

Featured characters: Chef; the boys; William Connelly; the Super Adventure Club.

Locations: the school, the club headquarters, the Peppermint Hippo, the rope bridge, the funeral.

Key events & continuity: Chef returns brainwashed and dies on the rope bridge; Stan and Kyle deliver the "they killed Chef / you bastards" bit; Kyle blames the club; Chef's corpse is rebuilt into a Vader-like suit.

Gerald buys a hybrid Toyonda Pious, shows it off, and campaigns to convert the town. He annoys Randy — talking with eyes closed, liking the smell of his own farts — and moves the family to San Francisco, vowing not to return until everyone feels as he does. Stan is horrified; Cartman is ecstatic, throwing Kyle a party without inviting him. Stan writes a hybrid-cars song; it's a radio hit, and everyone starts driving hybrids — as smugly as Gerald. Ranger McFriendly punches Stan: smog is down, but hybrid drivers emit toxic "smug" gas. South Park ranks second nationally, behind San Francisco.

In SF, Gerald meets progressives who fart mid-conversation, sniff with pleasure, and resume philosophizing. Kyle can't fit in; the local kids take drugs to cope with parental smugginess. He refuses acid — then, watching his dad sniff his own fart, asks for "maybe just half a hit"; Ike asks for three. Cartman tries filling the void by ripping on Butters as a "stupid Jew," but Butters won't fight back, and Cartman grows bored without his nemesis. The smug clouds merge; in a Perfect Storm parody, a reporter warns that George Clooney's 78th Oscars speech smug will join the supercell, forming "the perfect storm of self-satisfaction" to destroy both cities.

Stan must help eliminate hybrids, while Cartman — desperate to get Kyle back so he can resume hating him — infiltrates SF with Butters in an "anti-smug suit" fed by a ridiculously long air hose. As the storm rages across five states, Cartman finds the Broflovskis stoned on smug. The storm destroys thousands of South Park homes; San Francisco "disappears completely up its own asshole." All assume the Broflovskis dead — until Clyde reports they awoke on a bus, thanking a "guardian angel": Cartman. Cars destroyed, the town vows never to buy hybrids. Kyle notes hybrids are good — drivers just shouldn't be smug. The people admit they're not ready — "simply too much to ask" — and return to SUVs. Cartman and Kyle fight; Cartman is relieved the status quo is back.

Featured characters: Stan; Kyle; Gerald; Cartman; Butters; Randy; Ike; Ranger McFriendly; Clyde.

Locations: South Park, San Francisco, the Broflovskis' SF house, the storm supercell.

Key events & continuity: hybrids generate toxic "smug"; SF disappears up its own asshole; Cartman secretly saves the Broflovskis; the town returns to SUVs, smug-free driving being "too much to ask"; Cartman is relieved to have Kyle back.

Panic grips South Park when news reports that Family Guy will air an episode depicting the Muslim Prophet Muhammad; the town shelters in the community center fearing a terrorist attack. The next morning, Fox is revealed to have censored Muhammad at the last minute — but the episode was part one of a two-parter, and part two will show Muhammad uncensored. A terrorist video threatening the United States throws the town into panic again. Cartman decides to go to the Fox Network to get the episode pulled, posing as someone offended on behalf of Muslims. That night Kyle dreams of a terrorist attack killing his brother Ike in a bombing, and concludes the greater good requires pulling the episode. Doubting Cartman's motives, he goes along anyway.

At a town meeting, the proposal is to bury their heads in the sand — literally — to show they didn't watch, hear, or support the episode. Stephen Stotch gives a stirring free-speech speech against giving in to terrorism; Randy prefers the sand idea, and the town agrees. Stan protests; Randy snaps, "Stanley, there's no time for your immaturity! Do it!" Stan isn't seen again, presumably with his head in the sand. On tricycles, Cartman lets slip he's not after the episode but the whole show. Kyle points out Cartman's humor resembles Family Guy's and asks why he'd want it gone; Cartman threatens him never to make the comparison. Kyle realizes Cartman doesn't care about Muslims — he used fear as a weapon. Cartman explains: everyone compares his humor to Family Guy, but his jokes are deep, emotional, story-driven, while Family Guy "just has one interchangeable joke after another." He distracts Kyle, flees on his Big Wheel, and a chase ends with Cartman driving Kyle off the road with Cheesy Poofs; Kyle's tricycle tumbles off a cliff and explodes. Kyle vows he won't let Cartman win. Meanwhile George Bush meets the Fox president to get the episode pulled; the president says he can't — and there's something Bush needs to know about Family Guy's writers.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman; Kyle Broflovski; Stan Marsh; Randy Marsh; Stephen Stotch; Ike Broflovski (in Kyle's nightmare); George W. Bush; the Fox Network president.

Locations: South Park, the community center, City Hall, the road to Hollywood, the Fox Network (via Bush).

Key events & continuity: part one of a two-parter ending on a cliffhanger — the race to Hollywood and the secret of Family Guy's writers unresolved; the town literally buries its heads in the sand; Cartman's real motive is revealed as hatred of being compared to Family Guy; Kyle's tricycle explodes off a cliff; Stephen Stotch's free-speech stand is overruled.

A recap announces part two won't air — a Terrance and Phillip episode runs instead, featuring their friend Muhammad, censored. They demand the CBC re-run it uncensored; the head cites new censorship rules, noting someone is probably heading to FOX to pull the Family Guy episode. At FOX Studios, Cartman meets a Bart Simpson-like kid while waiting to see executives. Kyle reaches a diner of head-buried patrons; a gunman demands why Kyle's head isn't buried, then drives him to FOX — he's a Family Guy fan.

Cartman talks the Bart-like kid into letting him handle things alone. Posing as Danish boy Danny Pocket, Cartman claims his father was killed over a Muhammad cartoon and begs the executives to pull the episode; moved, they send him to convince the writing staff. Kyle asks Bart for directions and is tricked into a maintenance closet and knocked out with a skateboard. Outside, the President tells the press pulling Family Guy is unconstitutional; the media, dependent on the First Amendment, sneers at free speech as stupid. Cartman discovers the writers are manatees — the only mammals unmoved by terrorist threats. Their tank of "idea-balls" becomes jokes five balls at a time; remove one ball and they deem the subject unusable — and if one thing can't be used, nothing can. Cartman steals an idea-ball while Bart holds Kyle in a net. The manatees stop working. He tells the FOX president not to be pushed around by manatees, and the president decides — with difficulty — to pull the episode.

Kyle talks Bart into freeing him — he's on a slippery slope to becoming Cartman. Cartman and Kyle brawl across the studio, smashing through the King of the Hill studios. Cartman feigns surrender, kicks Kyle in the balls; Bart knocks Cartman out with his skateboard. Kyle reaches the president's office and argues against pulling it. Cartman arrives with a gun, but Kyle's anti-terrorism speech wins; Cartman tries to shoot them — the gun is empty. The episode airs: Muhammad gives Peter Griffin a "salmon-football helmet." We never see Muhammad, since Comedy Central refused to show him. The terrorists retaliate with a cartoon of Americans — the President, Tom Cruise — defecating on each other, Jesus defecating on all of them and the flag. The terrorist calls it way funnier than Family Guy.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman; Kyle Broflovski; the Bart-like kid; the FOX president; the manatee writers; Terrance and Phillip.

Locations: FOX Studios, the diner, the CBC.

Key events & continuity: the two-parter resolves with Muhammad still censored; the writers are manatees with idea-balls; Cartman's gun is empty; Kyle's speech wins; the terrorists' retaliation cartoon closes the saga.

Towelie works at P.F. Chang's, but he's high, too busy mixing sauce to care, and gets fired for cluelessness. Jobless and facing unpaid rent, he debates getting high — it causes problems, but it makes him smarter. He gets high and gets an idea: he types up his autobiography, "A Million Little Fibers." A publisher rejects it — nobody wants a towel's autobiography. So Towelie crosses out every "towel" and writes "person." Disguised with a fake mustache and hat as "Steven McTowelie," he sells it to a new publisher. The book becomes a hit and lands on Oprah's Book of the Month. Meanwhile Oprah's vagina (Mingey) and anus (Gary) complain about how little attention they get. Towelie's appearance makes the book a bestseller — so Mingey and Gary phone Geraldo Rivera to expose that Oprah gave the award to a towel, hoping she'll be disliked, lose her job, and they'll get more attention. Geraldo reveals it on Larry King Live. Oprah shrugs: people were inspired by the writing, not its truth. Mobs protest anyway; Oprah invites Towelie back, promising he can explain he only made it relatable — then erupts, whipping the audience into a lynch mob. Towelie is cornered at the First National Bank of Chicago.

As the mob closes in, Mingey — fearing the plan is failing — tears through Oprah's pants with a revolver, takes hostages, guns down a police officer, and demands an escape to France. Gary begs him to surrender; Mingey refuses — he killed a policeman, they'll fry him. Towelie resists the urge to get high, realizing a stoned idea will only get him into trouble. He squeezes through a gap in the door, opens it, and ushers everyone inside. A policeman shoots Gary; dying, Gary asks Mingey if they ever made it to Paris, and Mingey lies that they did — then shoots himself. The hostages thank Towelie and apologize for trying to kill him. Towelie concludes getting high should be a reward, not a source of ideas.

Featured characters: Towelie as "Steven McTowelie"; Oprah Winfrey; Mingey and Gary; Geraldo Rivera; the mob; the hostages.

Locations: P.F. Chang's, the publishers, Oprah's show, the First National Bank of Chicago.

Key events & continuity: Towelie's memoir becomes an Oprah bestseller after a find-and-replace of "towel" with "person"; Mingey and Gary's sabotage plot backfires into a hostage crisis; both die — Gary shot by police, Mingey by suicide after lying about Paris; Towelie resolves to treat getting high as a reward, not an idea generator.

Al Gore warns a school assembly about ManBearPig — a ferocious menace to mankind. Nobody takes him seriously. Gore finds the boys playing basketball and, dressed as ManBearPig, fails to scare them. He gets them to sign his awareness sheet and take a bumper sticker. Randy drives them home: no ManBearPig exists; Gore just wants attention. That night Gore phones Stan, begging the boys to attend a morning ManBearPig meeting. Stan pleads school; Gore accuses disbelief. Feeling sorry, Stan claims he's scared he can't stop ManBearPig, and agrees. The others demand why they're going; Stan admits pity for Gore.

Stan notes his geologist dad says ManBearPig isn't in the area — and lacks hooves. Gore's navigation screen pings in the Cave of the Winds: ManBearPig! The boys cite school, then change their minds when Gore offers to get them excused. Inside, Gore has them hunt for droppings — like pig droppings, but more manbear. He mistakes the cave's wind for ManBearPig, opens fire on the walls, and the rockfall traps the boys. Searching for a way out, Cartman finds a chest of apparent treasure; the only exit is a steep path, so they stay put. Cartman hoards the treasure and starts eating it, swelling grotesquely while the boys assume he's ill. Gore tells the rescue team to flood the cave with molten lead; the worker refuses — it would kill the boys. The dig plan targets "Smuggler's Den," a photo spot with fake treasure. Impatient, Gore diverts a stream to flood the cave himself. The boys realize what's happening; Kyle swims out with a bloated Cartman leaning on him. Outside, the rescue team assumes nothing survived, and Gore quietly celebrates having "killed ManBearPig once and for all." At the memorial, the boys walk in; Gore claims he saved them. Stan admits he was only nice out of pity and calls him a loser; Gore counters the man who stopped ManBearPig alone is hardly a loser. Cartman craps out the treasure — worth about $14, not real — and Kyle lectures him for making him carry his bloated body. Gore announces he'll make a movie about himself, dons a cape, and tries to fly. Cartman craps out a golden vase.

Featured characters: Al Gore; Stan, Kyle, Cartman, Kenny; Randy; Mr. Mackey.

Locations: South Park Elementary, the basketball court, the Cave of the Winds, Smuggler's Den, the memorial service.

Key events & continuity: Gore's ManBearPig crusade debuts; he floods the cave, trapping the boys; Cartman eats and craps out the fake treasure — worth $14, plus a golden vase; Stan calls Gore a loser; Gore vows a movie about himself and tries to fly in a cape.

Mr. Mackey summons Liane and Cartman to discuss Cartman's behavior; Liane bursts into tears over how uncontrollable her son is. Mackey recommends the TV show Nanny 911. At home, Cartman is on his Xbox 360 when Nanny Stella arrives with her camera crew. She takes his Xbox; he takes revenge by manipulating her into leaving — asking why she has no kids of her own, spitting on her mouth when she tries to speak, telling her it's because she's ugly and too old. Horrified, she marches out. Supernanny fails next, ending up in a mental institute feeding on her own feces. Her doctor recommends another show: The Dog Whisperer.

Cesar Millan arrives and instantly impacts Cartman — by treating him like a dog: nipping his neck, walking him on a leash, explaining dominance. Enraged, Cartman runs away from home. He begs Stan, Kyle, Kenny, Butters, Jimmy, and Craig for a place to stay; all refuse, and he sleeps in a rainy alleyway. He returns to find Cesar still there. Cartman threatens to call Child Protective Services, but Liane finally turns dominant, and her son turns submissive. Cartman starts behaving — and realizes, to his horror, that he's changing for the worse. He plots matricide; Stan, Kyle, Kenny, and Butters refuse to help. That night, about to act, he's stopped by the strange reemergence of his heavily repressed conscience, which convinces him the changes are for the best. He vomits up black fluid — the evil within — wrestles his two sides, and passes out. In the morning, Liane finds Cartman doing homework over a healthy breakfast. Cesar pays a final visit; Liane invites him to Madame Butterfly, but he says she's just a client and has other work. Disheartened, Liane invites Cartman instead, as if her son were her friend, promising a Mega Ranger if he goes. He asks for two; she agrees he can have whatever he wants. Cartman returns to "normal" — with a sinister look.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman; Liane Cartman; Cesar Millan; Nanny Stella; Supernanny; Mr. Mackey; Stan, Kyle, Kenny, and Butters.

Locations: South Park Elementary, the Cartman home, the alleyway, the mental institute.

Key events & continuity: Nanny 911 and Supernanny both fail catastrophically; Cesar Millan's dog-domination tactics actually tame Cartman; Cartman plots matricide, then vomits out his evil as black fluid; Liane's relapse into spoiling him restores his "normal" self with a sinister look.

The boys are playing World of Warcraft when Randy tells Stan to socialize. "I'm socializing," Stan says. "Online." A rogue high-level player kills them despite no agreed duel. They phone Blizzard support; the rep promises a fix and warns the men upstairs: complaints are mounting. The admins panic. The CEO explains the rogue has farmed every hour of every day for a year and a half, growing able to kill Game Masters and admins. "He has absolutely no life. How do you kill that which has no life?" Randy starts playing WoW and brags to a colleague — until the same player kills him.

Cartman summons his male classmates to his basement with a plan to team up that night. Butters admits he's been on Hello Kitty Island Adventure; Cartman orders him to buy WoW or be "murdered." The mass attack fails: Clyde stopped to read Playboy, Cartman barred Butters from playing a dwarf, and Randy joined in. The admins despair. Cartman pitches grinding boars alone in the woods, where no battles happen — 65 million XP in seven weeks. A "Live to Win" montage shows weeks of boar slaughter; they balloon to Cartman's size — Cartman doubles. Hope returns for the admins. Legend speaks of the Sword of a Thousand Truths, too powerful for the game; staff fetch its USB drive.

On battle day, Liane supplies a basement marathon. Two Blizzard staffers reach Stan's house: they must give Stan the sword or his character dies. Seventeen hours in, Kyle gets carpal tunnel; Cartman hands him cream. Randy and the staff find Stan's room empty — he took his computer to Cartman's. Randy has an account but is a noob; the staff relent. Cartman calls his mom for a bedpan. Randy hijacks a car to Best Buy, shoves a kid off a computer, logs in, and learns to pass items. Stan lifts the sword; Randy is knocked down. Stan blasts the rogue, dropping his defenses; the boys pour it on until Cartman — "Looks like you're about to get pwned!" — crushes his head with a hammer. The nerd stares in disbelief. Stan rushes to his dad's body; Randy declares his love, dies dramatically, and logs out. Stan asks what now. Cartman: now they can finally play the game.

Featured characters: Stan, Kyle, Cartman, Kenny; Randy; the rogue player; the Blizzard staff; Liane; the classmates.

Locations: Cartman's basement, Stan's house, Best Buy, the WoW world, Blizzard HQ.

Key events & continuity: the rogue farmed 18 months and can kill Game Masters; the boys grind boars for seven weeks; the Sword of a Thousand Truths exists only on USB; Randy dies dramatically to deliver it; Cartman's "pwned" hammer blow ends it.

entries.n: S10E09 — Mystery of the Urinal Deuce
entries.t:
Mr. Mackey interrupts class: someone defecated in the boys' bathroom urinal, and he takes it very seriously. The boys find his euphemisms hilarious. Cartman links it to 9/11 and builds a conspiracy theory; Kyle tells him to shut up. Police find nothing and call the Hardly Boys — young whippersnappers who follow their erections to evidence. They're incompetent. Cartman pushes the 9/11 conspiracy, noting a fourth of Americans believe it was planned; Stan and Kyle counter that a fourth of Americans are retarded, Cartman included. Cartman polls Butters, who blames Bush, and Cartman blames the Jews. His Show and Tell PowerPoint "proves" the conspiracy with math — framing Kyle with faked evidence, including a drawing of Kyle floating by the World Trade Center with a knife. The class shuns Kyle; a shocked Sheila takes it to the PTA, where some staff and parents now believe the conspiracy too.

Stan shows Kyle a website proving his innocence; they visit the 9/11 truth webmaster, who blames a government False Flag and hands Kyle two jars of anthrax. A SWAT team seizes all three. At the White House, the president kills the webmaster to cover up, and the boys learn 9/11 was indeed a giant government conspiracy — to justify invading the Middle East for an oil monopoly. Bush tries to shoot them, misses, and they escape. In Chicago they spot the webmaster alive; another man shoots him again and takes the boys home — he's the Hardly Boys' father. All conspiracy websites are government-run. Bush emerges and confesses: the government was NOT behind 9/11. They told the truth, but since a fourth of Americans are retarded, they let them believe the government is all-powerful enough to attack its own country. Asked how everyone knew they were there, Stan puts a gun to Kyle's head — then confesses: HE defecated in the urinal. He dragged Kyle along to sell the story; the government runs the sites to seem more powerful. The Muslims were behind 9/11, and everyone calls Kyle a retard. Stan's punishment: cleaning the urinal, laughing at Mackey's euphemisms.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh; Kyle Broflovski; Eric Cartman; Mr. Mackey; the Hardly Boys and their father; the webmaster; George W. Bush.

Locations: the school, the boys' bathroom, the PTA, the webmaster's house, the White House, Chicago.

Key events & continuity: Stan was the urinal defecator; the government runs conspiracy sites to seem all-powerful; Bush admits they didn't do 9/11; the webmaster dies twice; Stan cleans the urinal.

entries.n: S10E10 — Miss Teacher Bangs a Boy
entries.t:
Cartman is sent to the principal's office by a ginger hall monitor — after telling the kid he has no friends and should kill himself. Expecting discipline, Cartman is instead named the new School Hall Monitor: "Authoritah." He takes to it instantly, bullying students as a Dog the Bounty Hunter cosplay. He busts Ike for littering a crumpled drawing of his kindergarten teacher, Ms. Stevenson, covered in hearts. After class, Ms. Stevenson keeps Ike late: his feelings are inappropriate — but she shares them. An illegal relationship begins: love notes, dates, sex. Kyle is sent to collect Ike from supposed tutoring; the door is unlocked, and he walks in on them in the bathtub. They confess their love; Kyle is horrified.

At dinner, Kyle tries to tell his mother, but Ike's cuteness keeps interrupting; Sheila says he's way too young for the talk. The police see no problem — a beautiful woman with an underage boy makes him the luckiest boy in America. Kyle turns to his friends, who agree — until he lets slip they make out in the hallways. A hallway infraction! Cartman catches them and bear-maces Ms. Stevenson. He shows Principal Victoria the proof; Ms. Stevenson is arrested and fired, to the crowd's confusion — Randy especially can't grasp why a hot woman is being arrested. She dodges prison with the "Mel Gibson Defense," claiming alcoholism. Ike blames Kyle and cuts him off. After rehab — practically a revolving door — she drives to Ike's house; they sneak out to flee to Milan. Kyle is ready to quit, but Cartman drafts him, assembling a Dog-style team for $15 — Leroy, Earl, and Beth — who trace the couple via Travelocity to a hotel. They check rooms, bear-macing bystanders; the hotel calls the police, and the fugitives run at the sirens. Cartman's team chases them to the roof, police behind. Realizing it's the kidnapping-report woman, police close in. Cornered, the pair choose their backup plan: jump, since no one accepts their love. Kyle gives Ike a speech about truly living before ruining his life. Ms. Stevenson jumps to her death; Ike stops at the last second. The brothers reunite, and Cartman closes with: "If you don't go with Christ, you could end up like that splattered bitch on the pavement."

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, hall monitor; Kyle and Ike Broflovski; Ms. Stevenson; Principal Victoria; Sergeant Yates; Randy.

Locations: the school, Ms. Stevenson's house, the police station, the hotel roof.

Key events & continuity: Cartman gains "Authoritah" and cosplays Dog the Bounty Hunter; Yates declares Ike the luckiest boy in America; the "Mel Gibson Defense" frees Ms. Stevenson; Kyle's speech saves Ike; Ms. Stevenson dies jumping.

Satan throws a massive Halloween party in Los Angeles, as meticulously perfect as a sweet sixteen. The damned need a blue wristband and a costume; no-shows are losers. Nobody may dress as The Crow — that's his costume — so he swaps schoolgirl costumes with his minion Zazul: "No one can look hotter than me!" He obsesses over a dessert surprise: fondue fountain — Diddy had one. Doughnut machine — Diddy had it. Ice cream bar — Diddy had it. He settles on a Ferrari Enzo-sized cake, ordering serial killers Ted Bundy, Jeffrey Dahmer, and John Wayne Gacy to bring it. The uninvited Catholic Church plots to call the fire marshal and ruin the night.

The boys try a Bloody Mary-type ritual to summon Biggie Smalls; Butters succeeds. Biggie has a wristband but, on Earth, can't use Hell's vortex — so he demands Butters get him to LA. When Butters vanishes, the kids retry the ritual; Biggie, on a plane to LA with Butters, teleports back to South Park against his will and opens fire in a rage. Randy later summons him again. The Church tries calling the fire marshal, but Satan invited the marshals himself; the priests try crashing with Knott's Berry Farm wristbands and are stopped. The killers' cake run goes wrong: they've killed the bakers, and everyone they recruit, Gacy murders while Dahmer commits necrophilia and cannibalism; Bundy's discipline only slows them down. A failed lift destroys the cake; trying to bake a new one, they mutilate each other — Gacy pokes out Bundy's eye, Bundy gouges out Gacy's eyes, Dahmer stabs Bundy through the ribs, Bundy rips out Dahmer's tongue — and all three collapse. Satan's assistant Demonius finds a substitute on his BlackBerry: a cake the exact size and shape of an Acura TSX. Satan rampages over the Acura cake — the party is about HIM. The crowd turns, and he realizes he's become a My Super Sweet 16 girl. He apologizes: the party is for everyone who makes his life special. He invites everyone in, priests included. Butters reaches the party and mirror-summons Biggie straight there; Biggie brings Butters in as thanks, and Butters agrees — he's getting grounded anyway. Everyone dances, including the apparently pedophilic priests holding leashes attached to naked altar boys.

Featured characters: Satan; Bundy, Dahmer, and Gacy; Butters; Biggie Smalls; Zazul; Demonius; Randy; the priests.

Locations: Los Angeles, the party venue, South Park, the plane.

Key events & continuity: Satan's sweet-sixteen Halloween party; the killers destroy the Ferrari cake and each other; the Acura cake triggers Satan's meltdown and apology; the Church's sabotage fails; Biggie is summoned twice against his will.

Cartman paces outside the mall, impatient for the Wii — three weeks away. Liane drags him home. Mrs. Garrison refuses to teach evolution, calling it "bullcrap," until Principal Victoria forces her. Garrison teaches it her way: we were fish; a fish couple had a "retard baby" that survived and made more retard babies; one crawled out, had butt sex with a squirrel, making a retard frog squirrel; that had butt sex with a monkey — "you're the retarded offspring of five monkeys having butt sex with a fish squirrel." Cartman bolts, unable to stand the Wii wait; Garrison mistakes it for evolution distress. A shopkeeper repeats for the fortieth time that pacing won't make the Wii come faster. Sleepless that night, Cartman decides to freeze himself to skip the wait; Stan, Kyle, and Kenny refuse to help.

Parents complain their daughter thinks she's a "retarded fish frog," so Victoria replaces Garrison with Richard Dawkins. Garrison sabotages him until Dawkins mentions he's an atheist — she erupts. Victoria moves to remove her, but Dawkins defends her and asks her on a date. She's thrilled: her first date with a man since her sex change. Liane finds him in the freezer and orders patience. Cartman turns to Butters; they hike into the mountains, Butters memorizing the landscape so no one finds him early. An avalanche buries him that night. The date ends in sex. Cartman is unfrozen in the year 2546 — unbothered that everyone he knew is dead, but devastated the Wii doesn't exist. Back in the past, Garrison has flipped: religion is stupid, not science. She dunce-caps Stan with "I have faith," and she and Dawkins resolve to get rid of religion. Butters panics when his mother and police ask about Cartman; Dougie says freezing yourself is certain death. They can't find Cartman after the avalanche, and Dougie convinces Butters to stay silent or face jail. In the future, his unfreezers say a Wii might sit in the museum of technology — if he helps them. A great event made the world atheist; someone from his time founded the "Unified Atheist League." The rival "United Atheist Alliance" attacks, and the "Allied Atheist Alliance" — super-intelligent sea otters, also at war — declares open war over the "Time Child," wanting a sea-otter era.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman; Mrs. Garrison; Richard Dawkins; Liane; Butters and Dougie; Stan, Kyle, Kenny; Principal Victoria.

Locations: the mall, the school, the Cartman freezer, the mountains, the year 2546.

Key events & continuity: part one of a two-parter; Garrison's "retard fish" lecture; her Dawkins date flips her to militant atheism; Cartman wakes in 2546; three atheist factions war over the "Time Child"; Butters covers up losing Cartman.

Still trapped in the future, Cartman cooperates with the sea-otter Allied Atheist Alliance for a Wii from the abandoned technology museum, then warps back to United Atheist Alliance headquarters. The ancient Wii won't work with the Float Screen, but he finds the Crank Prank Time Phone, which can prank-call the past. His plan: talk his past self out of freezing. Richard Dawkins founded worldwide atheism. His wife Mrs. Garrison insisted "logic and reason aren't enough: you also have to be a dick to everyone who doesn't think like you." Atheism split into three factions over the "Great Question," each calling the others' answer illogical — the AAA also objects to tables instead of eating off "tummies," while ironically revering Dawkins. The otters bait the UAA with false clam fields, leaving both them and the Unified Atheist League (UAL) exposed. When the "Wise One" otter suggests the war may be unjust, a mob kills him.

Cartman Time-Phones his past self, Butters, and Kyle to stop the freezing. Nobody believes him. The Kyle call makes Kyle miss a ride, altering the future slightly — Cartman's clothes change; his robotic dog K-10 becomes cat KIT-9. In the UAA war room, Cartman learns the war is over the Great Question: "what atheists should call themselves." KIT-9 tells him to call Mrs. Garrison. Dawkins answers mid-coitus and learns Garrison had a sex change. Disgusted, he leaves on the spot. Garrison calls him an "atheist faggot" and reverts. The future shifts: Cartman sits with all three factions at peace — rid not of religion but of "all their --isms." He asks if war is over; a sea otter: "Of course there's war! The stupid French-Chinese think they have a right to Hawaii!" The leaders declare his purpose fulfilled — never revealed — and send him home: no single answer is the answer to everything. He materializes before EvGames and merges with his past self, overjoyed — until he realizes they sent him back to September, stretching his wait from three weeks to two months. An employee says there's a call: another future Cartman, pleading with him not to do what he's thinking. In that alternate future, future Cartman stands with bald people on giant purple bubbles. Cartman assumes it's Kyle's prank call. He learned nothing.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman, the Time Child; Mrs. Garrison; Richard Dawkins; Butters; Kyle; KIT-9; the Wise One.

Locations: New New Hampshire, the UAA headquarters, EvGames, the year 2546.

Key events & continuity: Dawkins founded atheism and married Garrison; the Great Question is what atheists should call themselves; the split rewrites the future; Cartman returns to September, dismissing the warning call as Kyle's prank.

Stan's boss Mr. Jarvis berates him for sloppy paperboy work — and Stan's bike is being towed. He fails to stop the council, and his job is in danger. The council offers a deal: coach the Park County Pee-Wee Hockey Team and get the bike back. At the arena, Stan finds the kids hopelessly inexperienced — especially Nelson Brown, a boy with cancer. Randy is convinced Stan is coaching to atone for his own pee-wee hockey draw years ago, which Stan doesn't even remember. Nelson takes a turn for the worse, and his parents beg Stan to tell Nelson he's dying instead of doing it themselves. Nelson asks one thing: win the next match against the Adams County team. It ends in a draw — which, per his doctor, Dr. Doctor, puts Nelson in "cancer limbo." Nelson pins everything on beating Denver next; a loss means certain death.

Stan talks to the team, who suggest finding a Canadian ringer. He auditions Ike, despite Kyle warning their mother will kill him if Ike gets hurt. Randy melodramatically announces he won't watch the match, then changes his mind unprompted. At the Pepsi Center, the opposing team no-shows, so the Colorado Avalanche lets Park County play the Detroit Red Wings instead. It's a slaughter: the Red Wings thrash the kindergarteners in a landslide, even mutilating them. One kid declares he hates Stan. At the hospital, Nelson loses hope — and dies. The Red Wings hoist the trophy and celebrate excessively while Stan looks on in shock.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh, the reluctant coach; Nelson Brown; Randy Marsh; Kyle Broflovski and Ike Broflovski; Mr. Jarvis; Dr. Doctor; the Detroit Red Wings.

Locations: the paper route, the council office, the hockey arena, the Pepsi Center, the hospital.

Key events & continuity: Stan becomes a pee-wee hockey coach to save his paperboy job; Nelson's "cancer limbo" hinges on a draw; Ike is recruited as the Canadian ringer; the Red Wings massacre the team; Nelson dies; the season ends on Stan watching the Red Wings celebrate.

entries.n: S11E01 — With Apologies to Jesse Jackson
entries.t:
Randy reaches the Bonus round on Wheel of Fortune, live on national TV. Category: "People Who Annoy You." Letters reveal N_GGERS with one letter left. A black camera operator glares; rushed, Randy yells his answer — shocking millions and enraging African-Americans. He's wrong: the answer was "Naggers." The next day, Stan braces for fallout. Cartman warns Tolkien will want to beat him up; Stan tries explaining his dad isn't racist, just stupid. Cartman tries to ignite a "Race War." Tolkien says Stan doesn't understand and walks away. Cartman screams, "Whites win!"

Randy seeks Jesse Jackson's forgiveness; Jackson has him apologize by kissing his butt. A photo hits the news. Stan expects Tolkien mollified; Tolkien snaps, "Jesse Jackson is not the emperor of black people!" Stan: "He told my dad he was..." The school hires little person Dr. David Nelson to lecture on sensitivity. Cartman laughs uncontrollably the moment Nelson takes the stage. At a comedy club, the comic singles Randy out as the "Nigger-Guy"; soon everyone calls him that. Nelson requests a meeting with Cartman via the principal; Cartman just laughs in his face. Nelson insists words can't hurt him — then snaps and screams, "Shut your fucking mouth!" Stan claims he now understands the N-word after watching Cartman laugh at Nelson. Tolkien's still mad.
