The volleyball coach laments empty stands while Stan cracks wise — then learns Wendy is captain. Yates, convinced Randy's performances are the rooster fights, arrests the kindergartner's mother for a false report. That night the boys (minus Stan) pay ten dollars at Panda Express's back room to face Gadnuk, Breaker of Worlds; Stan stays on the phone from the volleyball game while Kenny pilots McNuggets — nearly winning when the cops raid. Asked how they found it, Yates cites fliers nobody distributed. Then Randy takes the stage with his penis-magic routine; in the disgust and chaos, everyone escapes. Next day Stan decides to make amends properly: help the girls' volleyball team. It ends with South Park versus McNuggets in a volleyball/Magic hybrid.

Featured characters: Kenny McCormick; Stan Marsh; Eric Cartman; Kyle Broflovski; Butters Stotch; Wendy Testaburger; Randy and Sharon Marsh; Sergeant Yates; Stuart McCormick; Tuong Lu Kim; Slaughterhouse; McNuggets; Gadnuk, Breaker of Worlds; the school janitor.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the basement of City Wok; Panda Express; M Burgers; the Marsh and McCormick residences; the poultry dealer; the kindergartner's birthday party.

Key events & continuity: Kenny's elite Magic: The Gathering skills become the engine of an underground rooster-fighting circuit; Randy's parallel misunderstanding of "Cock Magic" accidentally becomes the perfect distraction for a police raid; Wendy's captaincy of the volleyball team finally gets Stan's attention — after everything else.

Kyle hurries home to game with Ike, who will not look up from PewDiePie's Let's Play videos. Kyle is baffled that kids prefer watching rehashed gameplay to playing; Cartman smells an audience and launches his own commentary channel over videos of Kyle and Stan — infuriating Kyle, especially learning Ike subscribes. Randy learns a benefit concert will feature the top pop acts, including his secret persona Lorde; he tries to back out over pitch-correction shame, but his producer cites Stan's freemium debts — and Shelly begs to see her "real" idol. Backstage, Randy balks; the producer says audiences do not care about sound — "pump your hips and rub your clit" — and Randy's objection sparks a scuffle with Iggy Azalea, who then performs with a Michael Jackson hologram. Randy feels something essential dying in the rehash of dead stars. Kyle invites Ike's friends for real gaming; they watch Let's Plays on their phones in Ike's room, dismissing Kyle and Stan as "grandpas." Kyle mourns his dying living room. Randy's off-key shambolic set turns the crowd; he accidentally frees the Jackson hologram, gropes himself to win them back, enraging them further — and Shelly rips her Lorde poster down. The producer schools him: fame was never about music, only the publicity of antics — which Randy has supplied. Randy resolves to reveal he is Lorde. The escaped Jackson hologram buses toward South Park on "important business"; Syntech activates its Tupac hologram, which steals a car in pursuit. Randy tells the producer he is going public; the producer says artists are revenue engines — a Lorde hologram will expose her anus on Fallon for publicity — and his henchmen move on Randy. He escapes home and tells Sharon; she is horrified she just slept with a hologram — Tupac's, not Randy's. The producer conspires with Cartman: install him as figurehead of a hologram-driven social revolution.

Featured characters: Kyle and Ike Broflovski; Eric Cartman; Stan Marsh; Randy, Sharon, and Shelly Marsh; PewDiePie; the Michael Jackson hologram; the Tupac Shakur hologram; Iggy Azalea; Randy's record producer.

Locations: The Broflovski and Marsh residences; the benefit concert; the bus to South Park.

Key events & continuity: The generational war over Let's Play videos — watching versus playing — becomes the season's cultural fault line, with Kyle cast as the "grandpa"; Randy's Lorde secret inches toward exposure as his producer pivots to hologram performers; the escaped Jackson hologram sets up the finale's confrontation.

Kyle narrates the wreckage — the trending, the scattered family, the dying living rooms — and answers with #savethelivingroom. Bill Cosby comes to the door wanting the trend for a holiday special; the door closes, and "Cosby" is revealed as a hologram. Randy tells the whole police station he is Lorde; an officer bursts in: they have arrested the Michael Jackson hologram at the Jeffersons' estate, and the cops cannot process a Black-guy hologram. Kyle rages that Cartman hijacked his idea; Stan is sure Randy is performing as Lorde again. The special — the ex-producer's and Cartman's brainchild, Cartman hired for youth perspective — packs celebrities, dead-star holograms, and Cartman's commentary. But Cartman's window is metastasizing: appearing in thin air, in living rooms and hallways everywhere. Randy and the Jackson hologram agree to stop it together. The Tupac hologram — Syntech's retriever — materializes at the station; the Marshes and Jackson flee home, where Randy learns Stan and Kyle are hostages and the Shakur hologram confronts him. Kyle demands the producer's motive: a grandfather five years on, he wanted to show his grandson entertainment's wonders — but the boy's favorite celebrity was PewDiePie, a Swedish internet nobody, unimpressed by every real artist offered. The special will absorb youth culture and force appreciation of real entertainment. Stan: "such a grandpa." The producer tries to kill Cartman's window — but Cartman is trending so hard he has hit "trend-scendence," like Johnny Depp, but cool. His price all along: he is now "trends-gender" and demands his own bathroom. The holograms corner the producer at his restaurant hideout; Jackson shoots him dead. Then Kyle — visible to everyone on Earth through their screens — speaks to Ike: sorry for being a "grandpa," accepting Ike's own tastes, admitting he was stung that Ike idolized Cartman, asking only to be a family again. Ike's crew answers with #webelieveinyou, which Kyle — breaking the fourth wall — urges the home audience to spread. PewDiePie's window appears; his commentary wipes Cartman's out of existence. Kyle suggests not getting it is the lesson — they have witnessed a new art form's birth — and YouTube stars are at least authentic, not corporate-made. PewDiePie thanks South Park for having him.

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski; Stan Marsh; Ike Broflovski; Eric Cartman; Randy Marsh (Lorde); the Michael Jackson and Tupac Shakur holograms; the ex-producer; PewDiePie.

Locations: The Broflovski home; the police station; the Washington Redskins holiday special set; the producer's restaurant hideout.

Key events & continuity: The three-part arc (#Rehash, #CockMagic, #Holograms) resolves with Kyle's fourth-wall plea; CartmanBrah's commentary window is erased by PewDiePie's; Randy's Lorde secret stays buried under his denials.

Mackey assembles the school: Principal Victoria is fired for ignoring a student calling rape a "hot Cosby." Her replacement, PC Principal, vows to punish the bigotry of past seasons — including Chef's presumed-suicide death. Kyle gets two weeks' detention for saying Caitlyn Jenner is no hero for surgery; Gerald's defense dies when he says "Bruce Jenner" and both are hurled from the office. The dads drown confusion at Crunchy's Micro Brew, where the PC frat bros strong-arm them into declaring Caitlyn "stunning and brave." The bros incorporate as PC Delta. Kyle, Stan, Kenny, and Butters urge Cartman to break rules like his hero Tom Brady. Cartman frames PC Principal for molestation with Butters' underwear in the restroom — but "capiche" and other trigger words earn him a savage beating as his friends watch. Randy wanders into the frat house and is inadvertently pledged and force-fed alcohol. Hospitalized, Cartman is ready to accept they are bigots; Kyle refuses, surer Jenner is a phony. Randy's crew wakes Kyle among pigs painted "Biggit." Cartman dreams he is Brady dodging Deflategate and vows to Butters to be newer, better. Told Kyle is now the frat's target, Cartman — disdaining Kyle's "bigoted" views but refusing violent intolerance — assaults the frat house with two hundred pregnant Mexican women, taco cannons, Syrian refugee children, and Jared Fogle. Kyle storms in mid-siege and calls Jenner a hero, and brave. Applause erupts, ESPY footage rolls, and the gang accepts PC is here to stay. Kyle's bitter read: the only winner was Cartman — like his hero Brady. Cartman savors it: he is going home to "fuck his hot wife, who kind of looks like a dude."

Featured characters: PC Principal; Kyle Broflovski; Eric Cartman; Gerald Broflovski; Randy Marsh; Stan Marsh; Kenny McCormick; Butters Stotch; the PC Bros; Caitlyn Jenner; Tom Brady; Principal Victoria.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the PC Delta fraternity house; Crunchy's Micro Brew; the hospital.

Key events & continuity: Principal Victoria's firing installs PC Principal and launches the season-long PC era; Chef's death is invoked as part of the town's original sins; Cartman — the least PC person in town — emerges as the story's winner, exactly as Kyle predicts.

Kyle is honored by Obama for embracing Caitlyn Jenner while Garrison, watching Canadians slip over the border, snaps. Calling his disruptive Canadian pupils "Canooks" earns him PC Principal's office and a second-language course; he daydreams a protest song, storms a Canadian history play, and is fired. American-Canadian student hostility flares; Cartman, Stan, Butters, Kenny, Tolkien, and Craig decide peace requires reenacting The Lion King II — an American "Hot Cosby"-ing a Canadian. Butters loses "not it." Garrison takes his wall crusade town-wide — "fuck 'em all to death," "make the country great again" — only to find Canada built its own wall first. He barrels over Niagara Falls to see what they are hiding. Meanwhile Butters falls hard for Charlotte, a Canadian girl; at her family's dinner, her father explains the exodus: in the last election a candidate said outrageous things, offered no solutions, was never taken seriously — and was sworn in before anyone got serious. Battered Garrison finds a post-apocalyptic Canada under its new president, storms his office, and the screaming match ends with Garrison raping the president to death. The Canadians stream home; Butters and Charlotte are torn apart. Triumphant, Garrison announces his 2016 presidential run with running mate Caitlyn Jenner. They ride for Washington — after Jenner runs over another young woman.

Featured characters: Mr. Garrison; Butters Stotch; Charlotte and her family; the president of Canada; Caitlyn Jenner; Kyle Broflovski; Cartman, Stan, Kenny, Tolkien, and Craig; PC Principal; Barack Obama.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the U.S.-Canadian border and its rival walls; Niagara Falls; Canada; Washington, D.C.

Key events & continuity: Garrison's anti-Canadian crusade mutates into a presidential campaign with Jenner as his running mate, setting the course for the next two seasons; Butters and Charlotte's cross-border romance is the story's collateral damage; Jenner's habit of running people over with her car begins here and becomes a running gag.

entries.n: S19E03 — The City Part of Town
entries.t:
Fallon mocks South Park on The Tonight Show as a hick town, fallout from Garrison's presidential bid, so the town chases a Whole Foods to rebrand as socially conscious. Mayor McDaniels and Randy fast-track SoDoSoPa — "South of Downtown South Park" — around Kenny's crumbling house, betting hipsters will pay for "rustic charm." Live-action commercials boast the artisanal shops "support" the original poor residents; none of Kenny's family works in or profits from any of them. Apartments, then luxury residences, rise as "revitalization" of the built-around poor. City Wok starves; proprietor Tuong Lu Kim hires child labor, and Kenny — "Dennis" to Kim — gets a job. Randy phones Whole Foods into sending a representative; the town performs virtue, and after PC Principal and SoDoSoPa, the rep is impressed. Then Randy's crew discovers Kim's counter-district: CtPaTown, the "shitty part of town," staffed by his child workers. A mob marches on City Wok; the brawl with the child laborers halts when everyone notices the representative watching. He has never seen a town try so hard to fake social consciousness — exactly what Whole Foods wants. South Park gets its market. All cheer but Kenny and Kim, who counts out Kenny's "child labor wage." Home to his father's cynicism, Kenny gives his sister a new doll — every cent of his wages — then tries to sleep through SoDoSoPa's thumping nightlife. It closes on a glossy Whole Foods commercial.

Featured characters: Randy Marsh; Kenny McCormick; Tuong Lu Kim; Mayor McDaniels; PC Principal; the Whole Foods representative; Kenny's parents and his sister Karen.

Locations: SoDoSoPa; CtPaTown; City Wok; the McCormick home; the Whole Foods Market.

Key events & continuity: South Park's gentrification arc begins in earnest, with SoDoSoPa and CtPaTown as rival monuments to performative progress; Kenny's poverty is put on display as a marketing aesthetic while he quietly spends his first wages on his little sister; the Whole Foods is won not by virtue but by the sheer spectacle of trying to look virtuous.

Randy and Gerald try Vernacular, a SoDoSoPa newcomer: quoted thirty minutes, seated instantly when Gerald admits he is a Yelper — a secret kept so restaurants would not "kiss his ass." Cartman wields the same power tyrannically, shaking a Mexican restaurant down for free dessert on a five-star promise. There he meets busboy David — "Dah-veed" — his own age, the owner's son. Two other citizen-Yelpers swagger in demanding tribute; Cartman is contemptuous: only he deserves critic status. Next day David enrolls at school; Cartman turns the screws — forcing him to claim he rides a "tiny bicicleta," threatening his father's rating, refusing to pronounce "Dah-veed" while demanding David drop his accent. Cartman now orders delivery at lunch. Gerald treats Yelping as high cultural office, neglecting family to perfect a fifty-page Applebee's review of soaring praise ending in a petty pan. Even Yates is drunk on reviewer self-importance. The breaking point: Whistlin' Willy's proprietor melts down and expels the Yelpers, triggering a town-wide ban on Yelpers and food bloggers. Cartman summons the wannabes to show them "how it's done"; the crowd packs the block, each smugly certain he is the destined leader. The mob storms Whistlin' Willy's, beheads the mascot — head ripped clean off — and rampages against the unworshipful. Cartman rules the school again, free to torment David. David denounces the Yelper leader on the news, unnamed; he and Kyle meet outside town to find the whole Yelper army there, all delivering "noble" speeches simultaneously, none hearing the others. Kyle's play with Mayor McDaniels: knight every Yelper as "the best food critic in South Park" with golden badges. Mollified critics return to restaurants — where kitchens quietly taint their food in every imaginable way, serenaded by "The Yelper Special."

Featured characters: Eric Cartman; David, a.k.a. Dah-veed; Gerald Broflovski; Randy Marsh; Kyle Broflovski; Mayor McDaniels; Sergeant Yates; Willy of Whistlin' Willy's.

Locations: Vernacular; South Park Elementary; Whistlin' Willy's; the Cartman residence.

Key events & continuity: David's arrival gives Cartman a new favorite target and plants a character who will keep colliding with him; the golden-badge "solution" lets every Yelper feel like the chosen one while the restaurants exact their own justice; Gerald's fifty-page Applebee's review stands as the peak of reviewer pomposity.

Cartman's underwear weightlifting selfie draws cruel comments and tears. PC Principal's fix: assign a student to filter his social media, printing only positives. Cartman picks Kyle, Wendy, and Butters; refusal means detention. Kyle and Wendy take the two weeks; Butters folds — his parents would ground him. At Whole Foods, a cashier ambushes Randy at checkout for starving-children donations, escalating each visit until Randy gives a dollar and is shamed harder. PC Principal imports Steven Seagal to lecture on body shaming; Seagal confesses he is a victim too, and Butters must filter him as well. The clientele grows — Demi Lovato, plus-size models, Vin Diesel — and the sleep-deprived Butters, scrubbing everyone's feeds all night, comes apart. Randy films a shantytown PSA for supermarket "safe spaces"; he, Cartman, and others perform a celebratory montage stalked by a leering villain, Reality, vowing to destroy them all. To dodge the cashier, Randy announces a "Shameless America" charity dinner where no one may be criticized for anything. Drowning in bile, Butters hallucinates Reality menacing him — and jumps out a school window, landing hospitalized. The Gigi Hadid-hosted dinner is crashed by Reality himself, insulting guests to their faces and forcing the town to face what happened to Butters. The answer: a new PSA spending the charity money on iPads for the starving children, so they can filter everyone's negatives and give the world a safe space. It ends at the town center, where Butters publicly hangs Reality on the gallows.

Featured characters: Eric Cartman; Butters Stotch; PC Principal; Randy Marsh; Kyle Broflovski; Wendy Testaburger; Steven Seagal; Reality; Gigi Hadid; the Whole Foods cashier; Demi Lovato; Vin Diesel.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the Whole Foods Market; the hospital; the town center gallows.

Key events & continuity: Reality is literalized as a personified villain the town can hang, the ultimate safe-space fantasy; Butters' window jump is the cost of being everyone's filter, and his hand on the lever is the town's idea of justice; Randy's war with the donation-shaming cashier drives the Shameless America campaign.

Wendy's assembly slideshow reveals the Asian girls' oeuvre: Craig and Tweek as a couple, in escalating explicitness. The girls swoon; the boys — especially the subjects — are horrified, and the halls debate whether they are gay and who is "next." Tweek spirals: "What if my parents find out?" PC Principal's office answers their denials with an "affirmative consent" lecture. Randy, self-declared "PC dad," briefs a confused Stan: Yaoi is anal intercourse, plus nonsense like "Maui Zaui." At the Tweaks', Tweek's parents announce pride in his gayness; his father presses cash on him. The "Book of Love" montage sweeps town: a giant mural on the school, a brisk Yaoi-print tent, Mayor McDaniels lingering over the boys' photos before glancing at her late husband's framed picture. Cartman recruits his imaginary cherub Cupid Me to the couple's cause; Cupid Me arrows a sleeping Craig, then pees in his mouth "just for fun." Craig's plan: publicly come out, then stage a breakup to kill the art. The staged breakup plays before the artists — but Tweek improvises a cheating "Michael," brands Craig a user, and flees in tears with Wendy chasing. The school turns on Craig; the "Say Something" montage replaces the art with mournful heartbroken-Tweek murals, and the Mayor is glimpsed at a gravestone. Cartman begs Cupid Me at the gay bar Ruffian's — visibly talking to himself — to reunite them; the price is one date. Tweek apologizes at Craig's door: Craig made him believe in himself like no one else. Craig refuses — too far, no girls ever now. Inside, Thomas tells Laura his generation never accepted it; Cupid Me arrows Thomas too, pees in his mouth, and Thomas emerges to bless Craig — with a hundred dollars. Finale in CtPaTown: Craig finds Tweek, says nothing, extends his hand; Tweek takes it. They walk hand in hand as the town swoons to a Japanese love song — everyone but the other boys — then play Assassin's Creed together, closing on a karaoke video revealing the singer as an Akihabara businessman.

Featured characters: Craig Tucker; Tweek Tweak; Thomas and Laura Tucker; Tweek's parents; Eric Cartman and Cupid Me; Wendy Testaburger; Randy Marsh; PC Principal; Mayor McDaniels.

Locations: South Park Elementary; CtPaTown; the Tweaks' coffee shop; Ruffian's gay bar; Whole Foods.

Key events & continuity: Creek (Craig × Tweek) becomes canonical — the fake relationship the fandom drew becomes real; Cupid Me returns as Cartman's cupid and price-setter; the Mayor's gravestone glance hints at her own past.

A "Code Red" pulls every officer to the elementary school; Barbrady breaches the gym to learn PC Principal called it to remove Leslie Meyers for talking to her friend — which she was not doing. A laser pointer in his eyes makes Barbrady fire into a Latino child's shoulder. The Mayor and Council fire him; policing is all he knows, he protests. McDaniels: he does not belong in a progressive town. In SoDoSoPa, the homeless occupy the decaying blocks; police will not come — terrified of being fired for beating minorities, one admits that was the only reason they joined. Their fix: make the department a Hula School. Cartman and Butters bring Stan and Kyle news: Kenny and Tolkien are gay — they have built a ninja fort and dress as ninjas. Cartman mocks it until a couple flees the ninjas in terror to Middle Eastern music; he is converted. The four join the SoDoSoPa Ninjas, swear the Warrior Code, and train; Cartman cannot tell the identical outfits apart — accusing the wrong kid, eating Butters' kick to the nuts. The ninjas scatter the homeless. Barbrady is thrown out of McDonald's for looking like a cop, cannot make rent, and joins the Shi Tpa Town homeless with his dog. Then rumor crowns the ninjas ISIS; on camera Cartman insists he never called ninja-play gay — nobody believes him — then brands Kyle a "lying, backstabbing Jew" while pointing at Stan. The town begs the police about ISIS and finds a literal Hula School, too busy to help. Out of options, the town rehires Barbrady with orders to shoot the kids — assured the minority ones are different this time: terrorists. The boys tie up Cartman and vote him out as Barbrady arrives, insisting he does not want to shoot and understands their anger. Randy tackles him; the falling gun fires into David's shoulder. The Council fires Barbrady again for drawing on innocently playing children, denying they ordered it, "Farm-To-Table"-ing him until he surrenders his sunglasses. It ends in a bare room: a mysterious man tells Barbrady the town's changes are a plot to take it down, and shows a photo — PC Principal pushing Leslie on a swing.

Featured characters: Officer Barbrady; Stan, Kyle, Cartman, Kenny, Butters, Tolkien, and Jimmy; PC Principal; Leslie Meyers; Mayor McDaniels; Randy Marsh.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the SoDoSoPa ninja fort; the police station turned Hula School; Shi Tpa Town.

Key events & continuity: Barbrady is fired twice in one episode and loses his sunglasses; the ninjas are mistaken for ISIS; the final photo — PC Principal with Leslie — tees up the ads conspiracy.

PC Principal hunts whoever runs the Super School News after it prints "retarded" about lunch policy, threatening broken legs — then learns the editor is Jimmy, who will not censor his writer. In the office, the principal softens to explain the word's harm; Jimmy asks if he is just "uncomfortable" around disabled people. Denied, the paper is banned from campus. Jimmy hand-delivers it town-wide, including PC Delta; the headline "PC Principal's 'Retarded' Policy" gets the bros branding Jimmy an "Uncle Able." The principal drags Nathan in to demonstrate the word's "effects"; Nathan hams that it makes his heart "piss its pants." Jimmy asks if anyone will ask Nathan what he means or if this is pandering discomfort; the principal stammers and loses. Alone, Nathan drops the act: the town's changes are no coincidence — a war is coming. At the 2015 debates, Hillary takes a Syria-refugee question when Garrison storms in, calls the refugees terrorists, insults her, and closes "Fuck them all to death!" Afterward, Principal Victoria intercepts Garrison and Jenner: they need to talk. The PC Delta disability-awareness party becomes a hookup scene; next morning's "'PC' Stands for 'Pussy Crushing'" headline panics the bros. A GEICO salesman offers Jimmy $26 million for ad space; refused, he draws a gun ranting that ads are unstoppable — and Barbrady shoots him dead, taking Jimmy along. The mysterious man and his ex-newsmen brief Jimmy: ads evolved past ad-blockers by disguising themselves as news, and Jimmy — who can tell news from ads on sight — is their weapon. He aces the test and is sent to Leslie Meyers. The bros' damage-control meeting splits between panic and branding opportunity. With Leslie, Jimmy learns the watchers are ex-newsmen. Garrison, Jenner, and Victoria compare notes on the anti-town plot: trust no one. The principal confides in Nathan, making him editor; a bro shows him an ad that sends him into a frenzy — as Jimmy realizes Leslie is an ad herself. The camera pulls back on the Leslie-and-PC-Principal photo: a State Farm advertisement. Garrison and Victoria slip into South Park disguised, trusting nobody; Jenner drives, running over pedestrians — "buckle up, buckaroo."

Featured characters: Jimmy Valmer; PC Principal; Nathan; Leslie Meyers; the ex-newsmen and their chief; Garrison and Caitlyn Jenner; Principal Victoria; Randy Marsh; Hillary Clinton.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the Super School News office; the PC Delta; the 2015 debates; Whole Foods.

Key events & continuity: The living-ad conspiracy breaks open — Leslie is an ad, and the PC Principal photo is a State Farm ad; Jimmy's ability to see ads makes him the season's key asset; Jenner's pedestrian flattening becomes a running gag.

Mackey summons Kyle: PC Principal has snapped, the Bros hunger-strike, Leslie and Jimmy have vanished — "you go against PC, you go missing too." Jimmy lectures the ex-newsmen on ad evolution: TV to internet to ad-blockers to human form. At the Marsh table, Randy wants the family to flee unlivable South Park; Sharon notes he loved it a month ago — Randy admits they cannot afford it; he took a second mortgage for the shiny new town. Jimmy spars with the newsmen over Leslie — he likes her — until the chief accuses him of thinking anatomically; Jimmy pitches an ad exposé and learns the GEICO man was a defected reporter. His assignment: learn the ads' plan. The boys try Nathan, who performs idiocy, then communes with the ads online for praise. Disguised, Garrison, Jenner, and Victoria infiltrate; a Whole Foods run ends with Jenner flattening another pedestrian as Garrison stares at the changed town. Jimmy's interrogation of Leslie stalls amid the chief's needling. At Skeeter's, Randy's affordability rant becomes a full "Where My Country Gone?" — then Jenner, Garrison, and Victoria jump him. Alone with Jimmy, Leslie plays her card: PC Principal is the real enemy. She floods the newsmen's monitors with ads and begs Jimmy to spring her. At a motel, Randy wakes tied to a chair: Garrison, Jenner, and Victoria show him a photo book of gentrified towns worldwide — the PC transformation is global, and PC Principal is behind it. Randy vows to kill him. Jimmy breaks Leslie out under the newsmen's noses; ordered to kill them, Barbrady refuses, joins the escape, and accidentally shoots a newsman. The four breach the PC Delta's "safe space" tape: empty. PC Principal's computer reveals he has been investigating the ads himself — maybe he is helping. Then ads flood the screen and they surface dazed in a shoe store, like the boys. Jimmy and Leslie confront Nathan; Leslie turns, beats Jimmy savagely, and tells Nathan to finish him. It ends at Kyle's door: Leslie asks his help — and his social security number. He gives it; they run off.

Featured characters: Jimmy Valmer; Leslie Meyers; Kyle Broflovski; Stan Marsh; Eric Cartman; Randy Marsh; Garrison and Caitlyn Jenner; Principal Victoria; PC Principal; Nathan.

Locations: The Marsh kitchen; Skeeter's bar; the PC Delta; the shoe store; the ex-newsmen's hideout; Kyle's doorstep.

Key events & continuity: Leslie's turn — beating Jimmy — exposes her as the season's true villain; the gentrification plot goes global in the photo book; Kyle hands his social security number to a living ad.

In Russia, PC Principal walks into a bar, is jumped, and kills every patron — one "not human" — as the camera reveals a freshly gentrified district. Kyle's bathroom war council — Butters, Stan, Kenny, Cartman — hears Leslie's intel: PC Principal murdered Jimmy and tried to kill Leslie; Randy is hunting the non-PC. Stan storms out; Kyle arms the rest — guns come easy — and guards Leslie personally. In the Marsh garage, Victoria, Garrison, and Jenner crack the principal's hard drive: he has been circling the globe's gentrified neighborhoods chasing an ads connection. At his apartment, Nathan holds Jimmy hostage — crutches confiscated — flaunting his prostitute "girlfriend" Classi and boasting that he has used the PC movement as free ad labor into wealth and power. Cartman and Liane's bedtime standoff escalates to mutual guns; Liane wins and marvels she never tried a gun before. Stan fetches Sharon to the garage discovery; minutes later the whole Marsh family is in a kitchen gunpoint standoff — which finally gets everyone talking honestly. Randy lays out all he has learned; the family agrees they should have bought guns ages ago. Leslie bats Kyle into agreeing to a comeback speech; his feelings override his retirement from oratory. At the Marsh house, the State Farm ad on the wall — Leslie and PC Principal — finally registers: Stan realizes Kyle is brainwashed by a living ad. They load Jenner's car with guns and roll. Nathan polishes his pre-written tragedy headline; when Classi objects, he slaps her — and unlike Mimsy, she beats him senseless, returns Jimmy's crutches, and drives him there in the Classimobile. The show becomes a three-way armed standoff: Marshes, Jenner, Victoria, and Garrison blame Kyle; Kyle and Leslie blame Randy and the PC crowd; then Jimmy, Classi, and Barbrady drop the truth — Leslie is behind it all, a human-seeming ad, and anyone could be one. Everyone lowers weapons, agreeing guns finally let them listen. The gentrification scheme is exposed; Leslie says the ads cannot be stopped — and PC Principal arrives to destroy her with one punch and a one-liner. PC Principal stays on: he will fight ads while staying maximally PC, and help the town do the same. Stan: "This is gonna be really hard."

Featured characters: PC Principal; Leslie Meyers; Kyle Broflovski; Jimmy Valmer; Nathan and Classi; the Marsh family; Garrison and Caitlyn Jenner; Principal Victoria; Randy Marsh.

Locations: Russia; the Marsh garage and kitchen; Nathan's apartment; Jimbo's Guns; the Whole Foods.

Key events & continuity: Leslie is punched out of the season — PC Principal's one-punch return redeems him; the Whole Foods literally flies away, ending gentrification; Mackey's confession about Victoria reframes her firing.

At a volleyball game, the anthem starts and Heidi sits in protest — then Meagan, then Nichole — until four people are left watching. PC Principal respects the protest; Heidi demands punishment for Cartman's trolling as Skankhunt42. Cartman arrives in a "Token's Life Matters" shirt. In the gym, Cartman seizes the mic, demands Wendy say something funny — "I'm not funny" — gets Bebe's mic-out-of-my-face and Nelly's "fat fuck," while Butters howls as Nelly tears into the boys over Skankhunt. Cartman's review: not funny, just angry and hateful. At home, Randy watches the Abrams coverage as a pollster asks: Giant Douche or Turd Sandwich? Both Marshes: Turd Sandwich — Hillary. Over dinner Randy rants about the surging Giant Douche, Garrison; Stan despairs of the quadrennial ritual. Hillary's presser urges calm. At Garrison/Jenner HQ, Garrison and Jenner dance to "Cake by the Ocean" over the polls — then Garrison panics: he has no plan for winning. Mackey comforts Kyle's anguish over German silence under Hitler and his own over Cartman's trolling: Abrams is rebooting the anthem, all will be well. Kyle snaps that Member Berries are not the answer and leaves. At Skeeter's, election talk with Jimbo and Stephen ends with Stephen inviting Randy to try Member Berries. Garrison's advisers workshop the logistics of fucking people to death; Christie proposes a Florida swim, Zika infection, slow mass-death. Garrison is miserable: jackass either way. Butters cackles at a fresh Skankhunt42 post; Kyle demands the boys care about the girls' feelings. Cartman sprints in screaming: the girls beat him and drew a testicled vagina on his face. Kyle: no more dividing the school. Garrison phones voters for the Turd Sandwich; news breaks that Abrams finished the anthem — Garrison will simply sit it out. Home, Randy falls under the membering Berries, then snaps out horrified at their ugly nostalgia. In his bathroom, Kyle is ambushed mid-toilet by Cartman, who insists he was right about the gender war; Kyle vows to hunt Skankhunt42 down. At the football game, both candidates attend; the anthem wrecks Garrison's stand-sit-kneel plan while Wendy, Bebe, and Nichole kill their TVs. That night Gerald checks on a despondent Kyle, retreats to his office, cues smooth jazz, and logs into the school boards as "Skankhunt42," grinning maniacally.

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski; Gerald Broflovski (Skankhunt42); Eric Cartman; Heidi Turner; Wendy Testaburger; Randy Marsh; Garrison and Caitlyn Jenner; J.J. Abrams.

Locations: The school gym and volleyball game; Garrison/Jenner HQ; Skeeter's bar; Kyle's bathroom; the football game.

Key events & continuity: Gerald is revealed as Skankhunt42 in the closing shot — the season's bomb; the Giant Douche versus Turd Sandwich election redux frames season 20; Member Berries debut as nostalgia's delivery device.

The gym hosts a parents' meeting on the troll crisis; Gerald sits quietly proud of his Skankhunt42 achievements. Walking home, he and Sheila discuss trolling's societal impact. Heidi stands on a bridge overpass above a raging river, looking ready to jump — instead she deletes Twitter and hurls her phone in. Next day brings heavy police presence; Mackey counsels students on the "loss" of their Twitter friend and urges memorial tweets. In the cafeteria, Stan says Skankhunt42 must be stopped now. Home, Gerald gives Ike a solemn talk, still glowing, then settles in for a night of Facebook hate-comments scored to Boston's "Smokin'." The girls plot revenge as the boys watch nervously; in the bathroom they decide Cartman must be "taken out" — dragged off social media via smashed electronics. They lure him to Jimbo's remote cabin with a Counter-Strike weekend; he comes happily. At a campaign HQ, a staffer reports Skankhunt42 trolling. Gerald strolls blissfully — near-misses with car and bike — buys groceries, heads home. Scott Malkinson keeps bursting into Mackey's office threatening to delete Twitter; Mackey talks him down twice, then takes a late-night call just to listen to Scott vent about happier screen-free kids. At the cabin, the trap springs in the dark: Cartman unpacks, the boys close in armed. No internet. He begs; they smash everything, he passes out, they bury it. Late, Gerald is mid-hate-session when CNN alerts: a Danish Olympian is answering his trolling. "Game on." Next day Kyle, Stan, and Clyde see the girls slamming lockers and learn Skankhunt was active last night — Cartman was never the troll; they destroyed him for nothing. The girls' punishment begins: Annie's breakup letter first, then the flood — Clyde weeping in the library, a kindergartner's "I brake up" note faceplanting its recipient into blocks, Nichole dropping Tolkien to his knees on the court, two bathroom boys clinging together. Kyle sits alone on a swing before a class photo Cartman is fading from, eaten by guilt. Hallways fill with sobbing boys and scattered notes; Stan wanders until Wendy steps up stone-faced: "This is goodbye forever, Stan. I can't fix you, Wendy." Every couple is over.

Featured characters: Gerald Broflovski (Skankhunt42); Eric Cartman; Heidi Turner; Kyle Broflovski; Stan Marsh and Wendy Testaburger; Scott Malkinson; Mr. Mackey.

Locations: The school gym; the bridge overpass; Jimbo's remote cabin; the campaign HQ; the school hallways.

Key events & continuity: The boys destroy Cartman's electronics for a crime he didn't commit — the season's cruelest mistake; every couple in school breaks up at once; Gerald's trolling escalates to a Danish Olympian.

Gerald basks in troll glory: on "Simply Heidi," Freja Ollegard discusses trolling while Gerald's rotating offensive usernames flood the comments and get read on air; he cackles in his office. The high ends at his door: police questioning about Cartman quitting Twitter. Gerald sweats; Kyle sweats harder and emergency-Skypes Clyde, Tolkien, Craig, Butters, and Jimmy about cops asking after Cartman. At the debate, Hillary the Turd Sandwich can only repeat "My opponent is a liar and can not be trusted" while Garrison the Giant Douche answers honestly: he has no idea what he is doing; vote Turd Sandwich. Both camps despair. PC Principal declares the town under attack and tasks the boys with the trolling. Heidi summons Cartman in the hall and leads him to the park's quiet gathering of social-media quitters; a passing couple films them. At his rally, Garrison begs the crowd not to vote for him — they cheer his honesty louder. Gerald smugly updates Ike on Skankhunt42 versus Freja. On a park bench, Heidi apologizes for the false accusation; they debate whether women are funny, and when Cartman says he has no friends: "You do now." Gingrich introduces the Giant Douche, who calls the crowd "pieces of shit" and says he will lose faith in humanity if elected — and Randy, watching, starts liking him. Then the news: after another Skankhunt attack, Freja Ollegard has killed herself. Gerald's triumph becomes horror; he hyperventilates in a bathroom stall. Randy tells Stephen he is voting Giant Douche now; a flustered Stephen prescribes member berry pie. The camera soars from South Park to Denmark: Freja's funeral, Lennart Bedrager's eulogy — and a vow that Denmark is coming for Skankhunt42. Cartman asks Heidi how she survives unfollowed; she used to show followers everything. "You want to go somewhere? I'll follow you." Home, Gerald finds "I know who you are" on his car and initiates "Protocol Zero": phone history wiped, phone hammer-smashed, computer deleted and destroyed, hard drive briefcased into Stark's Pond — then forced calm with Sheila. Ike's computer might hold evidence; tearing through it, Gerald finds "I know who you are" by email. He grills Ike; a new alert lands: "Meet me under the Freemont Bridge. 9am. tomorrow." 

Featured characters: Gerald Broflovski; Freja Ollegard; Eric Cartman and Heidi Turner; Kyle and Ike Broflovski; Randy Marsh; Garrison; Hillary Clinton; PC Principal.

Locations: Gerald's office; the debate stage; Skeeter's bar; the park's social-media quitters' gathering; Denmark; Stark's Pond; M Burgers.

Key events & continuity: Freja's suicide turns Gerald's trolling from sport to horror and summons Denmark's wrath; "Protocol Zero" becomes Gerald's panic routine; Cartman and Heidi's relationship deepens at M Burgers.

Narration warns of Denmark's coming anti-troll assault, cutting between hunched trolls and a paranoid Gerald turning over "I know who you are." Butters Skypes Charlotte, begging her not to cut him off; she must stand with her girlfriends, and hangs up mid-tirade. At the Freemont Bridge, Gerald meets his blackmailer: fellow troll Dildo Shwaggins. Gerald never meant to become a troll; Dick urges unity against Denmark. Kyle pitches the boys on peace with the girls via the volleyball game; Butters denounces "Uncle Kyle" and his boy-pride. At the game, the anthem plays and Butters drops trou — wiener out; Clyde, Tweek, Craig, and half the school follow as the girls stare and Kyle face-palms. Walking, Gerald ducks into a support meeting that is actually a Member Berries addiction group run by Randy and Stephen. He does not know what they are; the meeting derails when Michael is caught pocketing berries, squishes one — purple stain, total denial. The girls complain to PC Principal; he calls it a "PC Pretzel" — the boys acted peacefully: "That's what happens when you sit out the national anthem." In the halls, Butters leads a pants-down march behind "Which side are you on #WienersOut" as Wendy, Bebe, and Nichole stare in horror; Stan, swept up, joins. At 2:43 AM, Sheila wakes to Gerald shouting troll comments at his iPad from the bathroom. Cornered in the dining room, he confesses to porn — "piss porn"; that night, to smooth jazz, she does it, while Ike watches from the doorway and Kyle looks in horrified. Dick plays a BBC report: Denmark's TrollTrace.com will run any comment through its servers and expose name, IP, and location — simulation shows a SWAT team kicking in a troll's door. The CEO's Danish sign-off: "Come out, troll. Come out and die." Gerald knows he is finished; Dick says there is still hope. In the cafeteria, Kyle takes the stage: one answer only. He drops his pants; the boys roar and join as the girls walk out. Gerald is blindfolded into a room of trolls; Dick announces he is Skankhunt42 — Gerald hedges — and a troll says, "You're with your kind," as the door closes.

Featured characters: Gerald Broflovski; Dildo Shwaggins; Kyle Broflovski; Butters Stotch; Sheila and Ike Broflovski; Eric Cartman and Heidi Turner; Randy Marsh; PC Principal.

Locations: The Freemont Bridge; the volleyball game; the Member Berries support meeting; the trolls' hideout.

Key events & continuity: TrollTrace.com is unveiled — Denmark's doomsday device for trolls; Gerald is welcomed "with his kind"; the #WienersOut pants-down movement becomes the gender war's banner.

On the playground, Nelly's fists face Butters' exposed wiener; Cartman mediates, the girls scream, Heidi defuses — then she and Cartman kiss, and Annie faints. Coached to watch his tone with women, Garrison takes a Christie-introduced rally stage, opens with TSA jokes, and slides into misogyny as women stream out. In Denmark, the Danes sing for the TrollTrace launch and beg donations and buzz. The trolls convene at the Airport Hilton — an Anonymous-masked troll brusquely ordering extra coffee creamer — to plot the counterattack, Gerald lecturing on the craft. At assembly, PC Principal unveils Heidi and Cartman's Denmark fundraiser; hand in hand, whispering, the beaming couple urges all to "come together as a skewl" while jaws drop — Bebe vomits. Garrison's advisers grill him on the rally; he shrugs until supporters chase him through the streets crying the election was rigged. At home, Gerald benches Ike's computer for bandwidth, then settles in with Dildo at twin headsets; Dildo's origin — born a midget — seals their pact against Denmark's trolling crackdown. Fleeing the mob in the rain, Garrison washes up at the community center; Randy absolves him and hands him a Member Berry — this is why America wants him. The trolls' Denmark attack — on the country's Legos — trends as top news; Gerald and Dildo celebrate as Kyle watches, the world turning on the Danes. Reeling, Denmark decides to quit Twitter and abandon social media. Outside school, the fundraiser flops — one driver shouts "Fuck Denmark" — until Butters hurls the unsold danishes down; Kyle explains Denmark was itself trolled, and Butters' "working with a bunch of stupid girls" detonates a boys-versus-girls war. Heidi flees crying; Cartman comforts her: the trolling is a bigger play than anyone knows. Randy's verdict: America must admit Star Wars: The Force Awakens was not that good. His Member Berry history lesson leads Garrison to suspect J.J. Abrams is behind the whole election — eyeing Abrams in a "Make Star Wars Great Again" hat. Stunned Denmark receives an overseas VHS: Eric and Heidi, with Heidi claiming she has traced the troll attacks' source — Denmark may yet stop the trolls.

Key events & continuity: Heidi and Cartman's couple status goes public at the assembly; the trolls' Lego attack turns the world on Denmark; Heidi's emoji-pattern analysis gives Denmark hope of finding the troll.

Cartman daydreams himself floating over Mars, amusement park below — then snaps back to just eating with Heidi, confessing fear they are "losing Kyle." Gerald is mid-troll when the doorbell brings his celebrating fellow trolls; he pulls Dick into the kitchen and quits — no political trolling. In the Broflovski bathroom, Kyle is on the toilet when Cartman and Heidi barge in; Kyle scrambles to cover up while Cartman lectures on couple bathroom norms and spritzes air freshener. The news: Heidi has cracked the troll via emoji-pattern analysis. Heidi's bedroom wall maps nearly every student and adult at South Park Elementary; her analysis proves the troll is an adult — a parent. Randy abandons electrocuting the berry — unkillable — and finds the jar empty: escape. Cartman needles Kyle for under-crediting Heidi, then pales as Kyle explains TrollTrace: anyone's full internet history, public. Panic triggers a season-rewinding flashback stopping at the theater: Cartman, post-Ghostbusters with his mother, texting Butters that chicks ruined it. Present-day Cartman dreads exposure. The escaped berries cruise the highway in an RC car, membering — then open the trunk on a bloody gagged berry: "We're gonna kill you, member." At the door, Dick brings a gift and a friendship plea curdling into mutual unmasking: Gerald trolls for sadistic joy — a childhood bully, not a rebel; Dick is no activist either, just a "small giant" lashing out over no relationship. Dick cuts him off; Gerald slams the door. Denmark pinpoints Fort Collins, home of troll MLKKK, and publishes the whole city's internet history. Fort Collins implodes: chaos, crashes, fires, shattered marriages. MLKKK flees, crashes, is cornered, doused in gasoline by a man with his wheelchair-bound disabled daughter, and set ablaze. Gerald watches in horror and FaceTimes Dick, who hangs up. Cartman's Mars dream collapses in a storm; Heidi asks if he is okay, and he gets "honest" — lying that Jimmy took his phone at Ghostbusters — spiraling about his online sins as Martian winds sweep him away, hand in hand with her. Garrison addresses the nation: face it, the new Star Wars was not good. Hillary's advisers burst in: stop TrollTrace — handing her a "SkankHunt42" folder. The berries force their captive into a martini glass served to Caitlyn Jenner: "Buckle up, buckaroos."

Featured characters: Gerald Broflovski; Dildo Shwaggins; Eric Cartman and Heidi Turner; Kyle Broflovski; Randy Marsh; Garrison; Hillary Clinton; MLKKK.

Locations: Cartman's Mars daydream; the Broflovski bathroom; Denmark and Fort Collins; Heidi's bedroom wall.

Key events & continuity: TrollTrace burns Fort Collins to the ground; Heidi's emoji analysis closes in on Gerald; the Member Berries break out and take a prisoner.

At the Community Center, the town watches Garrison win the election. Randy screams the country is doomed; a man in the back shoots himself. Garrison's acceptance speech, Jenner beside him, promises to make the country great again — starting by fucking everybody to death. Cartman knocks on the Stotch door about a Ghostbusters email; Butters snaps — Cartman chose Heidi over the boys — and dismisses him. A helicopter circles the Broflovski house; the Secret Service arrives. Gerald is sure they have come for him; hiding behind Sheila — staunchly defending their mutual peeing — he surrenders to his baffled family. Beneath the Freemont Bridge, Hillary Clinton steps from the dark — Gerald mistook her for Dildo. Her offer: infiltrate Denmark and steal TrollTrace's tech. At school, PC Principal preaches post-election healing, then unveils Bill Clinton's Gentleman's Club — Clinton and Cosby crooning as students stare. A panicked Cartman bursts in on Heidi's homework: Mars, immediately — he has a plan. In Denmark, Gerald clears the airport, meets his escort, and faces Lennart Bedrager inside TrollTrace. At a restaurant, Stan talks to an emotionless Wendy while Clinton feeds him lines; Butters pounds the locked door, brands Stan a traitor, and rubs his wiener on the glass — "pressin' pickle," per Cosby. Inside TrollTrace, Lennart shows Freja's photo; Gerald chuckles silently. Lennart reads the fake aliases; Gerald laughs harder, rousing suspicion — but the server-room invitation stands. Gerald photographs everything through camera glasses — and walks into Dildo Shwaggins. The room is full of trolls: the Danes lured them all to answer for Freja's suicide. No exit. The briefcases beep, flip open — and play Rick Astley's "Never Gonna Give You Up." Confusion dawns: the Danes just rickrolled them. They have trolled the trolls. At the Stotches', Clinton asks Steven and Linda for Butters — grounded, wiener out the window. Their talk on "pickle pressing" ends with a crying Butters asking if a girl broke his heart; Clinton levels: near the end, women furious, men had better act reformed and kiss ass before TrollTrace goes public — or end up "underground and milked for their semen." It closes on Cartman and Heidi climbing hand in hand toward the gleaming SpaceX building: the Mars journey lives on.

Featured characters: Gerald Broflovski; Hillary Clinton; Lennart Bedrager; Dildo Shwaggins; Garrison; Randy Marsh; Eric Cartman and Heidi Turner; Bill Clinton; Butters Stotch.

Locations: The Community Center; beneath the Freemont Bridge; Denmark's TrollTrace facility; the Stotch home; SpaceX.

Key events & continuity: Garrison wins the presidency; Denmark rickrolls the world's trolls — the ultimate reversal; Cartman and Heidi's Mars escape plan becomes the season's closing image.

Garrison gets a new President-elect-mirroring hairstyle at Tom's Rhinoplasty, then declares himself ready after the UV machine. At SpaceX, Cartman and Heidi ask the desk for Mars — citing its shitty WiFi — take a number, and join the escapee crowd where Cher performs "Believe." At school, a seething PC Principal hurls papers over the election until Mackey brings news: the President-elect wants him. Garrison sweeps in with Secret Service and rubs the win in his face with crude needling. In Denmark, Lennart tosses the trapped Gerald an iPhone: call anyone, but explain why you are there. The plan: use the trolls to set the world ablaze. At SpaceX, Butters arrives wanting off the planet — "Shit's about to get a lot worse" — and Cartman turns jealous as Butters raves about Amy Schumer's humor. At the White House, berries descend as far as the eye can see, membering into the Oval Office. Ike photoshops a penis into a woman's mouth on Gerald's orders, chanting "You are a fat retard," when Sheila walks in horrified. Ike protests he only obeys Gerald — who has dropped the call, framing Ike as Skankhunt42. Sheila is disgusted; Gerald phones back all bluster — full of shit, not sorry, stay quiet — she agrees and benches Ike from the computer. The instant she leaves, Gerald is back: type "How you like a donkey dick." The SpaceX tour rolls under Elon Musk — gadgets, a pizza pocket — as Cartman demands the Mars rocket; Musk says eight years out. Butters suggests smart, funny Heidi could speed it up; Musk: "How funny?" At the White House, berries perform, then a squad pulls up in a tiny car, marches into the Oval Office demanding to know who is in charge; one draws a gun, shoots another, and declares "Member Stormtroopers." Boris Johnson phones Garrison: do not eat the memberberries — London is burning; "Don't let them get into your head" is taken as insult, and Garrison hangs up. Home, Kyle finds Ike cowering as Sheila rages that Ike is Skankhunt42. Kyle starts in — stops — thinks — and gets it: Gerald, his father, all along. He grabs Ike and they run as Sheila screams "What, what, what?!!"

Featured characters: Gerald Broflovski; Kyle and Ike Broflovski; Sheila Broflovski; Eric Cartman, Heidi Turner, and Butters Stotch; Garrison; Elon Musk; the Member Berries.

Locations: Tom's Rhinoplasty; SpaceX; the White House; the Pentagon; Denmark's TrollTrace facility; the Broflovski home.

Key events & continuity: Kyle finally realizes his own father is Skankhunt42; the Member Berries infiltrate the White House; Gerald frames Ike, and Sheila's rage sends the boys running.

TrollTrace is about to go live in Denmark, and South Park is bracing for everyone's internet history to be dragged into the light. At the Park County Police Station, Sergeant Harrison Yates tries to calm a panicked crowd by appealing to the common decency of the American people, which only sends them into a worse frenzy. Kyle Broflovski is stuck in timeout at home for running off with Ike, while Sheila rages at both boys over Ike's secret life as an internet troll. Their father Gerald calls on video chat and admits he trolls simply because he finds it funny, urging the boys to do something about the situation in Denmark. At SpaceX headquarters, a furious crowd demands passage to Mars while Heidi Turner puzzles over equations on a whiteboard, with Cartman hovering possessively and growing jealous every time Butters praises her. Meanwhile the captured trolls, Gerald among them, are herded naked into a viewing room at the TrollTrace facility, where Gerald finally confesses he is Skankhunt42. At the Pentagon, President-elect Garrison is goaded by his ex Mr. Slave into ordering a bombing of Denmark, then talks himself out of it after a furious phone argument with Kyle. Lennart Bedrager drops the act: he is not Danish at all, and built TrollTrace to turn the whole world against itself because he finds it hilarious. As the facility's screens fill with a looping Rick Astley video, Kyle and Ike lure Sheila into the pantry and lock her inside so they can get to the computer and save the family.

Featured characters: Gerald, Kyle, Ike and Sheila Broflovski; Cartman, Heidi Turner and Butters; Lennart Bedrager; President-elect Garrison and Mr. Slave; Harrison Yates; Dildo Shwaggins.

Locations: the TrollTrace building in Denmark; SpaceX headquarters; the Broflovski home; the Pentagon; South Park Church; Park County Police Station.

Key events & continuity: Lennart's true motive is exposed; Garrison nearly bombs Denmark; Kyle and Ike imprison Sheila in the pantry, setting up the finale; the Mars escape plan and Cartman's jealousy over Heidi and Butters intensify.

entries.n: S20E10 — The End of Serialization as We Know It
entries.t:
Kyle launches an all-out trolling blitz from his bedroom to overload TrollTrace's servers, recruiting Stan, Tolkien, Tweek, Craig, Jimmy, Kenny, Ike and even Dildo Shwaggins, while Sheila smashes her way out of the pantry in a fury. At the TrollTrace building in Denmark, Gerald cons a worker into giving up the conference room code, disguises himself, and starts killing the server breakers one by one. Lennart Bedrager confronts him on a shaking catwalk, and Gerald kicks him off the bridge before flipping the final switch. At SpaceX, Cartman finally sees through Heidi: her emoji analysis cracked the code for reaching Mars, and she has been steering him all along. He fakes a NASA bomb threat to evacuate the building, then has Kyle reroute the entire internet through SpaceX just as Gerald's sabotage peaks. The building detonates, every screen on Earth goes dark, and a single message appears: the internet has been reset and the global cache cleared. TrollTrace dies with it. Gerald comes home to a furious family; Cartman and Heidi reunite with a kiss; President-elect Garrison settles into the Oval Office surrounded by memberberries; and the first message sent on the rebuilt internet is an old man mailing a friend a photo of his own genitals.

Featured characters: Kyle, Gerald, Ike and Sheila Broflovski; Cartman, Heidi Turner and Butters; Lennart Bedrager; Dildo Shwaggins; President-elect Garrison; Elon Musk.

Locations: the TrollTrace facility; SpaceX headquarters; the Broflovski home; the Pentagon and the Oval Office; a computer cafe; South Park streets.

Key events & continuity: the season-long TrollTrace arc ends with the internet wiped; Lennart is defeated; Garrison's presidency begins with the memberberries at his side; Cartman and Heidi stay together despite his discovery.
k: the end of serialization as we know it

entries.t:
Randy and Sharon Marsh launch their own home-renovation show, built around knocking down kitchen walls for an open concept, but their filming keeps getting crashed by Darryl Weathers and his crew of torch-and-flag-waving protesters, who are furious that smart speakers are stealing working-class jobs. After a pepper-spray standoff outside Best Buy and a showdown at the Park County Courthouse, Randy decides the fix is to give the protesters work himself: he hires Darryl as a living, breathing stand-in for a voice assistant, barking shopping-list orders at him, then demolishes Darryl's load-bearing kitchen wall and remodels the whole house to prove starting over is possible. Meanwhile Cartman is falling apart over Heidi, who calls him passive-aggressive and walks out. He self-soothes by sweet-talking his Amazon Alexa until Liane replaces it with Jim Bob, a folksy human musician who answers questions with a guitar, which horrifies him. Drowning in a pile of smart speakers, Cartman finally marches into South Park Elementary and dumps Heidi on the spot, declaring he could not fix her and walking out to rock music while the other boys cheer him on.

Featured characters: Randy and Sharon Marsh; Darryl Weathers and his protesters; Cartman, Heidi Turner and Liane; Jim Bob.

Locations: Best Buy; Crunchy's Micro Brew; the Cartman and Marsh residences; Darryl's house; the Park County Courthouse; South Park Elementary.

Key events & continuity: Randy's renovation show becomes a recurring bit; Darryl Weathers is introduced as the aggrieved worker; Cartman and Heidi break up, though it will not stick.

Tweek Tweak is spiraling: the president's taunting tweets at North Korea have somehow made Tweek personally responsible for nuclear war in the town's eyes. Craig tries to steady him with cupcakes for Kim Jong-un and a fidget spinner, but every new presidential tweet sends Tweek back into screaming panic, even as a North Korean missile sails over his house. Parallel to the meltdown, Cartman hijacks the school's distracted-driving awareness week by staging an elaborate fake suicide campaign, complete with a hoodie, a mournful song and flyers, all to guilt Heidi into staying with him after she threatened to leave. Real deaths pile up offscreen as distracted drivers mow down townspeople, including Gary Borkovec, while Cartman keeps redirecting every tragedy back to himself. At the breaking point, Tweek admits in his bedroom that he feels like a pawn with no control over his life, and Craig helps him decide to take the pledge instead. The episode closes with a school assembly where Tweek and Craig lead the whole town in a song about putting the phones down, while Cartman barges in rapping about killing himself and then announces he will not do it after all.

Featured characters: Tweek Tweak and Craig Tucker; Cartman and Heidi Turner; President Garrison; Kim Jong-un; Richard Tweak.

Locations: South Park Elementary theater and cafeteria; the Tweek residence; an amusement park in Denver; Pyongyang.

Key events & continuity: Tweek and Craig's relationship survives the strain; Cartman's manipulative suicide threats become his go-to control tactic with Heidi; distracted driving deaths, Gary Borkovec among them, are treated as background noise.

When South Park Elementary cancels Columbus Day, the boys are furious about losing a day off, and Randy Marsh turns the holiday into his personal crusade: he rallies the town to tear down the Columbus statue, then gets caught on camera defacing it himself. Things get worse when Stan and Kyle confront him with photos of Randy dressed up as Columbus at his own wedding. Desperate to prove he has indigenous heritage, Randy orders a DNAandMe kit and secretly kisses a Native American man he hired, hoping to contaminate the mouth swab. The boys, meanwhile, resort to blackmail, getting Kenny to disguise his voice and threaten school administrator Peter Galtman over the phone, then kidnapping him and forcing him to watch a VHS of Randy assaulting the Native American man. The DNA results come back with no Native American ancestry at all, just a splash of Neanderthal, which sends Randy into a file-cabinet-kicking rage. Defeated, he punches Galtman in the face, then gives a town speech reinstating the holiday under a new name, Indigenous Peoples Day, which immediately devolves into townspeople insulting each other.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon and Stan Marsh; Kyle, Cartman and Kenny; Peter Galtman; the Native American man; the DNAandMe technician.

Locations: the Marsh residence; South Park Elementary; the Galtman residence; DNAandMe headquarters; the Columbus statue.

Key events & continuity: Randy's 2.8 percent Neanderthal result becomes a running joke; the holiday is renamed Indigenous Peoples Day; another entry in Randy's long history of schemes blowing up in his face.

The Coon and Friends are back together and holding auditions for a new teammate after Iron Maiden retires and Mintberry Crunch vanishes; Jimmy Valmer tries out and joins as Fastpass. The team is plotting a superhero franchise anchored by a Netflix series, but someone is sabotaging them: Butters, as his villain alter ego Professor Chaos, has built an entire operation spreading fake news about them on Facebook. When Netflix refuses to greenlight the show until the stories are addressed, the town's adults summon Mark Zuckerberg himself to South Park. Zuckerberg stonewalls every question, dodges every attempt to block him, and starts invading people's homes, cars and meals while the police insist he is not breaking any law. The boys discover Butters has paid Zuckerberg for protection, so Cartman stages a public beating, accusing Zuckerberg of trying to stop kids from fighting for justice, while Super Craig secretly livestreams the whole thing on Facebook. Panicking, Zuckerberg shuts the site down entirely, killing Butters' scheme. Stephen Stotch drags Butters off to Moscow to punish both him and Vladimir Putin for the idea, and the boys are free to pursue their franchise, until they immediately split apart arguing over franchise plans.

Featured characters: Cartman as the Coon and the Coon and Friends; Butters as Professor Chaos; Jimmy as Fastpass; Mark Zuckerberg; Stephen Stotch; the Netflix executive.

Locations: the Coon and Friends base; South Park homes; a town meeting hall.

Key events & continuity: the superhero franchise arc continues; Professor Chaos weaponizes fake news; the team fractures over creative differences at the end.

A costumed children's entertainer drops dead at Marcus Preston's birthday party, and Marcus swears revenge on whoever is killing party mascots. The trail leads to Shady Acres retirement home, where Marvin Marsh has Stan running a grim errand: delivering crocheted pillows to Ms. McGullicutty, the tyrannical resident who rules the home like a prison yard and collects porcelain hummel figurines as tribute. Stan has been trading the pillows to a guy in a Swiper costume for hummels without knowing the pillows are stuffed with opioids. When Marcus discovers hummels hidden inside the bodies of the dead entertainers, the boys realize Stan is an unwitting drug mule and start avoiding him. With Marcus closing in, Stan begs him for help instead of turning him in, and Marcus tearfully agrees. The boys stage a choir-boy distraction at Shady Acres while Stan raids McGullicutty's room for her entire hummel hoard. Armed with the figurines, Marvin beats McGullicutty and her enforcers into submission and seizes control as the home's new top resident, while McGullicutty gets thrown in the quiet room. Marcus turns his interrogation skills on the town's health professionals instead.

The episode leans into the retirement home as a prison: the residents trade contraband, fear the quiet room, and Ms. McGullicutty inspects every tribute like a warden. Stan's guilt over betraying his friends nearly breaks him, but Marcus, who started out wanting vengeance for a dead mascot, ends up the unlikely hero of the old folks' home.

Featured characters: Stan and Marvin Marsh; Marcus Preston; Ms. McGullicutty; Kyle, Cartman and Kenny; Randy and Sharon Marsh.

Locations: Shady Acres; Marcus's birthday party; South Park Elementary; the Park County Coroner's office.

Key events & continuity: Marvin seizes power at Shady Acres; the opioid pipeline hidden in the pillows is exposed; Marcus Preston's crusade ends with the retirement home, not the streets.

Every Halloween the dads of South Park sneak off to the mountains for Witch Week, dressing as witches and getting drunk, while Randy lies to Sharon to get out of pumpkin-patch duty with Stan. This year the outsider Chip Duncan brings an ancient spell book and reads a real hex, transforming into an actual cackling witch who takes off on a broomstick, torments the pumpkin patch carnival and starts abducting children, stuffing them into a magical bag of holding. Cartman, meanwhile, is stewing over Heidi's chronic lateness, and when he overhears the boys plotting to get rid of the witch, he assumes they mean Heidi. He dresses her as Gretel to his Hansel, lures her into the woods at night and abandons her to be snatched by Chip. The dads, embarrassed that Chip is ruining the reputation of good-boy witches, try to sacrifice the guilt-ridden Stephen Stotch to the devil before Chip interrupts. Butters phones President Garrison, who reveals he used to attend Witch Week himself, flies in, and has a military satellite vaporize Chip with a laser. The kids are freed from the bag, though Heidi needs extra time to finish getting ready for her own rescue, which infuriates Cartman all over again.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon and Stan Marsh; Stephen and Butters Stotch; Chip Duncan; Cartman and Heidi Turner; Kyle and Kenny; President Garrison.

Locations: the mountaintop party site; the pumpkin patch carnival; the woods; Ross Dress for Less; Park County Police Station.

Key events & continuity: Garrison's Witch Week history is revealed; Chip Duncan is killed; Cartman's attempt to ditch Heidi fails; the dads' Halloween tradition survives another year.

Kyle cannot understand why Heidi will not dump Cartman, and decides to intervene directly. Cartman, meanwhile, is working every angle: sobbing on the phone, blaming his blood sugar, pretending to go vegan while secretly eating regular KFC, and insisting Heidi is making him suicidal. When Heidi briefly leaves him, Cartman crashes with Tolkien Black's family, and Kyle and Heidi start spending time together, even holding hands on the swings. Convinced he has won, Kyle confronts Cartman at school and drops him with a single punch. But Cartman gets the last word: he lures Heidi back, and at the Broflovski doorstep Heidi tells Kyle she was being manipulated, then calls him a dirty Jew to his face and walks off with Cartman, who shoots Kyle a triumphant evil grin. In a parallel plot, President Garrison's White House descends into sordid chaos as his approval antics escalate, with Paul Ryan spinning increasingly absurd scandals. Heidi's arc completes its dark turn: the once-sweet girl now fully mirrors Cartman's cruelty, and the girls at school can only watch her sink back in.

Kyle's attempt to play the good guy keeps backfiring: Heidi accuses him of meddling, the girls mock him, and his hallway confrontation with Cartman only feeds Cartman's victim act. The White House subplot spirals in parallel, with Garrison's approval stunt and Paul Ryan's humiliating spin underscoring how chaos rewards the shameless.

Featured characters: Cartman, Heidi Turner and Kyle Broflovski; Tolkien Black and his parents; Wendy and the schoolgirls; President Garrison and Paul Ryan.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the White House; the Black residence; the Broflovski residence; Buca De Faggoncini.

Key events & continuity: Heidi chooses Cartman over Kyle, sealing her transformation into his female counterpart; Kyle and Cartman's rivalry turns physical; the breakup that seemed final in the premiere is undone.

Jimmy and Timmy enter the special-ed science fair with a project on water bears, microscopic tardigrades they learned about from a children's show, which they have trained to react to sound waves, especially Taylor Swift songs. Nathan, desperate to win the fair to impress girls, breaks in overnight with Mimsy and tries to electrocute the water bears with a hair curler. Instead of dying, the water bears evolve overnight and learn the Hokey Pokey, drawing the attention of supposed government agents who turn out to be the NFL, bleeding viewers and desperate to turn the water bears into replacement fans. Heidi, now fully Cartman-like in attitude and appetite, has been roped into judging the fair and spends the episode snapping at everyone, including her old friends. When the NFL men take the classroom hostage at gunpoint to seize the bears, Heidi grabs the bowl, delivers a bitter speech about how everyone mistreats her, and drinks the water bears alive. The NFL salvages hope from Nathan and Mimsy's forgotten volcano project, while Heidi ends the day farting on a horrified Cartman on his own couch.

Featured characters: Jimmy Valmer and Timmy Burch; Nathan and Mimsy; Heidi Turner and Cartman; the NFL representatives; PC Principal, Strong Woman and Mr. Mackey; Wendy and the girls.

Locations: the special-ed classroom; South Park Elementary hallways and auditorium; Cartman's house.

Key events & continuity: Heidi's transformation into a Cartman clone is complete, down to the cruelty and the farts; the water bears are destroyed; Nathan's sabotage backfires into a win for everyone but him.

PC Principal's world tilts when the school hires a new vice principal, the formidable Strong Woman, and he promptly falls head over heels, hearing a love ballad every time she enters the room. A disastrous HR seminar pairs him with Heather Conduct while Mr. Mackey falls for her instead. Meanwhile Kyle has a genuine crisis of conscience: watching an aged Terrance and Phillip fart on guests on their Netflix show, he is the only boy who no longer laughs, and he starts a Millennials Against Canada movement to get the show shut down. His crusade escalates absurdly: after a televised debate with Canada's Minister of Streaming, Kyle phones the president, and Garrison, delighted, opens the nuclear football and nukes Canada, killing over a million Canadians. Kyle watches the blast on TV in horror as Ike storms in, cursing him out for what he has done to their parents' homeland. PC Principal and Strong Woman finally admit their feelings while guiding kids to the gym, hands touching over a classroom door, as the love song swells again.

The Terrance and Phillip Show has visibly aged: the duo are old men now, Phillip needs a stepladder to deliver his signature gag, and only Kyle notices the cruelty in it. PC Principal's HR nightmare ends with Mackey falling for the HR rep instead, and the new vice principal's arrival quietly reshapes the school's power structure.

Featured characters: PC Principal and Strong Woman; Kyle Broflovski; Terrance and Phillip; President Garrison; the Canadian Minister of Streaming; Mr. Mackey and Heather Conduct; Ike.

Locations: South Park Elementary; Netflix headquarters; the White House; Canada.

Key events & continuity: PC Principal and Strong Woman fall in love, setting up their family; Garrison nukes Canada, a catastrophe that drives the season finale; Kyle's guilt over the bombing haunts him.

With Canada demanding President Garrison's head after the nuclear strike, Garrison has gone feral, lurking around South Park like a horror-movie monster, popping out of red campaign balloons and devouring rats in the woods. The town holds a panicked meeting where Officer Bright warns everyone not to approach, joke about shooting, or even reason with him. Kyle is drowning in guilt and sets out into the woods to find Ike, who has run off to join the Canadian side, eventually spotted riding a Newfoundland dog in a Mountie uniform. The search party stumbles on PC Principal and Strong Woman's secret tent rendezvous, which makes half the town vomit. Ike finally traps the wild president in one of his own snares, and just as the town celebrates, Bob White seizes a gun to defend Garrison. Heidi grabs the weapon herself, turns it on Cartman, and in a moment of clarity renounces her victimhood, dumping Cartman for good and walking away immune to his suicide threats. The president breaks free anyway, and Stan concludes only the Whites can stop him.

Featured characters: President Garrison; Kyle and Ike Broflovski; Heidi Turner and Cartman; Bob White and his family; Justin Trudeau; PC Principal and Strong Woman; Stan and Tolkien.

Locations: the South Park woods; the Park County Community Center; the White residence; Buca De Faggoncini; the mayor's office.

Key events & continuity: Heidi definitively breaks up with Cartman and rejects the victim lifestyle; Ike sides with Canada; Garrison remains at large; the PC Principal and Strong Woman affair goes public.

Another school shooting interrupts class at South Park Elementary, and nobody blinks: the kids keep answering math questions while SWAT storms the room. The only person rattled is Sharon Marsh, who drags Stan home and is horrified that Randy could not care less. Randy decides Sharon's distress must be hormonal and spends the episode dodging the issue with charades, a therapist ambush and a serenade of a love ballad on the school stairs, while Sharon spirals. Meanwhile Cartman is convinced Tolkien deliberately changed his test answers after Cartman copied them, and builds an entire conspiracy around whether Tolkien has secretly seen Black Panther, staking out his house and interrogating his parents, only to learn Tolkien is not allowed to see PG-13 movies alone. In the end Sharon learns the town thinks she is menopausal, snaps that she just had her period that morning, and gives up trying to make anyone care, just in time for a call that Stan has been shot, which she shrugs off to Randy's delight.

Cartman's bathroom confrontation with Tolkien goes nowhere, since Tolkien genuinely does not care about the movie, which Cartman reads as a deeper cover-up. Sharon's final surrender is total: when told Stan was actually shot this time, she just shrugs, and Randy beams, finally free of her worrying.

Featured characters: Sharon and Randy Marsh; Stan Marsh; Cartman and Tolkien Black; Steve and Linda Black; Mr. Mackey; PC Principal; Mrs. Nelson; Butters.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the Marsh residence; a therapist's office; the Black residence.

Key events & continuity: school shootings are established as background noise; Stan gets shot, leaving him in a cast next episode; Sharon surrenders to apathy.

entries.n: S22E02 — A Boy And A Priest
entries.t:
Father Maxi is getting heckled through every sermon with Catholic priest jokes, and the town has turned mocking him into a Sunday ritual. The only person who reaches out is Butters, who knows what being bullied feels like and befriends the lonely priest, dragging him to game night, campfires and Clyde's roller-rink birthday party. When Maxi vanishes and locks the church doors, the town spirals, and the Archdiocese of Denver dispatches a Catholic Cleanup Crew that scrubs crime scenes, snatches Butters, Stan and Clyde into a van, and tries to ship Maxi off to South America. Maxi confesses to Butters that he hates himself for failing to stop the church's abuse of children, but when the crew corners them at a campsite with a machine called the Kumboni, Maxi seizes it, runs all three cleaners over, and declares his purpose is to protect boys. He reopens the church and preaches on penance, and this time he simply accepts the jokes raining down on him.

The montage of Butters and Maxi's friendship, rowing, movies, marshmallows, plays out while the town watches in confusion, convinced something sinister is happening. The Crew's van, the bleach, the Kumby wipes and the bunny lure all fail, and Maxi's final sermon lands with the congregation laughing through it, which he now takes as affection.

Featured characters: Butters Stotch; Father Maxi; the Catholic Cleanup Crew; Stan, Kyle, Cartman and Clyde; Randy Marsh; the Archbishop of Denver.

Locations: South Park Church; the Marsh residence; Kidzone Roller Rink; a forest campsite; Skeeter's Wine Bar.

Key events & continuity: Maxi's arc resolves with him embracing his role; the Cleanup Crew is destroyed; Butters' friendship with Maxi endures.

entries.n: S22E03 — The Problem with a Poo
entries.t:
Mr. Hankey, director of the town Christmas pageant, is on the chopping block after a string of offensive tweets, which he keeps blaming on Ambien. The city council fires him, every lawyer in town turns him down, and only Kyle agrees to defend him, out of loyalty and his father's lawyer blood. The hearing goes badly when Hankey explodes at the judge, and a disastrous live Christmas show in the park ends with Hankey brawling with Kyle in front of everyone. Meanwhile PC Principal and Strong Woman are hiding a much bigger secret: she is pregnant, and after a hastily staged assembly about in vitro fertilization, her water breaks in front of the whole school. She gives birth to PC quintuplets, and the two of them spend the episode denying PC Principal is the father while the ultra-PC babies scream at everything. In the end the town watches Hankey climb into a rideshare and leave South Park for a place that tolerates bigotry, which turns out to be Springfield, where he is welcomed as a hero.

Kyle's loyalty costs him everything: Craig's gang glares at him in the hallway, the town shuns him, and even Hankey's apology tour collapses into another Ambien excuse. The PC babies, meanwhile, scream at a doctor's Speedy Gonzales shirt and turn a simple bedtime into a covert operation, with both parents insisting the father does not exist.

Featured characters: Mr. Hankey; Kyle Broflovski; PC Principal and Strong Woman; the PC babies; Mayor McDaniels and the city council; Gerald Broflovski.

Locations: City Hall; South Park Elementary; Hell's Pass Hospital; Denny's; Main Street; Springfield.

Key events & continuity: Mr. Hankey is exiled from South Park; the PC babies are born and their parentage becomes an open secret; the Springfield crossover lands with a cancel-hashtag.

Fed up with South Park, Randy moves the whole family out to the country to grow marijuana, rebranding himself as a farmer with integrity, tegridy. Stan is miserable about the hour-long commute, and Shelly keeps vaping. At school, Cartman and Butters are secretly running a vape-dealing operation to pay off a debt, with Cartman publicly punching Butters to protect their cover, and Kyle gets dragged in when he tries to expose them. Kyle ends up paying off their dealer with his birthday money and helping frame the man, while the 6th graders start circling. Randy, who despises vaping as pussy sticks, declares war on Big Vape Colorado after catching Stan with a vape pen, storms the shop on his tractor, and blows the whole building up with Towelie, who has shown up as the world's least reliable agricultural inspector.
