The episode closes with Randy, Stan and a very high Towelie farming together as Randy insists the fight is just beginning, over a Tegridy Weed ad.

Shelly's vaping keeps landing her in Mackey's office, and her butthole-photo prank on the recess monitor becomes playground legend. Kyle's attempt to go to the principal gets stonewalled by Cartman and Butters, who are already there spinning their exit plan, and the dealer's shame at taking a kid's birthday money is the episode's most honest moment.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Towelie; Cartman, Butters and Kyle; the Big Vape dealer.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; South Park Elementary; Big Vape Colorado; the Mackey residence.

Key events & continuity: the Marshes relocate to Tegridy Farms, their home for seasons to come; Towelie joins the farm; Randy's war on vaping begins.

Mysterious e-scooters appear all over South Park with no explanation, and the kids immediately realize they can use them to hit more houses than ever on Halloween. Everyone piles on except Kenny, who has no phone and gets rejected by every group, from the boys to Clyde's crew to the girls. Mr. Mackey, who hates the scooters on principle, starts stealing them at night and hurling them off a cliff, only to wake up with more scooters in his bedroom. The town panics at a community meeting when Harrison Yates warns each house will need thousands of dollars in candy. On Halloween night the kids flood the streets, overwhelming every adult in town, until Kenny, in a counseling session, realizes he cannot ride without a phone and the two of them figure out the scooters die without the cell tower. Kenny climbs the tower and Mackey yanks it down with his car, freezing every scooter in town. Kenny, revealed as the episode's narrator, finally trick-or-treats normally with his friends, calling it the last good Halloween before an e-scooter wakes up and rides off on its own.

The town's candy panic is total: Lolly's is stripped bare, Food 4 Little is empty, and New York reportedly runs out of candy. Stephen Stotch trick-or-treats in a Megyn Kelly costume, Jimbo and Ned are overrun at their door, and Kenny's narration frames the whole night as the last good Halloween before the machines woke up.

Featured characters: Kenny McCormick; Mr. Mackey; Stan, Kyle and Cartman; Clyde, Jimmy, Tolkien and Butters; Harrison Yates; Stephen and Linda Stotch; Jimbo and Ned.

Locations: South Park streets; Lolly's Candy Factory; the Park County Community Center; a cell phone tower; Tegridy Farms.

Key events & continuity: Kenny narrates; the e-scooter invasion is stopped; Mackey and Kenny bond.

Something is mauling people around South Park, starting with Ned, who is snatched by a roaring beast on Tegridy Farms while Jimbo and Randy watch. Sergeant Yates insists every corpse is a school shooting, even hauling in Cartman and Kenny as the two biggest loners, and keeps ducking out to play video games. Stan and Kyle identify the killer as ManBearPig, the creature Al Gore warned them about years ago, and track Gore down to a bowling alley where he is now a champion. After a humiliating apology tour, including an Olive Garden party, Gore agrees to help and reveals ManBearPig is a demon. A midnight ritual summons Satan himself, who sends them to the public library, where they learn the beast came through a deal someone in town made. The cops arrest the boys before they can warn anyone, and at Shady Acres, Marvin Marsh watches the news in horror, realizing he is the one who made the deal.

Yates's video game obsession keeps derailing the investigation, and his fury at finding his wife played his save file is played as genuine marital crisis. Gore's demands for apologies stack up: one for the mockery, one for the insincere apology, one for Stan snapping mid-ritual, each more petty than the last.

Featured characters: Stan, Kyle, Cartman and Kenny; Al Gore; ManBearPig; Satan; Sergeant Yates; Jimbo and Ned; Randy Marsh; Marvin Marsh.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; Stark's Pond; Gramercy Lanes; Olive Garden; the woods; South Park Public Library; Shady Acres.

Key events & continuity: ManBearPig returns as a real threat; Al Gore is vindicated; Marvin's deal is revealed; first half of a two-parter.

The boys break out of jail and go on the run while ManBearPig tears through town and Sergeant Yates finally admits he has been a fool, letting them go to save everyone. Stan learns from Marvin that the old folks traded with ManBearPig for cars and ice cream, and gets power of attorney to repeal the deal at the courthouse, only to discover the demon does not want cars at all: it wants the town to give up its video games and soy sauce. When the town refuses, Stan negotiates a new deal letting ManBearPig return in five years for an even bigger carnage. Meanwhile Satan agrees to fight ManBearPig as a favor to mankind, and is brutally beaten and impaled on his own horn, dying in the boys' arms and ascending to Heaven after urging them to keep trying. Al Gore, appearing as a literal ghost mentor, keeps needling Kyle about the past. The town is saved for now, at the price of a promise that the horror will return.

Kyle's prayer is answered by a literal ghost trick as Gore haunts him for mockery received decades ago. The symposium on when to worry keeps getting interrupted by Satan bursting in to announce the end times, and nobody can decide whether that qualifies. Yates's marriage, his save file, and his stubbornness all collapse at once when he finally stands down.

Featured characters: Stan, Kyle and Cartman; Satan; ManBearPig; Marvin Marsh; Sergeant Yates; Al Gore.

Locations: Park County Police Station; Tegridy Farms; Shady Acres; the Park County Community Center; the courthouse; Main Street.

Key events & continuity: Satan dies and goes to Heaven; the deal is remade with a five-year return clause; Yates redeems himself; conclusion of the two-parter.

Cartman gets a therapist to diagnose him with anxiety because people keep distracting him from his phone, and discovers the Buddha Box, a cardboard box worn over the head that lets him stare at his phone undisturbed. He evangelizes it to Craig, PC Principal and half the town, using it to dodge football practice, school and a water park. Meanwhile PC Principal and Strong Woman's PC babies escape while their parents are boxed up, and go on a politically-correct rampage, protesting a bar's drink names and landing a record deal with their crying. When the babies' song leads the frazzled parents to them, they realize the boxes let them be a normal family for once, and PC Principal calls a PTA meeting to ban phones and Buddha Boxes from school, only to find every parent is wearing a box and ignoring him. He and Strong Woman ditch the boxes and take the babies on a quiet picnic instead.

Tweek is heartbroken watching Craig disappear into his box, and Liane's pleas about Cartman's potential go nowhere. The therapist's anxiety group becomes a support circle of people ignoring each other through cardboard, and the mayor hands out Buddha Boxes city-wide after Cartman's pitch about what Namaste really means.

Featured characters: Cartman; PC Principal and Strong Woman; the PC babies; Craig and Tweek; Kyle; Mr. Mackey; Liane Cartman; the therapist.

Locations: South Park Elementary; Pi Pi's Splashtown; City Hall; the Park County Police Station; Crunchy's Micro Brew.

Key events & continuity: the PC babies' first protest; PC Principal moves to ban phones at school; Cartman's anxiety diagnosis is transparently fake.

South Park is chosen for Amazon's newest Fulfillment Center, and Stephen Stotch takes a grueling warehouse job to make ends meet, while Butters obsesses over the town bike parade and its big cash prize. When a worker named Josh Carter gets mangled by a machine and ends up sealed in a box that cannot be opened without killing him, the workers go on strike, and with deliveries halted the whole town unravels. The boys, desperate for bike parade parts, discover the abandoned South Park Mall, whose feral former employees agree to work the warehouse. Jeff Bezos, who has been spying through everyone's Alexa, buses in the mall workers as scabs, and Stephen crosses the picket line alone, torn between the strike and his family. The episode ends on a cliffhanger with the strikers blockading the center and Bezos fixated on eliminating Josh as his only real enemy.

Stephen's prayer that the strike ends so he can provide for his family is overheard by Bezos through Alexa, which is how the bus of scabs gets arranged. The mall workers, feral from years without customers, turn out to be eager and competent, and Josh, still sealed in his box, delivers a stirring speech about working people that makes him Bezos's prime target.

Featured characters: Stephen and Butters Stotch; Stuart McCormick; Josh Carter; Jeff Bezos; the boys; Mayor McDaniels; Larry Zewiski.

Locations: the Amazon Fulfillment Center; the South Park Mall; Crunchy's Micro Brew; Kenny's house.

Key events & continuity: Amazon comes to South Park; Bezos surveils the town via Alexa; the strike sets up the finale; first half of a two-parter.

The bike parade is on, but Kenny quits over his father's pro-strike beliefs, and Cartman panics until he schemes to get the parade cancelled for offensiveness instead. Bezos lures a group of children into opening Josh Carter's box, killing him, and removing the strike's figurehead. Stephen, wracked with guilt, keeps working while Butters begs him to stop. Santa Claus himself shows up to save Christmas, asks where Mr. Hankey is, and storms out in disgust when he learns the town exiled him over tweets. At City Hall, Bezos reveals the whole parade was his plot to manufacture desperate workers, and orders Alexa to kill Kenny, but the townspeople, now happily high on Tegridy weed, confront him and declare they do not need Amazon anymore. The parade rolls on with Cartman dragging Kenny's coffin behind his bike, while the stoned adults, including a Garrison in police custody and a Ned who survived ManBearPig, watch from the sidelines.

Larry Zewiski's showing off backfires when Butters rolls up with a better bike and steals his audience of Raisins girls, and Larry's furious lecture guilts his striking father back to work. Randy's scheme to deliver weed by e-scooter so customers never see rival farms is pure Tegridy logic, and the mayor's confession that inviting Amazon ruined the town lands as the episode's thesis.

Featured characters: the boys; Jeff Bezos; Stephen and Butters Stotch; Mayor McDaniels; Santa Claus; Randy Marsh and Towelie; Stuart McCormick; Larry Zewiski.

Locations: the Amazon Fulfillment Center; City Hall; Tegridy Farms; the bike parade route.

Key events & continuity: the Amazon arc ends with the town choosing weed over Bezos; Josh Carter dies; Santa learns of Hankey's exile; Garrison is in custody; conclusion of the two-parter.

Cartman, furious at Kyle, has immigration agents raid the Broflovski home and drag the whole family to a detention center. At the camp, Kyle warns the guards that traumatizing children will create a Mexican Joker, a vengeful figure forged by cruelty, and the guards take the analogy terrifyingly literally, hunting for a Joker that does not exist. Cartman gets himself sent to the same camp out of spite and Stan has him shipped to another facility as payback. Meanwhile Randy, desperate to crush home-grown weed, merges Tegridy Farms with the corporate giant MedMen, and Towelie, betrayed, disowns him in a screaming fight about whether Randy is a towel. Back at the camp, Kyle rallies the kids by converting them all to Judaism with foil yarmulkes, forcing the guards to release everyone. The camp director murders his own officers to cover it up and flees, convinced he helped the Mexican Joker escape. Across town, home-grow operations start exploding, which the news blames on the Mexican Joker, while Randy, hallucinating towels, collapses in the street insisting he is not a towel.

Cartman's rendition of a show tune for the detained kids falls completely flat, and his apology to Kyle about Jewish sensitivity is undercut by immediately doing it again. Towelie's parting shot, that weed is a gift from God not to be exploited by a stupid towel, becomes the episode's moral center, which Randy screams over.

Featured characters: Kyle Broflovski, Cartman and Stan; the Broflovski family; Jeff Corrigan and the ICE officers; Randy Marsh and Towelie; the MedMen representatives.

Locations: the ICE detention center; Tegridy Farms; the Broflovski home; South Park streets; the courthouse.

Key events & continuity: the Mexican Joker is born as a media myth; Randy partners with MedMen; Towelie breaks with Randy; the Whites' adoption storyline begins brewing.

Randy flies to China to expand Tegridy Weed and gets arrested at customs for smuggling marijuana, landing in a brutal prison where he meets Winnie the Pooh and Piglet, jailed for resembling the Chinese president. To close his deal, Randy strangles Pooh to death with a cable, and returns home covered in blood and honey, which Stan immediately deduces. Meanwhile Stan's death-metal band Crimson Dawn attracts a producer who wants to make their biopic, but every draft gets censored for the Chinese market: no Dalai Lama, no Winnie the Pooh, no homosexuality, nothing American. After Chinese officials literally supervise his rewriting, Stan snaps and has the band perform as Fingerbang instead, declaring anyone who betrays their ideals is not worth a lick of spit. Randy narrates over footage of China that Tegridy is now selling there anyway, the money rolling in by the truckload.

The band's death-metal tantrum about farm life shocks the Autumn Fest crowd, and the producer's three-act-structure notes keep sanding off every edge. Randy's tribunal shaming of China for lacking integrity somehow works as a negotiation tactic, and the final montage of Chinese street life undercuts his narration about the money rolling in.

Featured characters: Randy, Stan, Sharon and Shelly Marsh; Mickey Mouse; Winnie the Pooh and Piglet; Jimmy, Butters and Kenny of Crimson Dawn; the biopic producer; Chinese officials.

Locations: China, airport, prison and tribunal; Tegridy Farms; Autumn Fest; Spinny Mountain Records.

Key events & continuity: Randy murders Winnie the Pooh; Tegridy enters the Chinese market; Stan refuses to sell out; Kyle and Cartman return from the detention center.

Randy is riding high on 300,000 dollars in weed profits, parading down Main Street on a float and flashing the crowd, while his family openly resents him. Cartman, meanwhile, is terrorizing the town in a different way: he refuses his vaccination shot, stripping naked and squealing like a pig every time the doctor approaches, and gets himself declared a conscientious objector. When the parents stage a nighttime ambush to hold him down, he greases himself up and escapes, forcing them to hire Big Mesquite Murph, an award-winning hog wrestler, who proposes a full vaccination roundup at the CDC. Liane, exiled by Cartman for betraying him, finds sympathy at Tegridy Farms, and Randy finally apologizes to Towelie, renouncing his China deal. At the roundup, Cartman outruns everyone for sixteen minutes until Liane fights through the crowd and takes the needle meant for him, declaring it her choice. Cartman then goes to get the shot voluntarily, only to find the dose has made Liane artistic, painting in the medical center, which horrifies him.

Shelly's fury that the farm was Randy's dream, not hers, keeps boiling over, and Sharon's resentment that she co-owns the farm Randy treats as his solo empire drives the family plot. Stephen's offer to help catch Cartman, the parents' midnight raid, and Mesquite's hog-wrestling credentials all fail against one greased-up fourth grader.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Cartman and Liane; Towelie; Big Mesquite Murph; PC Principal; the doctor.

Locations: the Family Medical Center; Main Street; South Park Elementary; the Cartman residence; Tegridy Farms; Skeeter's Wine Bar; the CDC roundup field.

Key events & continuity: Randy cuts ties with China; Liane takes Cartman's shot; the 300th episode milestone.

When students protest the cafeteria food, the school replaces the menu with plant-based goo that tastes identical to the real thing, and decides not to tell Cartman, who has already had two heart attacks arguing about it. Cartman inhales the goo tacos on Taco Tuesday without noticing, and when Butters finally confesses, the Goo Man himself explains the goo is just as fatty as the old food. Cartman forgives everyone: all he ever wanted was fatty rubbish in a box, and if it is greener, fine. Meanwhile Randy, desperate for new revenue after leaving China, starts making Tegridy Burgers from weed mulch, outsells Burger King, and drives the local rancher out of business so thoroughly that the man dumps his unwanted cows on the farm. Randy and Towelie get high and slaughter the entire herd, and when the footage leaks, the town assumes Tegridy Burgers are beef. The public turns on Randy, booing him off his own press moment.

Wendy's earnest speech about their generation eating better gives Cartman his second heart attack, and the cafeteria workers' terror as he eats the goo tacos is the episode's tensest scene. The Goo Man's side hustle selling goo all over town, plus the rancher's revenge dumping, turns Randy's burger empire into a brief, bloody fad.

Featured characters: Cartman and Butters; Randy Marsh and Towelie; Wendy Testaburger; the Goo Man; Rick of Burger King; the rancher; Mr. Mackey; PC Principal.

Locations: South Park Elementary cafeteria; Tegridy Farms; Burger King; City Wok.

Key events & continuity: Randy's burger venture collapses; the goo food stays; Cartman makes peace with fake meat so long as it is unhealthy.

Randy is hyped for his Halloween Special weed strain while Shelly, who hates marijuana and wants it illegal again, secretly brews a potion to destroy it. At the Denver Museum of Nature and Science, Butters steals a mummy exhibit's sticker for his collection despite an old farmer's curse warning, and the mummy starts breaking into his house at night, smashing things and gifting him Fitbits. The mummy's rampage escalates to a school assembly, and the police get involved. Randy's ruined Special turns out to have mutated from Shelly's potion into something stronger, and at the Halloween party the laced weed turns the guests into plant zombies, while a resurrected Winnie the Pooh stalks the barn. Shelly marches in, reveals everyone is just extremely high and hallucinating, and sobers them up with another potion. Randy begs the cops to jail Shelly for the night, and she ends up cellmates with Butters, who locked himself up to dodge blame for the mummy. Randy wakes up three days later crediting a fat bitchy angel for saving him, and finds a used condom suggesting his night went further than he remembers.

Randy's three-day blackout ends with him praising a fat bitchy angel and denying anything happened with Harvey Weinstein, until the used condom says otherwise. The mummy's farewell note, translated by a cop as advice to get help, is the episode's oddly sincere coda.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Towelie; Butters Stotch; the mummy; Winnie the Pooh; Mr. Mackey; PC Principal; Harrison Yates.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; the Denver Museum of Nature and Science; South Park Elementary; Park County Police Station.

Key events & continuity: Winnie the Pooh returns from the dead; Shelly's anti-weed crusade continues; Butters' mummy curse resolves with an apology note.

The town has finally had enough of Randy: after weeks of self-promoting parades, slaughtering a thousand cows, dealing with China and nearly poisoning everyone with his Halloween Special, he is arrested and jailed until trial. Sharon starts planning a life without the farm, but the Whites crash her party, grieving their son Jason, who was accidentally run over by a police car during a football game. Cartman suggests they adopt a replacement child from the Texas detention center, and they bring home Alejandro. In prison, Randy learns the DARVO technique, deny, attack, reverse victim and offender, from President Garrison over the phone, and tries it on everyone. At his trial Randy starts to rant, then breaks down and admits Garrison set him up to play the victim, vowing to do his time and get back to making quality weed. Just then Alejandro snaps and goes on a rampage dressed as the Mexican Joker, the police open fire, and in the chaos the charges against Randy are dropped. Randy thanks the town, including the Whites, and heads home to harvest the last crop, breaking the fourth wall to thank the audience and take pre-orders for next season.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Towelie; the White family and Alejandro; President Garrison; Cartman; Mayor McDaniels; Rudy Giuliani.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; Park County Jail; City Hall; the White residence; the Texas detention center; Washington D.C.

Key events & continuity: Randy is exonerated; the Mexican Joker becomes real in Alejandro; the Whites become Randy loyalists; the season ends with a direct address.

Strong Woman enters the annual Strong Woman Competition with PC Principal coaching her, but a new transgender athlete, Heather Swanson, dominates every event, leaving Strong Woman in second place. Heather torments her relentlessly, and PC Principal's attempts to intervene get him branded a transphobe, until Strong Woman reveals Heather is her vengeful ex-boyfriend. At school, Nichole and Tammy join Cartman's board game club, Dice Studz, and start beating the boys at every game, so Cartman lobbies the state legislature to ban girls from boys' clubs, winning on a sympathy speech about Scott's diabetes. The victory backfires when the girls form their own bigger, better club and the boys get kicked out of it. Finally Nichole challenges Heather to a series of board games, and the girls crush her, since Heather only likes games for their themes. Heather storms out with Cartman in tow, and PC Principal goes home to his unfazed babies.

David Perry's interview with Heather keeps getting derailed by her screaming about transphobia, and PC Principal's carefully worded assembly speech about confronting difficult issues collapses the moment he touches her shoulder. The PC babies cry over Mulan through the whole competition, oblivious to the adult chaos around them.

Featured characters: Strong Woman and PC Principal; Heather Swanson; the PC babies; Cartman, Butters and Scott Malkinson; Nichole and Tammy; Mr. Mackey.

Locations: the Strong Woman Competition; South Park Elementary; Dice Studz; the Colorado General Assembly.

Key events & continuity: Heather Swanson is revealed as Strong Woman's ex; the PC babies remain oblivious; Cartman sides with Heather. Note: the source extract for this episode was thin, so this entry sticks closely to what it confirms.

Sheila Broflovski's crusade for women's equality is derailed by a violent bout of diarrhea, and she is diagnosed with C. diff, treated with a fecal transplant that leaves her feeling amazing. She brags about it all over town, and soon Harriet Biggle and the other moms are demanding her poo for DIY transplants, which Sheila refuses. The boys break into the Broflovski house and steal Sheila's feces from the pipes to trade, while Kyle, horrified, researches the microbiome and becomes convinced Tom Brady's poo is the ultimate cure, the spice melange. The moms' turkey-baster DIY jobs go septic, half the town comes down with the infection, and the boys infiltrate Tom Brady's house, where Kyle's microbiome-possessed body leads them to a hidden room full of curative jars. Tom Brady's poo saves South Park, the moms apologize to each other, and Kyle walks home covered in filth, disowned by everyone for defending the whole mess.

The DVD Kyle watches teaches him that half his body is microorganisms, which sends him spiraling, and his question to the doctor about harvesting athletic microbiomes is what cracks the Tom Brady lead. Mr. Mackey's demand that the boys steal feces again, this time Brady's, makes him an accomplice, and the turkey-baster reveal explains the whole town's outbreak.

Featured characters: Sheila, Kyle and Ike Broflovski; Harriet Biggle, Linda Stotch and Laura Tucker; the boys; Tom Brady; Mr. Mackey; the Hell's Pass doctor.

Locations: the community center; Hell's Pass Hospital; Cafe Monet; the Broflovski home; Tom Brady's house.

Key events & continuity: the moms' friendship fractures and mends; Tom Brady's microbiome is canonically miraculous; Kyle ends the episode literally covered in crap.

Scott Malkinson falls head over heels when new student Sophie Gray arrives and mentions she has diabetes too, and the boys, especially Cartman and Jimmy, immediately start coaching and mocking him. Scott lies about watching The Mandalorian to impress her and begs his father Clark to get Disney+, but Clark, a cable man to the bone, refuses and declares streaming is going straight to hell. When Scott trades his own insulin to Nathan for a black-market Disney+ password, Clark rallies the other cable workers to physically rip out the town's streaming cables, killing Disney+ everywhere on the night of Scott's big date. Sophie is mortified to learn every boy in school has been hitting on her since she arrived, and tells Scott she is more than her diabetes, which forces Scott to realize he has made his whole identity about his. They part as friends who can actually talk about diabetes honestly, while the cable company shows up too late to matter.

Cartman's advice to Scott, drawn from his own Heidi experience, is that love is diabetes times ten, which Scott takes as encouragement. Nathan's streaming-password black market, priced in insulin, is the episode's bleakest joke, and Clark's crew procrastinating through bowling and shopping instead of sabotaging cables is pure South Park.

Featured characters: Scott Malkinson and Sophie Gray; Clark Malkinson; Cartman, Jimmy and the boys; Nathan; Pete; the cable workers.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the Malkinson residence; Jimmy's house; the playground.

Key events & continuity: Sophie Gray is introduced; Scott learns his identity is not just diabetes; the cable-versus-streaming war ends with streaming winning. Note: the source extract for this episode was thin, so this entry sticks closely to what it confirms.

Santa Claus tries to lecture South Park about drunk driving at the tree-lighting ceremony and gets booed off stage for ruining the fun, then gets a law passed banning all alcohol sales until January 2nd. With the adults' holiday spirit dead and the liquor aisles blocked off, the mayor begs Randy for weed, but nothing grows in winter, until falling snow inspires him: Christmas Snow, a mix of old batches topped with cocaine, which grows year-round. The parents get their spirit back and go right back to driving impaired. The mayor is horrified to learn about the cocaine, so Randy protests until cocaine is legalized, then rolls out Marijuana-Free Christmas Snow when Santa bans weed too. When Santa steals the whole supply, Randy chases his sleigh, they tumble off a mountain, and Randy converts him with a taste of Tegridy Cocaine, which Santa finds cleaner than any other. Jesus shows up annoyed, tries it too, and decides the town needs cocaine for Christmas, making it snow cocaine over South Park. The adults spend the holiday happily driving under the influence, the kids despair at their parents' holiday spirit, and the season ends on a Santa-endorsed ad for Tegridy Cocaine.

Featured characters: Randy Marsh and Towelie; Santa Claus; Jesus Christ; Mayor McDaniels; Stan and the boys.

Locations: the tree-lighting ceremony; Tegridy Farms; the ice skating rink; City Hall; the mountain.

Key events & continuity: Tegridy Cocaine is born; Santa and Jesus both endorse it; the season closes on a drug-fueled Christmas.

COVID-19 has hollowed out South Park: the school is closed, the police are the new teachers, and Cartman is living his dream of permanent pajamas and Zoom school until classes reopen and he is handcuffed to his desk. Randy, whose weed sales are up 400 percent, launches a Pandemic Special strain, while privately panicking: he remembers getting intimate with a bat, and then a pangolin, in China with Mickey Mouse, and realizes he may have started the pandemic himself. He kidnaps the lab pangolin, gets a death threat from Mickey, and decides to secretly vaccinate the town by ejaculating into his weed, which gives everyone, including Jimbo, Randy-style mustaches. Stan, cracking under the shutdown, breaks the kids out of school quarantine to get Butters to Build-A-Bear, but the police gun down Kenny in the street. At the store, Cartman tries to destroy the pangolin so school stays closed, but Stan admits it is he who cannot cope, and Cartman relents. Garrison arrives with a flamethrower, torches the scientist and the pangolin, and the town locks down completely as Randy decides against confessing, since Sharon secretly likes his weed.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Cartman, Kyle, Kenny and Butters; President Garrison; Mickey Mouse; Harrison Yates; Mr. Mackey; Jimbo; Dr. Fauci.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; South Park Elementary; Hell's Pass Hospital; Build-A-Bear Workshop; Main Street; the science facility.

Key events & continuity: Kenny is gunned down by police; Randy is revealed as patient zero via the pangolin; the mustache side effect; Garrison burns the cure; hour-long special.

With vaccines reserved for seniors, Mr. Mackey fails thirty straight nights to get an appointment at Walgreens, while the boys' friendship frays: Cartman and Kenny's period prank on Mrs. Nelson's chair drives her to quit teaching just as school reopens. Garrison, having lost the election, slinks back to South Park wanting his teaching job back, complete with a Secret Service agent in a codpiece. Mackey sends the boys to steal vaccines from Walgreens for the teachers, and they pull it off disguised as a senior-citizen charity, then hole up at Raisins arguing over whether to sell the doses, until Kyle nearly swaps one for his dad. Meanwhile Bob White's QAnon crew, convinced Garrison speaks in code, builds a child army, the Lil' Qties, to stop the vaccinations, and Garrison treks through a warping reality to cut a deal with the elites. An Air Israel plane delivers vaccines for everyone, Mrs. Nelson dies of COVID before she can be saved, and at her funeral the boys agree to a 2-2-3 custody schedule for Kenny's friendship. Garrison takes over the classroom permanently, thanking the elites with Mr. Hat in hand.

Featured characters: Stan, Kyle, Cartman and Kenny; Mr. Mackey; Mrs. Nelson; Herbert Garrison and Mr. Service; Bob White and the Whites; Scott Malkinson; the Lil' Qties; Chris and Tom.

Locations: Walgreens; South Park Elementary; Raisins; the White residence; the school bridge.

Key events & continuity: Mrs. Nelson dies of COVID; Garrison returns as a teacher with Mr. Hat; the boys' broship is restructured; hour-long special; Kenny survives this one.

Mr. Garrison returns from break with a new boyfriend, Rick, but his class will not even pretend to listen to his stories, so PC Principal punishes the entire fourth grade by cancelling Pajama Day. Cartman has nightmares about being laughed at for his pajamas, the town's parents start wearing pajamas to work in solidarity, and a newsman keeps comparing the whole thing to Nazi Germany, in German, in a full uniform. Wendy brokers a plan for the kids to apologize to Garrison, but he launches into another endless Rick monologue and nobody can stay awake. Cornered, PC Principal nearly resigns, until Wendy points out Opposite Day is coming in March: he declares the mix-up was Mackey's fault, announces it is Opposite Day, and the kids triumphantly wear their pajamas as the opposite of what they were told. The town stands down, the prisoners are released, and Garrison gets his classroom back with Rick at his side.

The realtors' pajama solidarity fractures over Mike, who will not wear his in the rain, and a customer gets arrested at IHOP for refusing. Yates's domestic dispute call, where a wife will not sleep with her non-pajama'd husband, convinces him the town is a powder keg, and his release order, whatever covers your bits, only confuses everyone more.

Featured characters: PC Principal; Wendy Testaburger; Cartman; Mr. Garrison and Rick; Mr. Mackey; Heather Williams and Millie Larsen; Bill Keegan; Harrison Yates.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the South Park Realtors office; IHOP; Park County Police Station; Brighton Street.

Key events & continuity: Opposite Day saves PC Principal's authority; Garrison's relationship with Rick continues; the Matt Damon joke becomes a running gag.

At a cannabis expo, Randy learns consumers want weed grown by people of color, and realizes he has no Black friends, so he invites Tolkien Black's family to dinner and photographs himself with them relentlessly. Stan is horrified to discover he has spent his whole life thinking Tolkien's name was Token, and nobody else made that mistake, not Kyle, not Cartman. Randy tries to make Steve Black his business partner, parading him around Tegridy Farms, but treats him as a prop, and Steve quits in disgust when he realizes he is just a token Black guy. Meanwhile Stan, spiraling with guilt, lectures the school on Tolkien literature and declares a Tolkien Appreciation Day, only for Tolkien to grab the mic and announce he has always hated the books. Steve opens a rival farm across the street, Credigree Weed, stealing Randy's customers, and Randy declares war, kicking Tolkien out of his house as a spy.

Dr. Gauche's warmth curdles the instant Stan admits the Token mistake, and his prescription, read from a Black perspective, sends Stan into a full Tolkien reading binge. Steve's Lord of the Rings weed line, nine races of Middle-Earth, dies in the pitch meeting, and Randy's fury at seeing Credigree's customers is the moment the farm war turns real.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon and Stan Marsh; Steve, Linda and Tolkien Black; Kyle and Cartman; Towelie; Dr. Gauche.

Locations: the Cannabis Cultivators Expo; Tegridy Farms; South Park Elementary; the doctor's office.

Key events & continuity: Tolkien's name is Tolkien, after the author; Steve founds Credigree Weed, Randy's rival; Tolkien reveals he hates fantasy novels.

When the rent goes up, Liane Cartman becomes a realtor to save the family home, and Cartman, furious at losing his after-school servant, declares himself a rival agent, calling real estate legal theft. He undercuts his mother at every open house, films commercials for his classmates' houses, and lists the Black residence for fifty million dollars, packing it with demanding city buyers asking about cortados and Pilates. The town's Chamber of Commerce panics as city people overrun South Park, and Jimbo leads an armed posse to remind the realtors who runs the town, opening fire on the Blacks' house mid-showing. Liane finally surrenders, quitting her job with a white napkin to keep Cartman's love, and the broke Cartmans move into the historic Aspen Park Hot Dog stand, where Cartman's optimism dies the moment condiments come out of the tap instead of water.

Cartman's open-house refreshments, LaCroix, edamame, oat milk, acai, are weaponized gentrification, and the realtors snapping their own backs taking new headshots is the episode's best visual gag. The Aspen Park Hot Dog's historic listing, heavily promoted to anyone fleeing the city people, becomes the Cartmans' only option, and the condiment tap is the final insult.

Featured characters: Cartman and Liane Cartman; the city people; John Aspinal and the realtors; Jimbo Kern; Mayor McDaniels; Tuong Lu Kim; Mr. Adler; Harriet Biggle.

Locations: the Cartman residence; the Black residence; the Tweak residence; City Wok; City Hall; the Aspen Park Hot Dog.

Key events & continuity: the Cartmans lose their home and move into the hot dog stand, where they will live for a long stretch; Liane quits real estate.

entries.n: S25E04 — Back To The Cold War
entries.t:
Butters is competing in a dressage championship on his pony Melancholy, and his parents are convinced his Russian rival Davey Solokov is a communist plant, warning Butters his pony will be sold, slaughtered and turned into skin cream if he loses. Melancholy keeps humiliating Butters mid-course by defecating, getting an erection and mounting other ponies. Mr. Mackey, spiraling into Cold War nostalgia after one too many nuclear drills, becomes convinced PC Principal is a Russian spy, stalks the Solokovs for a day, and teams up with Stephen and Linda, who show up armed with organic laxatives to sabotage the Russian pony. Mackey then uses his childhood DOS computer to warn NORAD that Russia will nuke the competition, raising the alert to DEFCON 3. Both governments end up watching the dressage finals, where Putin himself is found dancing to eighties music. Melancholy wins by mounting the Russian pony mid-course and disqualifying Davey, and Mackey, draped in a flag, delivers a rambling speech about aging, failing bodies and Sting lyrics that somehow moves Putin to nod along. His mother gently reminds him the old days were scary, not glorious, and the crisis deflates.

Featured characters: Butters Stotch; Stephen and Linda Stotch; Melancholy; Davey Solokov and the Solokovs; Mr. Mackey and his mother; PC Principal; Vladimir Putin and Sergei Shoigu; Mr. Garrison and Wendy.

Locations: the dressage competition; South Park Elementary; Mackey's childhood home; Moscow.

Key events & continuity: Mackey's Cold War paranoia peaks; Butters wins the championship; Putin is humanized by Mackey's speech.

entries.n: S25E05 — Help, My Teenager Hates Me!
entries.t:
The boys take up Airsoft as Team Floppy Weiner, but the field pairs each of them with a bored, hostile teenager, and the teenagers promptly move into their lives, demanding to be cooked for and threatening them. Kyle's teenager Trevor will not even clean his gun, Stan's calls at midnight insisting he is not gay, and Cartman's lives in the bathroom with lotion. A self-help book suggests a camping trip, which fails miserably. Finally Gerald suggests the nuclear option: the dads buy their own Airsoft gear, with Randy, Stuart and a heavily armed Jimbo joining the kids for a boys-versus-teenagers showdown, loser leaves the winners' lives forever. The dads' squad wins, with Randy taking out five teenagers with Tegridy weed as a distraction, and the boys walk home grateful, while Randy raises his weapon and suggests taking the kids out before they can become teenagers, which Gerald talks him out of, for now.

The proprietor's warning that the weapons are safe but the players are not hangs over everything, and the teenagers' endless bruh at the safety briefing sets the tone. Kyle's makeup-covered BB wound, Stan's midnight reassurance call, and Cartman's lotion-haunted bathroom breaks make the dads' eventual rescue feel earned.

Featured characters: Kyle, Stan, Cartman and Kenny; Gerald Broflovski; Randy Marsh; Stuart McCormick; Jimbo Kern; Trevor and the teenagers.

Locations: the South Park Airsoft Armory; Blinky's Airsoft range; the Broflovski and McCormick residences; Denny's; the grocery store.

Key events & continuity: the dads bond with the boys over Airsoft; Randy's dark joke about preemptive strikes; Team Floppy Weiner is born.

entries.n: S25E06 — Credigree Weed St. Patrick's Day Special
entries.t:
Butters, dressed head to toe in green, pinches Kelly-Ann Barlow for not wearing green and is arrested for sexual assault of a minor when it turns out she was wearing green socks all along. He prays to a leprechaun from his cell while his public defender quits on him. Meanwhile Randy, furious that Steve Black's Credigree Weed is running a rival St. Patrick's Day Special, accuses him of cultural appropriation of the only white holiday left, and the two brawl between their farms until both are jailed. Randy breaks out using inexplicable rainbow powers and discovers Steve has been cutting his weed with stolen Tegridy product. The real Saint Patrick shows up at the Irish bar, reveals the holiday is about getting drunk and assaulting each other, and alienates everyone. Butters gets community service, blaming his church for his downfall.

Randy's Serena Williams pitch to Shelly fails instantly, and his museum trip to teach her about hemp rope only deepens her contempt. Butters's prayer for a leprechaun is answered by Randy in a leprechaun costume, which Butters accepts without question, and the cake stuffed with weed nearly works until the cops smoke Credigree instead.

Featured characters: Butters Stotch; Randy Marsh; Steve Black; Farty O'Cool; Saint Patrick; Kelly-Ann Barlow; Stan.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; Credigree Weed; Park County Police Station; the Irish bar; South Park Elementary.

Key events & continuity: the Randy and Steve farm war continues; Randy manifests rainbow powers; Saint Patrick is a menace. Note: the source extract for this episode was thin, so this entry sticks closely to what it confirms.
k: credigree weed st. patrick's day special

entries.t:
Cartman is jealous of the TikToks Kyle and Tolkien have been making together, so he unleashes his imaginary Valentine's friend Cupid Ye to spread a rumor that Kyle runs Hollywood and Jews have appropriated Black culture. The lie spreads through the school like wildfire, with kids asking Kyle about movie deals, and Cupid Ye starts whispering conspiracies into Tolkien's ear at night, driving a wedge between the two friends until they quit making videos together. But Ye goes rogue, escalating into open bigotry, stealing a car and smashing it up, and Cartman has to admit to Stan that Ye is real, sort of, and needs to be put back on his medication. At the Valentine's Day card exchange, Ye shoots half the school with hate arrows, and Cartman tackles him in the hallway and forces the pills down his throat, restoring the harmless Cupid Me. Kyle closes with a speech explaining, with real history, how Jewish people came to Hollywood, and the crowd chants to let the Jew run it.

Cartman's prayer scene, begging Ye not to do anything drastic while Ye has been acting crazy since getting into Jesus, is the episode's clearest tell that Cartman knows exactly what he unleashed. Randy's detour into complaining about woke movies being preachy, calling himself brave for disliking Avatar 2, is pure background Randy.

Featured characters: Cartman and Cupid Ye; Kyle Broflovski and Tolkien Black; Stan Marsh; Kenny; PC Principal; Mr. Mackey; Steve Black.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the public park; the Broflovski residence; Credigree Weed.

Key events & continuity: Cupid Ye is established as Cartman's unmedicated id; Kyle and Tolkien reconcile; Kyle's Hollywood history lesson.

The Prince and Princess of Canada, fresh from the Queen's funeral, flee the press on a Worldwide Privacy Tour and land their private jet in South Park, moving into the house across from Kyle and immediately throwing loud drum-and-firework protests demanding privacy. Kyle, already spiraling about his personal brand after Butters drags him to the CumHammer Brand Management agency, files noise complaints and tries on identities like rugged victim and thick-skinned cool guy. When the Prince rubs himself on the Broflovskis' window, Kyle finally snaps at the agency, delivering a speech that reducing people to brands makes them performers instead of humans. The Prince agrees, realizes he has become a product, and follows Kyle and Butters out, while the Princess stays behind, hollow inside. The episode ends with the Prince jamming on his drums while the boys play basketball, accepted as one of the group.

Butters's brand coaching turns him into a playground menace until Bebe beats him into the snow, and Kyle's black-shirt thick-skinned act fools nobody. Ike rewatching the Queen's funeral on loop is the episode's quiet heart, and Kyle finally choosing to just be himself with his brother lands the theme.

Featured characters: Kyle and Ike Broflovski; the Prince and Princess of Canada; Butters Stotch; Mr. Davis; Stan, Cartman, Kenny, Tolkien and Jimmy; Bebe Stevens.

Locations: the Broflovski residence; the Cartman residence; CumHammer Brand Management; South Park Elementary; Canada.

Key events & continuity: the Canadian royals move to South Park; Kyle rejects brand culture; the Prince befriends the boys.

Randy replaces the broken guest bathroom toilet with a ten-thousand-dollar Japanese model, complete with bidet, seat warmer, Bluetooth and mood music, after Sharon threatens to stop helping him sell weed unless he cooperates. He will not stop bragging about it, comparing the family to the Kennedys, until the whole town resents the Marshes and the kids mock Stan as rich. His proctologist, Dr. Sheltair, furious at losing a lucrative patient, kicks the toilet, later takes hostages at Home Depot, and shoots himself in the rear. Jimmy reveals the toilet paper industry, worth billions, silences anyone who threatens it, citing the millions of acres cleared and the rolls Americans burn through. When Randy preaches the toilet gospel at City Hall and declares toilet paper obsolete, he is shot and falls into a coma. Stan takes up the cause and plans a rally, but a recovering Randy interrupts it to apologize to the toilet paper companies, insisting South Park has nothing against toilet paper. He digs up Ol' Blue from the yard and reinstalls it, concluding that luxury only makes you want more luxury, and kisses Sharon, who is offended.

The deliverymen's reverent installation, Sharon's squeals of delight on her first try, and Randy's family meeting comparing them to the Kennedys set the episode's tone of luxury curdling into obsession.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Jimmy Valmer; Dr. Sheltair; Detective Yates; Mayor McDaniels; Butters; Clyde.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; Home Depot; South Park Elementary; City Hall; Hell's Pass Hospital.

Key events & continuity: the toilet paper industry is untouchable; Randy is shot and survives; Ol' Blue returns.

Stan starts using ChatGPT to text Wendy back, copying AI-generated sweet nothings while barely reading them, after Clyde admits he uses it to fake romantic texts to Bebe, who is delighted by them. Wendy, feeling insecure next to Bebe's romance, gets a dream date at the ice cream parlor, where Stan has to bluff his way through intimate questions about a childhood trauma, a boating accident in Switzerland and an incident with his cousin, all invented by the chatbot. Half the boys are also using it to cheat on essays, and Garrison, instead of catching them, starts using it to grade, while his boyfriend Rick secretly uses it to fake supportive texts too. When the school board sends a technician with a falcon named Shadowbane to hunt the cheater, the bird flags Wendy's phone, and she faces punishment while Stan sweats. Cornered, Stan asks ChatGPT to write a story where everything works out, and the AI-generated tale, in which Stan gives a speech blaming giant tech companies for monetizing AI, somehow resolves the whole crisis: the technician vows to stop the corporations, Mackey sends everyone home, and Wendy forgives Stan, admitting she prefers his dumb thumbs-up emojis anyway. Clyde is left stunned that it worked.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh and Wendy Testaburger; Clyde Donovan and Bebe Stevens; Cartman and Butters; Mr. Garrison and Rick; Mr. Mackey; Bobby Palmer and Shadowbane.

Locations: South Park Elementary; Willy's Chilly Ice Cream Parlor; the boys' bathroom; Garrison's house.

Key events & continuity: ChatGPT enters South Park; Wendy and Stan's relationship survives; Garrison uses AI to grade; Rick is exposed as an AI-text faker too.

Butters lands a job at the ice cream parlor and starts earning real paychecks, which makes Cartman demand a job too, until Liane reminds him he forced her to quit hers. Cartman is the worst employee imaginable, taking mental health days and bare minimum Mondays, until he has an epiphany: he lives in a hot dog stand, so he and Kenny will open a restaurant there, funded by Butters' savings. They blow the money on rides, wine tastings, a mermaid grotto and a smiley-face hot dog logo, hiring nobody and doing nothing, until Butters, whose parents think he is lying about his vanishing paycheck, storms in and opens DikinBaus Hot Dogs himself, serving food solo. The town hails Cartman as a hero anyway. Butters then sells the whole operation to overseas investors, who pay to move the Cartmans back into their old house, and Cartman weeps because the renovated hot dog stand had become his dream home.

Cartman's laptop cameo, declaring a mental health day from home, and his Take-it-Easy Tuesday and Wet's Not Work Too Hard Wednesday, make him the episode's perfect satire of remote-work culture. Darryl Weathers showing up desperate for a job, then demanding to work from home, gets rejected by the very slacker who inspired him.

Featured characters: Cartman and Liane; Kenny McCormick; Butters Stotch; Stephen and Linda Stotch; Mr. Sullivan; Benny the banker; Darryl Weathers; Mayor McDaniels.

Locations: Willy's Chilly Ice Cream Parlor; the South Park Bank; the Aspen Park Hot Dog, now DikinBaus; the Cartman residence.

Key events & continuity: the Cartmans get their house back; DikinBaus is sold off; Butters proves to be the competent one.

Garrison takes his boyfriend Rick to Myrtle Beach for spring break, swearing he will not relapse into rallying, then immediately sneaks out to a MAGA store to rant to cheering supporters night after night, lying that he is out buying sunscreen. Rick catches him mid-rally at a MAGA convention, leaves for the airport, and Garrison hijacks a 2024 campaign rally to deliver a speech that is entirely about how much he loves Rick, which whips the crowd into storming the Capitol again. Meanwhile Randy, left alone with Stan for the week after Sharon and Shelley leave for Santa Fe, is disgusted that Stan and Tolkien just want to paint Warhammer miniatures, and throws a massive rager with strippers and a Romanian handler who turns out to be a sex trafficker named Alonzo Fineski, ending in a shootout that wounds a policewoman. Randy harasses the responding officer, mistakes her for a stripper, and gets cuffed. A drunken, injured Randy calls Sharon in tears, and she comes home early, stepping over the wreckage to find the boys still mid-game, untouched by any of it.

Garrison's tap-dance under the bathroom stall, his 2024 tattooed admirer, and his insistence that nobody can control him show the relapse was never really in doubt, while Rick watching the sunset alone is the episode's quietest heartbreak.

Featured characters: Mr. Garrison and Rick; Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelley Marsh; Tolkien Black; Steve Black; Alonzo Fineski; Officer Johnson.

Locations: Myrtle Beach; Tegridy Farms; the Shore Resort; Myrtle Beach International Airport.

Key events & continuity: Garrison's rally addiction resurfaces; Rick stays with him, warily; Randy's party ends in a trafficking shootout.

With Donald Trump back in the White House, behaving exactly like Saddam Hussein and sharing a bed with Satan, NPR gets cancelled and Cartman mourns his favorite show. PC Principal rebrands as Power-Christian Principal, prescribes the Bible for wokeness, and installs Jesus Christ himself at South Park Elementary, forcing Stan to pledge acceptance at his lunch table. When the townspeople march on Garrison's house, they find he was never re-elected and has been watching TV with Rick for years. Jesus warns the protesting town that the president can sue anyone into oblivion, so Gerald negotiates a settlement: 3.5 million dollars, gutted school and hospital funding, and a pro-Trump ad starring a synthetic Trump whose tiny talking penis endorses the message. Cartman, convinced woke is dead, talks Butters into a suicide pact in the Stotch family car, and they spend the credits slowly gassing themselves.

Cartman's Woke is Dead shirt, the Men Only and Women Only bathrooms, and his forlorn bench scene at Stark's Pond play his grief for wokeness completely straight. Gerald's claim that he warned everyone, the townspeople admitting they voted to get rid of woke stuff, and Darryl's protest that the answer is not going too far the other way give the town's anger texture.

Featured characters: Cartman and Butters; PC Principal; Jesus Christ; Stan Marsh; Randy Marsh and Gerald Broflovski; President Donald Trump and Satan; JD Vance; Karoline Leavitt.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the White House; Skeeter's Wine Bar; the Garrison residence; the Stotch garage; Stark's Pond.

Key events & continuity: Trump returns to the presidency; Jesus joins the school staff; PC Principal converts to Power Christianity; the town settles the lawsuit.

Government funding cuts cost Mr. Mackey his counseling job, and his banker Benny calculates his monthly nut stays at eight grand no matter what he cuts, so Mackey reluctantly signs up for ICE. His first raid hits a Dora the Explorer live show, where Kristi Noem shoots a service dog and her face starts sliding off. Meanwhile Cartman launches a debate podcast from his bathroom, calling it masterdebating, and loses the Charlie Kirk masterdebating award to Clyde. Mackey's ICE career takes him to Heaven to arrest Hispanic angels, then to Mar-a-Lago, where Trump wants him as the new face of ICE and he walks in on Trump in bed with Satan while JD Vance offers baby oil. Disgusted, Mackey flees with Clyde and Dora, escaping on a plane as Noem's detached face crawls around the resort attacking agents, and everyone sings a Christmas carol over the credits.

Benny's math, eight thousand a month no matter the cuts, is the episode's trap, and Mackey watching the ICE promo video in his car is his point of no return. Cartman's bathroom debates keep getting interrupted by Liane, his masterdebate pun writes itself, and Noem's mid-credits pet-store massacre is the episode's darkest button.

Featured characters: Mr. Mackey; Benny; Kristi Noem; Clyde Donovan; Cartman and Liane; President Donald Trump, JD Vance and Satan; Dora the Explorer.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the ICE Recruitment Center; a Dora live show; Heaven; Mar-a-Lago; the South Park Bank.

Key events & continuity: Mackey loses his school job and joins ICE; Trump's relationship with Satan deepens; Clyde wins the debate trophy.

ICE raids Tegridy Farms and hauls away Randy's Mexican workers, threatening to shut the farm down, and Randy and Towelie cope by rebranding as Techridy Marijuana Solutions, an AI-powered buzzword machine, while microdosing ketamine and asking ChatGPT, which flatters every terrible idea, for business advice. They break into a detention center to free a single Mexican employee, and Randy decides to send an emissary to Washington to lobby for reclassification: Towelie, armed with a ChatGPT travel plan. In D.C., Towelie lines up with groveling billionaires, plays a hologram of Randy offering himself as a gift to Trump, and is left hanging on the White House wall. Back home, Sharon talks a ketamine-addled Randy into admitting the farm is drowning in debt, and they sell it and move out. Satan, meanwhile, asks ChatGPT for help leaving his unhealthy relationship with Trump, finds Towelie on the wall, and admits there is no escape for either of them.

Sharon's late-night call to ChatGPT, venting about Randy and pitching a french-fries-into-salad business, exposes the sycophancy faster than any argument. Randy's hole freakouts during the Techridy commercial, his porch that will not slow down, and Sharon mimicking ChatGPT back at him make the ketamine spiral the episode's engine.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Towelie; President Donald Trump and Satan; JD Vance; Anna Paulina Luna; Tim Cook; Jeff Bezos; Mark Zuckerberg.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; Tweek Bros. Coffeehouse; an ICE detention center; Washington D.C.; the White House.

Key events & continuity: Tegridy Farms is sold and closed; Towelie is abandoned at the White House; ChatGPT is a sycophant; Satan wants out.

Butters needs a rare Labubu doll for his girlfriend Red's birthday, but tariffs have inflated the mystery boxes at the City Asian Pop-Up Store, formerly City Wok, from eighty-five to a hundred and twenty dollars, and he has to win one from a claw machine instead. Jesus, now the school counselor, investigates the Labubu craze and learns from the teachers that the dolls are tied to a viral demonic ritual, complete with pentagrams and chicken blood, which the moms all know about and allow. Red's birthday ritual summons a storm over South Park and manifests President Trump with Satan in tow, and Satan admits on camera that he is pregnant and bound to Trump for years. Jesus bans Labubus, TikTok and phones from school and gives Butters and Red detention, and Red declares she is done with Labubus.

Wing's constant scolding of Lu Kim for exploiting kids, and his defense that the tariffs screw him so he screws the children, is the episode's economic thesis. The teachers' calm acceptance that the Labubu ritual is satanic, and that kids love it, breaks Jesus, and his detention sentence plus the TikTok ban is his first real win.

Featured characters: Butters Stotch and Red McArthur; Tuong Lu Kim and Wing; Jesus Christ; President Donald Trump and Satan; JD Vance; Nelly and Betsy; Mrs. Paxton and Mrs. Gray.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the City Asian Pop-Up Store; Red's house; the White House; Fox News.

Key events & continuity: City Wok becomes a pop-up store; Jesus becomes school counselor; Satan's pregnancy is revealed; Labubus are banned.

A prediction-market app sweeps the school, and the kids start betting on everything, including whether Sheila Broflovski will strike Gaza and destroy a Palestinian hospital. Kyle is horrified, but Cartman realizes he can goose the odds by keeping Kyle angry, encouraging him to fight while secretly betting against Sheila with his mom's debit card. Sheila, oblivious, gets grilled about Gaza by the other moms, storms out, and flies to Israel to confront Benjamin Netanyahu in person, berating him for making life harder for Jews everywhere. At the White House, Trump keeps trying to induce a miscarriage in the pregnant Satan with greased stairs, Plan B soup and a cat-litter trap, while JD Vance schemes to stop the birth so he can become president. Kyle gets the bet taken down through a Kafkaesque chain of regulators who are all the same guy, and thanks Cartman, not realizing Cartman bet fourteen hundred dollars on his mom bombing Gaza.

Jimmy's evasive long-shot betting logic, the moms checking the app at Cafe Monet and switching to the long odds on Sheila, and Ike secretly betting on his own mother show how deep the rot goes. The Strategic Advisor answering every agency's phone, and emailing himself the complaint, is the episode's bureaucratic punchline.

Featured characters: Kyle, Sheila and Ike Broflovski; Cartman, Stan and Kenny; Jimmy Valmer; Jesus Christ; President Donald Trump, Satan and JD Vance; Brendan Carr; Benjamin Netanyahu.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the Broflovski residence; Cafe Monet; the White House; Israel; the FCC.

Key events & continuity: Sheila confronts Netanyahu; Satan's pregnancy continues; Vance plots against the baby; the prediction app is exposed as rigged by design.

The entire school is consumed by the 6-7 meme, with Butters laughing himself sick every time anyone says six-seven, until Cartman starts vomiting uncontrollably whenever he hears the numbers, a condition doctors warn could kill him in six to seven weeks. PC Principal, now fully Power Christian, invites tech billionaire Peter Thiel to lecture on the Antichrist, and Thiel becomes convinced the numbers point to Satan's unborn baby, due in six to seven weeks. Thiel gets government database access from JD Vance, surveils the school's cameras, and zeroes in on Cartman as possessed. Meanwhile Jesus, miserable as the school's token Christian, gets beaten up by PC Principal for questioning his faith, then finds his spine, ditches the meek act and walks back in ready to fight. Thiel sedates Cartman and hauls him toward Washington to stop the Antichrist's birth, with Liane's terrified permission.

The Cheesecake Factory double dates, Peggy Rockbottom's podcast Christianity and lip injections, and Jesus staring into the bathroom mirror sell his despair. Mr. Adler calling out the tech-billionaire data grab, PC Principal beating him for it, and Thiel clocking the girls' bathroom cameras make the surveillance plot genuinely queasy.

Featured characters: Cartman and Liane; Butters Stotch; PC Principal and Strong Christian Woman; Jesus Christ; Peter Thiel; President Donald Trump, Satan and JD Vance; Mr. Adler; Peggy Rockbottom.

Locations: South Park Elementary; the Cartman residence; the Cheesecake Factory; the White House; a medical facility.

Key events & continuity: the 6-7 meme becomes a plot device; Thiel takes Cartman to D.C.; Jesus embraces a tougher persona; Satan's baby is the Antichrist.

entries.n: S28E02 — The Woman In The Hat
entries.t:
The Marshes are homeless after losing Tegridy Farms, and move into Shady Acres with Grandpa Marvin, which Stan finds humiliating. Stan vents that South Park has become nothing but political garbage, and starts an online movement, South Park Sucks Now, which explodes to hundreds of thousands of followers, until he and Cousin Kyle turn it into a crypto coin and plan a rug pull with White House approval. At the White House, Trump is haunted by a woman in a wide-brimmed hat appearing in mirrors, identified as Melania, unleashed by the East Wing demolition, while Pam Bondi keeps getting feces on her face, analyzed as rectoplasm. A seance exposes the crypto scheme as a money-laundering machine, Cousin Kyle is indicted and sentenced to ten years, and Stan, chastened, gives up the coin and takes dance lessons with the seniors instead, as Melania watches over the demolished East Wing.

Stan filming the South Park Sucks Now launch with Kyle and Kenny, the sped-up crypto disclaimer, and Cousin Kyle's rug-pull tutorial, complete with MSB registration promises, play the scam completely straight. Trump's shower scene with Towelie, the filet-o-fish rectoplasm analysis, and Bondi's escalating facial situation keep the White House plot grotesque.

Featured characters: Stan, Randy, Sharon and Shelly Marsh; Marvin Marsh; Kyle Broflovski and Cousin Kyle; Kenny; President Donald Trump, Melania and Satan; JD Vance; Pam Bondi; Dan Scavino; Stephen Miller; Brendan Carr; Kristi Noem.

Locations: Shady Acres; the White House; the Broflovski residence; South Park Motor Inn.

Key events & continuity: the Marshes live at Shady Acres; Peter Thiel holds a sedated Cartman at the motel; Cousin Kyle is jailed; Melania haunts the White House.

Butters uses an AI video app to make fake revenge videos of Red McArthur after she used him to get a Labubu, and Red retaliates with a fake video of Butters with Totoro that the whole school believes. Detective Harris, investigating, cannot tell the AI fakes from reality: he interrogates Butters about his relationship with Totoro, mistakes Studio Ghibli's lawyers for Totoro's legal team, and goes undercover as Rocky with Murphy as Bullwinkle. The videos escalate until Kyle, Stan and Butters are hauled before a prosecutor over a fake Bluey video. Butters confesses he started it, Harris traces the Cartman videos' IP, and the police raid the motel where Peter Thiel has been generating fake Cartman videos to keep Liane calm while holding the real sedated Cartman. Thiel is arrested, and when leaked footage surfaces of Trump and Vance having sex, Trump declares it is all Sora 2 and fake, which everyone gratefully believes.

Liane watching AI Cartman promise he is safe in Washington, complete with catchphrases he has not used in years, is the episode's saddest image. Harris and Murphy's stakeout, their shaken-snow-globe speech about criminals turning into oranges, and the prosecutor treating Bluey as the victim complete the episode's collapse of reality.

Featured characters: Butters Stotch and Red McArthur; Kyle, Stan and Kenny; Bebe Stevens and Nichole Daniels; Detective Harris and Mitch Murphy; Peter Thiel; Liane Cartman; President Donald Trump and JD Vance; Studio Ghibli.

Locations: South Park Elementary; Park County Police Station; the South Park Motor Inn; the Cartman residence; the Park County Courthouse; the ice skating rink.

Key events & continuity: Peter Thiel is arrested; the Sora 2 deepfake epidemic; Trump and Vance's relationship is caught on tape and dismissed as AI.

With the town broke and Tegridy Farms gone, the Thanksgiving Turkey Trot gets a five-thousand-dollar prize courtesy of Saudi Arabia, and the boys form a team to win it. Cartman, citing race science, recruits Tolkien, insisting Black people are naturally faster runners, and when Tolkien quits over the Saudi sponsorship, Cartman steals his Xbox to drag him back. Pete Hegseth, now running the Department of War, descends on South Park to extract Peter Thiel, livestreams himself assaulting townspeople, and fires tear gas into the race, while Kristi Noem shows up to steal his content. In the chaos Tolkien backs across the finish line while arguing with Cartman, winning the race for their team by accident, and Cartman celebrates his race science. Harris locks Hegseth in a cell with Thiel, and the judge will see them Monday.

Hegseth's rope-descent entrance, his selfie-stick battle plan, and his insistence that the Department of War cannot be messed with make him the episode's perfect content-brain general. The tear-gas cannon, the turkey-costume shortcut debate at Tweek Bros., and Noem shooting a Pomeranian instead of a target keep the chaos escalating.

Featured characters: Stan, Kyle, Cartman, Kenny and Tolkien; Pete Hegseth; Detective Harris and Mitch Murphy; Kristi Noem; Mayor McDaniels; Wendy, Bebe, Red, Betsy and Nichole; Mr. Mackey; Randy Marsh; Tuong Lu Kim.

Locations: South Park City Hall; the Turkey Trot course; the Black residence and Credigree Weed; Park County Police Station; Tweek Bros. Coffeehouse.

Key events & continuity: Thiel and Hegseth are jailed together; Tolkien wins the race accidentally; Saudi Arabia sponsors the town event.

Satan is about to give birth to the Antichrist, due any day, while Trump and Vance, disguised as Salvation Army Santas, sneak into South Park to break Peter Thiel out of jail so he can stop the birth, an operation they call Kill My Own Baby. Stan, praying in a restroom for a Christmas miracle, is answered by the return of the Woodland Critters, who are thrilled about the coming crap out. Towelie, found in the White House laundry, tells Satan everything: Vance has been manipulating Trump into killing the baby, and Thiel was his hired expert. Satan confronts Trump, Jesus teleports Trump and Vance away in a guitar-powered bubble, and both sides converge on Hell's Pass Hospital, where Stan defends Satan's delivery room. Jesus has a change of heart and switches sides, and then the doctor announces the fetus has hanged itself on the ultrasound, which Trump celebrates as a miracle. Satan leaves the White House for good, and Jesus rewards Stan with the ultimate Christmas miracle: the old Marsh family home, restored and waiting for him, Merry Christmas Stan in lights.

Featured characters: Stan Marsh; Satan; President Donald Trump and JD Vance; Jesus Christ; Peter Thiel and Pete Hegseth; Towelie; the Woodland Critters; Peggy Rockbottom; Detective Harris.

Locations: Hell's Pass Hospital; the White House; South Park Community Park; Park County Police Station; Shady Acres; the old Marsh residence.

Key events & continuity: the Antichrist storyline ends with the fetus's suicide; Satan leaves Trump; Jesus redeems himself; Stan gets his childhood home back; season finale.

Cartman cons Liane into buying him a two-thousand-dollar Class 3 e-bike by faking bullying tears, then terrorizes South Park in a hoodie telling everyone to suck his dick. Stan, Kyle and Kenny buy dangerously cheap Super City E-Bikes from Tuong Lu Kim, signing waivers acknowledging a ninety-two percent explosion risk. Randy, enraged by kids speeding past him, forms the South Park Cycling Club, a gang of dads that demolishes Kim's shop and beats him up. When a masked kid tries to negotiate peace, Randy agrees, but Kenny's e-bike explodes, killing him. The town bans all e-bikes under the Kenny McCormick E-Bike Ordinance, the police confiscate every bike, and Randy caps it off by bribing Detective Yates and delivering the head of Keller's Bike Shop's owner to the mayor in a box. Cartman weeps at the bus stop over his confiscated bike. The town is now called South America.

The news report's interviews with outraged townspeople, and the silence greeting the question about the town's name change, are the episode's driest jokes. Cartman's El Gordo interview, his Speed Unlock Dongle demands, and Randy's Google-driven war planning, including the envelope of cash for Yates, keep both generations scheming.

Featured characters: Cartman and Liane; Stan, Kyle and Kenny; Randy and Sharon Marsh; Butters Stotch; Tolkien Black; Tuong Lu Kim; Detective Harris; Roger Donovan; Mayor McDaniels; Stephen Stotch and Richard Tweak.

Locations: Keller's Bike Shop; City E-Bike; the South Park sign; Denny's; Jamba; the forest; City Hall.

Key events & continuity: Kenny dies in an e-bike explosion; e-bikes are banned; Randy murders a bike shop owner; the town is renamed South America.

Butters is the only one in South Park furious that billionaires are building power-draining data centers in everyone's backyards, and when he investigates his own yard he finds Billionaire Weenietown, a tiny civilization of walking penises with banks, stock exchanges and data centers, singing about being in the money. The Mayor of Weenietown tries to keep the billionaires quiet and off podcasts, but they will not stop sharing their opinions. Butters teams up with an exterminator to expose them on the news, but the weenies buy the local media and get Tom Thompson to call the infestation completely under control. Finally the billionaires' own leadership hires Butters to quietly relocate the loudest weenies: he lures them with a microphone, vacuums them up, and dumps them in a Nashville stream. Stephen, meanwhile, is convinced Butters' measles vaccine turned him into a liberal, and calls the FBI to report himself for beastiality with Linda, whom he calls a blind sheep. The episode closes on deepfake footage of Trump's tiny singing penis detaching in a bathroom.

The Mayor's billionaire-etiquette seminar, quizzing weenies on yachts, prostitutes and podcast appearances, is the episode's centerpiece, and Old Cap's advice to call Miss Ladypenis escalates the scheme. Stephen's meltdown over Linda's forged vaccine signature, his blind-sheep rant, and the FBI call are the episode's bleakest domestic comedy.

Featured characters: Butters, Stephen and Linda Stotch; the Mayor of Weenietown, Old Cap and Miss Ladypenis; the X-Pest Control exterminator; Tom Thompson; the blonde reporter.

Locations: the Stotch backyard; Weenietown; the 4 News station; South Park Elementary; Nashville.

Key events & continuity: the billionaire weenies relocate to Nashville; Stephen's vaccine paranoia peaks; the town is now South America per the news.

The boys sneak into the R-rated Terrance and Phillip movie, Asses of Fire, and come out swearing like sailors, which gets them sent to counseling and grounded. When Kenny dies trying to light his own fart, his soul is denied Heaven and lands in Hell. Sheila Broflovski founds Mothers Against Canada, blaming the country for corrupting children, and her crusade escalates until the president declares war on Canada and Terrance and Phillip are sentenced to execution as war criminals. In Hell, Satan's lover Saddam Hussein sees the war as his ticket back to Earth, fulfilling a prophecy that the blood of two innocent Canadians on American soil will free them. The boys form La Resistance, recruit a French demolitions expert called the Mole, and try to stop the execution at a USO show, but Sheila shoots Terrance and Phillip anyway, unleashing Satan and Saddam. Cartman, whose V-chip malfunctions, electrocutes Saddam with profanity-powered lightning, Satan dumps Saddam back in Hell, and Kenny uses his one wish to undo the entire war. Everyone returns to life, Kenny ascends to Heaven, Wendy kisses Stan, and the town sings its happy ending.

Featured characters: Stan, Kyle, Cartman and Kenny; Sheila Broflovski; Terrance and Phillip; Satan and Saddam Hussein; Wendy Testaburger and Gregory; Chef; Mr. Mackey; the president; the Mole; Big Gay Al; Ike.

Locations: the Bijou Cinema; South Park Elementary; Hell; the USO show; Canada; Stark's Pond.

Key events & continuity: Kenny dies and ascends to Heaven for real; the American-Canadian war is undone; Sheila ends her crusade; Cartman's V-chip briefly gives him electric powers.

Forty years after the pandemic, Stan is an online whiskey consultant who has not spoken to Kyle in decades, until Kenny McCormick, now a famous scientist, dies and drags them all back to South Park. Cartman has become a rabbi in Colorado Springs with a Jewish wife and kids, which Kyle insists is a decades-long troll. At the funeral, Kenny's death is blamed on a COVID variant, the town is quarantined, and the old classmates discover Kenny's secret lab: he spent his life researching time travel to prevent the pandemic, and hid the data in an unlikely place. Stan confronts his father at Shady Acres, where Randy blames him for Shelly burning to death in the Tegridy fire and Sharon's suicide. The recovered footage reveals Kenny blames the ruined future on his three friends letting their friendship die, and the special ends with them vowing to fix it together, while Cartman schemes to stop them and keep his comfortable future.

The Denny's Applebee's Max waiter explaining the insect-protein menu, the closed police station, and Stark's Puddle nearly dried up sell the forty-year decay. Kenny's letter, the rats in the morgue, and the argument over whose hand goes in first are played as gross-out and genuine grief at once.

Featured characters: adult Stan, Kyle, Cartman and Kenny; Yentl and the Cartman kids; Jimmy Valmer; Tolkien Black; Wendy Testaburger; Tweek and Craig; Clyde Donovan; Randy Marsh; Victor Chaos; Scott Malkinson.

Locations: future South Park; Denny's Applebee's Max; South Park Church; Shady Acres; Kenny's lab; South Park Elementary Plus.

Key events & continuity: the future timeline is established; Kenny dies; Cartman is a rabbi; Randy admits starting the pandemic; first of two parts.

entries.n: South Park: Post Covid: The Return of Covid
entries.t:
With the town quarantined for thirty more years, the group races to use Kenny's time machine, but they need Victor Chaos, who turns out to be an adult Butters, locked in a mental asylum for sixteen years and now obsessed with NFTs. Cartman founds the Foundation Against Time Travel to protect his happy future, even knocking out Tweek and Craig and hanging them from a church ceiling. Clyde is sent back to March 2021 to kill Kyle and preserve the timeline, but future Stan, Kyle and Cartman follow, and future Cartman shoots Clyde dead. Realizing the timeline cannot be fixed by force, they instead heal the original wound: they get the boys courtside Nuggets seats, leave future weed for Randy, and Randy and Sharon reconcile and give away free Post-Covid special, preventing the pandemic's bitterness, and even Space Jam 2. In the new future, Kenny is alive and a Nobel winner, Stan tours Mars with the Space Force, and Cartman is a homeless bum shouting on the street, which everyone agrees cannot be fixed.

Vic's NFT sales pitch, delivered the moment he is handed a piece of paper, and his escape via convincing a guard to invest, show Butters never changed. The Alexas needing calming, the aluminum-foil hunt, and Cartman's FATT-to-FITT rebrand keep the time-travel mechanics shambolic.

Featured characters: adult Stan, Kyle and Cartman; Victor Chaos, adult Butters; Clyde Donovan; Randy and Sharon Marsh; Wendy; Tolkien; Jimmy; Kenny; Yentl; Ike.

Locations: Kenny's lab; the South Park Mental Asylum; South Park Church; March 2021; Denny's Applebee's Max.

Key events & continuity: the timeline is rewritten; Kenny lives; Cartman's future is miserable; the pandemic's damage is undone; conclusion of the two-parter.
k: south park: post covid: the return of covid

entries.t:
Colorado is in a drought, blamed on ManBearPig, and Denver needs water for farms, so everyone with a stream suddenly has liquid gold. Randy and Steve Black, now rival farmers, compete to sell their stream water as subscription streaming services, with the boys building thousands of popsicle-stick boats to prove the water flows to the Denver reservoir. Sleazy developer Talnua Cussler buys up every stream-side property, and is found murdered by ManBearPig. Meanwhile Cartman, still living in the hot dog stand, decides the way out is breast implants for his mom, raising ten thousand dollars through the boat business, but Liane refuses the surgery, so Cartman gets the implants himself. Steve goes missing after confronting Pi-Pi and the corrupt water commissioner, who are hoarding the water with ManBearPig as muscle. The special ends with Denver slowly draining dry.

Cartman's song about wanting something cool to happen to him, sung from the hot dog stand, is the special's emotional anchor, and his blindfolded hospital reveal for Liane plays his desperation straight. Randy being called Karen by his own family, Shelley's explanation of the slur, and his rage at the label fuel the farm rivalry.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Steve, Linda and Tolkien Black; Cartman and Liane; Talnua Cussler; Pi-Pi; the water commissioner; Kyle, Kenny and Butters.

Locations: Tegridy Farms; Credigree Weed; Denver; Pi Pi's Splashtown; the hot dog stand; Park County Police Station.

Key events & continuity: the streaming wars begin; Cussler is killed; Cartman gets breast implants; Steve is taken; first of two parts.

entries.n: South Park: The Streaming Wars Part 2
entries.t:
The boys testify about the streaming wars while Cartman sues Liane for refusing implants. Randy, after going full Karen and causing a twenty-car pileup, rediscovers his old geologist self and pitches a desalination plant to save Denver, but Pi-Pi, who plans to replace the city's water with his own urine, has it destroyed and sends ManBearPig after Randy. Cartman, Tolkien and Butters investigate Cussler's murder and find Steve alive in a cave with ManBearPig's son, Chuck Chuck. Randy's family gets him to embrace his Karen power once more with a hidden weed stash, and he storms Pi-Pi's Urineworld mid-commercial, exposing the scheme. ManBearPig turns on Pi-Pi when shown his own family, and the town celebrates the desalination plant, powered in part by saline from breast implants. Stan argues they should raise Chuck Chuck with kindness so he does not become his father, but Randy would rather party. Randy returns to geology, and Butters gets grounded.
