Randy's We Miss You Randy montage, digging out the Lorde outfit and the magician's vest, sells his return to geology, and Sharon's hidden weed stash is the family's vote of confidence. The celebrities' crypto commercials, Matt Damon's fortune favors the brave through gritted teeth, and Butters's grounding button the special's end.

Featured characters: Randy, Sharon, Stan and Shelly Marsh; Steve, Linda and Tolkien Black; Cartman, Butters and Kyle; Pi-Pi; ManBearPig, Chuck Chuck and PigBearGirl; Harrison Yates; Matt Damon.

Locations: Park County Courthouse; Pi-Pi's Urineworld; the desalination plant; Denver; Credigree Weed.

Key events & continuity: the streaming wars end; Pi-Pi is killed; Randy quits weed farming for geology; the plant opens; conclusion of the two-parter.
k: south park: the streaming wars part 2

entries.t:
Cartman keeps dreaming he is a Black woman in a universe where all his friends are diverse women, and becomes convinced Disney is replacing him. The dreams are real: a Kathleen Kennedy from another universe has been abusing an ancient AI artifact, the Panderstone, to churn out pandering movies, tearing holes between universes and swapping Cartman with his diverse counterpart from Universe 216-B. While the displaced Cartmans bumble through each other's worlds, Randy leads South Park's adults in a revolt against AI and handymen, catapulting a rock at their old college. At Disney, Bob Iger discovers their Kathleen Kennedy is actually Cartman-faced, and the executives trace the Panderverse to Randy's broken oven door, the one place with integrity and a broken door. Randy, Cartman 216-B and Kennedy collide through the portal, Cartman and Kennedy reconcile over their mutual blame, and everyone returns home, with Disney promising original content and Randy importing an army of poor handymen.

The handyman economy, with Gerald and a news reporter offering specialized services for basic repairs outside Home Depot, is the special's other plot, and the adults' catapult protest at their alma mater is pure South Park. Cartman 216-B forging Sheila's permission for a computer, and her devastation at having no saved game, are the multiverse's best jokes.

Featured characters: Cartman and Cartman 216-B; Stan, Kyle and Kenny of both universes; Randy and Sharon Marsh; Kathleen Kennedy; Bob Iger and Disney executives; PC Principal; Butters.

Locations: Universe 216-B; Tegridy Farms; Walt Disney Studios; South Park Elementary; Home Depot.

Key events & continuity: the multiverse is breached via the Panderstone; Cartman 216-B returns home; Kenny 216-B dies; Disney vows original films.

When art teacher Mrs. Streibel is caught running an OnlyFans, the parents panic, and Randy decides to launch his own page, filming himself pantsless while Sharon watches in disgust. She starts her own account and immediately outperforms him, sparking a humiliating rivalry. At school, Cartman founds a Cred energy-drink affinity group to bully non-drinkers, but Clyde is exposed for faking it with apple juice, so the crew ditches school for a CVS in Pueblo where a limited Mega Cred is being given away, and the resulting child riot destroys the stock. Randy's influencer ambitions get him auctioned to the highest bidder, from foreign governments to cereal companies, before the FBI arrests him for exposing kids to pornography. The boys confront their influencer idol LoganLeDouche, who admits it is all fake before being assassinated on camera. In the end Randy quits influencing, Clyde finally calls his stepmom Janice mom, and Cartman shares a rare Jelly Roll Midnight Waffle House Cred with Clyde.

Clyde's Moonrise Mellow apple-juice fraud, Cartman's spit-take, and the affinity group's humiliation are the episode's tightest sequence. Randy's recipe video using his testicles as the nuts, Sharon's designer-clothing revenge spending, and the influencer auction, with governments bidding on Randy, keep the satire firing.

Featured characters: Randy and Sharon Marsh; Cartman, Butters, Tweek and Clyde; Mrs. Streibel; LoganLeDouche; Nathan; Spencer Hollis; Janice; PC Principal and Strong Woman; the FBI.

Locations: South Park Elementary; Tegridy Farms; the Donovan residence; a CVS in Pueblo; a motel; the FBI office.

Key events & continuity: Randy's influencer career ends in arrest; Clyde accepts Janice; the Cred craze collapses.
k: south park not suitable for children

entries.n: South Park: The End of Obesity
entries.t:
When Dr. Gauche suggests weight-loss drugs for Cartman, the 1,200-dollar-a-month price tag crushes him, and he is prescribed Lizzo instead: body-positive music for life. Kyle vows to get the drugs covered, but the insurance maze defeats them, so the boys start manufacturing their own semaglutide from Indian raw materials and open a compounding pharmacy, drawing the wrath of a sugar cartel led by cereal mascots like Tony the Tiger. The moms of South Park, meanwhile, are robbing pharmacies for the drugs themselves, and Randy falls in with a party crew of MILFs. After a truck chase with the cartel that kills Kenny, the shipment turns out to contain only the pale insurance man. Randy confesses to Sharon, they skip the drugs for molly at a Holiday Inn, and Kyle gives a speech convincing the school to stop mocking obesity, which is exactly what Cartman wanted: now nobody can insult his weight, he is free to insult everyone else, and he buys a plane ticket to Pakistan.

Cartman's cereal-bomb escalations, from the Oppenheimer to the Stormy Daniels, and his thirty-minute bathroom sessions, are the special's running gag. The moms' crop-top pharmacy robbery, Randy's MILF-party high, and Towelie's warning about falling in with a bad crowd give the adult plot its own arc.

Featured characters: Cartman and Liane; Kyle, Stan, Butters and Kenny; Dr. Gauche; Randy, Sharon and Shelly Marsh; Towelie; the moms, Laura, Linda, Harriet and Alexis; the sugar cartel; the insurance man.

Locations: Dr. Gauche's office; the compounding pharmacy; Tweek Bros. Coffeehouse; Laura's party; the factory in India; South Park Elementary.

Key events & continuity: Kenny is killed by Tony the Tiger; the boys' pharmacy collapses; Cartman weaponizes body positivity; Sharon qualifies for Ozempic via Lizzo-induced diabetes.
k: south park: the end of obesity

entries.n: South Park: The Stick of Truth
entries.t:
ACT I — THE NEW KID IN TOWN

The story opens with Eric Cartman delivering a grand speech about the great war between two kid factions: the human Kingdom of Kupa Keep, which he rules as Grand Wizard, and the Elves. Both sides fight over the Stick of Truth, a plain wooden stick that, in the lore of their game, grants whoever holds it absolute control over the universe.

The player's character — the New Kid — has just moved to South Park with his parents. The family relocated to escape something that happened to the boy in their old town, an incident his parents refuse to discuss. To keep him from dwelling on it, his parents shoo him outside to make friends. On the street he runs into Butters, who is dressed as a paladin and fending off an elf-costumed kid. The New Kid scares the elf off, instantly befriending Butters — who, conveniently, lives next door. Butters brings the New Kid to Kupa Keep — Cartman's backyard — to meet the Grand Wizard and join the game.

Cartman asks for the New Kid's name, then ignores whatever is entered and christens him "Douchebag." The New Kid picks a class — Fighter, Mage, Thief, or Jew — buys a weapon, and spars with Clyde, whom he beats handily. Cartman then unveils the Stick of Truth itself: an actual stick. Before the celebration is over, the elves raid the keep. With the New Kid's help they are driven back, but they still snatch the Stick. Furious, Cartman banishes Clyde from the game for failing to guard it, and sends the New Kid to rally Kupa Keep's three top warriors: Tweek, Tolkien, and Craig.

Tweek is won over after the New Kid and Butters run a chore for him — picking up a package from a pair of meth heads camped out in Kenny's garage. Tolkien joins once the boys beat the security guard posted at his gate. Craig's house turns out to be empty: he's stuck in detention at school, so Cartman orders a jailbreak. The New Kid and Butters battle Mr. Mackey's ginger hall monitors and bust Craig out.

ACT II — THE BARD AND THE ALIENS

With the full army mustered, word comes that the Stick is in the hands of the Bard — a fearsome level-10 elf whose power comes from his music. The humans storm the Inn of the Giggling Donkey (Jimmy's house), fight through the elves, and the New Kid personally takes down the Bard: Jimmy himself. The Stick is recovered and returned to Kupa Keep, and the kids head home to sleep.

That night, a blue light floods the New Kid's bedroom window. Figures appear in his doorway, and he is abducted — a beat-for-beat echo of Cartman's own anal-probe incident. On the alien ship he discovers the townspeople are being probed too. The aliens strap him to a machine and begin the procedure, but he breaks their probes — one ends up lodged in his rear — and escapes with Randy Marsh, who was being probed alongside him. During the getaway they kill the ship's pilots, and the vessel crashes into the South Park Mall, venting a strange green toxin. The government seals the crash site, disguising the cleanup as the construction of a new Taco Bell.

The New Kid wakes with a satellite dish stuck in his backside. Cartman intercepts him with the morning news: the elves "cheated" and retook the Stick overnight. To gear up for full war, Cartman orders the New Kid to recruit the Goth Kids — which means passing their trials: looking the part, proving himself a true nonconformist, and dancing like a Goth.

While working on the Goth look, the New Kid is cornered by the elves and dragged to their kingdom, where the truth comes out: Kyle is the High King of the Elves, Stan his second-in-command, and Cartman has been sitting on the Stick the whole time — which, by the rules, is cheating. The New Kid switches allegiance and runs jobs for the elves, including tearing down Kupa Keep banners all over the neighborhood.

ACT III — THE TACO BELL CONSPIRACY

To prove his nonconformity, the New Kid holds up an offensive sign at a PTA meeting. There, Randy Marsh corners him and strong-arms him into investigating the so-called Taco Bell construction site. Randy teaches him the Sneaky Squeaker — a directed fart that distracts enemies so he can sneak past them.

Inside the fenced-off "construction site," the New Kid uncovers the truth: the green toxin from the alien crash has seeped into the sewers, and anything or anyone it touches turns into a Nazi Zombie. The government plans to demolish three blocks to contain it and pass the blast off as an earthquake. One careless agent leaves a recorder of the whole briefing on a table, and the New Kid carries it back to Randy. As he leaves, the Nazi Zombies break loose and start terrorizing the town — a crisis South Park's residents barely seem to register.

Back at the PTA meeting, the adults are horrified — but Randy didn't rewind the tape far enough, so he thinks the whole scheme is about clearing space for a Mega-Taco Bell and never learns about the zombies. He snaps a photo of the New Kid holding the Goth Kids' sign and sends it to his phone as "proof."

Once the New Kid has fully impressed the Goth Kids and earned their loyalty, he gets to choose which side they fight for: Cartman's humans or Kyle's elves. Either way, it ends with an assault on the school to recover the Stick, capped by a one-on-one duel against whichever leader he opposes — unless he chooses to betray his own leader instead. Both Kyle and Cartman try to finish him off with ranged attacks (Kyle with a leaf blower, Cartman with lighter-ignited farts), but the New Kid's command of his own anus overpowers them both.

The winning leader sends the Goth Kids to check inside the loser's desk — but the desks have no insides, just tabletops. One Goth spots writing on a desk: "Check my locker." The handwriting trail leads to Clyde's locker and his laptop, where Clyde appears on video to gloat: HE stole the Stick, he's raising an army of darkness to destroy the Earth, and he's dissolved both the human and elf kingdoms, stripping Cartman and Kyle of their power.

The boys race to Clyde's house and find he has built a massive treehouse fortress in his backyard, staffed by his dark army: the Vamp Kids, the emo kids, and the Nazi Zombies. Craig has defected to Clyde's side, since Cartman no longer has any authority over him. Just as the boys prepare to storm the keep, Butters' parents arrive and drag him home — it's bedtime.

ACT IV — GNOMES, GIRLS, AND CLYDE'S FALL

That night, Underpants Gnomes sneak into the New Kid's room to steal his underwear. He wakes up mid-theft; the panicking gnomes try to kill him, fail because he's too big, and have a warlock gnome shrink him down. The chase leads into his parents' bedroom, where the New Kid overhears them discussing why they moved: their son has a special "gift" the government wants to weaponize. Then they start having sex. The New Kid battles the Gnome Wizard right there on the bed. The defeated wizard surrenders his shrinking powder and explains they were stealing underwear to fight the alien goo — before being crushed by the mother's breasts, while the New Kid is flattened by the father's scrotum. He wakes up in his own bed, unharmed, to find a gnome waiting with a side job: help them meet their underpants quota, since the New Kid killed so many of their best men.

On Facebook, Kyle calls a summit of humans and elves and begs both sides to unite. Cartman and the KKK react with disgust, but Kyle silences the squabble: if they don't join forces, Clyde's Nazi Zombie army will overrun the world. Most of their troops having defected, Kyle proposes recruiting the Pirates, the Federation, and the Girls. The New Kid — who accumulates Facebook friends at a freakish, unprecedented rate — is sent to win over the girls.

The girls' price is a detective job: someone spread a vicious rumor that one of them visited the abortion clinic, and the New Kid must identify the snitch. He poses as Bebe's boyfriend to see if the suspect, Monica, flirts with him (proof of two-facedness), then fights her boyfriend. Monica turns out innocent, so the New Kid heads to the abortion clinic for the records himself — and ends up performing an abortion on Randy. The clinic is then overrun by Nazi zombie fetuses; after fighting them off, he battles Khloe Kardashian's giant aborted fetus and secures the file. It's written in French, so he forges a passport and goes to Canada. In the Photo Dojo, the clerk turns out to be a pedophile (the real clerk is tied up); the New Kid beats him and crosses the border. The Prince of Canada demands the Bishop's balls as proof of loyalty before he'll free Montreal's translator. The New Kid can kill the Bishop — or spare him and bring back testicles from a Dire Pig, a famously nasty wild boar, instead. The translated records expose Heidi Turner as the rumor-spreader; she apologizes, and the girls join the alliance.

The united kids storm Clyde's fortress. After fighting past Craig, they meet Randy, who delivers terrifying news: the government has planted a "snuke" — an ass-nuke — inside Mr. Slave's rectum to wipe out South Park, and only an abortion can disarm it. Shrunk by gnome dust, the New Kid ventures into Mr. Slave's anus, battling Nazi Zombie Bacteria, the Sparrow Prince, and two SWAT officers, and — with Jimmy's help — aborts the snuke, saving the town. He exits through Mr. Slave's mouth and joins the boys in Clyde's throne room.

Clyde refuses to hand over the Stick. Mistaking the green goo for "Taco Green Sauce," he pours it on Chef's corpse and resurrects him as a Nazi Zombie. The New Kid defeats zombie Chef; Clyde gives up playing, and Cartman seizes the Stick and boots Clyde out of the treehouse.

ACT V — THE BETRAYAL AND THE END OF THE GAME

As the kids celebrate and crown the New Kid "King Douchebag," government agents arrive. Their chief reveals he knows the boy's real name — Dovahkiin — and that they've been hunting him for his uncanny power to amass Facebook friends faster than anyone alive. The chief confiscates the Stick, and when the kids explain its power, he keeps it for himself and offers the New Kid a place at his side as Ruler of the Universe. The New Kid refuses — but Kenny betrays the group and joins the agent. Enraged, the kids turn on Kenny, who doses himself with green goo and becomes an ultra-powerful Nazi Zombie. One by one the companions are knocked out of the fight, and Kenny seems unbeatable — until Cartman tells the New Kid to break the sacred oath he swore on his first day in South Park: never fart on another man's balls. Cartman pins Kenny from behind, the New Kid lets one rip on Kenny's testicles, and a white flash expands over all of South Park, curing every Nazi Zombie.

As the town rebuilds, the boys and the New Kid realize how far the battle for the Stick has spiraled, and they agree to end the game by hurling the Stick into the lake. Deciding what to play next, they ask the New Kid what he wants. He tells them to forget it — he's going home. He walks off, and Cartman mutters that he's quite the jerk.

Side quests:

- Big Game Huntin' With Jimbo — Jimbo tasks the New Kid with hunting down seven of the most dangerous creatures in and around South Park. Outcome: completing the full hunting checklist finishes the quest.
- ManBearPig — Al Gore is hunting ManBearPig again and needs the New Kid's help tracking it down; a separate beat has the beast attacking the church. Outcome: the New Kid assists Gore's hunt and confronts the creature.
- Unfriend Al Gore — Al Gore won't stop spamming the New Kid's Facebook, so the New Kid goes to his base and beats him up until he stops. Outcome: Gore is silenced and unfriended.
- Dropping the Kids Off — Mr. Hankey's kids have run off while their mother was out drinking; rather than mediate the domestic dispute, the New Kid is sent to round up the children. Outcome: the kids are found and returned.
- Find Jesus — Priest Maxi challenges the New Kid to find Jesus at the church. Outcome: Jesus is located.
- Flower For a Princess — a fair maiden needs a flower delivered to her. Outcome: the flower is delivered.
- Hide 'n' Seek — the New Kid plays hide and seek with the kindergarteners scattered around town. Outcome: all the hiding children are found.
- Magical Songs — Jimmy can't be a proper bard without a flute for his inspiring battle tunes; the New Kid helps him get one. Outcome: Jimmy gets his flute.
- Mongolian Beef — Tuong Lu Kim orders the New Kid to drive off the Mongolians by beating up their kids in the Tower of Peace. Outcome: the Mongolian kids are beaten and the tower is cleared.
- Mr. Slave's Package — the New Kid picks up Mr. Slave's package from the post office and delivers it. Outcome: the package is delivered.
- Nazi Zombie Bounty — Detective Harris pays for rings collected off the Nazi Zombies roaming town. Outcome: rings are turned in for the bounty.
- Phase One — the Underpants Gnomes need underpants to fill their quota, and the New Kid helps gather them. Outcome: the quota is filled.
- Rats in the Cellar — Skeeter's bar has a rat infestation in its cellar; only a true hero can clear it. Outcome: the rats are slain.
- Restoring the Balance — DogPoo asks the New Kid to tear down five human banners around town. Outcome: the banners are destroyed.
- The Homeless Problem — the New Kid locates the homeless camps around town and chases the homeless away to improve South Park's image. Outcome: the camps are cleared.
- The She-Ogre — Stan lost his iPhone to an ogre and needs the New Kid to get it back. Outcome: the phone is recovered.
- The Timmy Express — the New Kid collects 12 flags bearing the Timmy Express logo. Outcome: all twelve flags are collected.
- Vulcan Around — the New Kid finds Kevin Stoley's dad's iPad near the church and returns it to him. Outcome: the iPad is returned.
- Wasted Cache — Mr. Mackey asks the New Kid to "throw out" a computer monitor for him. Outcome: the monitor is disposed of.

entries.n: South Park: The Fractured But Whole
entries.t:
ACT I — THE COON'S ORIGIN AND THE MISSING CAT

Sometime after the war over the Stick of Truth, the kids of South Park take up a new game: superheroes. But a falling-out over Cartman's planned superhero film franchise splits the group in two, and rival factions start agitating for a civil war so each can launch its own franchise.

The story proper begins with the Coon's opening tale: he claims to have traveled back in time to "Ancient Zaron" in the year 627 A.D., where the King's soldiers are losing a war (the kids are play-fighting in the street). The King — played by the New Kid — has abandoned the battle to sit on his throne (a toilet). Called back outside to defend his troops, the King fights, and then the Coon appears, announcing he has come from the future to fix it. The kids agree to switch their game to superheroes. The New Kid heads to the Coon Lair, where the Coon spins him an epic superhero backstory, and is sent out to chase down clues about a missing cat — the case that kicks off the whole adventure.

From there the New Kid builds his hero from the ground up. The Origins missions walk him through inventing and re-inventing his backstory, picking up new character classes along the way (Origins, Origins 2: New Beginnings, Origins 3: The Visitor, Origins 4: The Omega Prologue). He fills out his character sheet piece by piece: talking with Father Maxi to face his fears for the Kryptonite section (A Touch of Faith), sitting through Mr. Mackey's talks for the Sex/Gender section (The Talk, and later the advanced Talk 2: The Gendering), and meeting PC Principal for the microaggression seminar (Microaggression Academy) and the Race/Ethnicity section (Race Academy: First Class). He has to build a following on Coonstagram (Coonstagram), fetch the Coon a taco from Freeman's Tacos (The Burrito Whisperer), discover the fast-travel flag on Main Street (Gotta Go Fast), and learn the basics of artifacts (Birth of a Coon Friend).

The cat hunt drives the early missions. At the bus stop, the New Kid finds sixth graders torturing a cat and teaches them the lesson every fourth grader dreams of delivering (Rise of the Fourthies). He saves Mosquito from the seductive Raisins Girls to complete his Kryptonite entry (Mosquito in a Honey Pot). The team realizes they need Toolshed to track the cat down (We Need a Tool). The trail leads into the Peppermint Hippo, where the New Kid must confront the Girl with the Penis Tattoo — the only one who knows where Scrambles, the missing cat, is (The Bowels of the Beast). Along the way he helps Super Craig find his missing guinea pig Stripe (The Chains of Super Craig), seeks Classi's intel on the cats (CLASSIfied), and learns new fart powers while fetching Classi's medication (Medicinal Fried Fiasco).

ACT II — CIVIL WAR

The franchise feud boils over. The Freedom Pals invade Main Street, and it's up to Coon and Friends to beat them back (Civil War). The Freedom Pals come back hungry for revenge (Civil War 2: Playtime's Over). Meanwhile the New Kid helps Human Kite destroy his evil alternate-universe self — twice (Alternate Universes Collide, Alternate Universes Collide Again).

Between battles, the New Kid runs errands that deepen the world: he performs with Tupperware and Wonder Tweek at the South Park Senior Center (The Samaritan Agenda), heads home to bed before each night's mission (Homeward Bound, Under Covers, Nocturnal Submission), and gets drawn into Sgt. Yates's investigation of a drug kingpin in town (Operation: Just 'Cause), which escalates into taking down the real "kingpin" (Operation: Blind Justice).

ACT III — CHAOS, MITCH CONNER, AND THE CATS

Professor Chaos becomes a major player. The New Kid storms U-STOR-IT to stop him once and for all (The Hundred Hands of Chaos), then recruits his help to infiltrate the Freedom Pals (The Chaos Gambit). A mysterious invitation leads to a meeting with Mitch Conner at SoDoSoPa (The Invitation). The New Kid solves Mitch Conner's riddles to track him to his hiding place (To Catch a Coon), consults Dr. Mephesto about the missing cats (The Many Asses of Dr. Mephesto), and joins the fight against the town's corrupt cops to recover the cat (The Thin White Line). A summons to the Freedom Pals' base brings important news (Freedom Calling).

Everything converges on Mitch Conner. Using time-traveling farts, the New Kid journeys through time to stop Mitch Conner from becoming mayor (Farts of Future Past) — the climactic gambit of the main story.

SIDE MISSIONS:

- A Perky Predicament — the New Kid helps Mosquito take down the Raisins Girls. Outcome: the Raisins Girls are defeated.
- A Randy Mystery — somebody keeps keying Randy Marsh's car; the New Kid investigates and puts a stop to it. Outcome: the culprit is found and the keying ends.
- Always Bet on Chaos — the New Kid helps Chaos secure a loan to fund his minions. Outcome: Chaos gets his financing.
- For Nippopolis — the New Kid obtains a cheesing vial to unlock a new summon. Outcome: the summon is acquired.
- Ghost Reconciler — the New Kid retrieves Craig's laptop from Tweek. Outcome: the laptop is returned.
- Peppermint Hippo Lost & Found — the New Kid finds Jimbo's lost wallet inside the Peppermint Hippo. Outcome: the wallet is recovered.
- Raisins on a Rampage — the New Kid defeats 15 Raisins Girls. Outcome: all fifteen are beaten.
- The Big Beatdown — the New Kid rescues Ms. Cartman from a pimp and his crew. Outcome: Ms. Cartman is saved.
- Therapy Wars — the New Kid helps Tweek and Craig through their couple's counseling. Outcome: the session is completed.
- Touch the Sky — the New Kid helps the little gay fish get his mother into Heaven. Outcome: the mission is fulfilled.
- Vigilante Marketing — the New Kid helps Ms. Cartman promote her tutoring service. Outcome: the service is promoted.
- (You Can) Call on Me — the New Kid helps Call Girl defeat the Crab People so she can fix her phone. Outcome: the Crab People are beaten and the phone is fixed.

SCAVENGER HUNTS:

- Big Gay Al's Big Gay Cats — the New Kid tracks down all of Big Gay Al's missing cats. Outcome: every cat is found.
- The Headshot Job — the New Kid places all of Mr. Adams' headshots around town. Outcome: the headshots are posted.
- The Yaoi Project — the New Kid collects all the Creek yaoi artwork for Craig's dad. Outcome: the collection is completed.

DLC — FROM DUSK TILL CASA BONITA:

Vampires have dragged Mysterion's (Kenny's) little sister Karen to Casa Bonita, and she is on the verge of being turned into one of them. Mysterion calls the New Kid and begs for help rescuing her before the transformation is complete. A bus carries the New Kid to the restaurant, where Mysterion is waiting on the roof. Mysterion trains the New Kid on the spot: with his Netherborn powers channeled through him, the New Kid unlocks a brand-new hero class and takes down the first wave of Vampire Kids outside. Mysterion joins as a fixed partner for the mission.

Inside Casa Bonita, they spot Karen dressed like the vampires, with their leader Mike Makowski presiding over what he announces is his birthday gathering. The host demands $17 per meal ticket, so the New Kid gets in by paying double, by knocking a ticket from the host's hand with Snap N Pops and freezing time to grab it, or by sneaking past a flaming stove to steal tickets from the cashier. Along the way, the Coon is found trapped behind a photo-stand "JAIL" cutout — he was investigating the vampire infestation and got captured; the New Kid takes his picture and he breaks out, joining the team.

The mission turns into a scavenger hunt when Mike flees through a locked door with Karen: Mr. Adams announces the New Kid must find vampire relics to open it. The search takes them through the restaurant — past a burrito spiked with hot sauce that sends the New Kid sprinting for the bathroom in a timed toilet mini-game (success earns the Shart Fiesta crafting item) — and into battles with the Vampire Kids, where Henrietta Biggle, a Goth kid mistaken for a vampire, joins the fight after clarifying she only smokes. The hunt continues through the arcade and the dining hall, where Chiquita the gorilla defends the vampires' sopaipilla operation. Relic by relic, the New Kid closes in on Karen before she is fully turned.

DLC — BRING THE CRUNCH:

The counselors at Camp Lake Tardicaca have vanished, and if they aren't found the camp will be shut down. Fastpass (Jimmy) calls the New Kid — the only hero who answered — for help. At the camp, Professor Chaos appears with a flashlight (the source of the thunder and lightning), and then a pink sphere of light descends from the sky: Mintberry Crunch (Bradley), who crossed interstellar space after receiving Fastpass's distress signal.

The investigation leads to the shower room, where the counselors were last seen making repairs, and then into the forest, where the team finds a pit of red paint and is ambushed by woodland monsters. Mintberry Crunch demonstrates his powers in battle — Flavor Burst and his Ultimate, Bringing the Crunch — until the monsters summon Spontaneous Bootay, who recognizes the New Kid and wants revenge. Mintberry Crunch admits his powers don't work on her, and the team flees into a nearby cabin, barricading the door.

Trapped, the New Kid must harness the power of the Final Girl: gathering an axe, a sledgehammer, hedge clippers, and a circular saw from around the cabin (each retrieval triggering its own scare), then channeling horror-movie survival energy to transform into the Final Girl — Bootay's one weakness. She backs out of the fight, and the New Kid unleashes the new powers: Saw Bleed, Hammer Bomb, and the Ultimate Final Vengeance.

DLC — DANGER DECK:

Tupperware has built the Danger Deck, a holographic battle simulator wired into a terminal at the Freedom Pals base. Activating it teleports the New Kid's hero team into hard-light combat scenarios staged in never-before-seen corners of South Park — custom gauntlets of holographic enemies drawn from across the whole game, growing steadily more punishing. Victories pay out in costumes, artifacts, and gear that carry over into other playthroughs.

Five scenarios, three battles each, every fight opened by one of Tupperware's "Danger!" briefings and twisted by an Ultra Modifier:

Sixth Grader Base — "Charm School": an onslaught of charm attackers, South Park's deadliest temptresses plus Rebecca; keep them out of striking distance with knockback powers. "Scorched Earth": the combat grid is saturated with area-of-effect attacks, so spread the team out fast. "Heavy Hitters": brutal bosses team up, and King Crab's healing reaches across the entire grid — focus him down first. Ultra Modifier: turns get skipped by real-time events. Rewards: the Nanobot Chassis DNA strand, Asgard headwear, and Asgard scars.

Lounge — "Shadow Swarm": a summoning algorithm floods the grid with clones; chill the summoners before the swarm gets out of hand. "Dead and Beary'd": twin Bearys backed by snipers; the bears are lethal up close, so pin them at the grid's far edges with knockback. "We Three Freemans": Morgan Freeman alongside two younger holographic versions of himself — he fights like a god. Ultra Modifier: every enemy death makes the survivors hit harder and tougher. Rewards: the City Ninja Assassination Contract mission item and the Amaze Ball artifact.

Graveyard — "Boneyard Bullies": abusive sixth graders and the hideous abominations that enable them; King Crab's infinite-range healing again demands he dies first. "Adverse Conditions": holo-thugs dealing area attacks laced with punishing status effects, led by the stone-cold Sixth Grader Leader — keep him chilled. "Disarray Unfoiled": General Disarray returns with an elite Chaos squad; never let his exploders get close, because he can detonate them on command. Ultra Modifier: team members start each turn shocked. Rewards: the High-Res helmet and the Avenging Nezumi artifact.

Waste Management — "Mental Assult": confuse attacks keep the battle shifting; use knockback or pull to separate medics from heavy hitters. "Beasts n' Priests": an unholy alliance of Catholic priests and woodland critters whose telegraphed attacks box the team in — lure them into a single row to stay safe. "Jared Reloaded": the second coming of Jared and his aides; stay away, because unlike most enemies he can attack even while charging a telegraph. Ultra Modifier: healing powers are nullified. Rewards: High-Res gloves and suit, plus the Danger Gyro artifact.

City Dump — "Emotional Violence": a legion of Therapy Kids wielding advanced shaming techniques; shut down the sixth-grader medic before he can heal the others. "Stand Your Ground": enemies rush and knock their way into the team's personal space — bring high-health heroes with heavy-damage powers. "Civil War 4.0": Tupperware's ultimate no-win test, a horde of Civil War combatants — Captain Diabetes, Doctor Timothy, Human Kite, Mosquito, Mysterion, Super Craig, Toolshed, and Wonder Tweek. Ultra Modifier: enemies are immune to status effects. Rewards: the Summons Decryptor mission item and the Asgard suit with bracers.
k: south park: the fractured but whole

entries.t:
THE ADVENTURE THEME — COWBOYS VS. INDIANS

The boys can't agree on which LARP game to play, until Cartman — dressed as Sheriff Cartman — breaks up the argument and pitches "Cowboys vs. Indians," inviting the New Kid to help the Cowboys finally beat the Indians. He video-calls the New Kid, tells him to show up in cowboy clothes with his phone in hand, and personally walks him through the first story stages. As the New Kid fights through the Adventure campaign, he takes on the Indian kids led by Stan of Many Moons. Stan retreats and calls in the pirates as reinforcements, but the New Kid overpowers every card Stan fields and defeats him.

THE SCI-FI THEME — ROBOTS VS. ALIENS

Cartman reappears costumed as A.W.E.S.O.M.-O 4000 with a new scenario: a war between robots and aliens. The New Kid battles through it and finally defeats Cyborg Kenny, who insists he is the one true Phone Destroyer. Between stages, Butters — calling himself "Don King" — introduces the New Kid to PVP battles. Kyle gets the New Kid on the line and tries to warn him that Cartman and Butters are using him, but hangs up before Cartman can catch him making the call.

THE MYSTICAL THEME — THE MASTER NINJEW

The boys discover the New Kid has beaten Kenny so badly they have effectively killed him. Sheriff Cartman shrugs it off and just wants the New Kid back on the Cowboys' side. Kyle is furious at how eagerly Cartman is tricking the New Kid into phone addiction, and storms off to return to his "spiritual roots." Feeling his control slipping, Cartman reinvents himself as Zen Cartman and manipulates the New Kid into fighting the Master Ninjew and his army of gods and holy warriors. The New Kid sides with Zen Cartman, brings down the Master Ninjew, and beats Kyle so severely that Kyle gives up arguing and rejoins Cartman.

THE FANTASY THEME — PALADIN BUTTERS' COUP

Butters contacts the New Kid directly to pull him into more PVP. Sheriff Cartman interrupts and orders Butters to change his costume; Butters obliges by becoming Paladin Butters, and gleefully uses the New Kid as his weapon to kill the Wizard King and seize the throne for himself. With Butters's whole army defeated, Grand Wizard Cartman — hiding in Kupa Keep — challenges the New Kid to a final duel. The kids cheer as Grand Wizard Cartman falls. They gather around the New Kid, congratulating him or sulking at him over how much money has been spent on the game.

THE SUPERHERO THEME — THE LEGENDARY CARD

Cartman, now dressed as the Coon, contacts the New Kid about a new Legendary card, urging him to obtain it before the other superheroes and villains do. Wendy — operating as Call Girl — hands out quests to the New Kid to identify which rivals are also hunting the card.

Join Cartman, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny — rendered in three dimensions — to celebrate the most magical day in any young child's life: a snow day. Team up with as many as three friends and fight your way through the snow-buried streets of South Park on a quest to save the world and savor a day with no school.
